title: Fantasy Football Start or Sit  Week 10: Jalen Coker, Bryce Young, Chuba Hubbard
full_text:
With the Carolina Panthers set to take on the New Orleans Saints in Week 10, it's time to make fantasy football lineup decisions on quarterback Bryce Young, wide receiver Jalen Coker and running back Chuba Hubbard.
It was tough sledding for both Hubbard and Coker last week versus an elite Denver Broncos defense .
Hubbard failed to register 100 yards from scrimmage and did not find the end zone and Coker tallied just 29 yards on four catches.
Young was on the opposite side of the spectrum after he finished with 276 passing yards and three touchdowns to one pick. Young's yardage output was his most since Week 6, and he scored three touchdowns in a game for the first time since Week 2.
Now, a look at what we're doing with the Panthers' offensive trio for the Week 10 game against the Saints.
After a strong start to the season , it has been tough sledding for Coker the last three weeks, as he's tallied seven catches for 74 yards and one touchdown in that span.
As a result, Coker now ranks as WR27 overall in fantasy points per game, according to Fantasy Pros , which makes him a flex option who is fairly reliant on his matchup.
This week, Coker draws a matchup against a Saints defense giving up the 13th-most fantasy points per game to wideouts this season, per CBS Sports .
That's a good enough matchup to justify putting Coker into lineups on Sunday afternoon.
Young is coming off a nice bounce-back showing in Week 9 and is ranked as QB11 overall in fantasy points per contest, which makes him an every-week starter in 10-12 team leagues.
Adding more optimism for him this week, Young will meet a New Orleans unit that has ceded the 11th-most fantasy points per game to signal-callers and the 12th-most touchdowns per contest.
Young should be in lineups this week.
Hubbard has easily been the Panthers' most consistent fantasy producer this season thanks to his impressive scoring output, yardage production and involvement in the passing game.
Entering this week, Hubbard ranks as RB6 overall in fantasy points per game, which makes him a locked-in RB1 every week.
Matchup is irrelevant with Hubbard since he's a lineup lock, but it's worth noting that the Saints are giving up the most fantasy points per game to running backs this season, so Hubbard has an opportunity to blow up.

title: Will the Panthers Beat the Saints? Here Are Our Staff Predictions
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have lost three straight, yet they somehow still hold first place in the NFC South . That could well change this afternoon. They're in New Orleans for what amounts to a first-place bout.
The two teams are 3-5, so the winner will grab sole possession of first once the clock hits zero. The Saints have had the Panthers' number recently, but they have yet to meet this season. How will this one go?
Here are the Panthers On SI staff predictions.
The Carolina Panthers have a chance to pick up a much-needed division win against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday. However, this will be a tough road test for Carolina.
The Panthers need better protection for Bryce Young and a strong defensive performance under interim coordinator Todd Wash. New Orleans is coming off an overtime win against Cleveland and will look to carry that momentum into Sunday’s matchup. Expect a close game, but the Saints get the edge at home.
Apparently no team in the NFC South is going out of its way to want to win the title. It’s a division where every team is at least 2 games under .500 and every club has a losing home record. A year ago, the Saints won just two games, which included a sweep of the Panthers.
Bryce Young has not been super sharp as of late, but he showed a lot of resiliency last Sunday. Carolina has turned over the ball 12 times this season, but Kellen Moore’s team has been even worse. There will be a lot of bend-but-don’t-break by the Panthers’ defense, who will limit the Saints to four field goals and one touchdown, so Dave Canales’s club will eke out a one-point win.
The margins are as thin as can possibly be this Sunday. These two teams are evenly matched. The Panthers have the best win (over Detroit in Week 4), but the Saints have been better of late (coming off an OT win over the Browns). They are not separated by much.
It's almost impossible to predict this one. Will the Saints' strong pass rush make mincemeat of the Panthers' weak offensive line? Will Bryce Young shred the Saints' fifth-worst pass defense? Can Tyler Shough take advantage of a depleted Panthers' secondary? Might Chuba Hubbard plow through the Saints' fourth-worst rushing defense?
The Panthers have more advantages than disadvantages, and they could get back a number of healthy contributors. Still, it won't be an easy one.
If there's ever a time for Carolina to get right, it’s on Sunday against the New Orleans Saints. This Saints defense is the second-worst pass defense Carolina has faced. New Orleans ranks 28th in the NFL in passing yards allowed, surrendering 236.6 per game. As an overall defense, New Orleans is arguably the worst, ranking 29th in rushing yards allowed per game.
Carolina may have reinforcements coming to the defense, as EDGE Jaelan Phillips and cornerback Will Lee III are both listed as questionable for Sunday. Even if the defense underperforms, this is a game where Carolina should be able to keep up in a shootout.

title: GM Dan Morgan’s Biggest 2026 Mistake Could Haunt Panthers’ Playoff Hopes
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are still in the hunt in the NFC South, but the lack of depth has been exposed by several injuries. This is a question for general manager Dan Morgan to answer.
Although the Carolina Panthers have a losing record, they are still in contention for the NFC South Division title. But the second half of the season will test the depth that general manager Dan Morgan brought in for this team.
The last three games for the Carolina Panthers have shown that there are many problems with this team, even though they are still in the race for the NFC South with a 3-5 record.
Morgan's biggest mistake this year was not bringing in more depth at cornerback.
Will Lee III and Akayleb Evans have also dealt with injuries, further depleting the Panthers' secondary. With Lee unavailable against Denver and Evans on injured reserve, Carolina had little dependable depth behind its starting cornerbacks. Against the Broncos, the Panthers were forced to start Wilson and Thornton, who struggled in the game.
We looked into the Panthers' issues with cornerback depth in a previous article , but now the problems are fully visible.
The Panthers were called for four defensive pass interference penalties against Denver. One of Wilson's penalties was declined in favor of a taunting penalty against him on the same play. Two of the accepted DPI penalties came on drives that ended in Denver touchdowns.
When a defense is getting beat consistently on the outside, that is a very difficult situation to overcome.
While injuries are part of football, Morgan did not do enough to make sure there were players available on the roster who could step in when a starter went down.
The secondary simply does not have enough dependable depth to handle the loss of both Horn and Jackson.
There were several cornerbacks who could have been of interest to the Panthers as the November 10 trade deadline approached.
The Panthers have limited salary-cap space and would have had to consider the cost of bringing in a player for the short term, as well as the draft capital that would be required to acquire that player.
As previously discussed in why the Panthers stayed quiet at the trade deadline, Morgan ultimately decided not to make a move.
The Panthers will have to find a long-term solution at the cornerback position, but for now, they are relying on the players already on the roster until some of the injured players return to the field.
In other news, Carolina's injured players are making progress toward returning to the field. On Wednesday, the practice windows for cornerback Mike Jackson, running back Jonathon Brooks and wide receiver Xavier Legette were opened, while Jaelan Phillips returned to practice after missing the last three games. Jackson was listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against New Orleans.
The Panthers are trying to build a team for years to come, and Morgan does not want to trade for a player who could hurt the team in the long run.
Carolina is currently in a position where every game counts, and the secondary cannot continue to be a liability.
Morgan's biggest mistake this season was not making a trade for a player who could help the team in the long run. He built a team with a lot of depth at many positions but not enough in the secondary.
The secondary must improve for the Panthers to have any chance of reaching the playoffs. If the team fails to do so, many will point to Morgan's decisions in building the roster.

title: Panthers' Biggest Problem Could Cost Them a Chance to Win the NFC South
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are still in the hunt to win the NFC South, but the first half of the season under third-year head coach Dave Canales has been anything but consistent.
The first half of the season for the Carolina Panthers has been a mix of good and bad. They have played some of the best teams in the league and shown they can match up with them. But there have also been some bad losses to teams lower in the standings. Right now, the Panthers are 3-5 on the season and on a three-game losing streak.
The biggest problem that the Carolina Panthers have had this season is their lack of discipline. The Panthers have committed too many penalties, and that is something head coach Dave Canales needs to work on with the team.
Carolina has been penalized 70 times for 635 yards this season, an average of 8.8 penalties for 79.4 yards per game. Last year, the Panthers averaged 5.6 penalties for 44.8 yards per game. That is a significant increase and a problem that has continued throughout the season.
The errors have hurt Carolina in several games this season, including the season opener against Chicago, when the Panthers were penalized 11 times for 84 yards; the game against the Eagles, when Carolina was penalized 13 times for 149 yards; and the game against the Broncos, when the Panthers were penalized 13 times for 119 yards.
In several games this season, the Panthers have extended opposing drives because of the penalties they have committed. This was especially noticeable against the Broncos, when defensive pass interference penalties repeatedly helped Denver keep drives alive.
After the Denver game, Canales said, “When you play a good opponent, you have to minimize the mistakes, and 100 yards of penalties in the first half was a big one. We're asking our corners to challenge outside, but we got to be clean with our hands.”
These errors must stop. The penalties are giving opponents better field position and allowing them to gain more yards than they would have otherwise.
Carolina Panthers head coach Dave Canales has some serious changes to make on the field, similar to the changes he has made with the coaching staff this season. He let go of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero and promoted defensive line coach Todd Wash to the interim defensive coordinator role.
The Carolina Panthers can still win the NFC South in the second half of the season, but they are going to have to play much better than they have in the first half. The Panthers have very little room for error if they want to make the playoffs at 3-5.
Canales has already made a major change to the coaching staff. Now, he needs to find a way to get his players to clean up the mistakes that keep putting the Panthers in difficult situations. If the penalties continue, Carolina could find its playoff hopes slipping away.

title: Panthers Have Bigger Aspirations, but Are They Good Enough to Get There?
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers find themselves in an interesting position for the second half of the 2026 NFL season. The Panthers have lost three straight games but still remain in the thick of the NFC South race with the opportunity to make the playoffs.
While Carolina is not a playoff-caliber team yet, it is showing signs of life as a 3-5 team. There are also many reasons for concern as to whether or not this team can play with any consistency.
The Carolina Panthers fell to the Denver Broncos, 26-21, in Week 9 action. Quarterback Bryce Young completed 28 of 39 passes for 276 yards and three touchdowns in the loss. However, he also had an interception in the end zone and lost a fumble late in the game that was recovered by the Broncos. The Panthers also had 13 penalties for 119 yards in the loss.
The Panthers have lost three straight to the Buccaneers, Packers and Broncos. In each of those games, mistakes were made that were capitalized on by the other team.
The reason Carolina is still in the hunt for the playoffs is because of the division it plays in. The Panthers and New Orleans Saints are both 3-5 and tied for first place in the division. Tampa Bay and Atlanta are both 3-6.
Carolina can remain in the division race without having to make up too many games on the first-place teams. Last year, the Panthers won the NFC South with an 8-9 record.
Winning the division and making a playoff run are two different things, though. The Panthers need to find a way to become more consistent.
This will be a huge game for the Panthers as they look to get back on track and win in New Orleans. If they can get a win against the Saints, then they will be in a good position in the division as well as stopping their current slide. Carolina has Baltimore and Tampa Bay after New Orleans.
There is still plenty of time for the Panthers to turn things around, but the NFC South gives them plenty of opportunities.
The main thing that the Panthers are looking for in the rest of the season is to be able to play some consistent football. The defense needs to be able to stop teams from scoring, and the offense needs to stop making mistakes like they have been in the last few games.
This team wants to do more than just compete in the NFC South this year. Whether or not they have the goods to make another run at the playoffs is yet to be determined, but the next few weeks will provide answers to that question.

title: Panthers’ Most Disappointing Player in 2026 Has Been a Huge Surprise
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have severely underperformed so far this season. At 3-5, Carolina has lost three straight and has clear flaws on the roster. The defense hasn't lived up to preseason expectations, but injuries are a huge part of why.
The secondary has been thin since Week 3, and that should change this weekend with Will Lee listed as questionable and Mike Jackson returning to practice despite being listed as doubtful on Friday.
The biggest question entering this season was how much of a leap, if any, would Bryce Young take. It's clear that Young has improved; his poise, conviction, ball placement, and subtle pocket movement have all been outstanding.
Two years ago, when the Panthers were objectively awful, Bryce Young was the problem for the first half of the season; that's not the case anymore. The Panthers' biggest problem right now is the offensive line . One player in particular has been at the forefront of that unit's issues.
Rasheed Walker was supposed to be one of the steals of free agency for Carolina. In 2025, Walker started at left tackle for the Green Bay Packers and excelled as a pass blocker. Walker posted a 94% pass-block win rate, which ranked 11th in the NFL.
Walker allowed five sacks for the entire 2025 season with Green Bay. Now, through eight games in Carolina, he's allowed five sacks. It's not just giving up sacks; Walker has allowed 45 QB pressures in 2026. For context, the league leader in pressures allowed is Spencer Fano, with 52.
Walker remained the starting left tackle for Carolina against Denver, and as he's done throughout the season, he allowed pressure, as Nik Bonitto won the one-on-one matchup, and forced a fumble from Bryce Young, which ended the game.
Walker got beat badly on that play, but, to give him a little bit of grace, he shouldn't have been on an island against one of football's best pass rushers.
It's still a failed assignment, though, and the problem is that Carolina's offensive line is too injured to make a change. If Taylor Moton were healthy at right tackle, then Monroe Freeling would have to get a chance at left tackle.
From an offensive line perspective, the schedule is daunting. After Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints, Carolina plays the Ravens, Buccaneers, and Vikings. All three teams rank in the top 13 in pass-rush win rate; the Buccaneers are eighth, and the Vikings are No. 1 in the league.
Not a very encouraging schedule to look at with how bad the offensive line, and especially Rasheed Walker, has been in 2026.

title: Ideal Offensive Line Solution is Sitting on FA Market Waiting for Panthers
full_text:

Veteran right tackle Taylor Moton missed the start of the season recovering from blood colts. In his second start of 2026, he went down with a broken fibula and is currently on injured reserve.
Former Packers’ blocker Rasheed Walker has started all eight game at left tackle for Canales’s squad, while 2026 first-round pick Monroe Freeling began the season at right tackle, gave way to Moton for two games, and is now back in the starting role. There have also been three different starters at left guard. Entering Week 10, Carolina had the 27th-ranked offensive line in the league via Pro Football Focus . title: Panthers Need Ickey Ekwonu, But Other NFL Teams Might Have Final Say
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers continue to wait for the return of Ikem Ekwonu, the team’s starting left tackle, who suffered a torn patellar tendon in his right knee during the team’s playoff loss to the Los Angeles Rams in January.
The Panthers have the 26-year-old left tackle under contract for the remainder of the season, but then he could become a free agent. Bleacher Report lists Ekwonu as the No. 46 potential free agent for 2027 , which means other teams could be willing to pay more for a starting left tackle than the Panthers can afford.
Ekwonu was the No. 6 pick in the 2022 NFL Draft by the Carolina Panthers. He has been the Panthers' starting left tackle for the past four seasons.
In Carolina’s loss to the Los Angeles Rams in the playoffs last January, Ekwonu suffered a torn patellar tendon in his right knee. He has yet to play in any games this season as he continues to recover from the injury.
Kristopher Knox of Bleacher Report believes that several teams could be interested in signing the 26-year-old left tackle if he is healthy. He is young enough to be a long-term solution at the position for another team.
Of course, any team considering signing Ekwonu would have to be concerned about the serious knee injury that the tackle sustained in January. He hasn’t played in any games this season, and there’s no guarantee he’ll return to the same level of play that he displayed before the injury.
But the Panthers have another problem to deal with, as Ekwonu's contract will expire at the end of the season. If the Panthers can’t come to terms on a new deal with him, then other teams in the NFL could look to sign him.
Carolina picked up the fifth-year option on Ekwonu’s contract in April 2025. This kept the tackle under contract with the Panthers through the 2026 season.
Carolina is going to have to make a decision on whether to sign Ekwonu to a long-term contract or go with the current group of offensive tackles.
The Panthers have had so many problems this season with their offensive line that having to worry about the left tackle position after this season is the last thing Carolina needs.
Carolina signed Rasheed Walker in free agency to play left tackle while Ekwonu recovers from his knee injury. However, Walker’s struggles in pass protection against Denver were on full display in the loss to the Broncos.
In the Panthers’ loss to the Broncos, Walker was beaten by Nik Bonitto, who forced a sack-fumble on Bryce Young and recovered the ball. The turnover effectively ended any hopes of a comeback by the Panthers.
The other young offensive tackle on the roster is Monroe Freeling. The Panthers drafted Freeling in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft , and he is currently listed at right tackle.
While Carolina does have another young tackle in Freeling, it doesn’t mean that the team has to move on from Ekwonu. It all depends on how he looks when he returns to the field.
There is also the question of when Ekwonu will return to the field. Head coach Dave Canales said recently that the left tackle is making progress, but he has not given a time frame for when Ekwonu will be back on the field.
Carolina would like to see Ekwonu back on the field before the season ends. That way, the team can see what he is capable of, and Ekwonu can show that he is still a very good player.
Ikem Ekwonu wants to stay with the Carolina Panthers, and general manager Dan Morgan wants to keep the 26-year-old left tackle with the team.
Morgan has previously expressed his desire to keep Ekwonu in Carolina, although the two sides have yet to announce a long-term agreement.
There is a possibility that Carolina wants to keep Ekwonu, but another team is willing to pay more for his services. This is something that the Panthers would have to deal with if Ekwonu were to hit free agency.
Right now, the team needs Ekwonu to return to the field, and then it can deal with the rest of the season and other teams potentially searching for a left tackle.
Carolina has had Ekwonu protecting Bryce Young’s blind side since Young entered the NFL in 2023. Whether or not the Panthers can keep him there for several more years remains to be seen.

title: Do the Chicago Bears Play Today? Schedule, Win-Loss Predictions for Rest of Season
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have played nine games of the 2026 season and the team is looking very much like a Super Bowl contender.
The Bears are in first place in the NFC North with a 7-2 record going into the weekend of Week 10 and will keep the spot atop the division if both the Detroit Lions (vs. New England Patriots) and Minnesota Vikings (vs. Green Bay Packers) lose.
Not only has the Bears' offense been playing at a high level thanks to Caleb Williams' ascension to elite status, but the defense has been playing better-than-expected football, also.
Entering Week 10, the Bears rank top 10 in total yards, rushing yards and points allowed per game, and their pass defense has been pretty good, with Chicago ranking 14th.
And there's hope for even better moving forward, as the Bears may be getting Dayo Odeyingbo back soon, and the addition of Jeffery Simmons has already provided a major boost and will continue to do so the rest of the way.
No, the Bears do not have a game in Week 10. That's because Chicago is enjoying its bye week.
But the rest of the NFC North will be in action, and with the Bears owning a loose grip on first place, we'll be paying close attention to what their division rivals do.
The Lions play the Patriots in Germany at 9:30 a.m. ET, and the Packers are hosting the Vikings at Lambeau in the 1p.m. ET window.
Here's how we see things shaking out for the Chicago Bears the rest of the season.
Week 11: vs. New Orleans Saints - Sunday, Nov. 22, 1 p.m. ET, FOX (win)
Week 12: at Detroit Lions - Thursday, Nov. 22, 1 p.m. ET, FOX (loss)
Week 14: at Miami Dolphins - Sunday, Dec. 13, 1 p.m. ET, CBS (win)
Week 15: at Buffalo Bills - Saturday, Dec. 19, 8:20 p.m. ET, CBS (loss)
Week 16: vs. Green Bay Packers - Friday, Dec. 25, 1 p.m. ET, Netflix (win)
Week 17: vs. Detroit Lions - Sunday, Jan 3, 4:25 p.m. ET, FOX (win)
Week 18: at Minnesota Vikings - TBD (win)
Final record prediction: 13-4 (1st place in NFC North)
The NFC North is once again very competitive this season, so it might take every one of those 13 wins to secure the division.
What's important for the Bears moving forward is shoring up some of these divisional tie-breakers they are behind in. The two most important ones are head-to-head record against NFC North opponents and divisional record.
Chicago has lost games to the Vikings and Packers, so both teams hold the head-to-head tie-breaker over the Bears for now, and as a result of those two losses, the Bears are 0-2 in the division, which amounts to the worst mark in the NFC North.
The next divisional game for Chicago comes in Week 12 against the Lions, and then they'll close out the season with three straight divisional contests against the Packers, Lions and Vikings.

title: One Midseason Poll Consensus Labels Bears as NFC's Super Bowl Team
full_text:
A 7-2 first half by the Bears with the only losses marked by a major asterisk has convinced some they are Super Bowl material , and even eventual winners of the Lombardi Trophy.
Making it there for the first time in 20 years would be a major step forward from last year, winning it would be the dream of all Bears fans since the 1985 season. It would also squash regression talk , as if this first half hasn't already done it.
It's all on Caleb Williams and a defense fortified greatly by the addition of Jeffery Simmons.  Two Sports Illustrated writers see the end result as the trophy case at Halas Hall welcoming a new addition.
In their midseason report, SI writers and editors comprised their picks for the remainder of the season and the playoffs. A panel of eight put forth their picks and the Bears came away with more Super Bowl appearances than any other NFC team. The Bears were the NFC team for five of the eight, with the 49ers getting the nod for two writers. Albert Breer was the only one naming someone besides the Bears or Niners representing the NFC. He picked the Rams, even after their terrible start.
. @AdamHoge thinks the Bears, who are 7-2, really need to get to 12 wins in the regular season. And of course 13 victories would be awesome. Hoge thinks it's in the realm of possibility that an 11-6 team could get left out of the playoffs in the NFC. pic.twitter.com/QbKuFMF2II
The Bears as the favored team in any poll for a Super Bowl must shock all of those who saw them as regressing prior to the start of the season.
HOW ROME ODUNZE RATES IN QUEST FOR BEARS TO PICK UP OPTION
The Bears and the Jaguars are hot commodities at this time, surprising considering both Buffalo and San Francisco have started 7-1. John Pluym and Mitch Goldich both have the Bears winning in the Super Bowl over the Jaguars with Caleb Williams earning Super Bowl MVP. Pluym has it 28-24 and Goldich 29-26.
"Williams played in two wildly entertaining playoff games last season, and if the Bears can outlast the rest of this season's NFC North, all that experience will serve him well in the season's biggest moments," wrote Goldich.
Yards allowed per game tells a lot - if you want more, the Bears have allowed 5.8 yards per pass the last two weeks. Currently 7-2 and 1st place tells the only story that matters. Your first sentence in that reply tells all the story I need to know about you. https://t.co/q1ZGIW297B
Pluym saw the Jeffery Simmons trade as the last needed piece to complement Williams.
"I’m going all in on the Bears and Williams to beat Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars in a Super Bowl featuring two of the best offensive minds in the game, Chicago’s Ben Johnson and Jacksonville’s Liam Coen," Pluym wrote.
This is impressive considering Pluym is a long-time Vikings guy and Minnesota was one of two teams to beat the Bears.
Conor Orr had the same two teams but with the Jaguars winning it late on a field goal after an interception thrown by Williams. The defenses will be punished, he says: Jaguars 37, Bears 35. "After the defensive counterrevolution of 2025 and the dominance of the Seahawks, we’re all tired of pretending to admire defensive gameplay and just want a game so full of chunk passes and explosive runs that our eyes glaze over," Orr wrote.
Bears vs. Jaguars Super Bowl confirmed 👀 pic.twitter.com/S48zixpQhm
Perhaps they could call that matchup the Regression Bowl, because it was Ben Johnson who brought up how his team was being named top regression candidates after Coen had been popping off prior to the season about how many national telecasts the Bears are on this year.
The other two writers who had the Bears making the Super Bowl were Mike Kadlick and Eva Geitheim. Kadlick called it Chiefs 28, Bears 17 and Geitheim Broncos 28, Bears 21.
Let's check in on the Super Bowl Contenders and the trade deadline! Jaguars: I got Jesse Bates and Jordan Davis! Bears: I got Jeffrey Simmons! 49ers: I got Deforest Buckner! Brett Veach: pic.twitter.com/XaTQZGMZjY
"Their defense has been better than I anticipated—even before the Jeffery Simmons trade—and they are the most balanced team in the NFC North," Geitheim wrote.
For a team everyone was far too willing to label regressive, the Bears have sure come a long way at the midpoint.
Considering they play four games yet within the division and both the Jaguars and Bills, the Bears will have the ability to indicate how accurate those Bears-Jaguars Super Bowl predictions are long in advance of the game.

title: How Rome Odunze Rates in Quest for Bears to Pick Up Fifth-Year Option
full_text:
One player whose Bears future looked somewhat murky as this season began was wide receiver Rome Odunze. At the mid-point , it actually appears more partly cloudy than murky.
Drafted ninth overall in 2024, Odunze's fifth-year option comes due in May. It would seem likely the Bears would pick this up based on his performance to date, even if some dropped passes and his lack of huge receiving numbers seem to set off some Bears fans on social media. His injury last year might have been the only reason he didn't come up with really nice numbers through two seasons.
Odunze is trending up with three straight four-catch games and 216 yards in those three games . His first TD catch of the season came in the last game. Pro Football Reference lists him with three drops this year.
There are some reasons to suspect Odunze might not be part of the Bears' long-term future. For instance, the receiver position he plays wasn't a vital one in Ben Johnson's offense at Detroit and the positions played by Colston Loveland and Luther Burden III were. However, Johnson has Caleb Williams use Odunze enough as a downfield threat to show he has already adjusted the attack to provide for more balance.
Bust: #Bears WR Rome Odunze can’t catch this. pic.twitter.com/3YSepVRW68
The main reason Odunze would seem an ideal candidate to remain in Chicago at least through 2027 is the very low bar for first-round NFL wide receivers looking to get their fifth-year options picked up.
The most productive first-round receiver to have his fifth-year option declined during this decade was Jahan Dotson, who had 103 catches for 1,257 yards and 11 touchdowns for three years. Odunze is already well beyond the first two numbers at 130 catches for 1,923 yards and is one TD short of Dotson's 11-TD mark but still has eight games left in his third season.
The other first-round receivers whose fifth-year options were declined this decade were Jalen Reagor, Kadarius Toney, Treylon Burks, and Henry Ruggs. None of them came close to Dotson's numbers.
The route work from Rome Odunze on the TD catch! 😮‍💨 (via @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/2ATIbV5HPZ
Teams rapidly made decisions on  those players and traded them before they had to pick up the fifth-year option. Ruggs wasn't traded, though. He was imprisoned after pleading guilty to felony DUI causing death, as well as misdemeanor vehicular manslaughter.
Just because a player gets his option picked up doesn't mean he's part of the future.
It wouldn't be a first for the Bears to pick up a fifth-year option and then not extend a player. See Leonard Floyd as an example. However, it's a rare thing in the league, and that was GM Ryan Pace and not GM Ryan Poles who did it. Still, that would be classified as the Jerry Jeudy route. The Broncos picked up Jeudy's option but then traded him after the fourth year.
Rome Odunze Just Dropped This Wide Open Catch That Would’ve Been A Touchdown From Caleb Williams. That Thing Literally Came In At A 100 MPH Fastball, I Swear. But Damn, He Still Probably Could’ve Got This One. pic.twitter.com/lKOZADhzIt
The big question will be the cash for Odunze's extension, if they do decide on picking up the option and don't trade him. With Caleb Williams' extension possible at the same time as Odunze's, the cash can become tight.
Jaxon Smith Njigba got a four-year extension at $168.6 million and Ja'Marr Chase four years and $161 million. Another group has come in at deals ranging from four years and $130 million to $141 million, including Zay Flowers, Drake London, Garrett Wilson, Justin Jefferson, and Chris Olave.
Rome Odunze seemed to be in some pain after this play but still lined up for the next play just before the challenge flag came out. Had his neck/head forced into extension. *Looks like he’s on the field coming out of the challenge so should be fine pic.twitter.com/letaevknqL
Some first-round receivers who did get their options picked up wound up with three-year extensions. Detroit's Jameson Williams was one. He got $83 million for three years but had knee injury problems that kept him off the field when he first came to the Lions. Others were Jaylon Waddle at three years and $84.75 million and DeVonta Smith at three years and $75 million.
Something with fewer years is always a possibility, depending on Odunze's continued production this year. Smith averaged over 1,000 yards in his first three seasons but still had just a three-year contract. Waddle was over 1,100 yards averaged in his first three years. Odunze hasn't hit 1,000 yards yet for one season.
Fourth time this season Rome Odunze has made a play after getting cut by Bears Twitter.
Odunze's production the rest of this season will dictate where he comes in cash-wise with that huge group of first-round receivers from the 2024 class, one that includes Marvin Harrison Jr., Malik Nabers, Brian Thomas Jr., Xavier Worthy, Ricky Pearsall, and Xavier Legette. As it stands, Odunze is fifth among his own draft class in catches, fourth in yardage and sixth in touchdowns.
What's important, though, is how the Bears see his fit within their own offense's future and their cap.
It can't hurt that Odunze has forged a good relationship on and off the field with his quarterback as members of that 2024 class.  This is the kind of thing that can weigh heavily on a player's side when the production is borderline.
In Odunze's case, he still has the rest of this season to show he's far above that low bar for fifth-year options, as well as a good fit for the offense's future.
Rome Odunze on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers Game: "It was a weird one for sure. The energy was there. We thought we were going to kind of run away with it, and then the offense kind of got in a lull. Defense was playing great ball, and then we had the Jaylon Johnson pick-six. We… pic.twitter.com/04qAV9AaCu

title: NFL Executive Reveals Why Bears Are Favored to Win NFC North in ESPN Midseason Poll
full_text:
The Chicago Bears currently sit atop the NFC North with a 7-2 record. However, that's not to say they have a stranglehold on the loaded division, as every team has at least six wins.
The Bears are riding a four-game winning streak into their Bye Week, including back-to-back wins against the two teams that played in last season's Super Bowl. They've firmly established themselves as contenders .
For the first time in a long time, the rest of the NFL has seemingly taken notice. ESPN spoke to executives around the league , and the consensus is that the Bears have a good chance to come out on top of the NFC North marathon by season's end.
"Chicago is the best-coached," an AFC executive told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. "He's elite. One of the best in the NFL and only in Year 2. One of the best offenses week-in and week-out, as well. Defense is solid. Caleb [Williams] just has to play within the scheme and they will win it easily, I believe."
The conversation about the most important factors to establish contendership has always been an interesting one. Some believe that having a star quarterback is vital, while others think an elite coach is the best elixir.
With the first half of the season in the books, the Bears have passed both prerequisites with flying colors. Caleb Williams has cemented his status as one of the league's rising stars, while Ben Johnson has continued to prove his worth among the coaching ranks. They're both essential to the team's success.
However, it's worth noting that the Bears went 2-1 without Williams earlier this season. Sure, the loss was an embarrassing 31-7 defeat to their hated division rivals in Green Bay, but the two wins were impressive. Them achieving those wins with two different backup QBs under center is even more impressive.
The Bears came out on top in those games because Johnson is one of the league's premier offensive play-callers. The players (on both sides of the ball) have also fully bought into his confidence that probably borders on arrogance. They want to be the best and think they can be the best, and he's the one who injected that belief into the organization.
While they still have work to do on both sides of the ball, their impressive wins over the past month have earned them the right to be arrogant. They're playing like one of the NFL's best teams.
The Bears are also the most trendy Super Bowl pick around the NFL at the midseason point. Fowler planted his flag in that territory.
"Look out for this matchup: The Chicago Bears against the Buffalo Bills," Fowler wrote. "Both teams have multifaceted offensive attacks, star quarterbacks with dual-threat ability and enough roster talent to get hot... Both teams were aggressive [ahead the NFL trade deadline] because they know they have something."
Jerry Markarian has been an avid Chicago Bears fan since 2010 and has been writing about the team since  2022.  He has survived the 2010 NFC Championship Game, a career-ending injury to his favorite player (Johnny Knox), the Bears' 2013 season finale, a Double Doink, Mitchell Trubisky, Justin Fields, and Weeks 8-17 of the 2024 NFL season. Nevertheless, he still Bears Down!

title: Predicting the Path the Bears Will Take to an NFC North Championship
full_text:
Before the start of the 2026 NFL season, I said that the Chicago Bears faced a long road to a second division title . The NFC North was expected to be the toughest division in the league, but after nine weeks of football it's looking more like the toughest division in NFL history. Nevertheless, the Bears currently stand atop the crowd with a 7-2 record and are well on their way to meeting my preseason prediction of a 12-5 record.
That makes this a good opportunity to look ahead at the second half of the Bears' 2026 schedule and chart a course to winning the NFC North. Obviously, winning out would do the trick, but that's not a realistic expectation. Instead, let's go game by game and predict the winner, and whether that will be enough to rise above their division rivals.
The NFC South is a joke this year, and the Saints are no exception. Despite a strong finish to the 2025 season, they've been generally bad and second-year quarterback Tyler Shough has been inconsistent. Meanwhile, the Bears will be coming off their bye week and playing at home. This will be the get-right game Caleb Williams needs after his career-worst four-pick game in Week 9.
The Lions have somewhat surprised me so far this season. Their offensive line solidified faster than I expected, and that has kept the offense running at a high clip. Even with the addition of Jeffery Simmons, the Bears' will struggle to slow down Jared Goff and the Lions' offense. It will be close, but with home field advantage on a short week, I'm giving this Thanksgiving showdown to the Lions.
I've said before that the Jacksonville Jaguars are the AFC version of the Chicago Bears, and that makes this game difficult to predict. Both offenses are led by elite quarterbacks with genius play-callers, and each defense has enough firepower to give most teams absolute fits. Similar to the previous game, I'm giving the edge to the home team here, especially with the Bears getting some extra rest off of a mini-bye.
On a related note, there's a decent chance that this game will be a Super Bowl preview .
The Miami Dolphins are 1-7 and may be without starting quarterback Malik Willis, who landed on IR last week, in this one. I don't feel the need to justify this prediction any further than that.
You can almost copy what I said about the Bears-Jaguars game and put it here. Super Bowl preview. Two elite quarterbacks. Brilliant head coaches. Defenses doing just enough to get wins. This may be the game of the year at Highmark Stadium, and in keeping with my prediction trends, I'm giving the edge to the home team.
In my preseason predictions of the Bears' most important games of the 2026 season , I said that this Christmas Day showdown would likely decide the division winner, and I stand by that prediction today. The Packers have done extremely well given their injury situations this year, and they've been winning despite a historically bad running game.
However, these improbable wins won't last. Teams have to be able to run the ball well to win in December and January, especially at open-air stadiums like Soldier Field. I expect Chicago's defensive line to dominate Green Bay's offensive line, stuffing the run and making Jordan Love's life miserable for 60 minutes, while Chicago's running backs go for over 200 yards and multiple scores in a gritty, old-school win for the Bears.
After three straight losses to his former team, this is where Ben Johnson will finally defeat Dan Campbell and the Lions. With the No. 1 seed in the NFC playoff field likely still within reach, the Bears will win their second consecutive division game at Soldier Field, but don't expect it to be pretty.
This is a tough one to predict. The Vikings' trade for Kirk Cousins has completely reset expectations for their moribund offense, and I'm not sure how it will look. Furthermore, one or both of these teams could have already secured a playoff berth by this point and may rest starters. That said, I don't think any NFC North team will sweep a single one of their rivals this year, so I'm marking this a win for the Bears.
After a 7-2 start for the Bears and seeing just how far Caleb Williams has grown in his second year with Ben Johnson, I'm picking the Bears to surpass my 12-5 preseason prediction, finishing with a 13-4 record.
And now for the million-dollar question: will a 13-4 record be enough to win the NFC North? It's insane to say this, but that remains to be seen. It certainly ought to be good enough to win, especially if the Bears win three of their four remaining divisional games, but never say never with this division.

title: Four Chicago Bears Are Earning Contract Extensions For 2027 and Beyond
full_text:
With Caleb Williams still on a cheap rookie deal for the next few years before his inevitable monster contract extension kicks in down the road, the Chicago Bears will have some financial flexibility.
And, with that flexibility, the Bears can dump resources into some players at other positions who have proven their worth during their time in Chicago.
At the halfway point of the season, there are four Bears players who are either in a contract year or will be in 2027 that have earned an extension from the team with their play.
After falling short in the starting left tackle competition at camp, Benedet was thrust into the role after Braxton Jones went down with an injury that proved to be a season-ending issue .
The Bears probably could've turned to Ozzy Trapilo at some point in the last few weeks, but with Benedet playing well, they haven't done that.
Through nine games, Benedet sports a respectable 68.4 pass-blocking grade, according to Pro Football Focus , and he has allowed just one sack and 18 pressures.
In the run game, Benedet is sporting a grade of 73.3, which ranks 19th among tackles in the NFL.
Benedet is an exclusive rights free agent after this season, so the Bears have some control. However, they might want to lock him up for more than just next year as a potential long-term left tackle or, at the very least, a long-term swing tackle.
When the Bears acquired Jackson in a trade with the Rams in 2025, his career was in trouble. Jackson missed most of the season with an injury and wasn't effective when on the field.
But Jackson has flipped the script with the Bears and once again looks like one of the best guards in the NFL. This season has been particularly impressive, with Jones ranking fourth in run-blocking grade (85.1) and fifth in overall grade (83.1) among guards while not permitting a sack and giving up just 16 pressures.
Jackson is under contract for another year, but he doesn't have any guaranteed money left on his deal, which makes him an obvious candidate for a long-term extension even more.
Chicago would benefit from locking him up long term, also, as the team can lower his $12.2 million cap hit for 2027 in the process.
Jackson started his ascension last season, when he was a pleasant surprise for the Bears in his first year in Chicago.
And the veteran linebacker has picked up where he left off and is seeing an increased role as a result, with his snap share going from 26% last season to 43% this season.
Jackson remains one of the best coverage linebackers in the NFL, as evidenced by his PFF grade of 76.2 in that area, which ranks sixth at the position. He also has one interception.
His run defense hasn't been great, but Jackson's coverage ability makes him a great complement to Devin Bush.
Jackson still has one more year left on his deal, but with T.J. Edwards getting long in the tooth, the Bears might want to lock Jackson up for the long haul before his value rises even more.
Lewis has no doubt proven his worth this season thanks to his versatility and amounts to a home-run signing for the Bears.
With injuries at slot cornerback and safety, Lewis has split his time between the two positions and has played well, with his 70.2 coverage grade ranking 17th among safeties.
Lewis isn't going to be a free agent in 2027, but the Bears might be wise to lock him up for another year or two before 2028, and he certainly deserves a raise, also.

title: Jeffery Simmons Was Frustrated With Titans After Trade to Bears
full_text:
Defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons has expressed on a few occasions how happy he is to be with the Chicago Bears.
But upon initially being traded to Chicago from the Tennessee Titans, he wasn't exactly thrilled about it.
Simmons made the honest admission during an appearance on "The Rich Eisen Show," saying he was initially frustrated because he didn't think Tennessee would trade him since he was such an important member of the franchise.
"I just didn't think that would happen to me, especially going into Year 8," Simmons said.
"I was really pissed off that it really happened right then and there because... I was still going out there playing my tail off and giving Tennessee and their organization everything I had when I stepped on that field, in the locker room, practice field, in this community."
It's understandable why Simmons felt that way. He had become a stalwart in Tennessee and the face of the franchise and many, including Simmons himself, believed he was untradeable.
Simmons was one of two players left from the 2019 Titans team that went to the AFC Championship Game, along with safety Amani Hooker, who has now also been traded , also.
In fairness to the Titans, they didn't want to trade him, but the historic package Bears general manager Ryan Poles threw at Tennessee was just too good to pass up on, especially for a rebuilding team like the Titans.
Despite his frustration with the Titans, Simmons said he is happy in Chicago and it's already feeling like home. Simmons even went as far as to say he hopes to finish his career with the Bears.
"These last two weeks have been unbelievable," Simmons admitted. "The fans of Chicago, they breathe football. To pack out the stadium, even on Monday night in Seattle, I got chills to hear how many fans and see how many fans we had in Seattle."
"Then you come back home to another primetime game Sunday night in Chicago, that was unreal running out of that tunnel for the first time. It's definitely feeling like home and I'm looking forward to hopefully end my career there, whenever that may be," he added.
Going from the Titans' fan base to the Bears' is quite the jump for Simmons.
Tennessee's fans have often been criticized for allowing fans of the opposing team to invade their stadium, so seeing Bears fans show up in big numbers at a road game is definitely something Simmons hasn't seen during his career.
Simmons is also going from a team that has been terrible for years now and is currently in the process of a rebuild to one that is a legit Super Bowl contender in 2026 .
And, being on a true contender and playing in a bigger market and in more primetime games means Simmons has more eyes on him than ever. Simmons has often flown under the radar in Tennessee, but that will no longer be the case now that he's with the Bears.

title: Five Chicago Bears Who Improved the Most in Season's First Half
full_text:
Improvement is easier to measure subjectively than objectively.
The Bears completed nine weeks of an 18-week season with several players standing out above their previous performances with the team. Although some of said improvements can't be entirely gauged with regular team statistics, most can be detected this way or merely by looking at analytics.
Coach Ben Johnson threw out a rew names of role players who have improved over the course of the season, like James Lynch and Daniel Hardy. However, they're participating in less critical roles than the starters as backups and special teams players.
There are five players in particular who stepped up their games when called on to start or play most of the downs.
Here are the most improved Bears for the season's first half.
The Bears are 7-2 and are getting 4 key players back: • Kyle Monangai: Expected back Week 11 • Malik Muhammad: Expected back Week 11 • Dayo Odeyingbo: Eligible to return Week 11 • Coby Bryant: Potential December return Getting healthy couldn’t come at a better time. pic.twitter.com/C56IXIRhn9
Enough with all of the motivated Dayo jokes. Odeyingbo only got to play in five games prior to his quad injury, and now will likely return either at home in the next game with New Orleans or at Detroit on Thanksgiving. Odeyingbo's numbers did reflect better play than last year, when he played eight games and then suffered a season-ending Achilles injury. It's remarkable, in fact, that he showed up better statistically considering the injury he had.
Maybe it's the experience factor. He's already been through an Achilles injury in his past and knew what to expect. Although he played only 147 snaps on defense, he had three sacks. That was two more than he had all last season. He also had nine pressures, or three more than last year. His three tackles for loss were one more for five games than he had last year in eight. The Bears definitely haven't had their money's worth out of him considering his contract, but the little they got to see before his injury indicates they could get another nice boost on their defensive line when he returns.
3 players are expected to be back for Bears as we head into second half of the season & @BearsCork looks at their importance! As we head into the bye, I genuinely think this team still has another gear to find. And the best part? Help is on the way all fresh heading into the… pic.twitter.com/oQtNeiKjm0
Maybe you can't teach an old dog new tricks but he can perform old ones pretty well when he's healthy enough.
Jarrett hasn't had the knee sprain to worry about that he had last year. A bit different defensive line approach emphasizing a quicker attack by all defensive linemen and less time tied up with blockers definitely played to his strength. Jarrett has the NFL's highest run-stop win rate for defensive tackles in the first nine weeks, according to ESPN's run-stop win rate metric. He's at 44%.
Expect his pass rushing to improve now, as well, with Jeffery Simmons lining up alongside. Jarrett will rarely get a double team now. The eight pressures he has for the first half is only three short of what he had for all of last year. He has missed only three tackles as a Bear.
Bears Grady Jarrett ate his Wheaties before these two HUGE pass rush plays! pic.twitter.com/pelZYWyBHG
The more people start to pine for Ozzy Trapilo, the more Benedet produces. He did it last week while playing through a shoulder injury. Benedet's weakness last season in his first extensive playing time was pass blocking. This year he is fourth in the NFL in ESPN's pass block win rate among tackles, at 92%. Benedet began taking starter's reps in Week 4 against the Jets and has been rock solid. Pro Football Focus has Benedet graded 22nd among 71 tackles in the NFL, 19th blocking the run and 41st as a pass blocker. He's at one sack allowed and four penalties committed. They can afford to wait on Trapilo as long as Benedet is performing this way, that is, if Trapilo can even get his job back. Fighting through the shoulder injury alone in the last game earned him high marks in the eyes of Ben Johnson. "I think it's tremendous growth," Johnson said. "Certainly him as being a young player, just understanding that this team still needs him. We talk about how there are going to be games over the course of the season where you're not 100%, and yet we need you going out there and giving every little ounce you got in your 90% or you're 85%.
Theo Benedet is one tough football player who has done a good job protecting Caleb Williams' blind side, even when banged up, as @kfishbain discussed on the @RahimiGrote Show. pic.twitter.com/jqmhNw8l4j
"I think that was a case of him (Sunday) night pushing through and being out there for his buddies. I think that's all over this roster right now."
Already emerging as a force by the end of last season and the playoffs, Booker has only improved despite not being used as a starter. He still gets starter's reps but they kept him off the field for the first play of the defense's opening series seven out of nine games. Booker already is only eight tackles short of last year and has half a sack more than he made all of last season with a team-high five. He has reached a career high for tackles for loss with six, and needs six pressures in his final eight games to pass last year's total of 18. "His intensity, his effort, they keep getting better week-in and week-out," Johnson said.
If an Austin Booker extension had to look something like: 3 years, $45M (30M in guarantees) Would you do it? Booker’s stats so far this season: 🏈: 27 tackles 🏈: 5.0 sacks 🏈: 2 forced fumbles 🏈: 1 pass defended (turned into INT) pic.twitter.com/JYGvcG81Zj
It would be easy to join the dog pile on him after the nightmare four interceptions against the Buccaneers but a first half of brilliance despite that game and three missed due to injuries says he'll have fairly impressive numbers by season's end.
PFF just got done shocking everyone with its examination of passers to date and determining: "Nobody has a higher adjusted completion pct (81.5%) than Caleb Williams."
This hardly seemed possible last year when everyone blasted him for wildness or for taking the tough pass over the easy win. He is 16.6% higher in completion percentage (68.7%) than he was for last season. PFF has Williams second among regular starters for overall accuracy, trailing only Joe Burrow. They have Lamar Jackson and J.J. McCarthy ahead of him but obviously Jackson isn't going to play again this year and McCarthy is playing only as a sub for Jaxson Dart. They also list him behind only C.J. Stroud, Bryce Young, Joe Burrow and Drake Maye among starters for ball placement.
He also has the highest EPA per attempt on non-first reads in the league.
That's the leap Bears fans were waiting for. Accuracy was the knock coming out, and now he's at the top of the league in it.
Footwork improvement and accuracy throwing have combined with his knowledge of the offense in Year 2 to lead to this boost, one not apparent on Sunday night but definitely there when the Bears beat the two Super Bowl teams from last year, among others. When the season was about to begin, Johnson noted the changed approach from Williams. This especially pertained to professionalism and his accuracy as a passer.
“He’s taking a lot of pride in his approach right now and it trickles down to everyone around him," Johnson said.
Williams' total reversal when it comes to accuracy is the type of thing that can carry a team a long way, maybe even into mid-February.

title: Which Chicago Bears Are on Pace For an All-Pro Season?
full_text:
We're officially halfway through the season, and the Bears sit atop the NFC North with an impressive 7-2 record. They're also riding high with four straight wins going into their Bye Week.
With it being midseason, season-long predictions are being revisited in droves. They're also handing out awards for how players have performed over the first half of the year. ESPN's Bill Barnwell named four Chicago Bears (Joe Thuney, Darnell Wright, Jeffery Simmons, and Devin Bush) to his midseason All-Pro team.
We made our All-Pro predictions back in July , and three of the five players we mentioned are enjoying great seasons. Another has started heating up after a rough start to the campaign, and the fifth... Well, we don't need to talk about how the fifth player has performed.
How might the Bears favor when it comes to All-Pro voting at midseason?
Joe Thuney might not be playing as well as he did last season, when he was named the NFL's inaugural Protector of the Year . Still, he's played well enough to be in strong consideration for an All-Pro nod by the end of the season.
Thuney will also be aided by name recognition. That's not supposed to matter when it comes to All-Pro voting, but it almost always does. Thuney is still recognized as one of the league's best o-linemen, and the voters are well aware of that fact.
Darnell Wright was actually previously a victim of name recognition. While he didn't reach the All-Pro level until last season (when he received his first All-Pro nod), he was also a notable Pro Bowl snub in 2024. It took him playing through a torn UCL before the league gave him the recognition he deserved.
Wright has taken his game to another level this season. With a few other right tackles falling off (or moving to the left side), his path to another All-Pro nod got a bit easier. The fact that he's all but cemented his status as the league's premier right tackle doesn't hurt matters, either.
Was there ever any doubt? Jeffery Simmons was named a first-team All-Pro on a 3-14 Titans team last season. He's now on a 7-2 Bears squad with at least three more standalone games the rest of the way.
Simmons has completely reshaped Chicago's defense , and he already has six sacks over the first half of the season. The NFL landscape features quite a few elite DTs, but Simmons is arguably the best. He's a near-lock to be recognized with his fourth All-Pro nod.
Admittedly, I was a bit surprised to see Bush on Barnwell's All-Pro list. He's obviously stacked a few great performances in recent weeks, but a few quiet ones earlier in the season place him well behind a few other 'backers in the stat sheets. For what it's worth, it's also a stat-stuffing position, so the quiet start makes it difficult to overcome a lack of early-season production.
Still, Bush has put together a few great performances in recent weeks . If he can carry that momentum over the rest of the season, and Chicago's defense reaches another level with Simmons commanding opposing offenses' attention, he'll have a chance. His progression has been one of their most promising developments on defense.
Caleb Williams' four-interception performance on Sunday night might've put the nail in his MVP candidacy. His All-Pro hopes are still alive, though. He has played lights out in four of six games this year. One of the other games was in monsoon-like conditions, so it's easy to give him a pass there.
The most significant factor that could prevent Williams from All-Pro recognition is how many QBs are playing at a high level. The league is oversaturated with quality QB play, and, unlike Williams, many haven't missed any action. Still, it's certainly possible if he can consistently play as he did over his four great games.

title: Why It's Only Going to Get Tougher for the Bears in Season's Second Half
full_text:
The first half of the season tested the Bears in numerous ways and the second half figures to be trying for different reasons.
With all due respect to Tampa Bay's defense, the Bears' offense seemed to hit a wall of its own making in the last game.
It didn't represent their efforts through much of the season's first half, although turnovers have been a consistent problem. More precisely, fumbles have been an issue, not the interceptions. Caleb Williams' one bad day truly was this compared to what he'd done both throughout the rest of his season and his career.
Their defense saw only a teaser of what defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons can mean to them, as he had shortened work weeks for both games played. He played after two practices, and then the entire team had a short work week due to the Monday night game and extra day off after travel back from Seattle. They're overworking him and perhaps in the season's second half they'll find a way to better distribute his reps.
“I’m still super high on Caleb, but we need to be honest about the year he’s having so far. At times spectacular… but he’s played 6 game - 4 he was excellent and 2 he was awful.” @getnickwright pumps the breaks on the Caleb Williams hype pic.twitter.com/jeppKq47wd
The second half of the season challenges the Bears most because half of their eight opponents will be very familiar divisional teams, all over .500. They'll also get division leaders Buffalo and Jacksonville, with only New Orleans and Miami ranking among the league's have-nots over the first half.
Then again, the actual matchup challenges their second-half opponents represent are a bit less taxing for their offense. They'll need Simmons at his best and eventually even get Coby Bryant healthy and in the lineup if they're going to stop some of the offenses they'll face down the stretch.
Williams and the offense will face the league's worst pass defense twice. That's Detroit. Coming out of the break they face a Saints pass defense ranked 28th. The Bears play a Jacksonville team very balanced, but one problem the Jaguars have had is against the pass. The Jaguars rank 22nd stopping the pass, although they have made changes with three defensive additions.
"The answer is Caleb Williams. ... Caleb Williams has got that 'IT' factor." @EvCoRadio weighs in on the NFC North QB he trusts the most in the playoffs 🔥 pic.twitter.com/3i4QPxulOr
The Bears play a Buffalo defense ranked 29th in stopping the pass. The only top-10 pass defense they play is Minnesota in the season finale. The Vikings are No. 2 at stopping the pass. Green Bay is 11th, and the two Packers safeties and an improved pass rush do make them a challenge for Williams and his receivers.
With Kyle Monangai possibly returning for the next game after missing five straight, the offense badly needs the balance he brings to the running attack. They were a cold 98.6 yards a game rushing in those five without him, a torrid 196.2 in four games with him. The 196.2 yards included a Week 2 game against Minnesota's dominant defense.
Scenes when Kyle Monangai comes back and puts together the greatest RB season in NFL history pic.twitter.com/I6JQD9Jpth https://t.co/XXVmnKdGG2
“Kyle's a big part of that running game, and I think he's proven his worth over the last year and a half," coach Ben Johnson said. "So, like I said last week, whenever we're able to get him back on the field, it's going to make us a better team and certainly a better running game.”
They'll need the running game at full force because the second half of their schedule includes only one run defense in the league's bottom tier and that's the Saints in the first game back.
They're going to run up against four top-10 rushing defenses and, after New Orleans, none ranked worse than 18th. It's been tough sledding for D'Andre Swift and the ground game in the last five weeks, and the opposition doesn't figure to get easier.
Bears are a problem. On their worse day thry beat the #3 defense in the league. Simmons turned our D into animals.
The Bears' offensive line came charging out of the early bye week last year and took over. They could use the same thing coming out of this bye, even after half the NFL schedule.
Adding Simmons gives them the help stopping the run and rushing the pass that they could need to get through a second-half of opponents loaded with the ability to put up points.
They're going against the top-ranked yardage and scoring offense in Buffalo, twice face Detroit's fifth-ranked scoring and yardage offense, host Jacksonville's fourth-ranked scoring offense, must stop Green Bay's second-ranked passing attack, and no one could really know what they'll see from Minnesota's offense by the finale with Kirk Cousins back but it can't be as bad as it was in the season's first half or even in the game the Bears squandered against the Vikings and Carson Wentz.
There are only a few anemic offenses on the slate. Miami is 31st in scoring and 28th on offense but they can run it (12th) with a QB who might be better at that than passing it. New Orleans' offense is nowhere near as bad as its defense has been and beyond the Saints and Dolphins, all of the remaining opponents could have one real strength offensively to lean on against the Bears.
“[The Buccaneers] actually put out the formula of how to … potentially beat the Chicago Bears.” @TheSamAcho breaks down his takeaways from SNF’s game after the Bears beat the Bucs with a last-minute field goal ✍️ pic.twitter.com/CnNf8rYI5m
Only a few NFL teams in the first half displayed as much balanced statistically as the Bears, ranking third in offense and rushing and 12th in passing, but ninth on defense -- sixth against the run and 14th against the pass. It shows an ability to handle whatever the second half of the season throws at them.
The offense seems poised to regain the explosiveness shown in the season opener, while it doesn't hurt having a defensive weapon now in the middle of the line to snuff things out before they get started.
"I think there's a great opportunity at hand just to look at these first nine games and come away with what we're doing well and what we can lean on going into the last stretch of the season and certainly some areas of improvement that we need to get better at moving forward," Johnson said.
They'll have to because it doesn't get easier in the season's second half, particularly with four games within the NFL's toughest division.

title: Key Bengals Veteran Puts MVP Stamp of Approval on Joe Burrow
full_text:
After a shootout victory one week ago, the Cincinnati Bengals' trip to Spain could have been the perfect excuse for the team to have a slip-up. Instead, the Bengals played one of their best games of the season.
The fans in Spain were treated to a stellar performance by the Bengals in their 34-17 win over the Atlanta Falcons. This team puts up points in bunches, and the offense was once again on another level.
Quarterback Joe Burrow was nearly perfect on the day. Burrow was 24 of 29 in pass attempts, throwing for 271 yards and three touchdowns. After the game, one of Burrow's great protectors on the offensive line took to X to support his quarterback on his quest for a potential NFL MVP selection.
Bengals left tackle Orlando Brown Jr. shared his belief that Burrow has firmly planted himself in the NFL MVP conversation.
"Joe Shiesty better be in your MVP conversations," Brown shared on X . "Just tore up the dirty birds in Madrid!!"
No one can deny Brown's comments. The Bengals quarterback is second in the league in passing yards with 2,386 and leads the league in touchdown passes with 23. Burrow is having a very strong season, but that doesn't guarantee MVP love.
Burrow has seen this story play out before, and the fairy tale ending didn't go his way. Back in 2024, Burrow was playing the best of any quarterback in the league. Yet, the MVP award was not his when things were all said and done.
A quick scan around the league will tell you that the MVP conversation doesn't have a guaranteed leader at this point, other than the Bengals star.
The quarterbacks that may be in the conversation currently are Jordan Love and Trevor Lawrence, and those two are not having nearly the season that Burrow is having. But there is one skill position player who is making a strong statement for his MVP campaign.
Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba is having a historic season. Smith-Njigba is on pace to surpass Calvin Johnson's record for most receiving yards in a single season.
It would be pretty on-brand for Burrow to be the best quarterback in the league, then lose the MVP award to a non-quarterback, which is something the league hasn't done since 2012.
How this season plays out is going to be important for Burrow's potential career milestone. However, something tells me that's the last thing on his mind.

title: Cris Collinsworth Reveals What Bengals Must See From Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight Jr.
full_text:
Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight Jr. have both shown flashes of improvement for the Bengals this season, but plenty of questions remain. They need to continue to improve if the Bengals are going to reach their full potential. During an appearance on First Word With James Rapien, Cris Collinsworth dissected how difficult the linebacker position is to learn in the NFL and how having Bryan Cook helps both young players.
"Linebacker in the NFL is a little bit like playing quarterback on the other side because you're the one with the green dot, you're the one that has to make the adjustments, we've got all these motions and shifts and think of the Bengals [offense] and all the stuff they do pre-snap," Collinsworth explained . "You need either or both really, one of those linebackers who really knows what it is that he's doing, and then you got Cook in behind it, so I always though that would get better as the year went along."
Collinsworth further explained that the second half of this season is the final test for the linebackers. He confirmed that the key for both Knight and Carter is to hold their own against duo blocking schemes when multiple defensive linemen are double-teamed.
"We're kind of into final exams right now, and if they can hold their own against some of these duo blocking schemes, where they go double-team here and double-team here, they're going to leave that linebacker, you figure it out," Collinsworth explained. "It takes a little patience, it takes a little experience, and they're getting there, they're playing hard, but they're young."
Knight and Carter combined for three missed tackles and allowed five receptions for three first downs against the Steelers in Week 3. Those numbers have to improve this week, with Carter showcasing better communication as the green-dot communicator in the middle of the defense.
Answers should start to show themselves in this second half of the season when it comes to the Bengals' young linebackers.
Cincinnati is banking on both of them to continue to develop. They didn't make a significant addition to the linebacker room this offseason. They also didn't make a move at the trade deadline. The Bengals are clearly all in on Knight are Carter for the rest of this season.

title: Joe Burrow Gets Honest About His Recovery From Multiple Serious Injuries
full_text:
Joe Burrow is no stranger to severe injuries in his NFL career. He suffered a torn ACL in his rookie campaign, tore a ligament in his wrist in 2023, and suffered a turf toe injury that required surgery last year. The largest hurdle he has had to overcome with each injury however, are the mental gymnastics that occurred with each one.
Burrow confirmed this week that each injury presented larger mental hurdles than the injury itself. He stated that while his knee injury in his rookie campaign posed less concern mentally, and that the injuries to his wrist and toe are what caused the most anxiety mentally.
"It's always more mental for sure, I tore my ACL in 2020 in my rookie season and that one was tough for sure, but I didn't know any better, I was young and had never experienced anything like that before, so you're just putting one foot in front of the other," Burrow said of his knee injury. "In 2023 I hurt my wrist, and then last year I hurt my toe, and then its like 'oh come on man what's going on' because I put so much work into this."
Burrow added to his thoughts in a press conference later and said that the mental process is always different with every injury. He said he allows himself to feel emotions through anger and sadness and has quickly bounced back from those feelings, adding that once he has done so, the rehab process is easy.
"The mental process is always different with every injury that you have, the first thing is I'm always just really mad and sad, I let myself feel those emotions and then pretty quickly you just get back to work," Burrow said on his mental process . "I love what I do, if you love what you do and you wanna be better every single day, the rehab process is easy once you can flip your mind to just try and get better and try and to get back there with your guys."
He explained that he is fortunate to have improved with each injury, pointing to the rehab process and that it intensely works different muscles that do not see normal activity.
"Fortunately I've been able to improve after every injury I've had, and I think with the rehab process, a lot of times those exercises that you're doing hit muscles that you haven't quite worked that intensely as you are at the time, and that can help you come back better and stronger," Burrow said.

title: Joe Burrow Ranked Shockingly Low in Latest QB Stock Report
full_text:
It has been an interesting week for the Cincinnati Bengals. After an impressive victory over the Atlanta Falcons in Spain on Sunday, the focus shifted to what the team might do before the trade deadline.
Well, fans got their answer to that on Tuesday when the Bengals made one trade, but then rescinded the move not very long after. It was a day filled with hot takes as the fan base now wonders if the rest of the AFC has passed the team by. However, they still have to line them up and go to work.
This weekend is a major matchup for the Bengals. The team will be looking to get revenge on the Pittsburgh Steelers, who bested the Bengals earlier this season. The Bengals will need to be on their A game, which hasn't been an issue for quarterback Joe Burrow.
Burrow has been at MVP level of play this season, and Fox Sports' recent quarterback rankings have the Bengals' quarterback's stock rising before a massive AFC North showdown.
Henry McKenna has Burrow as the sixth best quarterback in the league heading into Week 10. That's one spot higher than McKenna had him last week.
"Every week, Burrow has put on a clinic," wrote McKenna . "The only downside has been his six interceptions."
The quarterbacks ahead of Burrow on the list are Trevor Lawrence, Brock Purdy, Patrick Mahomes, Jordan Love, and Josh Allen.
It seems the interceptions seem to be an issue with Burrow's stock; however, Love and Allen have the same number of interceptions but with fewer touchdown passes than Burrow.
Six interceptions isn't ideal, but the 23 touchdown passes are enough to look past the turnovers at the moment.
Three of Burrow's six interceptions on the year came in the team's 43-36 win over the Tennessee Titans. It wasn't the ideal performance, but the Bengals quarterback still managed to throw five touchdown passes and add a rushing touchdown in the win.
Burrow is once again playing at an elite level. If he continues at this pace, it would be foolish to not have him as one of the top names in the MVP conversations.
There's really no excuse to have Burrow sixth. He's been one of the best players in the NFL all season long and is in the MVP race. A win over the Steelers on Sunday would help his stock—and his case for MVP.

title: Bengals Have Clear Opportunity to Bolster O-Line After Veteran OT's Release
full_text:
A lot of the Cincinnati Bengals' fan base was not thrilled over the team's lack of movement at the trade deadline. While the team did have one deal in place, it appeared that a backpedal move may have scared the front office away from making any other moves.
The rest of the AFC contenders made moves before the deadline, however, the Bengals may feel they already have the roster to lead the conference. Whatever the case may be, that doesn't mean the team still can't add to their roster.
On Friday, the Philadelphia Eagles made a roster move that could be of great interest to the Bengals. But will the team take a closer look at making a roster addition?
The Eagles have announced that the team has waived offensive tackle Fred Johnson. Johnson has not made a start for the Eagles this season, but did start in the 2025 season in eight games.
That may sound like a familiar name to many fans. Johnson spent the first three years of his career with the Bengals. During his time in Cincinnati, Johnson made eight starts for the Bengals from 2019 to 2021.
Not that the Bengals are having issues on the offensive line this season. Recently, Pro Football Focus ranked the Bengals' offensive line as the eighth-best offensive line in the NFL heading into Week 10.
It may not be a move that makes the headline splash fans were hoping for a few days ago, but this could be a massive move if the Bengals were to see the injury bug hit their offensive line.
While the Bengals could put a claim on Johnson since he is on waivers, the team could also wait to see if the former Eagles lineman clears waivers and sign him potentially for the practice squad.
It's definitely a strategic move if the Bengals decide to add Johnson to the roster. The Bengals are entering the most vital part of the season.
Sunday's matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers is going to tell a lot about this team. A win will keep them in the driver's seat of their own postseason destiny. On the other hand, a loss will give the Steelers the edge as the postseason race heats up.
If the Bengals plan on a deep playoff run, it can't hurt to add a little depth to the unit that is tasked with protecting the most important asset on the roster.
