title: Bengals Rule 1 Player Out for Sunday, Don't Appear Ready to Return Anybody from IR
full_text:
Cincinnati Bengals head coach Zac Taylor declared starting left guard Dylan Fairchild good to go for Sunday night’s game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
Fairchild suffered a pectoral injury late in Sunday’s 34-17 win against the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid, and he was a limited participant in Wednesday evening’s walk-through practice. But Fairchild was a full participant Thursday and Friday.
The only player ruled out on the injury report is safety Kyle Dugger, who has missed four of the last five games with a quadricep injury.
Asked if Dugger, a former Steeler, is a candidate to land on Injured Reserve, Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said he was not, indicating the safety could be close to returning to action.
Three Bengals, who are currently on IR, had their 21-day practice window opened Thursday, but the team is listing all three as doubtful for Sunday night’s battle for first place in the AFC North Division.
Cornerback Jalen Davis, wide receiver Andrei Iosivas and rookie guard Brian Parker II were all listed as full participants Thursday and Friday.
Parker, the team’s fifth-round pick out of Duke, has been on IR since Aug. 30 with a knee injury.
Iosivas has been on IR since Sept. 26 with a thumb injury. He had three catches for 19 yards before suffering the injury in Week 2 at Houston.
Talking after practice Thursday, he sounded encouraged about his chances of playing Sunday.
Davis went on IR on Sept. 30 with a hamstring injury suffered in the first meeting with the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 3.
The Bengals currently only have 52 players on the active roster, so they have room to pull one of those three off IR without making a corresponding move. But the “doubtful” designations make that seem unlikely.
Look for Josh “Fig” Newton to get the second start of his career if Davis isn’t activated.
Newton has played sparingly in his three seasons before getting a full snap load Sunday in Madrid. Defensive coordinator Al Golden said Newton’s performance had both ups and downs.
“(Cornerbacks coach Chuck Burks) did a great job with him just bringing him along to the point where, OK, he's ready to do it. Let's see what it looks like,” Golden said. “And then Fig did the rest.
“Fig has great energy. Smart player. And he's vocal. He's a good communicator,” Golden said. “I thought he played really hard. There are some plays I know that he would like to have back, but overall, he really, really responded well.”
Not only are the Bengals coming off a trip overseas, but the Steelers are also coming off their bye.
Since the international series began, there have been five instances where a team returning from an overseas game played a team coming off a bye.
The teams coming off the bye are 5-0.
"I don't know what the stats are. I just know they're not great. I honestly can't even give you a ballpark of what they are," Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said. "I just think common sense would tell you it's probably a little challenging. But I think we have a great mindset right now."
Golden praised Taylor for the way he has handled the long trip to Spain and quick turnaround, along with all the other ways he has schedule practice and recovery throughout the offseason and training camp.
“I think Zac is on the front end, if not pioneering in terms of how to take care of the players during the season,” Golden said. “How do you respond as a player, or as in our case, the defensive unit or by position, at the end of the day.
“If he's taking care of us physically, we better be on the game plan,” Golden added. “The walkthrough's got to be great. Overcommunicate. Whatever you have to do to establish that you know exactly what you need to do.”

title: Bengals-Steelers Rest Disparity Could Be Even More Problematic Than First Thought
full_text:
A lot has been made about the rest disparity that will be in play Sunday night when the Cincinnati Bengals, who are coming off their international game in Madrid, play host to the Pittsburgh Steelers, fresh of their bye.
This will be the sixth game in which one team is returning from an international game and the other a bye, and the teams returning for their off week are 5-0.
But that’s only part of the history working against the Bengals this week.
That’s because the Steelers are on one of the best post-bye runs in NFL history with a nine-game winning streak.
The last time Pittsburgh lost a game after its bye week was 2016, when it fell 21-14 at Baltimore as 3.5-point favorites.
The nine-game, post-bye run is the second longest active winning streak in the league and the third longest since the NFL began using bye weeks in 1990.
The Buffalo Bills own the longest active streak at 12 in a row after knocking off the Ravens 36-10 following their Week 7 bye this year.
The NFL record is 13 in a row, set by the Philadelphia Eagles from 1999-2011 (there were two bye weeks in 1993).
During the Steelers’ current nine-game streak, four of the wins have come on the road, including two of the last three.
And four of the last five have come with Pittsburgh as the underdog.
Here is the list (with point spread):
2025: Week 6 vs Cleveland, W 23-9 (-6)
2024: Week 10 at Washington, W 28-27 (+2.5)
2023: Week 7 at LA Rams, W 24-17 (+3)
2022: Week 10 vs. New Orleans, W 20-10 (+1)
2021: Week 8 at Cleveland, W 15-10 (+4.5)
2020: Week 5 vs. Philadelphia, W 38-29 (-7.5)
2019: Week 8 vs. Miami, W 27-14 (-14)
2018: Week 8 vs. Cleveland, W 33-18 (-8.5)
2017: Week 10 at Indianapolis, W 20-17 (-10.5)
The Steelers are 25-12 all-time in the week after a bye. That .676 winning percentage is tied for fifth best in the league behind the Ravens (22-8, .733), Eagles (27-10, .730), Broncos (27-10, .730) and Bills (27-11, .711).
The Bengals have been the Steelers' opponent after a bye six times, but the most recent was way back in 2008, with the Steelers winning that game 38-10 in Cincinnati.
From 1990-98, the Steelers came out of their bye to face the Bengals five times, with Cincinnati winning three of those contests.
The Bengals are 12-26 after a bye for a .346 winning percentage that ranks last in the league. But they have won four of their most recent six, including the Week 7 game at Baltimore this year.
The other teams in the bottom five of post-bye winning percentages are the Raiders (13-24, .351), Browns (12-20, .375), Seahawks (14-23, .378) and Jets (15-22, .405).
Under Zac Taylor, the Bengals are 4-4 in the week after the bye.
Surprisingly, the Taylor-led Bengals have only played three games in which the opponent was coming off a bye, and they are 1-2 in those contests.
They lost 27-18 at Green Bay last year, won 17-13 vs. Seattle in 2023 and lost 19-17 to the Giants in 2020.

title: Cris Collinsworth Makes Powerful Statement About Joe Burrow Ahead of Bengals-Steelers Showdown
full_text:
Joe Burrow is in the middle of an MVP-caliber season for the Bengals. However, this week's matchup is arguably the most critical game of the season so far, as the Bengals welcome the Steelers to Paycor Stadium on Sunday Night Football. Cincinnati legend Cris Collinsworth is set to call the game nationally and recently shared his thoughts on Burrow's elite performance this season so far.
Collinsworth acknowledged the effort Burrow has put into his performance and the weight he has placed on himself as the leader of the football team. He also acknowledged how the Bengals offense functioned during his time with the team in the 80's.
"He works very hard at his craft, but he's basically taken this entire team on his shoulders, and I think everybody down there would tell you that," Collinsworth said . "From just analyzing football, it's always been you got to have a little bit of everything, when Cincinnati's been good in the past and my teams went on to the Super Bowl, it was Pete Johnson, Ickey Woods, James Brooks and we had that sort of balance."
Collinsworth admitted after that both the Packers and Bengals have shifted that balance into the most drastic pass-heavy approach he has witnessed.
"We're seeing two teams that are taking all of that and shifting that paradigm in a way that I've never seen," Collinsworth said . "The Green Bay Packers being one, their offensive line can't block anybody running the football, the Bengals are much better than that, but it's like maybe they do just have to throw it, as you're watching the Atlanta game and I was like 'why would you not give it Joe Burrow and throw it every time?"
He later explained that Burrow separates himself from other elite quarterbacks in the league by throwing at the exact correct moment. Collinsworth then detailed that this facet of Burrow's ability allows Zac Taylor to call deep passes more often. He also said that Burrow and Mike Gesicki work the middle of the field better than other combinations he watches.
"He seems to throw it every time it's the absolutely correct thing to do, and so as a coach what that does for you is it allows you to call a lot of deep passes, he just doesn't miss the opportunities," Collinsworth said . "They also have this great combination with Gesicki being enough of a threat going down the middle of the field that they work the middle of the field better than a lot of the combinations that I see."

title: Cincinnati Bengals WR Ja'Marr Chase Gives 2, Um, Thumbs Up to Disrespecting Steelers
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals 2022 season opener against the Pittsburgh Steelers is most known for Joe Burrow’s four turnovers and the loss of long snapper Clark Harris, resulting in missed game-winning kicks at the end of regulation and in overtime of a 23-20 loss.
Wide receiver Ja’Marr Chase remembers the game for something else.
Actually, two of something else – both of his middle fingers.
Chase infamously threw double birds in the face of Pittsburgh safety Minkah Fitzpatrick, and the gesture was immortalized by a photographer. And that picture has been printed and made into shirts, blankets and other mementos that often find their way back to Chase.
The receiver said he’s often asked to sign items with the photo on them.
“Because I want to do it again,” Chase said. “But I don’t want to get fined. But I love it. It’s a cool picture, honestly.”
The display in 2022 resulted in the first fine of Chase’s career, as the NFL docked him $23,870 for “multiple unsportsmanlike conducts.”
The double birds didn’t draw a flag on the field, but he was penalized 15 yards for taunting after an incomplete pass on fourth and 2 with 1:51 remaining and the Bengals trailing 20-14.
Chase has been fined five other times in his career, although the one for obscene gestures in Week 2 against Houston was rescinded.
He also drew a $15,914 taunting penalty and fine later in 2022 against Kansas City; a $31,599 fine for verbally abusing an official in 2024 at Kansas City; a $19,697 fine for an obscene gesture against Baltimore in 2024; and a one-game suspension that amounted to a loss of $507,156 for spitting on Pittsburgh’s Jalen Ramsey last year.
Sunday’s game against the Steelers will be two days shy of the one-year anniversary of that incident.
While Chase said he doesn’t want to get fined again, he said he would accept the punishment and flash the double birds to another team in the right situation.
“If it was the Super Bowl, yes,” he said. “I would definitely do it again.”
What about an AFC Championship Game against the Steelers.
“I might have to call Chad (Johnson) for that one,” he said.
While Chase won his appeal of the fine in Houston this year, he knew there was no way he would win an appeal after the double birds in 2022.
“There's no appealing that fine because I'm red handed in photos. It's hard to get out of that one.”

title: Ja’Marr Chase Delivers Brutally Honest Take on Bengals-Steelers Rivalry
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers enter Sunday night's game tied for the top spot in the AFC North at 6-2.
It's one of the biggest regular season meetings between the teams in years, but Ja'Marr Chase still puts the Bengals' rivalry with the Kansas City Chiefs a tier above it.
Asked where Pittsburgh ranked among the rivalries he's been part of in his career, Chase said on Thursday that it was "pretty up there." The Bengals superstar stopped short of picking a No. 1, saying, "I don't have nobody number one."
The follow-up yielded a more definitive answer from Chase. When asked whether the Pittsburgh rivalry was on par with Cincinnati's rivalry with Kansas City when both teams were rolling, Chase replied, "No, no, no." He put the Chiefs rivalry "way higher."
Some of the biggest games of Chase's career came against Kansas City, and the first one produced one of his best individual performances. As a rookie, he caught 11 passes for 266 yards and three touchdowns in a 34-31 win over the Chiefs. The Bengals overcame three separate 14-point deficits that afternoon and clinched the AFC North on Evan McPherson's field goal as time expired.
Four weeks later, the teams met again at Arrowhead Stadium, with a Super Bowl berth on the line. Cincinnati fell behind 21-3 but rallied to win 27-24 in overtime. The following season, Kansas City earned a rematch in the AFC Championship Game and won 23-20 with a field goal as time expired.
In just over a year, the teams had played a game that clinched a division title and two others that determined who would represent the AFC in the Super Bowl.
Sunday's meeting with Pittsburgh has its own stakes, though they aren't as high as the stakes in the matchups with the Chiefs.
These AFC North rivals are both 6-2, which is the best combined winning percentage for a Bengals-Steelers matchup this late in the season since 2009 according to NBC. The winner will also take sole possession of first place in the AFC North.
The Bengals are trying to win their fifth-straight game and avoid being swept by Pittsburgh for the first time since 2023.

title: Browns Rookie Earns High Praise From Head Coach Amid Growing Pains
full_text:
There have been plenty of storylines following the Cleveland Browns all season long.
However, one that has lost some of its spotlight since the opening few weeks is the development of the team's rookie offensive linemen.
Following several struggles along the offensive line in recent weeks, most notably from veteran Tytus Howard, rookies Austin Barber and Spencer Fano have been overshadowed.
And honestly, it isn't hard to understand why.
Even with both Barber and Fano playing well, quarterbacks Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders have been sacked a total of 38 times across nine games , averaging out to over four sacks a game. If Cleveland wants to legitimately contend by the time the playoffs roll around, the line is going to have to be better.
Head coach Todd Monken spoke about Fano in particular, saying that the issues the line has gone through have allowed the ninth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft an opportunity to learn and grow.
"It’s so cool for him because of the way he’s wired, how he works at it — highly intelligent, very prideful, but it’s not easy being indoctrinated into playing left tackle as a rookie," he said. "And every week it feels like there is no off week, right? There isn’t an off week of these guys that are paid to get to the quarterback.
"And it really stresses your mental stamina, play after play, right? There is no ‘oh, I get a little bit of a smoke break here’. Oh, no, right. You don’t get that."
Fano currently ranks 17th out of 71 in the league in overall Pro Football Focus grade , placing him among some of football's best offensive tackles. In pass rush, there is still work to be done, with him ranking 39th out of 71, but his rushing ranking of 22nd pushes him back up towards the top of the ladder.
As Monken mentioned, even with him being moved from right tackle, which he was accustomed to in college, to left tackle, the 22-year-old has made incredible strides quickly.
He went on to say that the difference in competition is something that Fano has had to learn to be ready for, especially with edge rushers being so dynamic at the NFL level. One play he could be going up against a veteran before a shifty, young rusher comes flying his way the next.
Browns HC Todd Monken talked about the growing pains Spencer Fano is going through as a young tackle in the NFL and said there's "no smoke break" to catch your breath "It’s so cool for him because the way he’s wired, how he works at it, highly intelligent, very prideful, but… pic.twitter.com/qE0e7PTtyt
"You know, and then they roll (Jadeveon) Clowney in there, and they roll other guys that are young and trying to get the quarterback," Monken continued. "Like, that’s what’s the coolest thing about being a part of professional sports and being in professional football. Everybody’s got really good players, and it really challenges you.
"And I like his mental makeup. I like the way he’s wired. He’s only going to continue to get better."
Fano's next chance to return to the field and try to lead the Browns' offensive line comes on Sunday, Nov. 15.
The Browns play host to the Houston Texans from Huntington Bank Field at 1:00 p.m. EST.

title: Texans Rule Out Two Key Players Ahead of Browns Matchup on Sunday
full_text:
On Friday, the Cleveland Browns, just two days ahead of their matchup against the Houston Texans at home, announced that they would be without safety Ronnie Hickman and fullback Mike Burton.
Rookie Browns wideout Denzel Boston was also ruled questionable , putting the team in an even more difficult spot on Sunday against the Texans.
But the Browns aren't the only team banged up.
Following the Browns' injury report, a few hours passed, and the Texans issued their injury report ahead of Sunday's game, ruling out newly acquired wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. and defensive end Danielle Hunter.
Most importantly, the Texans may be without defensive end Will Anderson Jr., too, as the 6-foot-4, 243-pound defensive end is reportedly dealing with an ankle injury.
The #Browns won't face DE Danielle Hunter or WR Marvin Harrison Jr. on Sunday—and DE Will Anderson Jr. is in question with an ankle injury. https://t.co/wM1hRzoezb
For the Texans, not having Anderson Jr. on Sunday is something that could be a big impact, as the two-time pro bowler has put together a great season with 9.5 sacks in only eight games . Anderson Jr. has surpassed his 2023 rookie sack total (7.0 sacks) and will look to surpass the career high he set last season with 12.0 sacks.
Offensively, the Texans are looking to get Harrison Jr. involved more following their trade with the Arizona Cardinals, as Harrison Jr. became a part of the franchise on October 12 and has only been targeted 11 times in the three games played.
On the season, with both the Cardinals and the Texans, he has only been targeted 24 times with 11 receptions, averaging around 13.2 yards per reception. That is good enough for just 145 receiving yards and two touchdowns.
He hasn't had a big impact on the game this season, but missing Sunday keeps him behind the curve as he tries to adjust to the new system in Houston.
With Harrison Jr. out, the Texans will have to work in other guys on the offensive side of the ball.
While Anderson Jr. ruled questionable, the Texans know they will be without at least one defensive end in Hunter, as he is dealing with a hamstring injury.
Hunter has played in all eight games ahead of the matchup against the Browns and has played in all games since 2022, dating back to his days with the Minnesota Vikings. Hunter has been with Houston since 2024 and will miss his first game as a Texan on Sunday.
With the Texans' injury report being out and a good chunk of important pieces being on the list, Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson could have bought himself another week to succeed as the starter.
Defensively, the Browns will have a much easier time at locking down the passing game with Harrison Jr. inactive.
The two sides will clash at 1:00 p.m. EST from Huntington Bank Field on Sunday, Nov. 15.

title: Browns vs. Texans: 3 Matchups That Could Decide Sunday’s Game
full_text:
Houston has won three of its last four after a 0-4 start.
A Texans win would pull them within half a game of Cleveland and give Houston the head-to-head edge in the AFC playoff race.
Luckily for the Browns, the Texans are beatable, and here is why:
Denzel Boston leads the Browns with 507 receiving yards and averages 15.8 yards per catch. The Houston Texans have allowed 31 completions of 20 yards or more this season, tied for the third most in the NFL. Boston will have a chance to build on his six catches for 98 yards against New Orleans, including a 60-yard reception.
DENZEL BOSTON MOSSED HIM pic.twitter.com/ZZdzSZtnpj
The caveat comes down to blocking, as the Browns' offensive line has struggled in recent weeks and has allowed 38 total sacks this season , the most in the NFL. If Deshaun Watson has time to get the ball deep to Boston, the Browns have a fighting chance.
Rookie left tackle Spencer Fano will be central to Cleveland’s chances of keeping Watson upright. Fano ranks 17th out of 71 qualifying NFL tackles with a 74.5 overall grade, according to PFF. Fano allowed a season-high eight pressures against Pittsburgh in Week 8.
Now he faces a Houston pass rush led by Will Anderson Jr., the Defensive Player of the Year betting favorite with an NFL-high 9.5 sacks.
Love to see this. KC - orbit motion decoy (holds BS LB) Fano - down block on Simmons (All-Pro) Boston - crack block on PS safety Barber - counter kickout Fannin - counter pull for PS ILB Judkins - tight course, make CB miss Every key player mentioned here is 22yo or younger. pic.twitter.com/XW4Xue6x7h
Fano’s best game of his young career came against the Tennessee Titans, when he earned a 92.2 overall PFF grade and allowed just two pressures on 41 pass-blocking snaps.
If Fano can come close to that performance, Cleveland will have a better chance to give Watson time to attack Houston downfield.
Jared Verse’s production has been debated in Cleveland this season. Verse has just 15 pressures, according to PFF, and no sacks through nine games, despite being a key part of the Myles Garrett trade and viewed as a cornerstone of the Browns' defense.
Verse acknowledged that he hasn’t played well and said he spoke with the team psychologist about what he described as a “mental block.”
#Browns DE Jared Verse said he's reflected a lot on his struggles this season and believes he's identified areas to help him be more productive, but a lot of that work has been on the mental side. It's why he took time to meet with the team psychiatrist to help him "self-build."… pic.twitter.com/8pxPv0OxgX
His next test comes against Houston right tackle Trent Brown. Brown ranks 42nd among 71 qualifying tackles with a 64.2 overall PFF grade. Brown has allowed 19 pressures and two sacks on 342 pass-blocking snaps, according to Core Football Labs.
Even if Verse doesn’t get his first sack, forcing C.J. Stroud out of the pocket could help limit Houston’s deep passing game.
Make no mistake, the Texans are not an easy matchup. Stroud has four 300-yard passing games this season, including a 384-yard, five-touchdown performance last week against the Chargers.
If Cleveland gives Watson time to find his receivers downfield and keeps Stroud from doing the same, the Browns can head into the bye at 6-4.

title: Browns Hit With Major Injury News Ahead of Week 10 Showdown With Texans
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns might have seen the return of quarterback Deshaun Watson from concussion protocol after he missed last week's game.
But the team will now potentially be without a different key member of the offense this weekend.
On Friday, Nov. 13, the Browns announced another batch of injuries ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Houston Texans at Huntington Bank Field on Sunday.
First announced by ESPN NFL Insider Daniel Oyefusi, rookie wideout Denzel Boston was listed as questionable heading into the weekend due to a toe injury.
Browns WR Denzel Boston (toe) is questionable. FB Mike Burton and S Ronnie Hickman have been ruled out.
The 6-foot-4, 215-pound rookie has been one of the Browns' most exciting offseason additions to the offense , coming out of the draft quickly and making his impact. Across his first nine games, he has 32 receptions for 507 yards and three touchdowns, averaging 15.8 yards per reception.
His connection with Deshaun Watson has been o ne of the more welcomed things this season , even though the two had no prior experience with one another before this past offseason.
Without him on Sunday, Cleveland would have to turn to a combination of Tylan Wallace and Isaiah Bond to slide into the final wide receiver spot.
Alongside Boston potentially being inactive, the Browns received unfortunate news that safety Ronnie Hickman and fullback Mike Burton would be out on Sunday. Not listed as questionable, Burton is dealing with a calf injury, while Hickman is still recovering from a concussion.
Burton missing Sunday's game is going to be a hit to the rushing attack for the Browns, an area of the offense that has struggled all season long. With him out, the workload is going to be pushed even more onto the passing attack, especially with Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson still searching for a rhythm as the back half of the season gets underway.
While having any bodies on the injured list is going to be an issue, the Browns have found a nice replacement for Hickman for the time being.
Taken in the second round of the draft this past year, Emmanuel McNeil-Warren's initial status in the Browns' defense was somewhat unknown.
However, through limited opportunities, he has shown that he has an awful lot in the tank to give the team. Through nine games, he has 42 combined tackles, three tackles for a loss and three pass deflections , all while routinely being in the right position at the right time.
His role has changed each week, but in Week 10, it seems his opportunity to become a long-term, key piece of the Browns' defense is his for the taking.
The Browns and Texans will face at 1:00 p.m. EST from Huntington Bank Field, with Boston's final status expected to be released prior to the game.

title: Deshaun Watson’s Return Against Houston Comes With a Major Opportunity for Cleveland
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns host the Houston Texans at a pivotal point in their season. They are the AFC's eighth seed, just one spot out of a wildcard position.
If they lose, they will head into their bye week on a three-game losing streak at 5-5. However, if they win, they start their four-game home stand with a win and improve to 6-4.
#Browns Todd Monken said "the intention was for Deshaun to start." Just wanted to run it by the staff.
Todd Monken turns back to Deshaun Watson as starting quarterback after he missed last week to rest from a concussion injury. Watson returns to face the team that drafted him before things went sour and they were forced to trade him.
He is 1-0 against the Texans, winning his first game in a Browns uniform.
No game has been bigger than this one for the Browns. The Texans come into Cleveland after drubbing the Los Angeles Chargers, improving their record to 3-5. CJ Stroud has had a great season, and he is looking to translate his stat line into more wins. The Texans will come in with all the momentum and motivation, as they need this win to keep their playoff hopes alive.
The Browns return to Cleveland after a three-game road trip. Cleveland is ready to welcome them back after starting the season 3-0 in their home stadium. The Texans are 3-1 on the road, so it will be a great test of which team has the advantage.
Watson and the offense will have to start faster than normal. Their tendency is to start games slowly before turning it on in the fourth quarter and winning late in games. Houston’s offense has been high-flying, and all their wide receivers are finally healthy. The Browns’ defense has been gashed on the ground, but Houston has thrived through the air.
The Texans are probably the second-best team that the Browns will face the rest of the way, outside of the Cincinnati Bengals. If they can win this game, then the playoffs become more likely entering the bye week.
They are tied with the New England Patriots in the standings, but the Patriots earned the last wild card spot due to their record against AFC opponents. The Browns can help their cause by beating the Texans as the Patriots play an NFC team this week.
Watson also needs to beat the Texans personally. If the Browns fall and there is breathing room between them and the playoffs, then they will likely pivot to Shedeur Sanders at quarterback. After three quarters of undesirable play last week, Sanders put together an incredible fourth quarter and overtime.
Monken remained steadfast that Watson would start following his return from concussion protocol.
A similar situation arose early in the season when it was believed that the team would switch to Sanders if Watson performed poorly against Baker Mayfield and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Watson led a fourth-quarter comeback, and he kept his job.
He now faces the next piece of what is considered one of the worst trades in NFL history, with a familiar consequence on the line . The Browns will complete the revenge tour after their bye week against Kevin Stefanski and the Atlanta Falcons.
Monken took a lot of heat for naming Watson the starter at the beginning of the season, but he proved right after they started 5-2. He now goes back to Watson with full faith that he gives the team the best chance to win. Monken can earn a lot of credibility with a good performance from the offense and a win on Sunday.
Both teams in Sunday’s matchup need the win just as much as the other. The Texans tanked the Browns for four seasons after the trade for Watson. The only winning season the Browns had since was in 2023, in which Watson was injured.
It ended after a blowout loss in the playoffs to the Texans.
The Browns have their chance to bury the Texans’ season and force them to make a decision on extending their quarterback, which could alter their franchise.
Watson has returned just in time for the Browns’ biggest opportunity of the season to beat his former team.

title: Browns Have 3 Major Offseason Needs That Their Trade Deadline Silence Made Clear
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline passed at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, and the Browns made zero moves. Cleveland finds itself in a strange position with a 5-4 record; however, the Browns aren't in "win-now" mode like many teams that were active at the deadline.
There were a few position groups the Browns could have considered trading for, but since they didn't make a move, here are three offseason needs that Cleveland must address in 2027.
The Browns have one of the best pass-catching tight ends in the NFL in Harold Fannin Jr., but the lack of depth behind him is concerning. Cleveland has only two tight ends on the active 53-man roster: Fannin and Blake Whiteheart. Many teams carry four to five tight ends, so the Browns need to figure out how to add more depth at the position next offseason.
The good news is that the Browns don’t need to add a high-level tight end since they have Fannin. But they should look for additional blocking tight ends so Fannin can focus more on the passing game instead of having to stay in to chip-block. It’s also important to have tight ends who can contribute in the running game.
Expect the Browns to sign a veteran tight end in free agency and to draft one in the first four rounds of the 2027 NFL Draft.
The Browns faced challenges coming into the season, particularly on defense, after trading away the NFL's best pass rusher, Myles Garrett, to the Rams and getting Jared Verse in the deal. Verse performed solidly during his two seasons with Los Angeles, recording 12 sacks in 34 games. But this season, he has yet to register a single sack in nine games.
Additionally, the Browns' second-best pass rusher entering the season was expected to be Alex Wright, who unfortunately tore his Achilles during training camp.
Cleveland will need to address the pass rusher position in the offseason. The Browns may consider making a move in the first or second round of the draft and could also sign a veteran free agent at a lower cost.
The Browns have two strong starting linebackers in Carson Schwesinger and Quincy Williams, but like their tight end position, there isn’t much depth behind them. If the Browns lose Schwesinger or Williams for any length of time during the season, the defense could take a significant hit.
They have struggled to stop the run in recent weeks, allowing an average of 130.6 rushing yards per game, which ranks among the worst in the NFL.
Cleveland needs to add more depth at linebacker. This would let it use three or even four linebacker sets at times to improve its chances of stopping the run game.
Daniel is a sports writer from Northeast Ohio. He has followed the Browns, Cavs, Guardians, and Buckeyes for years and loves sharing his thoughts on the team.

title: Todd Monken Gives One Concerning Update on the Browns' Offensive Line
full_text:
As the Cleveland Browns get ready to try and cut a two-game losing streak that would throw them back in the thick of the race for the playoffs, the offensive line’s play will be heavily scrutinized over the second half of the season.
No position group received more attention on the open market during the offseason than the O-Line, and after the first nine games, it’s safe to say the experiment isn’t working.
The Browns' offensive line ranks among the bottom-dwellers in the league when it comes to yards before first contact in the run game, and things look even worse in the passing game. Cleveland’s two starting tackles, Tytus Howard and rookie Spencer Fano, have the two highest pressure rates allowed in the entire NFL, and as a whole, Cleveland is the team that has allowed the most sacks (38) for the year, too.
Here's a look at the worst 10 starting tackles in the NFL right now when it comes to pressures allowed. And man, do I have bad news for the Browns... pic.twitter.com/Mby8wczjTd
To top things off, Howard leads the league with seven false start penalties , while guards Zion Johnson and rookie Austin Barber are among the six players tied for second place in holding penalties, with four apiece.
But if you were expecting to see some personnel changes for the second half of the season, don’t hold your breath.
Monken told reporters on Wednesday that his offensive line is set, and he isn’t planning on making any changes along the unit.
“I don’t see it that way. I mean, our starters are the starters. We addressed it again today: who the biggest culprits are. And they’re our guys. And they’re like, like we said before, I mean, they’re like our kids. We’re not going to just change out our kids. I mean, we’re not going to change out our players. They’re our best players. We got to get our best players. And we have a very diligent team. We have a lot of guys that love playing football, but the stats are what they are. I mean, we’ve got to look in the mirror and say, ‘at some point, this is it.’ I mean, that we just can’t continue down this road.”
When pressed about not reaching the point where changes are needed, Monken doubled down on his stance.
“I haven’t reached that point. We can’t change out our starters. I mean, I’m not changing out our starters. I mean, they’re either going to, they’re either going to buy into those types of things and the mental stamina that it takes to hold their water on defense or for us to have discipline offensively. But we’re not going to be the team we can be, because there are starters for a reason, right? If the other guys we thought gave us a better chance to win, they’d be in there.
"So, it’s all of us. How do we coach it better? How do we get our guys to dial in in the most critical moments, when it matters most?”
The Browns understandably didn’t want to pour more resources into this unit before the trade deadline after an offseason deal for Howard, adding Johnson and Elgton Jenkins in free agency, and then spending two draft picks, including a one inside the Top-10 on the group, but staying this course will lead nowhere... fast.
But zero roster changes doesn’t necessarily mean no changes at all . At some point in the preseason, Teven Jenkins was projected as the team’s starting right tackle before a back injury opened the door for Barber, who hasn’t looked back since. And there were some doubts about Fano too, with Monken acknowledging at one time that Dawand Jones could open the season at left tackle.
If that’s the case, then it’s not like the five current starters have always been head and shoulders above the rest.
And who’s to say Fano wouldn’t actually play better at right tackle than Howard? And Barber better than Fano on the left side? Both are coming off playing those positions in college for Utah and Florida, respectively. Those moves could open the right guard spot for Jenkins, as it seemed was intended.
Finally, Monken admitted during the offseason that he’d prefer to see Elgton Jenkins at guard instead of center, so there’s another possible piece that could be moved in search of a better fit overall.
Because at the end of the day, you do want your five best players on the field, but you also want them playing in their best possible spots, and sometimes leaving out one of the top five players for a better fit in one specific position maximizes the talent of the unit.
Alas, with Monken steadfast in keeping his “kids” where they are, and reinserting Deshaun Watson and his elongated dropbacks at quarterback --not that Shedeur Sanders fared much better in avoiding sacks against the Saints-- the inevitable result for Cleveland is written on the wall.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: 3 Winners, 2 Losers from Browns 2026 Trade Deadline Stand
full_text:

title: Why Browns Didn’t Move Shedeur Sanders or Dillon Gabriel at Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns chose not to make any moves at the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday, surprising many who expected them to trade a quarterback, especially with four currently on their active roster. With injuries surging across the league, demand for quarterbacks is higher than ever.
While it was clear that Deshaun Watson and Taylen Green weren’t going anywhere, players like Shedeur Sanders and Dillon Gabriel could have been potential trade candidates.
The Browns likely didn’t receive the price they wanted to trade either Gabriel or Sanders, so they decided it was wiser to maintain their quarterback depth instead.
Cleveland selected Gabriel in the third round of the 2025 NFL Draft. Although he may not seem like the franchise’s future quarterback, he could still play a backup role in 2027 and 2028. Sanders, another 2025 draft pick, just started a game against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday.
While he might not be the ideal candidate for the starting quarterback position, the Browns likely want to give him a fair evaluation before the next season.
The Minnesota Vikings were in urgent need of quarterback assistance at the trade deadline but ultimately opted for veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders. They probably had no intention of trading for either Sanders or Gabriel, which is another reason the Browns didn’t make any moves; teams in need of quarterbacks were unlikely to reach out to them.
With a 6-2 record, the Vikings weren't going to consider Sanders or Gabriel, since neither has made a significant impact in the NFL. They were searching for someone who could lead them to the Super Bowl immediately.
However, the Browns may still part ways with Sanders or Gabriel during the offseason. Cleveland is likely to draft a quarterback in the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft and intends to keep Green in the quarterback room. They will probably need to sign a veteran quarterback to start, at least until the rookie is ready.
This could lead to five quarterbacks in the room, making it unlikely that the Browns will carry all five into training camp next season. Therefore, either Sanders or Gabriel is likely to be the odd one out.
Sanders still has an opportunity to start a few more games this season. The Browns could enter their bye week 5-5 if they lose to the Houston Texans on Sunday. This situation might prompt head coach Todd Monken to change quarterbacks and move away from Watson.
Daniel is a sports writer from Northeast Ohio. He has followed the Browns, Cavs, Guardians, and Buckeyes for years and loves sharing his thoughts on the team.

title: Browns' Jared Verse Opens Up On Health Questions Amid Strugglesome 2026 Season
full_text:
The 2026 NFL season h as not been kind to Cleveland Browns edge rusher Jared Verse.
After joining the team this past offseason in a blockbuster trade with the Los Angeles Rams, the expectations were set high for Verse, especially with the Browns giving up future Hall of Famer Myles Garrett in the process.
But through the first nine weeks of the season, Verse has struggled greatly.
On Thursday, Nov. 12, he gave an update on where his health was at and if it was affecting his play at all, while also giving Browns fans some grace on their frustrations with him.
"I am upset with the way I have been playing," he said. "I don't think it is anything physical. There's nothing wrong with my body. I don't think it is anything like that. I think it is the mental aspect of the game, and I think I attacked it."
If the 26-year-old had been dealing with some sort of injury, it would have made sense to see him with just 20 combined tackles and four for a loss.
But instead, it looks like it is just something upstairs he is trying to work through.
"I think it was definitely a mental block," he said. "I train my body every day to push myself to the limits of what I am physically capable of doing...I think I have taken the steps to figure out what it was after meeting with a couple of people and everything like that."
Verse went on to defend Browns fans who have been frustrated with his lack of productivity, as the criticism that has come his way as of late has been heavy.
"...We can be here all day, and I can talk to you about each key play we have played all season... It is just simple to say the Browns fans are upset about it; I am upset about it; we all have a reason to be upset about it," he said about Browns fans being upset with his play. "I just haven't done enough, and I think that I have taken the time to figure out what the issue was and attacked it. I think I am ready for this week."
Whether or not he wants to admit it, that likely is also playing a part in his mental state. Having to fill such big shoes that Garrett once had in Cleveland is a tough task, and with his slow start to the year, his lack of production has to be weighing on him.
Either way, Cleveland needs the 2024 Defensive Rookie of the Year to return to that dominant form he once displayed, not just to show that the trade wasn't a complete flop on the Browns' end, but also to help guide this team to a playoff spot in the back half of the season.
The Browns return to the field on Sunday, Nov. 14, from Huntington Bank Field against the Houston Texans. The two sides play at 1:00 p.m. EST.
Against a dynamic and mobile quarterback like CJ Stroud, all eyes will be on how Verse can disrupt their passing attack.

title: Dallas Cowboys vs. San Francisco 49ers Predictions: Expert Picks For Week 10 Game

title: Will George Pickens Play Today? Injury Update, Start-or-Sit Advice for Week 10
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys were down one of their top players in Week 9 as George Pickens had to sit out due to a hamstring injury.
Pickens has been bothered by a shoulder problem dating back to Week 5, but the hamstring issue proved to be too much for him to overcome. With the team now preparing to take on the San Francisco 49ers in Week 10, the health of Pickens is front and center once again.
When asked about his status, however, Pickens gave a strong response. He
"You gonna see me out there. You got to turn the TV screen on," Pickens said via Calvin Watkins of The Dallas Morning News .
As a follow-up Pickens was asked if this was the best he has felt in a while. His response there was even better.
"When you turn that TV on, get some food make sure if you have a wife or girlfriend, make sure you hug her, love her and when you turn the TV on, you should see me," Pickens said.
While Pickens was adamant that he would play this week, the team had yet to officially claim he would be on the field against the 49ers. There was good news, however, as he was not listed on the Friday injury report , suggesting that he will be able to play.
For the Cowboys, this is a relief since their offense is far more dangerous when Pickens and CeeDee Lamb are out there together.
As for fantasy value, it's fair to ask if owners should start or sit the Dallas wideout. It's true that Pickens hasn't had the same explosive play he did during the 2025 season, but that doesn't mean we should give up on him.
Despite the drop in numbers, Pickens is still more than capable of putting up huge numbers. He proved that in Week 5 when he had 130 yards and a touchdown on nine receptions against the Bucs. He's also going up against a San Francisco team that is dealing with injuries in the secondary.
Cornerbacks Renardo Green, Deommodore Lenoir, Upton Stout, and Nate Hobbs are all listed at questionable . That could open the door for Pickens to put up some big numbers this weekend, which is why it would make sense to start him.

title: Grading Dallas Cowboys Rookies After First Half of 2026 Season
full_text:
With nine games in the books, the Dallas Cowboys have a strong understanding of what each member of their 2026 rookie class has to offer .
Dallas had multiple picks in the first round and used that to bring in Caleb Downs and Malachi Lawrence, in an attempt to shore up their defense. They continued to focus on that side of the ball for much of the draft, with only two picks being dedicated to the offensive side of the ball.
Unsurprisingly, that means Dallas has seen multiple rookies play a large role on defense this season. That said, let's check out each rookie and see what grade they have earned for the first nine games of the year.
One member of the rookie class won't get a grade since he was unable to make the 53-man roster. Seventh-round pick Anthony Smith was always seen as a project player and he's spending this season on the practice squad. For now, he gets an incomplete grade.
Devin Moore gets the same grade for now as the fourth-round pick from Florida has yet to make his debut. Moore spent the first half of the season on IR, but could be back soon. His 21-day practice window was recently opened , and given the Cowboys' issues at cornerback, he could find himself on the field quickly once healthy.
Undrafted free agent Camden Brown was able to make the 53-man roster following a strong offseason. He plays at a crowded position, meaning he has spent much of the season inactive. He did get his first chance to play in Week 9 and while he didn't catch a pass, Bron had 78 yards on three kick returns. There's room to grow, but he deserves a passing grade for what he's accomplished thus far.
The last of three picks in Round 4, LT Overton has been a fixture in the defensive line rotation. He has yet to start, but has appeared in 29 percent of the defensive snaps this season. Overton has eight tackles and a fumble recovery. He has an overall PFF grade of 51.1 , but considering where he was selected, this has been a solid pick.
The Cowboys brought in Drew Shelton likely as a potential starter down the road on the right side. He has played in five games, but has just five snaps on offense. He's played 23 special teams snaps, but there are still more questions than answers with Shelton.
Early in the season, Jaishawn Barham began to make waves. He was asked to move into the green-dot role with DeMarvion Overshown injured and played well. However, his snaps have dropped in recent weeks, throwing cold water on the Barham hype train.
He has a chance to change that with Donovan Ezeiruaku out in Week 10 . Dallas is thin on the edge and Barham, who played the position at Michigan, will do more pass-rushing against the 49ers than we've seen thus far. That could help Barham improve his grade, but overall, he has lived up to his draft status.
After a slow start to the season, Malachi Lawrence began to turn things around and became a starter. He then unfortunately suffered a high-ankle sprain, which has him on the IR currently. Still, Lawrence has shown enough promise for Dallas to believe he can be a long-term starter, he just needs to start seeing the production match his effort.
Caleb Downs joined Dallas with plenty of hype , and it was hard not to buy in. He was easily one of the smartest rookies in the class and filled a major need for the Cowboys.
Through nine games, there have been some ups and downs for the rookie. He has been beaten often in coverage, giving up a 75% completion rate and allowing a 107.3 passer rating when targeted. Still, he has shown promise and is coming off his best game against the Colts, which included a game-clinching interception as well as his second sack of the season.

title: 3 Dallas Cowboys Facing Make-or-Break Game in Week 10 vs. San Francisco 49ers
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys will face what might be their toughest test of the 2026 season thus far when they host the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday in Week 10.
The Cowboys were already up against it because the 49ers are one of the best teams in the NFL, but Dallas is also very banged-up, which only makes the uphill climb even steeper.
But those injuries have opened the door for a few players to make a statement and earn themselves more playing time moving forward if they can answer the bell.
Here's three players who qualify.
After it looked like Barham was going to be a major factor in Dallas' defense this season, the rookie has seen his playing time dip big time in recent weeks and Barham saw a season-low three snaps last week.
In Week 10, Barham is expected to get snaps at edge rusher with Donovan Ezeiruaku ruled out , defensive coordinator Christian Parker said.
"Then we'll get Jaishawn more involved there. He's kind of been involved there in some spotlight duty already with some different packages we've had throughout the season. We'll be able to deploy him there some too," Parker said .
The Cowboys desperately need a jolt at edge rusher thanks to the lackluster showing from the group overall this season. If Barham can provide that, he'll open up a new avenue to get more looks.
If not, it'll be back to irrelevance for the third-round rookie.
The Cowboys were hit by the injury bug at the running back spot once again last week after Tyler Goodson suffered a knee injury that is slated to keep him out for multiple games.
With Goodson on the shelf for now, the Cowboys are going to call up Abanikanda from the practice squad to serve as the RB2 , the Cowboys announced.
A former fifth-round pick of the New York Jets, Abanikanda hasn't gotten into a game since his rookie season in 2023.
Safe to say, this amounts to a huge and long-awaited opportunity that the veteran running back must capitalize on to give himself a chance to see more playing time moving forward. If he doesn't, Dallas could turn to Kendre Miller next week instead.
With Jonathan Mingo ruled out, Brown has an opportunity to see some snaps on offense, assuming the Cowboys don't give all of Mingo's looks to KaVontae Turpin.
The WR4 job is very much up for grabs considering Mingo has done nothing signficant in that role this season.
Brown, who has routinely been a healthy scratch in 2026, could wrestle that job away from Mingo if he can put together a strong performance on Sunday. The failure to do so will put him back on the inactives list for the foreseeable future now that Turpin has returned from injury.

title: 4 Bold Predictions For Cowboys vs 49ers in Week 10
full_text:
A narrow win over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 9 might not be impressive, but it might be exactly what the Dallas Cowboys needed. A big win might have built too much confidence, but the issues they had against the Colts mean they need to continue to work hard to reach their potential.
That should give them the right mindset as they prepare to host the San Francisco 49ers in Week 10. That's going to be a difficult showdown for the 49ers, who have won their past four games against Dallas . They're also the No. 1 team in the NFC with a record of 7-1.
On paper, this seems like an easy win for the 49ers , but the games aren't played on paper. That means there's a chance the Cowboys could surprise everyone, something that becomes more likely if these four bold predictions come true.
Dallas is going to be without Donovan Ezieruaku this week as he's dealing with an ankle injury. That's a major blow after they already lost Malachi Lawrence to a high ankle sprain . With both players out, rookie Jaishawn Barham is expected to spend more time on the edge against the 49ers.
He played the position during his time with Michigan, so it's not going to be completely foreign to him. He's also going to be eager to prove himself after losing snaps in recent weeks. That's why our first bold prediction has him securing his first career sack as he steps up in this new role.
Barham isn't the only rookie who will be needed in this one. Caleb Downs has been one of the more consistent players in the secondary and the Cowboys will rely on him heavily this week. San Francisco utilizes motion as much as any team in the NFL as Kyle Shanahan runs one of the more complex offenses in the NFL.
The complexity of their offense is exactly why a high-IQ player such as Downs is so vital this week. The Cowboys need him to keep everyone on the same page and while the 49ers will put together some drives that will make fans pull out their hair, Downs secures an interception for the second week in a row in this bold prediction.
Dallas was without George Pickens in Week 9 as he has been dealing with a nagging shoulder injury. He emphatically stated that he would be back on the field against the 49ers and that's great news for the Cowboys. In order to shock the NFL world and win on Sunday, they will need to put up plenty of points.
That means Pickens should see plenty of targets. That leads to this bold prediction, which sees Pickens putting up his best performance of the season by recording 150 yards and two touchdowns against a banged-up San Francisco secondary .
The 49ers have had Dak Prescott's number for years. After he led Dallas to two wins during his first two starts against them, things have fallen off the rails. The 49ers have four consecutive wins since then, including two in the playoffs. During those four losses, Prescott has thrown for just five touchdowns with eight interceptions.
If the Cowboys are going to win this one, they need Prescott to be at his best. Throughout this season, Prescott has had his ups and downs, but this final prediction has him playing his best game of the year with four touchdown passes without a turnover.

title: Cowboys Legend Leighton Vander Esch Drills $1M Kick in Pat McAfee College GameDay Contest
full_text:
Dallas Cowboys fans tuning into ESPN College GameDay got a treat when a familiar face made an appearance. Leighton Vander Esch, a first-round pick in 2018 out of Boise State, was there to represent his Broncos.
LVE was also there to try and make a kick for $1 million.
Every week, Pat McAfee allows a fan to kick a 33-yard field goal for $1 million. This week, they also had Vander Esch come out to try a kick, although he was playing for charity.
After missing badly on his first attempt, Vander Esch was allowed to try again. This time, he drilled it right down the middle , which meant McAfee would donate $1 million to the Make-A-Wish foundation.
Leighton stepped up for Luca and @MakeAWish with a $1 Million kick 💰❤️ pic.twitter.com/MPl7ytklyB
Boise State fan Easton Hanson also got a chance to kick for $1 million and he drilled the attempt.
GameDay is live from Boise State on Saturday as the No. 24 Broncos host the Oregon State Beavers. Kickoff is at 6:00 p.m. EST and will take place at Albertsons Stadium.
The Broncos are 8-1, whereas the Beavers come into this one with a record of 5-4.
Vander Esch wasn't a popular selection when first announced as Cowboys' fans felt he was selected too high. Dallas had the 19th overall pick and linebacker wasn't seen as an impactful enough position for such a selection. There were also concerns about his medical history as Vander Esch entered the league with a lingering neck issue.
That feeling changed in a hurry as LVE made a huge impact. He recorded 140 tackles and two interceptions as a rookie, leading to a Pro Bowl selection. That was impressive enough on its own, but he also started just 11 of the 16 games he played.
Unfortunately, the neck injuries ended up playing a major role in his career. He suffered another neck injury in 2019, leading to surgery. He missed nine games that year and another six in 2020 due to a broken collarbone.
Vander Esch suffered yet another neck injury in 2023, forcing him to miss all but five games. He then retired from the game at just 28 years old . It was tough to see him go, especially at such a young age, but he proved to be a stud during his six-year career, even if he never earned the respect he deserved.

title: Jerry Jones' Comments on Brian Schottenheimer Suggest Cowboys Coach Won't Get Fired
full_text:
When it comes to Dallas Cowboys fans right now, head coach Brian Schottenheimer is public enemy No. 1.
Since taking over the Cowboys in 2025, the team is a dreadful 11-14-1 under Schottenheimer, including a disappointing 4-5 this season.
But it isn't just about the record.
Despite having the fifth-best scoring offense in the NFL, it still feels like the Cowboys aren't operating at their best, something many believe is on the play-calling of Schottenheimer. There is also an incredible lack of discipline, which is another stain on Schottenheimer's tenure as head coach.
All of this has led fans and analysts alike to believe that Schotty should get fired . However, based on what Jerry Jones said recently, that might not happen anytime soon.
During his latest appearance on 105.3 The Fan on Friday, Jones made it sound like Schottenheimer isn't going anywhere anytime soon, with Jones once again expressing his confidence in the embattled head coach.
Jones also noted that he believes Schottenheimer will get better as a head coach in the year or years ahead.
That's right, year or years.
"Given the ability to live to tell about it, Brian will be a year from now, two years from now, three years from now, he'll be much more (prepared) for the kinds of challenges a head coach has," Jones said. "There's no question, you pay a price when you're doing it for the first time. ... I still like (our) bet (on him)."
Cowboys fans don't want Schottenheimer to finish out the season, let alone get one or more years. So, that's what makes Jones' comments especially jarring.
What makes Jones' faith in Schotty even more perplexing is the fact that the Cowboys believe they have the talent necessary to succeed, which is part of the reason why they didn't make any trades on deadline day.
“It shows you that we’re confident in our roster and our best football is still ahead," Schottenheimer said after the trade deadline passed without a Cowboys deal.
So, if the roster is good enough but the team is still playing at an unacceptable level, there's only the coaching left to blame.
To be fair to Schottenheimer, he isn't the only culprit on the staff, as defensive coordinator Christian Parker has left a lot to be desired with his play-calling, also.
But Schottenheimer is the head coach and the buck ultimately stops with him. There is a lot of blame going his way, whether it's because of the play-calling, his in-game decision-making or the lackluster culture that, according to a few former Cowboys , has players not giving full effort and doing boneheaded things like DeMarvion Overshown did in Week 9 with his penalty .
If this season ends the way we think it will, which is with Dallas not making the postseason yet again, and the Cowboys give Schotty another chance in 2027, the fan base will be beside itself and hope for this franchise getting on track will be at an all-time low.

title: Cowboys Named Landing Spot For Former Pro Bowl RB in Free Agency Amid Tyler Goodson injury
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys' No. 2 running back spot has had a run of bad luck this year because of injuries.
Before the 2026 season started, the Cowboys lost Malik Davis to a season-ending hip injury . Now, Dallas' latest RB2, Tyler Goodson, is expected to miss multiple weeks with his knee injury.
That leaves the Cowboys depending on Israel Abanikanda behind Javonte Williams this week. Dallas also added Kendre Miller to the practice squad.
Safe to say, neither one of those backs are reliable and Dallas may want to explore the free-agent market if Goodson misses an extended period of time.
In an article listing off the best bargain free agents still available after the trade deadline, Bleacher Report's Moe Moton linked Dallas to former Pro Bowl running back Najee Harris.
"Dallas Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones expects backup running back Tyler Goodson to miss time with a knee injury," Moton said.
"The Cowboys signed Kendre Miller to their practice squad, but he has a history of injuries. Harris could be a solid complement to Javonte Williams in the Cowboys' ground game.
"Best fits: Dallas Cowboys, New England Patriots."
In 2026, Harris latched on with the New York Giants and played in five games before he was cut for complaining about how the Giants handled their backfield touches.
“It’s hard to get into a rhythm with one or two plays,” Harris said to reporters in October. “If you’re getting a play here and then get taken out for a series, there’s nothing you could do. I’ve never been through none of this before.”
Harris didn't see much success with the Giants, with the veteran running back tallying just 3.2 yards per carry. He did have one solid game, though, when he posted 52 rushing yards on nine carries, good enough for 5.8 yards per tote.
That showed Harris still has something left in the tank after suffering a torn Achilles in 2025.
Harris totaled four 1,000-yard seasons and one Pro Bowl nod over the first four years of his career when he served as a workhorse back for the Pittsburgh Steelers.
But things have gone downhill for him since then, as he suffered a torn Achilles in 2025 and didn't do much during his stint in New York.
While Harris isn't an explosive back and won't offer much of a change of pace from Williams, he is good between the tackles, and is an asset as a pass-catcher and in pass protection.
Most importantly, he's just a reliable back who is going to offer more stability than anyone the Cowboys have on their roster currently.
We suspect the Cowboys will stand pat for now if Goodson is only going to miss a game or two, but if he's going to be out any longer than that, we could see a Harris-Cowboys union in the near future.

title: How Close Broncos Came to Acquiring RB Tony Pollard Before Deadline
full_text:
Jonathan Taylor wasn't the only running back who interested the Denver Broncos prior to Tuesday's NFL trade deadline.
ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported Saturday that Denver "checked in on" Titans RB Tony Pollard but were rebuffed by Tennessee's apparent price tag of "anything less" than a third-round draft pick.
"The Packers and Broncos checked in on Titans running back Tony Pollard, whom Tennessee would not have traded for anything less than a third-round pick," the report stated.
This tracks with what league insider Jordan Schultz previously reported -- that the Broncos (and New York Giants) were among the teams in the short-lived Pollard sweepstakes.
"But Tennessee was adamant for weeks that they were unlikely to move him, as he’s been vital to the locker room and the continued development of Cam Ward," Schultz wrote on X on Nov. 10.
A prototypical dual-threat back, Pollard has accounted for 665 yards from scrimmage (595 rushing yards, 4.5 yards per carry) and six total touchdowns (all on the ground) across eight appearances this season.
Pollard was among several NFL RBs who were viewed as potential trade candidates prior to the deadline, along with Taylor , the Jets' Breece Hall, the Eagles' Saquon Barkley, and the Ravens' Derrick Henry. In the end, none of these players were moved by their original clubs.
It's clear that Denver was seeking an upgrade to pair with ascending rookie Jonah Coleman and pass-catching extraordinaire RJ Harvey. What's more, had they acquired Taylor or Pollard, the Broncos likely would've made veteran J.K. Dobbins available for trade .
Obviously, none of that transpired, and the club now heads into the second half of its 2026 campaign with the status quo at the position: Coleman and Dobbins on early downs, with Harvey seeing extensive third-down opportunities once he returns from injured reserve.
The Broncos will hope the trio can find their collective groove following a less-than-impressive statistical start prior to the bye. Entering Week 10, the rushing offense ranks 29th in yards per carry per game and 27th in total yards per game.
"Those runners are going to be important," head coach Sean Payton said after last Sunday's victory over the Panthers. "I'm not going to answer running-back depth questions, and certainly our running backs are not going to sit in front of a 15-minute interview about their playing time. Man, those guys are really important. [Running backs] J.K. [Dobbins] played, Jonah [Coleman] played, RJ [Harvey] will be back here shortly, and I'm glad we got both of them. I didn't feel like we ran it particularly well with either of them, and it wasn't back driven. It was ‘Oh, that was a Buffalo front.’ Like, it took us a minute. And now, we threw it better for chunk plays than we ran it, but we got the runs when we needed it later."

title: Broncos Midseason Awards: MVP, Breakout Star, and Biggest Disappointment
full_text:
The NFL put the Denver Broncos' bye week at an ideal spot, about as close to halfway through the season as is possible in a 17-game campaign.
The Broncos are 7-2 entering Week 10's bye, leading the AFC West. They're favored to win the division , though one or two slip-ups down the stretch could change that, and the AFC's No. 1 playoff seed is still very much on the table.
The bye has offered us a chance to breathe and take a deep dive into the Broncos, from cumulative player grades to rookie report cards and five warning signs . Today is a day for superlatives, though; we're handing out midseason awards to the deserving Broncos, and there's been plenty of sample size to feel confident about each one.
Let's start with the most important award.
I know, I know. Nix has had a weird campaign, returning from the broken ankle that ended his 2025 season and torpedoed the Broncos' championship ambitions on the doorstep of the Super Bowl. He doesn't rank highly in any of the common quarterback stats, and most of the advanced analytics aren't kind to him.
However, Nix remains the Broncos' most valuable player. Even amid a step-back of a third season, without him, this team's outlook would immediately fall into the gutter, just as we saw in the AFC championship game last year.
Nix was bad at times against the Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Rams, and Seattle Seahawks, but as a thought exercise, imagine how those games would have shaken out if Jarrett Stidham had been the quarterback. Yeah. That's right. Denver loses all three of those games without Nix.
Even amid his early-season struggles, the one thing that no one could take away from Nix is his clutch-time excellence. There isn't a better NFL quarterback when the chips are down, and that clutch-time will to win is a big reason why the Broncos were able to weather their early-season gauntlet of a schedule.
CHUNK PLAY MARVIN MIMS JR. DENvsAZ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/o13qfZGfzC
Since Week 7, Nix has been improving by leaps and bounds. His confidence is back, and he's no longer so painfully hesitant in his decision-making. In fact, he's hunting with the football again .
There's every reason to believe that Nix's upward momentum will continue coming out of the bye. He wanted to be peaking at the right time, and the stars are aligning for the Broncos to get the best possible version of their young franchise quarterback down the stretch and into the playoffs.
Waddle hasn't exactly been an off-the-charts producer, but he's been the Broncos' most important non-quarterback player on offense. Amid Nix's early slump, Waddle bided his time, finding ways to make an impact in Denver's low-percentage passing attack.
But even when the ball doesn't go his way, or isn't intended to go his way, Waddle's presence on the field has changed the math for opposing defenses. It has opened things up for other players, and will continue to do so as the Broncos' schedule opens up down the stretch.
Jaylen Waddle gets his first big play as a Bronco! 🐧 JAXvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/FAioYbx0Fs
Waddle has dealt with some minor injuries and he suffered a concussion in Week 9, but he's appeared in all nine games, leading the team with 30 receptions on 52 targets for 337 yards and two touchdowns. He's also made some big plays on two-point conversions, without which, the Broncos don't come back in two of their one-score victories this season.
The Broncos don't have any buyer's remorse after giving up a first- and third-round pick to acquire Waddle. He's just getting started.
Allen is in the middle of perhaps his best season as a pro, which is saying something, given that he's been an All-Pro in each of the past two seasons, and was a first-team selection last year.
Allen is near the top of the NFL in pass-rushing metrics, including quarterback pressures, and his 4.5 sacks are tied with Nik Bonitto for the team lead. Allen affects the quarterback on every snap, commanding double teams, which frees up other guys to make plays. He even blocked a field-goal attempt in Week 4.
IT'S BLOCKED! 📺: @CBSSports / @paramountplus pic.twitter.com/8wHodVFVIN
He makes his own fair share of plays, even against double teams because Allen is just that good. Against the run, he's one of the NFL's best interior defenders, too. He's just an all-around elite player at the point of attack. Without him, this defense wouldn't be nearly as formidable.
Only two of Denver's 2026 draft picks have actually seen the field this season, but Coleman has easily been the club's top rookie. That's saying something, given that he missed four games on injured reserve with an ankle sprain.
In four of the five games he's dressed for, Coleman has touched the ball and has been a key contributor. In fact, the Broncos haven't lost a game yet in which Coleman has touched the ball, so Sean Payton may want to remember that.
Coleman has 47 times for 191 yards and three touchdowns, averaging a team-high 4.1 yards per attempt. He's also caught 13 passes for 128 yards and six first downs.
JONAH COLEMAN DOWN TO THE 4 KCvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/nRd1e0xIhC
As the Broncos' new RB1, the sky is the limit for Coleman, especially if Payton is able to get to the bottom of the offensive line's blocking issues, as promised to do during the bye. It's a pretty distant thought, but with eight games left to go, the rookie still has the chance to rush for 1,000 yards, though it will take the O-line stepping its game up significantly.
Wide receiver Pat Bryant may have been my choice here, were it not for his missing four games with an ankle injury. He's been a tremendous player for this offense and has taken some big steps forward since his rookie year.
What Bryant and Robinson have in common is they're both in Year 2. Robinson has appeared in every game thus far — another illustration of his improvement, given that he was a healthy scratch in 11 games as a rookie — and without him, I'm not sure Denver would have been able to weather Jonathon Cooper's absence so successfully.
Robinson has 28 tackles (12 solo), three tackles for a loss, one fumble recovery, and a tipped pass. He's tied for third on the team with 25 pressures, despite not being a starter.
Zach Allen leads the pass rush 😤 JAXvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/awIGMbyXcq
The Broncos love Cooper, but given his off-field drama and cost, if the team was of a mind to move on in 2027, Robinson's emergence would likely be a big reason why. The 2025 fourth-round pick out of Alabama has been an absolute stud in Year 2.
This is a bit of a cheat because it's not an individual player, but the Broncos' offensive line was billed as the NFL's best unit entering the 2026 season. Alas, this O-line has been far from it.
Nix faced the most pressure of his career through the first six weeks of the season, and the Broncos still haven't been able to generate at reliable run game, Coleman's emergence notwithstanding. The presence of All-Pro tandem Garett Bolles and Quinn Meinerz hasn't been enough to elevate the unit, not with center Luke Wattenberg and right tackle Mike McGlinchey playing so poorly.
The Broncos have a lot of money tied up in Wattenberg and McGlinchey, which is why fans shouldn't expect any personnel changes over the bye, even though Payton threatened it earlier this week . Left guard Ben Powers has gotten a lot of grief from fans this season, but he hasn't been the biggest culprit in the O-line's blocking inefficiencies, and has taken on more responsibility to cover for Wattenberg's foibles.
The continuity Denver has maintained up front is rare, fielding the same starting five for the third straight year, but the O-line, as a unit, hasn't been able to capitalize on it. There's time yet, though. Let's hope the Broncos are able to get to the bottom of the problem during the bye.

title: Broncos' Season Has Exposed a New 2027 First-Round Draft Priority
full_text:
At 7-2, the Denver Broncos are enjoying a well-earned bye week .
The Broncos remain one of the NFL's deepest and most talented rosters, but halfway through the 2026 season, some of the holes have become obvious. This team could use reinforcements and upgrades at tight end, inside linebacker, safety, and running back.
But offensive tackle may be rising to the top of the Broncos' list of needs, especially as it pertains to the first round of next year's draft. NFL Draft On SI 's Justin Melo seems to be evolving on this subject, going from projecting Oregon tight end Jamari Johnson in several of his most recent mock drafts to offensive tackle.
Projecting the Broncos to be picking at No. 29 overall (as it currently stands), Melo mocked Texas offensive tackle Trevor Goosby to the Mile High City.
"Texas left tackle Trevor Goosby now faces a complicated pre-draft process after suffering a season-ending knee injury. The Denver Broncos can afford to be patient, but need an eventual successor for the aging Garret Bolles. With Mike McGlinchey underperforming, the Broncos could address both offensive tackle spots," Melo wrote .
Listed at 6-foot-7 and 325 pounds, Goosby would step in as the biggest and likely the longest tackle on the Broncos' roster. For his size, he's extremely athletic, and balances that with a fair amount of power.
Goosby was named first-team All-SEC last year, which is no mean feat in that Conference, and has been Arch Manning's blind-side protector at Texas. Goosby has played in some big games and has excelled against quality opponents.
As a red-shirt senior, this will be Goosby's last collegiate season. It will be interesting to see how he tests at the 2027 NFL Combine. He could go earlier in the draft than No. 29 overall.
Both Bolles and McGlinchey are well on the wrong side of 30. At 34, Bolles is still performing at an All-Pro level , and while he's getting up there, he's actually young for his age, given his late foray into football after serving a two-year LDS mission.
Meanwhile, McGlinchey will turn 32 in January. He's never been an All-Pro-caliber talent, but up until this season, he's been a competent and reliable right tackle.
That has changed rather dramatically this season. McGlinchey's run blocking has devolved and as a pass protector, he's become a liability for Bo Nix.
Bolles isn't showing any signs of slowing down. With McGlinchey, though, alarm bells have to be ringing at Broncos HQ — so much so that it wouldn't completely shock me if the coaches were to make a change at right tackle during the bye and give Alex Palczewski a crack at the job.
It's unlikely to happen, given McGlinchey's $23.775 million cap hit — the highest on the team this year — and his leadership. Teams often fall prey to the sunk-cost fallacy, where the highest-paid players simply have to play, and the Broncos aren't immune to this flawed line of thinking.
He may not be a team captain, but McGlinchey is very much a leader that guys look to on offense, and that will always factor into any conversation about potentially benching him.
The Broncos started thinking ahead by drafting Kage Casey in the fourth round earlier this year, anticipating the coming departure of left guard Ben Powers. Denver's center situation isn't great, with Luke Wattenberg playing poorly on a second contract and backup Alex Forsyth hitting free agency after this year, so it wouldn't be a shock to see the team prioritize interior offensive line in the draft.
If you're going to invest a first-round pick, though, it should be offensive tackle; a position that Denver hasn't drafted since Bolles in 2017. Casey was a career tackle at Boise State, but the Broncos drafted him to play guard.
As we inch closer to draft season, fans will likely be pounding the table for a tight end, running back, or linebacker, but don't be surprised if the Broncos finally go back to the offensive tackle well in Round 1.
