title: Five Bold Predictions for Second Half of Packers’ Season and Playoffs
full_text:
The Green Bay Packers are halfway through the season, and will take on the Minnesota Vikings as a jumping-off point for how the rest of their season could play out.
With a win, the Packers would be tied with Minnesota in the loss column and avoid losing what could be a crucial tiebreaker in the NFC North playoff picture.
A loss would keep the Packers in the basement of the NFC North, and will essentially put them three games behind Minnesota by virtue of the tiebreaker the Vikings would own over them.
The month of December is no cakewalk, either, with a home date against Josh Allen’s Buffalo Bills, and a Christmas Day showdown against the Chicago Bears. The Packers will earn whatever comes to them for the rest of the season.
With nine weeks down and nine weeks to go and the calendar having turned to November, here are some bold predictions from our crystal ball for the rest of the Packers’ season.
The Packers are only able to move the ball on offense one way. That’s Jordan Love carrying out an aerial assault on opposing defenses. Their run game is virtually nonexistent, and Green Bay’s top two receivers have done their part to help Love find his way to the top of the NFL in passing yards.
Can it continue? The answer is yes. The Packers are going to be playing in big games down the stretch, which will require Love to play well for them to win. Since our season forecast has the Packers winning six of their last eight games, the bet here is he will continue to play well.
As a result, Love will end up leading the league in passing yards, edging out Cincinnati’s Joe Burrow, who enters Week 10 with a slight advantage in yards per game.
In that scenario, Love would be an MVP finalist, but we think he loses out to Buffalo’s Josh Allen at least in some part due to Allen’s team finishing with a better record than Green Bay.
The Packers have not had two receivers top 1,000 yards in the same season since Jordy Nelson and Randall Cobb accomplished that in 2014. The 2014 offense was one of the best the Packers fielded under the stewardship of Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarhty. They rode that group all the way to the NFC Championship Game.
This year, Matthew Golden and Christian Watson have both been top-tier targets for Jordan Love. They’re both pushing 1,000 yards already, with Watson leading the way with 879.
Now, the question is whether they will set the NFL record for most yards by a duo . Detroit had Herman Moore and Brett Perriman reach the record of 3,174 yards in 1995, when it was a 16=game season.
Throw in an asterisk if you’d like, but Watson and Golden are on pace for 3,139 receiving yards. Can they find an extra 36 yards somewhere? The bet here is yes. The Packers are going to have to continue throwing the ball to sustain any semblance of success on offense.
“Those guys have been making play after play,” Love said this week. “MG, when he first got here last year, was making a lot of plays. Obviously, the situation we had, we had a lot of depth in the room (and) he wasn’t getting a lot of those opps. Christian’s been making play after play since he’s been here. He’s been getting better and better each year. It comes down to I know these guys are going to make the plays.
“It just is us seeing it all as one, being on the same page with how we’re seeing routes, how we’re seeing the coverages that teams want to play against us, and then me putting the ball in a great spot and them making those plays. I know we’re more than capable of doing it every play.”
As long as Watson and Golden are healthy for all 17 games, we’re betting they break the record held by the Lions’ crew.
The Packers are just one game out of first place in the NFC North in the loss column, and they’ve already knocked off the Chicago Bears with a 31-7 drubbing at Lambeau Field.
The Bears did not have two massive pieces for that game. Jeffery Simmons was in Tennessee and Caleb Williams was nursing a hamstring injury.
Chicago has not lost a game that Williams has started and finished this season, and their defense has looked formidable in the two-game sample following Simmons’ addition to their defensive line.
The bet here is that both teams will have the same record going into a Christmas Day showdown at Soldier Field, which will have NFL executives licking their chops.
The Packers have lost the last two games at Soldier Field, including a disastrous ending in the postseason last year. This year, they’ll give their fanbase a big lump of coal on Christmas, as the Bears will knock off the Packers, giving them the inside track to winning the NFC North.
Much like last year, a loss against Chicago will prove to be the difference between winning the NFC North and having to go on the road in the postseason.
This time, things will be different. The Packers will enter the playoffs with the fifth seed of the NFC playoffs and knock off a Tampa Bay team that is only in the postseason by virtue of playing in the worst division in the conference.
A big day from Jordan Love and Christian Watson vs. the Buccaneers will send them on a short flight back to Chicago, where they will meet Williams and the Bears again.
This time, however, the Packers are the ones who emerge victorious, avenging their Christmas Day loss to Chicago. Jordan Love will have another big day against Chicago, with Matthew Golden setting up a game-winning field goal by rookie Trey Smack, which splits the middle of the uprights.
That win in the divisional round will put the Packers just one game away from the Super Bowl.
Matt LaFleur and Kyle Shanahan have met three times in the postseason as head coaches, and Shanahan’s teams won all three.
In the 2019 NFC Championship Game, Raheem Mostert ran around, over and through Green Bay’s defense en route to a 37-20 victory that was not as close as the final score would indicate.
Two years later, the Packers were the No. 1 seed with everything lined up for a Super Bowl run. Za’Darius Smith and Jaire Alexander returned from long-term injuries for this game against a San Francisco team that was in the postseason but not as good as that year’s Packers team, which felt destined to give Aaron Rodgers a second title.
It was not to be. Poor offense and disastrous special teams wasted an otherwise strong defensive effort, and Rodgers never played another postseason game for the Packers.
In 2023, Jordan Love had the upstart Packers in position to upset the No. 1-seeded 49ers in the divisional round but they fell just short due in part to a missed field goal.
This time, the Packers will travel back to San Francisco in search of their first trip to the Super Bowl since winning Super Bowl XLV to cap the 2010 season.
This place, however, is a house of horrors for Green Bay, and Brock Purdy will get the best of Green Bay’s defense late. A late touchdown pass to George Kittle in the middle of the end zone with minimal time left will break the Packers’ hearts and send the 49ers to the Super Bowl.

title: Saturday’s Packers Roster Moves: Two Key Additions, Two Critical Non-Moves
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers activated two key cogs to their offense on Saturday, making them available for Sunday’s huge NFC North game against the Minnesota Vikings.
Here’s a look at the Packers’ roster moves, starting with the two roster moves that were not made that send a strong and important signal.
After missing the first two days of the practice week due to a back injury, starting edge and top pass rusher Lukas Van Ness returned to practice on Friday and was listed as questionable.
Backs can be tricky, but Van Ness must be fine. Otherwise, the Packers would have added Arron Mosby or Nyjalik Kelly to an edge group with a limited depth chart of Van Ness, Barryn Sorrell, Brenton Cox and Dani Dennis-Sutton.
“I’m doing good, thank you,” said Van Ness, who leads the team in sacks . “It felt good to get back on the grass today.”
Mosby has been elevated three times; the next time the Packers want him to play in a game, they’ll have to sign him to the 53-man roster. Kelly, an undrafted rookie who had a strong training camp, still is awaiting his NFL debut.
“I think both those guys have done an outstanding job,” coach Matt LaFleur said on Friday. “Obviously, Mosby has played more ball than Nyjalik. But in the event we had to pivot and go that route, we’d feel comfortable with that.
Among the players who were questionable on Friday’s injury report were safeties Javon Bullard and Xavier McKinney. The Packers have only four safeties on the roster – starter Evan Williams and backup Kitan Oladapo being the others – but they did not pull up John Saunders from the practice squad.
Even though he missed the first two practices of the week, Bullard declared he would play .
“We been able to battle adversity,” Bullard said. “That was really our focal point going through offseason, man. Finishing and just battling, withstanding adversity, because you don’t know when adversity is going to hit. It’s going to hit at some point for everybody in this league – every team in this league, every player in this league.
“So, you got to withstand those storms and really just fight battles. Chin up and chest out. And I think this team has done that. We’ve weathered a lot of storms. We’ve weathered a lot of misfortunes with things like that. I think this team is one of the best, if not the best in the league, and we just got to continue to put that on tape.
Just in time to face the blitz-happy Vikings, the Packers regained the services of Chris Brooks, their top pass-protecting back. He just competed his second week of practice.
“Oh, yeah,” coach Matt LaFleur said of the perfect timing for Brooks’ return. “You’ve got to do a great job in all phases in terms of in the run game and in the pass game versus this unit.”
Brooks carried the ball seven times for 29 yards, a 4.1-yard average with a long run of 14, during the Week 1 game against the Vikings. He had a 27-yard run in Week 4 against the Buccaneers but sustained an ankle injury in that game. He missed the last five games and just completed his second week of practice.
There is an interesting dynamic in Green Bay’s backfield for this game. One, Josh Jacobs is out following last year’s broken finger. Two, Kaleb Johnson had a breakout game in Jacobs’ absence last week. His 68 rushing yards was the most by any Packers player this year and beat their season average. Three, given the Vikings’ propensity for blitzing on any down and any situation, Brooks would seem to be a necessity to have on the field as often as possible.
“I think he ripped off a couple nice runs in that game the first time we played him,” LaFleur said of Brooks. “And I think the running game, especially the later you go in the season, the more important it is. As the weather turns, especially at home, you better be able to run the football.”
Skyy Moore, who leads the team with a 16.0-yard average on punt returns and a 27.5-yard average on kickoff returns, will make his return after missing the last four games with an ankle injury. He returned to practice this week.
Moore had a 63-yard punt return against the Jets in Week 2. That’s as many yards as his replacements, Coleman Owen and Matthew Golden, combined the last seven games.
“Yeah, yeah, for sure,” he said when asked if it was disappointing to be sidelined after emerging as a threat on offense as well as special teams. “Just being away from the guys, when they go to practice and I'm just on the sideline and everything, I'm just happy to be back around and moving around out there.”
Moore’s ability to provide a first down’s worth of field position as a returner and perhaps contribute in the slot as a runner or receiver should make him an immediate asset.
“It would be huge” to get him back, quarterback Jordan Love said this week. “We’ve definitely been down a couple guys and I think guys have stepped up, but Skyy, just to have him in the receiver room, but also special teams – he’s been such a great returner for us – it’ll definitely be huge to get him back and I’m grateful that we’re able to get him back this week. I’m excited to have him out there.”
The additions of Moore and Brooks meant the Packers needed to create two roster spots.
Not surprisingly, one of them was releasing receiver/returner Coleman Owen, who had been promoted from the practice squad to take Moore’s role on special teams.
In four games, Owen averaged 9.0 yards on four punt returns, with a long of 16 in his debut against Dallas. He fielded all 10 punts cleanly. Owen returned kickoffs in one game, the Thursday night matchup against Carolina. He fumbled his first opportunity and finished the night with a 26.3-yard average on four returns.
“There weren’t as many opportunities just based on the flow of the games we've been playing,” Moore said. “But I think he stepped in and did a great job. You know, came in, caught all the punts confidently and he followed his training. I felt like he did a great job.”
Tight end Josh Whyle suffered a concussion in the Carolina games and has not practiced the last two weeks. The Packers added a tight end, Kenny Fletcher Jr., to the practice squad this week, which seemed like a signal that Whyle might have a prolonged absence.
Without Josh Whyle, the Packers for a second consecutive week elevated Drake Dabney from the practice squad. He played six snaps on special teams against New England.
The #Vikings have elevated TE Devin Culp and WR Jeshaun Jones to the active roster for tomorrow's game. Culp has changed jersey numbers from 48 to 83. pic.twitter.com/OU2Al6Oh0J
The Vikings elevated tight end Devin Culp to help offset the injury that will sideline T.J. Hockenson. Interestingly, with starter Jordan Addison questionable and Jauan Jennings out, they also elevated a receiver.

title: Predicting Packers-Vikings Winner, Plus Final Record, Playoffs and More
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers will renew their border war against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday at Lambeau Field. It’s a critical game for both teams. The Packers remain in last place in the NFC North, even while winning five of their last six games. The Vikings have lost two consecutive games following a 6-0 start.
Who will win the game? And, with this being the halfway point of the season, who will lead the team in rushing, receiving and sacks? And, ultimately, what will be the team’s final record and playoff fate?
Here are our Packers-Vikings picks and midseason predictions.
The Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins this week. It’s a huge move for the Vikings, who somehow are 6-2 despite their quarterbacks’ inability to get the ball to Justin Jefferson.
Cousins has faced the Packers 10 times while with the Vikings. He topped a 110 passer rating in seven of those games. OK, but what about this season? With the Raiders, Cousins ranked fifth in passing yards, second in touchdown passes and 11th in passer rating. Plain and simple, he remains a quality starting quarterback.
Maybe I’m guilty of overvaluing Cousins. Maybe I’m undervaluing Jordan Love’s ability to consistently make plays against a Vikings defense that has won every matchup this season.
Ultimately, I think Cousins will make one more big play, Love will be forced into one more big mistake and the special teams will get in the way.
Score: Vikings 20, Packers 17
Yes, Kirk Cousins is back, but Green Bay's defense is for real until proven otherwise. The Packers had some answers for Brian Flores' group in Week 1 until Jordan Love was snowed under by Minnesota's pressure.
This time, Lambeau Field will be the X-factor as the offensive line will be able to hear Love manipulate the line of scrimmage, which will help him make one more play than Cousins, as the Packers score a big win heading into their bye week.
Score: Packers 21, Vikings 17.
Bill: 11-6 (Losses at home to the Vikings and Bills and at the Bears).
Jacob: 12-5 (Losses at home against Buffalo and at Chicago).
Bill: Last (with the same record as the Vikings but by losing the tiebreaker).
Jacob: Second (Chicago wins the NFC North thanks to a win on Christmas Day at Soldier Field).
Bill: Lukas Van Ness. I came up with this question in light of Micah Parsons’ presumptive return for the game against the Rams. Tucker Kraft has had a quiet season following last year’s torn ACL. It’s just part of coming off a major injury. So, while I thought about going with Parsons here, Van Ness will maintain the team lead and finish with eight sacks.
Jacob: Lukas Van Ness. Van Ness has 4.5 sacks, which leads the team. His job should get a little easier with Micah Parsons' return to the lineup as he'll see less double teams. Parsons is a good bet here, as well, but has noted it may take him a while to look like himself again. The goal for the Packers is going to be to have him at his best in the postseason.
Bill: Kaleb Johson leads the team with 172 rushing yards, just ahead of MarShawn Lloyd (149) and about double Josh Jacobs (80). Jacobs might only miss two games with his broken finger, meaning he’ll have five or six games to surge to the front.
Jacob: Kaleb Johnson leads the team in rushing, which is incredible considering how his season has gone to date. The guess here is that he's out of Matt LaFleur's doghouse and going to be a more focal point of Green Bay's offense in Josh Jacobs' absence. That will continue even when Jacobs returns to the lineup.
Bill: Christian Watson has 879 receiving yards, putting him on pace to blow past 1,650 yards. Matthew Golden has 783 receiving yards, putting him on pace to push for 1,500 yards.
I’ll take Golden to surge to the lead, though. He has five consecutive games of six-plus catches and four consecutive games with 10-plus targets. The sheer volume of passes going to Golden will push him past the explosive play off Watson, especially if last week’s game signals that his drops are behind him.
The big question: Can they set the combined yardage record?
Jacob: Christian Watson. This might be one of the most intriguing storylines down the stretch. Watson and Golden are neck and neck in this category now, with Watson holding a slight advantage.
Watson is used to playing this late in the season and has made some big plays in big games. Golden has, as well, so this will be really close as the season comes to a close, but give us Watson to go over 1,200 yards for the season and earn the team's receiving title.
Bill: Entering Sunday, Cincinnati’s Joe Burrow leads the NFL with 298.3 passing yards per game. Jordan Love is hot on his heels with a 290.9-yard average. That’s less than a first down per game. Playing five consecutive cold-weather games down the stretch isn’t going to help Love in his pursuit.
Jacob: Yes, the only way the Packers can move the ball is on the right arm of Jordan Love. There's little reason to believe that's going to change, even when the elements start turning colder. Add in some games that could be potential shootouts, like a home game against Buffalo or a road game against Chicago. That could cause Love to pile up some big numbers.
Bill: With the entire NFC North earning their way into the playoff field, the last-place Packers will squeak into the postseason as the No. 7 seed. It’s obviously a familiar place for the Packers.
And it’s a death sentence. The No. 7 seed has to play at the No. 2 seed. If the No. 7 pulls off an upset, it will have to play at the No. 1 seed. So, let’s roll with the Packers upsetting the rival Bears in the wild-card round but meeting their maker against the playoff-rival 49ers in the divisional round.
Jacob: The Packers will earn the NFC's fifth seed and have a date with the NFC South-winning Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the first round of the playoffs. A big game from Jordan Love and Christian Watson, coupled with a suffocating defensive performance in which Micah Parsons will collect three sacks and a forced fumble against Baker Mayfield, will give the team its first playoff win since 2023.
They will follow that by avenging last year's loss in the playoffs to the Chicago Bears by knocking them out at Soldier Field in the divisional round on a game-winning field goal from Trey Smack.
That sends them to San Francisco, a house of horrors, for the NFC Championship Game, where the season ultimately will end with Brock Purdy leading a late touchdown drive to send the Packers into an offseason short of the Super Bowl.

title: It Took Nine Games for Christian Watson to Do What Hadn’t Been Done in Four Seasons
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – It’s true that the Green Bay Packers haven’t had a 1,000-yard receiver since Davante Adams in 2021. It’s more than that, though.
The Packers haven’t had a receiver reach even 860 yards since 2021.
Well, Christian Watson has put that sentence in the past tense.
Through just nine games and headed into Sunday’s rivalry showdown against the Minnesota Vikings, Watson has 879 receiving yards. That ranks third in the NFL. He’s on a pace to not just break the team’s 1,000-yard drought but to blow past it like a rocket blows past the speed of sound.
Watson is on pace to finish with 1,660 yards and 13 touchdowns. Only nine receivers in NFL history have hit 1,600 yards and 13 touchdowns in a season, though Seattle’s Jaxon Smith-Njigba is on pace to crush those numbers, as well.
It took Watson about half a season to obliterate his career-high 620 receiving yards from 2024 and match his career-high seven touchdowns catches from his rookie season in 2022.
The 1,000-yard marker has always been a notable milestone for running backs and receivers alike. Watson, however, is not impressed.
“Honestly, you’d have to ask me at the end of the season when I achieved that or surpassed that,” he said on Thursday a few days before Sunday’s showdown against the Vikings. “Right now, it’s not something I’m looking into too much.
“We’re only halfway through the season so just hitting 1,000 – for me, the way I’d look at it is getting 120 more yards for the rest of the season doesn’t really sound too exciting for me. It’d be something that I’ll look at it at the end of the season, but I’m excited about how much I’ve been able to be an impact for this team so far. Obviously, God willing, hopefully I’m able to continue to do that and celebrate the stats after the season.”
Watson is having a season worth celebrating.
Adams in 2021 set the franchise record with 1,553 receiving yards in 16 games, a 97.1-yard average. Watson is on pace to beat that number by more than 100 yards. In terms of receiving yards per game, Watson’s 97.7-yard average would rank fifth in Packers history; Don Hutson averaged 110.1 yards per game in 1942 and Billy Howton averaged 102.6 yards per game in 1952. During the Super Bowl era, only Adams’ 98.1 yards per game in 2020 would beat Watson’s production.
Watson, of course, has made a killing in the vertical passing game. On passes thrown 20-plus yards downfield, Watson has caught 10-of-19 targets for 382 yards and three touchdowns. He’s third in catches, first in yards, tied for first in touchdowns and 10th in catch percentage (out of 45 receivers targeted at least eight times).
After the New England game, coach Matt LaFleur said the Packers were turning low-percentage throws into high-percentage plays.
With his size, speed and skill, Watson has changed the math.
“I think theoretically it’s a low-percentage throw when you look at it across everybody doing it,” Watson said. “I think if you really dive into individually, it’s going to be a higher percentage for certain individuals and a lower percentage for other individuals.
“I think it’s just something that we got a lot of reps at. Obviously, something that we’ve built a lot of trust in that area so, at the end of the day, that’s what it comes down to: Obviously, 10 [Jordan Love] just trusting us to go make a play. I think we’ve got a lot of banked reps in that area. That’s obviously been a big part of our explosiveness in our offense, a big part of our offense in general. We’ve done it a lot so, obviously, we rely on each other in those moments when we need those plays.”
Incredibly, Watson is 5-of-5 in contested-catch situations on the deep passes, so it’s not as if it’s been a bunch of wide-open connections.
Watson rather sheepishly admitted to being impressed by some of his catches, whether it was the bomb for his second touchdown against Chicago or last week’s one-hander on a crossing route.
“It’s definitely times where, obviously, made a big play,” Watson said. “Obviously, I like to say that I expect myself to make those plays all the time but it’s definitely times where I look back and a little proud of myself for making that kind of play or that level of play. Probably the answer that you don’t want is I expect myself to make those plays. That’s usually my first thought is really just excitement overall.”
The Packers will face a big challenge against the Vikings on Sunday. Minnesota in first in the league in touchdown passes allowed and opponent passer rating and second in passing yards allowed per attempt.
The Vikings have allowed only one 100-yard receiving game all season. That was Watson’s 147 yards in Week 1.
Their blitz, blitz, blitz-some-more scheme has made life hell on quarterbacks. However, the Vikings’ all-blitz defense also leaves voids in the secondary if everyone can take care of business. That’s easier said than done, obviously, considering the Vikings are No. 1 in points allowed, but the Packers made a bunch of big plays in the Week 1 loss.
“Honestly, it gives us a lot more opportunities, to be honest – obviously, as long as we take care of things up front,” Watson said. “We definitely have to be more on top of things, too, just being able to recognize that stuff with adjustments to our routes and stuff like that, too. If we handle it the right way, it’ll be opps for us, for sure.”
If the Packers handle it the right way, Watson might be walking off the field on Sunday with his first 1,000-yard season and the team might be celebrating its seventh win.

title: Packers-Vikings Final Injury Report: Seven Starters Out or Questionable
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers listed 12 players as out, doubtful or questionable, including seven starters, for Sunday’s game against the Minnesota Vikings.
Four players are out: running back Josh Jacobs (finger), edge Micah Parsons (knee/illness), center Sean Rhyan (ankle) and tight end Josh Whyle (concussion). Jacobs, Rhyan and Whyle didn’t practice this week; Parsons practiced all week but the team wants to give him one more week to get ready.
“He looks great but he just doesn’t have a ton of reps under his belt,” coach Matt LaFleur said before Friday’s practice. “So, we want to try to continue to build him up.”
Linebacker LB Zaire Franklin (shin), who didn’t practice all week, is doubtful and almost certainly will miss a fourth consecutive game.
Jacobs, Parsons, Rhyan and Franklin are starters. Four more starters are questionable: safety Javon Bullard (ankle/knee), safety Xavier McKinney (foot) and edge Lukas Van Ness (back).
McKinney (foot) was added to the injury report on Friday. Right guard Kevin Zeitler (ankle and triceps) practiced on Wednesday and Thursday but did not practice on Friday. Zeitler’s status could impact the team’s plan at guard; left guard Aaron Banks (knee/hip) is off the injury report.
McKinney is tied for the NFL lead with five interceptions.
"This is a must win for us... Being last in the division, losing to them the first time, understanding how competitive this division is?" - Xavier McKinney #packers #vikings pic.twitter.com/uX4TCDNS1k
Van Ness and Bullard returned to practice after missing the first two days of the week. Bullard said he’d play after Thursday’s practice and Van Ness essentially said the same thing on Friday.
“I’m doing good, thank you,” Van Ness said. “It felt good to get back on the grass today.”
Van Ness leads the team with 4.5 sacks. Of the 70 edge defenders with at least 140 pass-rushing snaps, Van Ness ranks 13th in pass-rush win rate, according to Pro Football Focus.
“It’s a weekly challenge, always finding something to improve on,” Van Ness said. “Coach LaFleur always says it’s 1 percent. You’re either getting worse or you’re getting better. No matter who you’re talking about, anyone can find something to improve on.
“We’ve come back week after week, evaluated the tape and continue to keep our nose down and our head down and keep working. If we see that, you talk about December and January football, that’s when you see these teams really come together and then compete for a Super Bowl.”
Running back Chris Brooks (ankle) and receiver/returner Skyy Moore (ankle), who have been designated to return, were limited participation all week and are questionable. To play on Sunday, they will have to be added to the roster on Saturday.
After Friday’s practice, Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell told reporters that Kirk Cousins will start at quarterback.
“The way he threw the football this week, it’s a really cool thing to see,” O’Connell said.
However, tight end T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest) and linebacker Blake Cashman (concussion) are out. Another starter, defensive end Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins (ankle), is out, as well.
Cashman is a stud. With 76 tackles, he is one of 18 players with 70-plus tackles this season. He leads that group with 4.5 sacks, eight tackles for losses and 10 quarterback hits and is tied with Packers safety Evan Williams for first with seven passes defensed.
Hockenson leads the team with 35 catches; the next Vikings tight end, Gavin Bartholomew, has only seven.
Receiver Jordan Addison (thumb) was added to the injury report and is questionable. He was limited participation at Friday’s practice.
For the second consecutive year, Lukas Van Ness is Green Bay’s nominee for the NFL’s Salute to Service Award. In its 16th year, the award honors a league member who demonstrates “an exceptional commitment” to honoring and supporting the military.
Van Ness’ grandfather served 27 years and earned the rank of lieutenant colonel in the U.S. Army.
“It’s really an honor to be able to recognize all the amazing men and women that support our country and allow us to do what we do out here on the football field,” he said. “Being able to do this for my second year is really special, especially with my grandfather, who served.”
He added: “We have a platform of being able to bring recognition to those service members and those who have served and then, ultimately, those who have paid the ultimate sacrifice for not only us but our country, it’s really, really special. It’s a really cool initiative that the NFL does.”
The Packers have won five of their last six games, due in large part to the play of the defense, which has done more than survive without Micah Parsons.
“We just have a really competitive group of guys,” he said of the edge group of Van Ness, Barryn Sorrell, Brenton Cox and Dani Dennis-Sutton. “Whether it’s myself or Barryn or B-Cox or Dani, there’s no fall-off in talent.
“We’re all super-capable. We can all go out there and play at a high level. It’s been really fun to be able to rotate out there with different guys, work on some different packages and have the flexibility to throw us wherever on the field on any given circumstance. I’m really proud of how we’re all playing. It’s been cool to see us all step up.”

title: Packers Friday Update From Practice: Two Starters Return; New Questions Emerge
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – On Thursday, Green Bay Packers standout slot Javon Bullard proclaimed he “definitely” would play on Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings.
“I ain’t missing no game. I ain’t missing no game, man,” Bullard said after missing a second consecutive day of practice. “I care about this team. I care about my brothers, man.”
Sure enough, Bullard was suited up and went out for the start of Friday’s practice, the last one of the week before Sunday’s rivalry rematch. Also returning to practice after missing the first two days was starting edge Lukas Van Ness.
However, new questions emerged.
On Fridays, reporters only get to watch the players go through their lengthy pre-practice routine. Two players who had practiced on Wednesday and Thursday did not participate.
One was star safety Xavier McKinney. The NFL co-leader with five interceptions stretched in the back a bit and talked with a trainer but did not go through warmups. He was not on the injury report to start the week.
If any player can play while missing one day of practice, it’s the two-time All-Pro.
“Honestly, I think it’s just the way I prepare,” he said after picking off two passes against the Patriots. “Every day, I try to give these guys in this locker room my best self, the best version of me, whether that’s in the meeting room, the practice field and then, obviously, when we get out here on gameday, I go out there and you see the product I put out there.
“But that’s throughout the week something that I’ve worked on. I think it’s me getting into a feel of things and just me playing free, being an instinctual player that I am and going out there and making plays.”
The other was right guard Kevin Zeitler, who was in the conversation to start this week after making his Packers debut last week against New England. He had been limited participation this week with an ankle injury. Zeitler did have a practice jersey on, so it’s possible he went out later.
If Zeitler is too banged up to go, the Packers could revert back to Aaron Banks at left guard and Laken Tomlinson at right guard – the duo the past two weeks. Mekhi Becton would be an option, too, and Travis Glover returned to practice this week after missing the last two games with a knee injury.
Four more players didn’t practice on Friday, missed the full practice week and almost certainly won’t play on Sunday.
Linebacker Zaire Franklin will miss a fourth consecutive game with a shin injury. Fortunately for the Packers, Isaiah McDuffie and Ty’Ron Hopper practiced all week after dropping out of the New England game.
Center Sean Rhyan will miss a third consecutive game with an injured ankle, with John Williams getting thrown into the fire against the blitzing Vikings.
Running back Josh Jacobs was scheduled to have surgery on Friday to repair his broken right ring finger.
Tight end Josh Whyle will miss a second consecutive game with the concussion he sustained during the Thursday night game against Carolina.
Star edge Micah Parsons was back on the practice field after going through team drills during Thursday’s padded practice. He looks great, LaFleur said, but said the team wants to “continue to build him up” before returning him to game action.
So, no, he will not play against the Vikings.
The status of Lukas Van Ness and Javon Bullard, obviously, will be critical given the stakes of the game.
Bullard, a second-round pick in 2024, is having his best season. He had a total of four passes defensed during his first two seasons but has seven this season.
“I know he’s going to do everything in his power to be there,” LaFleur said of Bullard before Friday’s practice. “We’ll see how he’s feeling today. It’s always concerning when a guy doesn’t practice twice but if I know Bull the way I think I do, he’s going to do everything in his power to be out there.”
Van Ness leads the team with 4.5 sacks. He ranks 13th among edge defenders in pass-rush win rate, according to Pro Football Focus, just behind the Vikings’ Dallas Turner and the Raiders’ Maxx Crosby
Also, running back Chris Brooks and receiver/returner Skyy Moore, who have been designated for return from injured reserve, completed 3-for-3 practice weeks and “definitely” have a chance to play on Sunday.
“We’ll get through today and then see where they’re at and make a decision,” LaFleur said.
The final injury reports of the week will be released after Friday’s practices. For now, here are the reports from Thursday.

title: Packers-Vikings: A Big Rivalry Rematch With Big Ticket Price
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – It doesn’t get much bigger than Sunday’s Packers-Vikings game at Lambeau Field.
It’s a rivalry game and a border war between a pair of six-win teams with an eye on reaching the playoffs – and much more.
According to TickPick, the average ticket price is $559. It’s the most expensive Packers-Vikings game on record and also the second-most expensive Packers home game on record, behind only the Oct. 11 game against the Bears, which had an average ticket price of $755. The previous high was $494 against the Cowboys in 2022.
According to TickPick, the average ticket price for this Packers-Vikings matchup is 90 percent more than it was for the Week 1 game in Minneapolis.
The get-in price for this game is sitting at $313, up a little over Thursday.
Based on TickPick data, 24 percent of ticket buyers have a Wisconsin billing code and 19 percent have a Minnesota billing code, with the rest of the purchasers coming from outside the neighboring states. TickPick usually sees Wisconsin accounting for about 36 percent of sales for Packers home games.
That could be noteworthy, because the Packers are counting on Lambeau Field being a big advantage in the rematch.
“It’s a division game. It’s like the playoffs already,” cornerback Keisean Nixon said. “I think everybody’s got six wins in our division, right? It’s going to come down to our division, so every time we play somebody in our division, it’s a playoff game. When they come to Lambeau, that’s just like homefield advantage. You’ve got to take advantage of it.”
The Packers lost to the Vikings 39-22 in Week 1. Green Bay led 22-17 after three quarters but got destroyed 22-zip in the fourth.
The Vikings started 6-0 but have lost two in a row. To save their season, they acquired quarterback Kirk Cousins at the trade deadline.
“It’s a different system, but at the same time, Kirk, he’s a savvy vet,” Javon Bullard said. “A quarterback that’s played a lot of ball in this league, that’s  seen a lot in this league, and we got our hands tied with him. But, at the same time, he’s coming into Lambeau and playing us. This is a nasty defense also.
“Of course there’s going to be certain tendencies that he has. Certain things just don’t go away from last week because he was just with a (different) team; they just not going to go away. But, at the same time, he is a quarterback that’s capable of making those tough throws. He’s a quarterback that has a great mind, sees things before the play. So, you better be dialed into that.”
The bad news for the Packers is they lost the first matchup so are in last place in the NFC North, even with their 6-3 record. The good news is the teams have split the series five of the last six years. Green Bay has won three of the last five at Lambeau, including 23-6 last year.
The Packers are 3-0 in noon games this year.
According to the Opta Supercomputer , the Packers have a 60.8 percent win probability. They are 3-point favorites at FanDuel Sportsbook . The over/under is 42.5, with both teams’ defenses posting top-10 EPAs .
The key to the game will be handling the attacking Vikings defense, which will blitz Jordan Love off the bus.
“Absolutely, and he does a great job of that, just playing each play as its own play,” coach Matt LaFleur said on Friday of Love playing with patience. “That’s the mindset. We’ve gotten in trouble, and I think most teams do, when you try to force it.
“You’ve got to allow it to come to you and try to take what they’ve giving you. If that’s a checkdown, take the checkdown. If it’s a deep shot, then certainly we want to capitalize on those opportunities. This defense doesn’t give you a ton down the field.”

title: Vikings Thrive in ‘World of Chaos.’ Here’s How Packers Can Survive Blitzing.
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Brian Flores has tipped decades of defensive philosophies upside down.
Flores’ blitz-happy defense will take center stage when Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers host the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday.
Asked if there was any rhyme or reason to how Flores will attack, Packers coach Matt LaFleur offered a simple response.
“Yeah, it’s called pressure,” he said.
That’s for sure. It’s pressure at an unprecedented and unthinkable level.
The Vikings hired Flores to run their defense in 2023. In 2022, they blitzed 24 percent of the time, according to Stats Perform’s Opta Data . That means they did not blitz 76 percent of the time. This season, their blitz rate is 75.3 percent.
Incredibly, since 2000, the second-highest blitz rate during that span was the 2009 Jets at 56.4 percent. So, the Vikings’ blitz percentage is almost 20 points higher.
“We see those conversations about the blitz rates, and everybody thinks it’s wild – and rightfully so. It is wild,” safety Harrison Smith said on former All-Pro cornerback Richard Sherman’s podcast. “We talk about it sometimes inside. Who decides that four was the baseline amount you’re supposed to send?”
Not long ago, defensive coordinators saved their blitz packages for third downs or other need-to-pass situations. Flores will blitz anytime, anywhere, any situation.
According to Sumer Sports, Flores blitzes a staggering 80 percent of the time on first-and-10 passing plays. On third-and-long (third-and-7-plus) it’s “only” 70.6 percent.
“They’re going to pressure the crap out of us, and we’re going to have to either take advantage of it or prepare to play against it,” tight end Tucker Kraft said.
How can the Packers take advantage?
Minnesota’s defense is one of the best in the era. Maybe one of the best of all-time. It ranks first in points allowed, first in total defense, first in sack percentage and first in the red zone.
With the Vikings’ defense taking the offensive, opponents are averaging 4.5 yards per play on first down. That’s the second-best mark in the league.
Teams have a fighting chance on the ground, with the Vikings ranked 14th with 4.04 yards allowed per first-down carry. The Packers, of course, have struggled to run the ball for most of the season.
There’s a lot more risk-reward through the air, where the old-school mantra of three things can happen when you throw the ball and only one is good. The Vikings are first with 5.1 yards allowed per first-down passing play. They have a league-high 11 sacks.
“Just look at what they’ve done consistently week in and week out,” LaFleur said. “It’s a struggle for every offense to go out there and score points on them. Not even score points but move the ball consistently.
“I think they do a great job of getting people behind the sticks. There’s more third-and-longs than I feel like I’ve ever seen at this point of the year, in many cases, throughout the entire course of a year, and we’re halfway through. I think they do a great job of just applying pressure and you make mistakes. That’s why it’s so important for us to play a clean game.”
Yes, because it’s going to be hard enough to get 4 yards on first down as it is, let alone with false starts leading to 5-yard penalties or missed assignments setting up sacks.
First-down success is a big reason why the Vikings rank third on third down. The average third down against Minnesota requires 8.3 yards, tied for the longest in the league. The Vikings are allowing a league-low 4.2 yards on those plays with a league-high four interceptions.
Flores has such a diverse bag of tricks that even experienced quarterbacks have looked completely unprepared.
“You’re guessing a lot of the time out there,” quarterback Jordan Love said. “I think that’s why you’ve got to be great as a quarterback trusting your reads. I think your eyes are really critical against this defense. They’re very vision-based, kind of just melting and flowing with the quarterback, where they’re looking, and I think guys got to be great in their routes and recognizing what coverages they’re getting, what we’ve got, pressure, things like that.”
While Love destroyed the Patriots with a series of bombs last week, that can’t be the plan this week. That doesn’t mean dinking and dunking the ball down the field, but it does mean trying to take advantage of the voids in the secondary created by the extra rushers before those extra rushers clobber the quarterback.
Last week, Buffalo won at Minnesota 23-6. Bills quarterback Josh Allen was 15-of-16 on passes thrown within 10 yards of the line of scrimmage. The quick passes got them going in a game that was 3-3 until late in the first half.
“We’ve to be able to take advantage, get the ball out quick,” Love said. “There was a couple opps in that first game where we missed just being able to get the ball out to guys in space, and we just couldn’t convert on some of those. You’re guessing a lot of times and, when you know they’re coming, you’ve got to find ways to get the ball out because they’re bringing extra guys every time and you know that.
“So, we’ve got to have a great plan, and I think we do have that. It comes down to just seeing it, not panicking when you get those pressures and just getting the ball out quick.”
The second key is running the football. That, of course, is a dicey proposition for the Packers.
However, the last three games, the Vikings allowed 154 rushing yards against the Colts, 230 rushing yards against the Lions and 134 rushing yards against the Bills.
Last week’s game against Buffalo is noteworthy. The Vikings allowed only 3.0 yards per carry, but the Bills kept giving it to James Cook, who thundered away for 2, 3 and 4 yards at a crack. It was ugly football at times but it kept the Bills in manageable situations. He averaged 2.2 yards per carry in the first half but 4.0 yards in the second half.
It was a similar plan of attack with Emanuel Wilson in the home win over the Vikings last year.
“Eventually, you end up making it a game that they weren’t willing to play,” Bills coach Joe Brady told reporters in Buffalo. “That’s a good football team and that’s a great defense. …
“The runs that go for 2 yards, you hope as the game continues on that that 2-yard run can go to 7. You have to stick with it, and it’s really hard with Josh Allen. I’ve got Josh Allen, and you’re running the football. But we felt like that was the way to win this football game, be able to wear the team down and not make it a dropback fest.”
The Packers don’t have James Cook, obviously, though they finally had a bit of a breakthrough last week against the Patriots. Still, they entered Week 10 ranked 32nd in rushing yards per game and 31st in yards per carry. But do they do have Love, which maybe will give Kaleb Johnson and Chris Brooks room to grind out 3 and 4 yards a pop.
Third, the Packers must continue to live in shotgun. While the league is migrating a bit more toward under-center offense, that’s not the way to attack the Vikings. In shotgun, the quarterback has vision on the defense throughout the play. Under center, he has to turn his back for a moment.
When the opposing quarterback is under center, the Vikings blitz 87.5 percent of the time, according to Stats. The Vikings allow almost 1.0 yard less per passing attempt when quarterbacks are under center.
Flores’ plan of attack when facing the Packers has been to blitz even more than usual. In Week 1, Love was blitzed on an astounding 87.0 percent of his dropbacks. (Blitzing used to be about the element of surprise. It was the opposite in this game; Love was not blitzed on six dropbacks and didn’t complete a single pass in those situations.) At Lambeau Field last season, Love was blitzed 83.3 percent of the time, so the communication factor might not matter.
Love knows the Packers must make the Vikings pay. More blitzers, obviously, means fewer players in coverage.

title: Packers-Vikings Thursday Injury Report: Three Promising Updates for Green Bay
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Javon Bullard, the Green Bay Packers’ standout nickel defender, missed a second consecutive day of practice on Thursday. Does that put his status for Sunday’s showdown against the Minnesota Vikings in doubt?
“I ain’t missing no game. I ain’t missing no game, man,” Bullard said after practice. “I care about this team. I care about my brothers, man. So, I’m definitely going to play Sunday. For sure.”
After the team conducted a job-through practice on Wednesday, Bullard was one of five starters who did not practice on Thursday – the big workday of the week with the players in pads.
The Packers lost to the Vikings in Week 1 but enter Sunday’s game having won five of their last six games to improve to 6-3. The Vikings started 6-0 but have lost two consecutive games, though they acquired quarterback Kirk Cousins on Tuesday to perhaps right the ship.
“I think, honestly, that’s a good football team over there,” Bullard said. “They well coached and got a lot of good players. I think they’re out of rhythm right now, just truthfully from what we’re seeing on film, and I think we got to capitalize on it. I think we got to capitalize on them not being in-sync right now.
“I think offensively it’s all about rhythm. If you clicking and moving on the offensive side of the ball, it’s really all about rhythm. Because at one point of time, our offense wasn’t clicking and now look at them. So, it’s all about rhythm. We know they got the players to do so. I think it’s all about one play at a time, dialing into our job and doing what we need to do. We don’t take them lightly at all. That’s a good football team over there, despite their offensive struggles and recent happenings, but that’s a great football team there so we can’t take them lightly.”
Along with Bullard’s optimism, kicker Trey Smack progressed from limited participation to full participation due to an injured right calf. He was the only change on the injury report.
Finally, with the team working in pads, Micah Parsons was on the field. The plan was for him to be integrated into team drills this week. That happened, as Tucker Kraft happened to mention when talking about the growth of the offense.
Micah Parsons races Dani Dennis-Sutton. pic.twitter.com/Ibaf1Ss4dG
“I'd say our offensive line, for sure. We've come together as a unit a lot more – a lot more gel now with these reps and some of the guys we brought in,” Kraft said. “Going to get Sean (Rhyan) back soon, but John (Williams has) been playing great. I'd say our defense right now is on a roll, and we're awaiting the comeback of Micah.”
And then came the money line.
“It's been good out there pressing against Micah. Took on a bull rush from him today. He's trying to back me into Jordan (Love's) lap. … No comment. Maybe it was a stalemate. I'm going to say it's a stalemate. Yeah, he'll be making his return soon. He's looking great, but our defense is rolling, and we just hope that they can remain consistent.”
Along with Bullard, linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), running back Josh Jacobs (finger), center Sean Rhyan (ankle) and edge Lukas Van Ness (back) did not practice. Those five players aren’t just starters but important starters.
Franklin, who was inactive for the last three games, and Rhyan, who was inactive the last two games, would seem to be long shots to get ready for Sunday given their extended absences. Jacobs will have surgery on Friday, at which point the team will have a more definitive timeline.
The wild card is Van Ness; coach Matt LaFleur gave him a chance to practice on Thursday. That didn’t happen, obviously, but it signals that he is perhaps close.
Josh Jacobs won’t play, but the expectation is Chris Brooks will be activated from injured reserve.
That will be a key return. He’s carved out his niche in the NFL as a pass-protecting back, and that obviously will be vital against a Vikings defense that will blitz from the first game to the last.
However, Kaleb Johnson gave the Packers a breakthrough rushing performance against the Patriots, when MarShawn Lloyd was inactive with a knee injury. Lloyd isn’t on the injury report this week. Plus, Pierre Strong’s versatility has been an asset.
“I think the running game, especially the later you go in the season, the more important it is,” coach Matt LaFleur said. “As the weather turns, especially at home, you better be able to run the football.”
MarShawn Lloyd is not on the injury report. pic.twitter.com/dsfjl3UgvF
One of the Vikings’ best players, linebacker Blake Cashman, did not practice against due to a concussion.
Cashman was one of four Vikings who did not practice. Tight end T.J. Hockenson, defensive end Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins and safety Theo Jackson were the others. Versatile backup Kyle Van Noy did not practice, either.
Their injury report was unchanged from Wednesday.

title: Packers Thursday Update From Practice: Parsons, Smack, OL, Injured Starters
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – With the biggest game of the season looming on Sunday, the Green Bay Packers kicked off Vikings Week with a season-high 16 players on the injury report. Five of those players are starters.
Plus, rookie kicker Trey Smack was among a long list of players who were listed as limited participation on Wednesday. Smack is dealing with an injured right calf, but coach Matt LaFleur was not concerned.
“Not on what I saw yesterday,” LaFleur said before practice on Thursday. “He went out there and did a good job, so I think he should be full go today.”
The Packers did not have a true practice on Wednesday. If they would have, five starters would not have participated. At Thursday’s practice:
Edge Lukas Van Ness (back), who leads the team in sacks, worked in the rehab group but was not on the field for the start of practice.
“Potentially,” LaFleur said when asked if Van Ness would practice. “We’ll try to loosen him up and see where he’s at.”
S Javon Bullard (ankle/knee) also stretched but did not go out for practice. He played in every game last season and the first nine games of this season. He is fourth on the team with 43 tackles, tied for fifth with four tackles for losses and tied for second with seven passes defensed.
LB Zaire Franklin (shin) missed the last three games following an injury sustained at practice before the Detroit game. He did not practice and seems destined to miss another game.
With Edgerrin Cooper on injured reserve, Franklin inactive and Ty’Ron Hopper missing almost all the game with what was called a chest injury, the Packers essentially played last week with their No. 3 (Isaiah McDuffie) and No. 5 (Nick Niemann) linebackers. Hopper was limited participation on Wednesday – due to illness, not injury – and practiced again on Thursday.
C Sean Rhyan (ankle) went down during the opening series at Detroit, then missed the last two games. LaFleur called him “day-to-day” on Wednesday but he did not practice on Thursday. John Williams, presumably, will start again.
RB Josh Jacobs (finger) will have surgery on Friday, LaFleur said. That’s when the team will have a better handle on his timeline; the early indication is it was a “clean” break and he might be back after missing only two games.
Here’s Zeitler and Belton working a combo drill today. pic.twitter.com/zHrLGjgQbr
Jordan Morgan will start at left tackle, Anthony Belton will start at right tackle and John Williams probably will start at center.
What about the guard positions? Based on the start of practice, it might be Laken Tomlinson at left guard and Kevin Zeitler at right guard, though that comes with the enormous asterisk that whatever the team shows at practice might not be (and oftentimes has not been) the same as how the team lines up in the game.
“Interested to see how it plays out this week with Zeitler, Laken, all of that and just how that’ll shake out,” offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said on Tuesday. “That’s going to be big, but I like what I’ve seen from Zeitler in there. When he went in and played, he did a really nice job. So, it’ll be interesting to see how it plays out.”
Same as yesterday, Packers not practicing today: Bullard Jacobs Franklin Rhyan Whyle Van Ness Here is Micah Parsons. pic.twitter.com/xHScvBXWhK
Star edge rusher Micah Parsons went through drills with reporters present on Thursday. The goal was to have him take part in team drills this week; the Packers worked in full pads, so this would be a big day.
Parsons and running back Chris Brooks had their return-to-play window opened last week and receiver/returner Skyy Moore had his opened this week. They also were on the practice field.
“Well, he’s a big-time weapon, so if he’s able to go, that will definitely boost our returns, and then also we’ll see how we use him on offense,” LaFleur said of Moore.
The Vikings signed running back Damon Bankston to their practice squad. He served two stints on the Packers’ practice squad so might be willing to share a little intel.
On Wednesday, Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley explained why they reacquired quarterback Kirk Cousins at Tuesday’s trade deadline.
“He made sense for a lot of reasons,” he said. “There's familiarity with the offense, with the organization, with the coaching staff. His level of play; his production to this season; and everything just aligned. The quarterback position is one that can impact the entire team, and this roster, in all honesty, has earned the right to explore the potential to maximize where we can take this thing.”
The teams will release updated injury reports after they are done practicing on Thursday. Until then, here are the reports from Wednesday.

title: Texans vs. Browns Week 10: How to Watch, Stream and Game Preview
full_text:
The Houston Texans are fresh off a much-needed win from last weekend against the LA Chargers, and now head into Week 10 against the Cleveland Browns looking to claim their first back-to-back victory of the season.
But things might not be so simple for this Browns roster that's been one of the league's more pleasant surprises over the first half of the season. They're 5-4, right in the AFC Wild Card mix, and will certainly be hungry to get back on track after suffering back-to-back losses in their last two matchups.
Here's everything you need to know about the Texans' upcoming matchup against the Browns, including where to watch, betting lines, and more information :
All odds are provided by FanDuel Sportsbook .
Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change.
If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER.
How Texans adjust without Danielle Hunter, Azeez Al-Shaair: The Texans are dealing with no shortage of injury troubles in this game against the Browns, but the two most notable injuries they'll be dealing with are none other than their pair of Pro Bowlers on the defense, Danielle Hunter and Azeez Al-Shaair. As to who's expected to step into their respective roles, Jadeveon Clowney will be the next man up on the edge, and Jake Hansen will likely move into a starting role within Houston's linebacker unit. The Texans could still stay afloat without each of their defensive studs, but it won't be a simple task.
C.J. Stroud's first meeting against Deshaun Watson: Believe it or not, this will be the first time that we see a matchup between C.J. Stroud, the Texans' current starting quarterback, and Deshaun Watson, Houston's former signal-caller since Stroud entered the league back in 2023. The last time the Texans faced up against Watson, though, it wasn't a pretty sight. Houston fell to Cleveland and Watson back in 2022, 14-27, in a game where the Texans gave away four turnovers. In this game, they'll be hoping for a different result and thus claim their first-ever win over their former star quarterback.
Who wins the war of penalties?: This will be a contest between two teams that have struggled in the penalty category throughout the first half of this season. Houston and Cleveland are each one of 10 teams in the league who average eight or more penalties a game, with the Browns leading the league in total penalties with 82. Whichever team is able to get the edge in terms of limiting their mistakes will be due for a notable leg up on the other side. For the Texans, they'll be hoping to continue their positive trend of improvement from last week, as they only logged six penalties for 36 yards against the Chargers.

title: Texans Facing RB Shortage vs. Browns With David Montgomery Out
full_text:
The Houston Texans are right around the corner from their Week 10 matchup against the Cleveland Browns .
And it's shaping up to look like another shorthanded day for the Texans when it comes to their backfield.
According to an update from the Texans, running back David Montgomery has been ruled out for Sunday with a groin injury.
Houston Texans Week 10 Injury Report Updates: RB David Montgomery (groin) and CB Jaylin Smith (hamstring) will not travel with the team to Cleveland and have been ruled out for Week 10 at the Browns. T Braden Smith has been added to the Week 10 Injury Report with an illness… https://t.co/aqvEigvHGz
Montgomery has been out with the same groin injury since Week 5 against the Tennessee Titans, and was seemingly trending up for a chance to play this week.
He was a full participant in practice on Friday after being limited the day before, and was previously listed as questionable to play against Cleveland.
However, it turns out the Texans will be cautious surrounding their veteran running back's availability for this weekend, and hold him out of the action. And as a result, this Houston offense will be rolling into Week 10 with a pretty slim running back room, all things considered.
Without any reported practice squad elevations for this weekend, the Texans will be heading into Week 10 with just two running backs on the active roster: Woody Marks and Emari Demercado.
The Texans did have three running backs on the roster earlier this week, which did provide an extra sense of depth and security in the position. However, following their decision to sign wide receiver Nikko Remigio , the team also decided to cut ties with veteran Dare Ogunbowale.
Ogunbowale had been on the roster dating back to Week 4's game against the Dallas Cowboys in an effort to add depth within the backfield and some special teams prowess. However, as Montgomery was trending up and the running back room was looking healthier, the Texans decided to let him go earlier this week.
But Montgomery won't be ready to play this week, and will instead be targeting his return for Week 11 on Thursday night against the Indianapolis Colts––which means the Texans’ running back depth (or lack thereof) will be tested in Cleveland for this weekend.
Since Montgomery has been out of the lineup for the Texans, the offense has primarily relied on Woody Marks to handle the bulk of the work in the backfield throughout.
Dating back to Week 5, Marks is averaging 16.8 rushing attempts per game for 63.5 yards, paired with an average of two receptions for 16.0 yards.
Perhaps the Texans could sprinkle in a bit of Demercado this time around in order to take some of the weight and heavy workload off of Marks' shoulders with a quick turnaround for Thursday’s game. However, for the majority of carries, you can expect them to be in the hands of Marks.
And against a matchup like the Browns' rushing defense, there's a chance that Marks could expose some of their holes that have popped up frequently this season. Cleveland currently ranks 27th in the NFL for rushing yards allowed (1,175) and 28th in yards allowed per rushing attempt (4.7).
Kickoff against the Browns lands at 12 p.m. CT, where a victory would make for their fourth on the season, as well as make for their first back-to-back win of the season.

title: Texans' Jadeveon Clowney Embracing Next Man Up Mentality Amid Injuries
full_text:
The Houston Texans are entering their Week 10 matchup against the Cleveland Browns a little more banged up than usual.
And that's especially so as it relates to their edge rusher unit. Not only has Danielle Hunter already been ruled out for Sunday's action due to a hamstring injury, but Will Anderson Jr. has also been listed as questionable with a knee injury after not participating in team practice on Friday.
Of course, being without one of those two studs on the front seven–– let alone both of them–– is a huge loss for the Texans and their overall ceiling on the defensive side of the ball.
Houston's pass-rush is really the engine that makes their defense go on a week-to-week basis. And for as up and down as this unit has been over the course of this season, losing any of their Pro Bowl talents for a near-must-win game against Cleveland is a less-than-ideal outcome.
However, in the wake of those injuries to the Texans' defense, veteran edge rusher Jadeveon Clowney doesn't seem to be too phased. And in fact, he seems ready to go for what should be an increased role for him on the team's road trip to Cleveland.
"It's the National Football League. It happens. Next man up mentality," Clowney said of the Texans' injuries, via Aaron Wilson of KPRC2 . "That's why you go and prepare like a starter, no matter what role you're in. You just prepare, and make sure you're ready when your number is called."
Throughout the first half of the Texans' season, Clowney hasn't seen the most snaps on a week-to-week basis. He's averaging only a 36.5% snap share on the defense, and hasn't seen a game in which that number has eclipsed 50%.
But that's been a result seen with the combination of Anderson and Hunter on the field, each seeing around 70% of the defensive snaps coming their way.
Without one of those pieces, or perhaps even both, Clowney––one of the league's best DE3s––immediately slots into a starting role, and does so coming fresh off his best performance of the season so far.
Against the Los Angeles Chargers , Clowney was one of three defensive linemen to total a pair of sacks on the day, and did so on just 24 total snaps.
On Sunday, that snap count could be double what it was this past weekend. And against Clowney's former team in Cleveland, paired with the fact that he'll be going up against his former quarterback from Houston in Deshaun Watson , the stage could be set for a strong performance on his behalf.
"I'm looking forward to it, man. Next game on the schedule is a big one for us," Clowney said of facing the Browns. "Trying to get two wins back-to-back. Haven't had that all season, so I'm looking forward to that."
The Texans will reveal closer to kickoff on Sunday afternoon whether or not Anderson will be there to accompany Clowney on the defensive line. Regardless of whether or not he's a part of the equation, though, expect Clowney's next-man-up mentality to remain the same.

title: Texans' 3 Biggest Keys to Victory vs. Browns in Week 10 Matchup
full_text:
The Houston Texans have a pivotal Week 10 game on the horizon against the Cleveland Browns , where a win would take them just one game away from getting back to a .500 record, and put them one step closer to clawing back into the AFC playoff picture.
However, taking home a win in this week's road trip against Cleveland is shaping up to be a task a bit easier said than done. Not only is this Browns team a surprising 5-4 through the first half of the season, but the Texans are heading into this game with multiple key injuries to account for.
That means for Houston, they'll have to hone in on a select few keys to victory in a select few areas of the game in order to secure that much-needed win, and continue building momentum before their short week of preparation for Week 11.
With that in mind, let's break down the Texans' three biggest keys to victory in this weekend's matchup against the Browns:
The Browns' passing defense could make things a bit tougher for the Texans through the air, especially with a talent like cornerback Denzel Ward likely locking down his side of the field . But where Houston could expose Cleveland's defense is within the run game.
Cleveland's run defense through the first half of the season has not been the most consistent. They rank 27th in opposing rushing yards allowed and 28th in rushing yards per attempt. On six occasions this season, the Browns have alllowed over 125 opposing rushing yards, and they're 2-4 in those same games.
If the Texans can lean on Woody Marks––and maybe even David Montgomery if he's deemed available for Sunday––for a strong showing, even without a fully healthy offensive line, that's an easy route for Houston to gain a leg up on an otherwise solid Browns defense.
The Texans were finally able to tweak some of their penalty issues in their latest matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers. Houston incurred just six penalties for 36 yards in Week 9, which was a much better result than the past few weeks in which this team had shot up towards the top of the league in total flags and yards given up from penalties.
However, that success in the penalty category has to continue moving in the right direction for the Texans in the second half of the season. Especially in a game like this where Houston will be without multiple key starters, the margin for error becomes a bit thinner than usual.
So for the Texans' offensive line in particular , limit the holds, the false starts, and the illegal shifts, and Houston can take advantage of a team in the Browns who have also struggled when it comes to penalties––as they currently lead the NFL in total penalties called against them with 82 (over nine per game).
The Texans will be without Danielle Hunter for the first time of his tenure in Houston this Sunday, as he's been ruled out with a hamstring injury that was seemingly suffered earlier this week in practice.
There's no doubt his loss is a big hit to the Texans' pass rush. However, being without Hunter only increases the responsibilities someone like All-Pro edge rusher and current NFL sack leader Will Anderson has on Sunday to make the job a bit more difficult for Deshaun Watson and the Browns offense.
The only problem? Anderson's status is also in question for Sunday. He's been listed as questionable due to an ankle injury suffered in Thursday's practice, and had left him as a DNP for the following day.
For one, the Texans need to hope that Anderson is good to give it a go against the Browns. If he's out, the task gets even tougher for this defense and their overall pass rush. But if Anderson is indeed healthy, he has to bring his A-game for a Defensive Player of the Year-level performance to keep this unit afloat.

title: Texans Need This Veteran to Step Up With Danielle Hunter Out vs. Browns
full_text:
The Houston Texans are officially without Danielle Hunter this weekend against the Cleveland Browns.
After Hunter had been deemed a limited participant in the Texans' team practice on Thursday with a hamstring injury, to then turn to a DNP one day later, the decision was quickly made for Houston to sit out their veteran pass rusher for Week 10.
Houston #Texans Friday Injury Report & Game Status Report for Week 10 at the Cleveland Browns: pic.twitter.com/qrw9og0Fa0
There's no doubt that losing Hunter is a significant loss for the Texans–– no matter how long the timeline for his absence is.
Hunter has been a massive part of the Texans' pass-rush success since he arrived back in 2024. This season, he's been active in each of Houston's eight games to this point, recording 19 tackles, three TFLs, four sacks, and a forced fumble.
In fact, Hunter has yet to miss a single game for the Texans throughout his two years in the building. He's had a perfect 17-game attendance in both 2024 and 2025, and was on pace to do the same again this year after being active for all eight games before.
But this week against the Browns, the Texans will have to improvise without Hunter as a piece of their defensive puzzle. And keeping that in mind, it means one key veteran on Houston's defensive line will need to step up for a big game in his place–– which is none other than Jadeveon Clowney.
Throughout the Texans' season so far, we've seen Clowney established in his role as the third defensive end on Houston's front; a valuable rotational piece operating behind Anderson and Hunter for depth and pass-rushing prowess in the stints that either of them are resting on the sidelines.
And it's a role that Clowney has performed rather solidly in. Through the six games he's been healthy for, Clowney has put together 12 tackles, four TFLs, and 3.5 sacks despite playing in just 37% of Houston's defensive snaps.
That 37% snap share is the lowest that Clowney has seen on any team throughout his entire career . He's being used less often than ever, but still remaining a potent contributor off the edge who can get to the quarterback and be a stout run-stopper.
However, when someone as pivotal as Hunter is taken completely out of the equation due to a hamstring injury, the role for Clowney quickly shifts into one that is way more important than before.
Clowney becomes the clear starter right next to Will Anderson (so long as he's also healthy), and his snap count likely jumps to around 70% of the Texans' reps on the defensive side; a similar count to what Hunter sees when he's on the field.
That means Clowney will be on the field for twice as much as he is on a week-to-week basis, and his abilities as a stout pass-rusher and run defender become even more vital than they were before as the Texans' third defensive end. More snaps mean more down-to-down responsibilities.
The Texans have a lot of talented players on their defense, yet their depth off the edge isn't nearly as strong when Hunter is out of the equation.
That puts the challenge on Clowney's shoulders to step up and be a worthwhile complement to Anderson Jr. throughout the day in Cleveland as someone who can limit the Browns' ground game, and getting a handful of pressures sent in on Deshaun Watson in the process.
While losing Hunter undoubtedly stings for the Texans over any stretch of time, having an experienced and productive depth piece behind him in Clowney might make the absence a bit easier to stomach.
Time will tell if Clowney will be able to excel in his expanded role this weekend against the Browns. But if he can, the road to a second straight victory for Houston becomes a whole lot easier to imagine.

title: Texans' Final Week 10 Injury Report vs. Browns Brings More Bad News
full_text:
The Houston Texans have released their third and final injury report heading into their Week 10 matchup against the Cleveland Browns .
And simply put, their injury report for this week is a lengthy one–– and it only grew larger over the course of the week in practice .
The Texans will be dealing with several absences heading into the weekend, and possibly more, depending on how the status of a few others shifts leading up to Sunday's kickoff.
Let's break down the latest from the Texans' injury report after the team released everyone's official statuses on Friday afternoon.
LB Azeez Al-Shaair (groin/personal) TE Brevin Jordan (finger/foot) DE Danielle Hunter (hamstring) WR Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) OL Keylan Rutledge (neck/shoulder)
CB Jaylin Smith (hamstring) RB David Montgomery (groin) LB Jake Hummel (groin) DE Will Anderson (ankle) OL Wyatt Teller (back/illness) OL Trent Brown (wrist)
So there's a lot to take away from the Texans' injury report. Yet, the biggest and perhaps most surprising absence that Houston will be faced with this weekend surrounds their veteran star edge rusher Danielle Hunter, who's been ruled out after logging a limited practice on Thursday and didn't participate on Friday.
As to how severe Hunter's injury is long-term, we don't really know yet. All we know is that Hunter likely suffered a hamstring injury during practice on Thursday, and it's serious enough to keep him out for one week–– and possibly more, knowing that the Texans are on a short week for Week 11.
Without him, Jadeveon Clowney becomes an immediately more important piece on the Texans' defensive line, and will likely start next to Will Anderson Jr. if he's indeed ready to go (more on him in a minute).
Azeez Al-Shaair is out for the Texans once again, seemingly with another groin injury that's kept him limited throughout the past several weeks .
And Al-Shaair's absence is notable for the Texans. He's a team captain, a Pro Bowl talent at the linebacker position, and the green dot signal-caller on Houston's defense who's often heralded for his communication and play recognition in the middle of the field in the front seven.
Without him, keep an eye on either Jake Hansen or Wade Woodaz to step up in the linebacker room as the starter who will play next to Henry To'oTo'o in the second level of the defense.
Onto the offensive side of the ball, the Texans will ultimately be without their rookie left guard Keylan Rutledge , who suffered a stinger, according to DeMeco Ryans, and didn't practice throughout the entire week in all three team sessions.
Without Rutledge, KPRC2 's Aaron Wilson reported that fourth-round rookie Febechi Nwaiwu––not Wyatt Teller––will be the next man up as the Texans' left guard. And that's a bit of an eye-catching decision from the Houston brass, if it holds leading up to gameday.
Nwaiwu has yet to be activated for a game this season. But should see that trend change in a big way for this weekend as a starter on the team's trip to Cleveland.
Another noteworthy name from the Texans' lineup who won't be playing on Sunday: their big trade acquisition of Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring), who was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, but would not suit up for Thursday or Friday.
And knowing that Harrison Jr. is dealing with a hamstring issue, there's a possibility that the Texans' wideout suffered that hamstring tweak in the middle of Houston's team session on Wednesday, and will now be forced out for a period of time.
Again, with the Texans having a short week to prepare for their Week 11 game against the Indianapolis Colts for next Thursday, that could wind up turning Harrison Jr.'s absences into one spanning multiple games, depending on how severe his hamstring issue really is.
As for those who still have a chance to play this Sunday in Cleveland, the two most important names to keep a watch on from now until inactives are revealed this weekend are David Montgomery and Will Anderson Jr.
Montgomery's case is simple: he's been dealing with a groin injury dating back to Week 5 against the Tennessee Titans, has been out for the past three games, but was a full practice participant on Friday, that gives him hope to finally get back on the field for Week 10.
However, for Anderson Jr., he deserves a bit more attention for his situation. He was a limited participant in practice on Thursday due to an ankle issue, and would inevitably not practice on Friday as a DNP.
If he and Danielle Hunter are forced to miss Week 10, that'd be a devastating loss for the potency of this Texans' pass rush. So stay tuned for more on his status in the coming days.
