title: What Texans WR Nico Collins Said About Facing Browns CB Denzel Ward
full_text:
THe Houston Texans will see their No. 1 wide receiver Nico Collins face up against one of the better cornerbacks in the NFL this weekend as they take on the Cleveland Browns –– and that's none other than Denzel Ward.
Ward has been at the top of his game for multiple seasons in the league now, logging five Pro Bowl appearances throughout his nine years pro, and could be on the verge of another selection by the end of 2026.
Pro Football Focus has graded Ward as the No. 1 cornerback in the NFL through the first 10 weeks (90.5), as he's totaled some impressive stats with 26 tackles, two forced fumbles, three interceptions, three PBUs, and ranks top 10 in the NFL for passer rating allowed (42.5) and yards per reception allowed (7.2).
So there's no doubt this week against Ward will be a tall task for Collins to take on. However, he's certainly accepting that challenge to take on one of the best cornerback matchups in the NFL.
When Collins was asked on Thursday about the matchup he's set to see this weekend against Ward, there's no denying that he's excited to face the challenge of taking on one of the best cornerbacks in the NFL, but also facing a strong Browns secondary as a collective.
"Look forward to it, man. Denzel, man, been one hell of a player for a long time in this league. Great Pro Bowler, man. Great with his feet, hands, technique," Collins said to KPRC2's Aaron Wilson . "It's a great feeling to go against the best in this league, man."
"One of the best secondaries, great corners, great safeties. So, got to come ready... It's going to be a great weekend, man... All respect to Denzel, man. He’s one of the great corners in this league for a long time, and it's going to be a great game, man. Just excited to go against a high-level corner like that."
This season, Collins hasn't quite been the explosive downfield threat that he has been throughout the past two seasons. However, he also hasn't seen quite as many targets as he's been accustomed to in both 2024 and 2025 .
While Collins has averaged eight or more targets a game through the last two seasons, that number has shrunk to just 6.5 throughout the five games he's played in 2026. He's averaged 4.7 receptions and 64 yards per game, along with four touchdown receptions.
And this week, it might be tough for Collins to get those numbers back on track when facing one of the best cornerbacks in the NFL, but also one of the better secondaries in the NFL with what the Browns have to offer.
As a part of their impressive 5-4 record to date, the Browns also rank sixth in the NFL for passing yards allowed (1,809), eighth for passing touchdowns allowed (12), and fifth in net yards per passing attempt (5.6).
Cleveland's offense has had its own holes that have been exposed throughout the first half of the season––considering they're ranked 29th in total points––but their defense has remained a calling card for a lot of their early success.
So not only will this weekend be a tough outing for Collins with his matchup against Ward, but the same could be said for C.J. Stroud and his plans to attack the Browns through the air.
And if that limited day does happen to be the case for Stroud and their offensive attack, the road to victory for the Texans tends to become a whole lot tougher.

title: Texans at Risk of Losing Starting Offensive Lineman for Browns Game
full_text:
The Houston Texans could be without one key name on their offensive line for Week 10 against the Cleveland Browns.
And that's none other than their rookie left guard, Keylan Rutledge, who is at risk of missing his first-ever regular season game on Sunday.
According to KPRC2 's Aaron Wilson, Rutledge is still dealing with stinger symptoms from the injury that he suffered earlier this week in practice, thus making him unlikely to play on Sunday against the Browns.
#Texans starting left guard Keylan Rutledge, first-round pick, still dealing with stinger symptoms (neck, shoulder), per source. Considered unlikely to play vs. #Browns , barring unexpected change, and team is prepping rookie Febechi Nwaiwu for his 1st #NFL start, per sources
Without Rutledge in the lineup, fourth-round rookie Febechi Nwaiwu is expected to get the start at left guard, per Wilson.
There's no doubt that losing Rutledge is a notable loss for a Texans offensive line that's remained relatively healthy all season long. The only injury they've had to deal with through the first half of the season has been when Ed Ingram missed Weeks 2 and 3 due to a groin injury.
Throughout the first half of his rookie season, Rutledge has collected an overall grade of 45.6 via Pro Football Focus , which ranks 71st out of 75 eligible guards.
He's totaled over 500 offensive snaps played with two penalties, two sacks, three hits, and a whopping 25 pressures allowed through eight games.
Despite the numbers not exactly looking optimal for Rutledge, Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans has gone on record saying how impressed he's been with their first-round pick over the course of his rookie season due to his consistency.
“Keylan, he's stepped in and done some really good things for us," Ryans said heading into Week 9. "He’s played aggressive. He’s had some challenges as a rookie, but he’s weathered it really well. One bad play doesn't determine how his game goes. He's able to eliminate a bad play and move onto the next play."
"He's done a really good job of being steady in there; consistent force for us there on the inside. And I'm pleased to see how the rest of his season continues to progress. But, he's done a good job as a rookie. “Sometimes you lose sight that he’s a rookie, because he's been one of our most consistent guys up front."
Since the injury seems to be a minor stinger, we shouldn't expect Rutledge to be out of the lineup for long, even if he has missed back-to-back practices this week, and could be in to miss Week 10 against the Browns.
It is worth mentioning that the Texans do operate on a short week for Week 11, as they'll be facing the Indianapolis Colts on Thursday night. So that could make Rutledge's status a bit more interesting to watch unravel over the course of next week.
But until he's officially deemed ready to play once again, the Texans are expected to roll with another rookie at left guard in Nwaiwu; someone who showcased his positional versatility throughout his time in college at Oklahoma, and might be due for his first NFL start this Sunday .
Nwaiwu has been largely a non-factor on the Texans' offensive line so far this season, having frequently been a gameday inactive for most weeks.
However, it seems that Houston's coaching staff has built up some trust in Nwaiwu based on what he's showcased throughout his time in practice.
Knowing that the Texans also plan to start Nwaiwu over a more experienced name like Wyatt Teller speaks to how they feel about the young talent they have in the building and his ability to step in for Rutledge if he does ultimately miss out of Week 10.

title: Texans Cut Veteran RB to Sign WR Nikko Remigio to 53-Man Roster
full_text:
The Houston Texans have done some roster shuffling ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the Cleveland Browns .
One of those moves was to bring in former Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver and return specialist Nikko Remigio to the 53-man roster, who was recently waived from the Chiefs because of their recent trade deadline move to bring in wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts.
But for the Texans to bring in Remigio, they had to make a move to cut another name within their roster to meet the NFL's 53-man roster limit.
And in this case, the Texans decided to let go a veteran in their running back room to make that space–– which was Dare Ogunbowale.
Ogunbowale was picked up from the Texans earlier in September from the Las Vegas Raiders' practice squad, which was where he had resided dating back to August after Houston had decided not to re-sign him this offseason.
And in the brief time that Ogunbowale was in the building for the Texans, he provided a bit of depth in the running back room , but also brought some of his special teams prowess to the table for a team that was struggling in that phase of the game.
Ogunbowale ultimately played 62 special teams snaps (43% snap share) and 16 offensive snaps (5% snap share) within the five games that he was with the Texans this season.
However, heading into Week 10, there's a chance that the Texans' running back depth could be looking a bit healthier than it has been throughout their past few meetings.
More specifically, David Montgomery's status is trending up from his groin injury suffered back in Week 5, as he was able to be a limited participant in Thursday's practice before facing the Browns.
So if Montgomery is healthy for this weekend, that leaves the Texans with four running backs on the roster, including Ogunbowale.
And in the case of Ogunbowale, he's been a nice piece to incorporate on the special teams side, but not as much on the offensive end that makes his spot on the roster a bit more expendable. In the five games he had played with Houston, he had zero rushing stats recorded, and just one reception for three yards.
Therefore, as the Texans decided to add another name to their receiver room–– likely in an effort to bolster their special teams–– it only made sense for Houston to cut ties with Ogunbowale in the running back room.
That means, for the Texans' running back room, they'll have three on their 53-man roster for Week 10 in Cleveland: that's Montgomery, Woody Marks, and Emari Demercado.
As to who will be available for that contest against the Browns remains to be seen, considering Montgomery was a limited participant on Thursday, and Marks didn't practice at all on Thursday with a knee injury.
At the very least, though, Ogunbowale won't be a part of that unit and will now move on from Houston to try and land on his feet somewhere else for the second half of the 2026 campaign.

title: 3 Texans Predictions That Could Define Week 10 vs. Browns
full_text:
The Houston Texans' Week 10 game against the Cleveland Browns is slowly approaching around the corner.
And it's a game for the Texans that'll be extremely important to take advantage of. They'll be taking the road trying to climb one game closer to .500, face up against another AFC Wild Card contender, and will be trying to build upon the 44-point outing they saw last weekend against the LA Chargers.
So what can we expect from the Texans in this game against the Browns? Will they rise to the occasion for a second straight win, or fall into similar pitfalls that they have in their five losses so far this season?
Well, let's sort through a batch of three bold predictions for the Texans to take our chances at guessing how things will unravel in Cleveland on Sunday:
This season has looked a whole lot different than 2025's output on the offensive side of the ball for Houston. The Texans are scoring a lot of points on a week-to-week basis, looking strong through their air attack thanks to some C.J. Stroud heroics , and they'll be looking to continue that trend in Week 10.
The Browns, while they haven't allowed 30 points to an opponent dating back to Week 1 against the Jacksonville Jaguars, have certainly gotten close a few times. And on top of that, they haven't really played a high-powered offense like the Texans many times this season.
If the Texans can keep their momentum through the air and the offense can continue to limit the penalties setting them back as they did last weekend, 30 points is wildly possible for this team.
So far this season, the Browns are 0-1 in games where they allow 30 points or more, and have yet to score 30 points a game themselves. This might be a simple recipe for Houston's success this weekend.
Last week, we saw Tank Dell get involved in a big way for what was his second game back from his 2024 knee injury . And with that extra involvement, he turned in about as good of a performance as you could expect from him: four receptions on nine targets for 105 yards and a touchdown.
And really, there's no reason why the Texans should stop trying to feed the ball to Dell in Week 10.
He's looking closer and closer to his pre-injury self, is comfortable with the extra workload , has given Houston another layer of playmaking to account for in the wide receiver room, and when he's firing on all cylinders, the better it is for C.J. Stroud.
C.J. Stroud to Tank Dell for the TD 🗣️ HOUvsLAC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/r0q9mBmr5d
So we'll predict Dell to find the end zone once again in Week 10. It might not be as sweet as last week's, considering that reception marked his first touchdown in nearly two years, but points are points, nonetheless.
The Texans' secondary has not been the ball-hawking, interception-happy unit that they were all throughout last season in their first eight games of this year.
That becomes clear when looking at Houston's interception totals in the secondary. Not one player has recorded more than one interception on the season so far. In all, the Texans' defense has just four interceptions, which makes them one of nine teams in the NFL to log four or fewer interceptions on the season thus far.
It's a result that needs to turn around in the right direction for Houston in the second half of their schedule for this defense to be at it's true elite potential. And there might not be a better time to add onto their interception totals than this game against their former quarterback in Deshaun Watson.
I'll be keeping an eye on Calen Bullock to handle those takeaway duties: Houston's Pro Bowl talent heralded as one of the best ball-hawks at his position throughout the past two seasons, and needs some balls to come his way to hold up that status.

title: Colts vs. Dolphins Best Bets: Feed JT and Cash In
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts have a legitimate chance to finally get back in the win column Sunday, and I think we have an even better chance to make some money off the game plan they’ll need to use.
Indianapolis is 2-7 and riding a five-game losing streak, while the Miami Dolphins come to Lucas Oil Stadium at 1-7. Call it a Toilet Bowl, but ugly football can still give us some clean betting angles.
We’re 16-9 on Colts-specific best bets this season, and this week feels pretty straightforward.
Indianapolis doesn’t have many proven answers left, which means Shane Steichen should be putting the ball in Jonathan Taylor’s hands as often as possible.
Run the rock and make Kyle McCord beat you.
Here are my three best bets for Week 10.
I’m going right back to Taylor.
He probably should have gotten his get-right touchdown last week. Taylor ran six yards down to the Dallas 2-yard line, lost his shoe, and had to come out before Seth McGowan scored his first NFL touchdown on the next snap.
Taylor has gone two straight games without scoring, with his last touchdown coming in Week 7 against Minnesota. He still enters Sunday with eight rushing scores this season.
Forget the trade rumors. Taylor is still here, and with how limited this offense has become, there aren’t many other options near the goal line.
One play could cash this line.
Dulin caught one pass last week, but it went 55 yards for a touchdown against Dallas. With Downs and Allen gone, those opportunities should become more available.
The Colts have to manufacture yards somehow when defenses load up against Taylor. Dulin’s speed makes him an obvious candidate for screens, shot plays and anything designed to create a chunk gain.
At 14.5 yards, I’m betting he gets at least one opportunity and makes it count.
This one is simple: I’m betting on the first-time starter making a mistake.
McCord will make his first NFL regular-season start Sunday and throw his first official pass against Indianapolis. The Colts have only two interceptions this season, so I understand the hesitation.
But the young defensive front showed life against Dallas, including Laiatu Latu’s strip-sack of Dak Prescott. If Indianapolis can create pressure and force McCord into obvious passing situations, there should be an opportunity for this secondary to finally make a play on the football.
First NFL start, on the road, against a defense that showed some juice last week. I’ll take my chances on one mistake.
Good luck and bet responsibly.

title: 3 Things Colts Must Do Against Dolphins to Snap Their Five-Game Skid
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts have lost five straight, but Sunday might be their best chance in weeks to finally stop the bleeding.
Miami comes to Lucas Oil Stadium at 1-7, and with Malik Willis on injured reserve, the Dolphins are turning to Kyle McCord for his first NFL start. For a Colts team sitting at 2-7, this is absolutely a game they should believe they can win.
But with this offense as depleted as it is, Indianapolis needs to keep things simple.
Daniel Jones is left with a thin group of proven weapons. The path to victory is pretty straightforward: lean on the stars who are still here and make the rookie quarterback uncomfortable.
Here are my three keys to a Colts victory in Week 10.
After all the trade deadline chaos, Jonathan Taylor is still here. Now, let him remind this league just who he is.
Taylor enters Sunday with 656 rushing yards and eight touchdowns on 161 carries. If Indianapolis establishes him early, this entire offense changes.
If Taylor dictates the game, the Colts can stay ahead of the sticks, control the clock, and avoid forcing Jones to carry this barren passing game.
This isn't complicated. Run the damn ball.
McCord is in line to make the first regular-season start of his NFL career after Miami placed Willis on injured reserve with a groin injury.
The Colts don't have an elite pass rush, but this is exactly the kind of matchup where their young defensive ends need to step up. Show pressure, disguise coverage, and force McCord to make decisions before he gets comfortable.
We've seen defensive minds like Bill Belichick and Mike Vrabel make life miserable for inexperienced quarterbacks. Indianapolis needs to bring that same aggressive mentality Sunday.
You cannot let McCord settle in.
The Colts want to run the ball all afternoon, but eventually there will be a third-and-long where Jones has no choice but to throw it.
That's where Tyler Warren is going to have to be the dominant physical force he is.
With Allen and Downs gone, Warren is clearly the most dangerous receiving option left. He has 38 catches for 275 yards and two touchdowns on 53 targets this season, plus another score on the ground.
Miami knows that, too. The Dolphins can crowd the middle, bracket Warren, and force someone else to beat them.
It might not matter. Warren has to win through contact, create after the catch, and make the handful of plays this offense simply cannot get from anywhere else right now.
Miami is averaging just 15.8 points per game, 31st in the NFL. Indianapolis does not need to be perfect.
Feed Taylor, make McCord uncomfortable, and let Warren be the difference-maker. If Indianapolis sticks to that formula, there's no reason this five-game losing streak can't end Sunday.

title: 3 Storylines to Watch in Colts Week 10 Clash with Dolphins
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts will return to Lucas Oil Stadium this weekend looking to put an end to a difficult stretch of football. After beginning the season with a 2-2 record, Indianapolis has dropped five consecutive games and finds itself in a lost season, where the focus has shifted from a playoff pursuit to evaluating the future.
The Colts have undergone significant changes over the past several weeks, both on and off the field. Sunday's matchup presents an opportunity to start moving in a different direction, but Indianapolis will need a much more complete performance to take advantage of the opportunity.
Miami arrives in Indianapolis having experienced plenty of its own struggles this season. At 1-7, the Dolphins are equally desperate to find some momentum, setting up an important matchup for two teams that desperately need a positive result.
Here are three storylines to watch as the Colts prepare to host the Dolphins in Week 10.
The Colts traded away their two most productive wide receivers in Keenan Allen and Josh Downs at Tuesday's deadline, leaving behind a receiving corps that looks drastically different.
While the organization added to its draft capital, it also left a substantial void in its passing attack that needs to be filled.
The two receivers combined for 73 receptions, 705 receiving yards and two touchdowns. They also accounted for 67% of the Colts' targets, 70% of their receptions and 61% of their receiving yards from the wide receiver position. Replacing that level of production will be a considerable challenge for an offense that has already struggled to find consistency.
With Alec Pierce still on injured reserve, Indianapolis' wide receiver room consists of Laquon Treadwell, Ashton Dulin, Anthony Gould, Deion Burks and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine. The five of them have combined for 49 targets, 27 catches, 375 yards and one touchdown. Needless to say, the group lacks consistent production.
Gould and Burks are two younger players who could also benefit from the increased opportunities. Head coach Shane Steichen shared that Gould will take on a larger role in the slot following Downs' departure, while Burks will rotate in.
Tyler Warren will also need to be a regular feature of the passing attack. The second-year tight end has already established himself as one of Jones' more reliable targets, leading the team with 38 receptions for 275 yards.
With fewer established options available at wide receiver, Warren could see an even greater share of the offensive workload moving forward. Still, he can't do it all himself, and at least one wide out will have to take the bull by the horns.
Ultimately, the Colts need several players to take advantage of opportunities that simply weren't available to them before the trade deadline. Sunday's matchup against Miami will provide an early indication of whether Indianapolis has enough depth and versatility to remain competitive offensively with its reshuffled receiving corps.
The Dolphins placed starting quarterback Malik Willis on injured reserve with a groin injury, meaning second-year quarterback Kyle McCord will step into the starting role.
The change under center presents an opportunity for a struggling Colts defense to regain some confidence. Indianapolis has struggled to consistently get off the field, ranking near the bottom of the league in several defensive categories. Perhaps more importantly, they've struggled to create turnovers, ranking 31st in the NFL with 5 total takeaways, though it has produced three in the last two games.
McCord has yet to attempt a pass in a regular-season NFL game, making it difficult to know exactly what to expect from the young quarterback. He does bring a live arm and has experience operating in high-pressure situations dating back to his college career, which included stops at Ohio State and Syracuse. However, making a first NFL start on the road presents an entirely different challenge, particularly against a defense that should be hungry to make his afternoon uncomfortable.
Rushing the passer will be key. The Colts will need to find ways to generate consistent pressure. Defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo has several young players who could make an impact in this matchup, including Laiatu Latu, Adetomiwa Adebawore and rookie Caden Curry. Creating difficult passing situations and forcing McCord to make quick decisions should be among the priorities for Indianapolis, as speeding up his internal clock will help generate turnover opportunities for the back end.
Of course, the Colts cannot afford to overlook Miami's other offensive weapons. The Dolphins still have a capable running game and will likely look to establish it early to take some pressure off their quarterback. Indianapolis will need to contain the run and force Miami into obvious passing situations rather than allowing the offense to dictate the game on the ground.
How successful the Colts are in frustrating McCord will have a direct impact on the outcome of the game. Fail to do so, and Miami may sneak away with a victory.
Turnovers have become one of the most significant problems for the Colts this season, and Daniel Jones has been at the center of those struggles.
Jones has struggled mightily protecting the football, with his mistakes putting additional pressure on an offense that has already had difficulty finding the end zone. He enters Week 10 with 10 interceptions through nine games, giving him one of the highest totals among NFL quarterbacks.
Even more concerning is the frequency with which those mistakes have occurred. Jones has thrown an interception in eight of his nine appearances this season, including each of his last four games. He has also thrown just six touchdown passes during that span, leaving Indianapolis deprived of the efficiency Jones showed he could operate at a season ago.
Giving the opposing offense additional possessions will made an already struggling defense's job even more difficult, while the offense has frequently been forced to overcome mistakes that could have been avoided.
There are certainly some circumstances working against Jones. The Colts have dealt with injuries throughout their offensive lineup and have a huge question mark at the wide receiver position. Allen and Downs were important parts of the passing game, particularly in providing Jones with reliable options underneath and in the middle of the field. Adjusting to an entirely different group of receivers could create some communication and timing issues early on.
However, that makes protecting the football even more important. Jones does not need to force difficult throws or attempt to manufacture big plays on every possession. Indianapolis still has Jonathan Taylor available in the backfield, and the Colts should look to lean on their running game to take some pressure off of Jones. Taking what the defense gives him, avoiding unnecessary risks and being willing to throw the football away when necessary would represent an important step in the right direction.

title: 3 Matchups That Will Test Just How Bad the Colts Really Are
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts are back home Sunday for a matchup that, if we’re being honest, isn’t exactly must-watch TV.
Indianapolis is 2-7 and riding a five-game losing streak, while Miami enters at 1-7. But beneath the surface, there are a few battles that could bring some life to this game.
More than anything, this feels like a litmus test for how bad this Colts team really is. If Indianapolis struggles against this Miami team, things are really, REALLY bad.
Here are three matchups I’m watching closely.
After all the trade deadline chaos, Jonathan Taylor can finally put the noise behind him and get back to playing football.
Taylor has 656 rushing yards and eight touchdowns, but he has managed just 69 rushing yards over the last two games. I think some of that had to do with everything transpiring around him and this organization.
This feels like the perfect get-right spot.
Miami is allowing 111.8 rushing yards per game, and the Dolphins just lost defensive tackle Zach Sieler for the season with a torn biceps. This game pretty much comes down to whether the Colts can run the rock against a Miami front that suddenly looks much more vulnerable.
If Taylor gets rolling early, Indianapolis should control this game.
Normally, I would call this a get-right game for Daniel Jones, too. The problem is the front office just stripped away almost every proven weapon he had.
Josh Downs is in Kansas City, and Keenan Allen is in San Francisco. Tyler Warren is now the centerpiece of the passing game, while Laquon Treadwell and Ashton Dulin are being asked to do more.
Now, Jones hasn’t been good. He has thrown for 1,722 yards, six touchdowns and 10 interceptions, and he still hasn’t looked like the same quarterback he was before the Achilles injury ended his 2025 season.
He also made it clear this week that he wasn’t thrilled with the deadline moves. But what are you going to do?
Miami only has 12 sacks this season, with Chop Robinson leading the team at four.
If Jones is going to create anything through the air with this depleted group, he is basically going to have to do it all.
This matchup might tell us the most about Indianapolis’ defense.
Kyle McCord is making his first NFL start Sunday and has never thrown a regular-season pass. For a young Colts defense that looked at least somewhat competent last week, this is about as favorable of a quarterback matchup as you can ask for.
Indianapolis still has Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward outside, with Cam Bynum behind them. The Colts rank 17th in passing yards allowed at 224.8 per game.
They should make life miserable for McCord early. If a quarterback making his first NFL start finds consistent success against this secondary, then this unit really is that bad.
The Colts have every opportunity to take control of this game, and frankly, there's no excuse for another lifeless performance. If Indianapolis can't handle a depleted Miami team at home, this season might be even worse than we thought.

title: Revisiting the Colts' Blockbuster Sauce Gardner Trade One Year Later
full_text:
374 days ago, the Indianapolis Colts made one of the biggest trades in franchise history, surrendering two first-round picks and wide receiver Adonai Mitchell to acquire New York Jets cornerback Sauce Gardner.
The move came with Indianapolis sitting at 7-2 and looking like a legitimate Super Bowl contender. General manager Chris Ballard believed he had an opportunity to acquire one of the NFL's premier young defensive players and address a major weakness in the secondary.
Fast forward 12 months, and the circumstances surrounding that decision look drastically different.
The Colts are 2-7, Ballard is no longer with the organization and Indianapolis has begun accumulating draft capital for its next rebuilding effort. Gardner remains in Indianapolis, but the franchise has yet to see the kind of return it envisioned when making such a substantial investment.
Meanwhile, the Jets have already begun seeing solid returns from the compensation they received for Gardner.
Let's take a look back at the trade and how both sides have fared from it a year later.
The Colts' decision to pursue Gardner made plenty of sense at the time.
Indianapolis was the top team in the AFC, with an explosive offense and a defense that appeared to be one piece away from becoming a legitimate contender. However, injuries and inconsistent play in the secondary had created a weakness that opposing offenses could exploit.
Gardner offered an opportunity to address that problem with one of the league's most accomplished young cornerbacks.
The former No. 4 pick had earned first-team All-Pro honors in each of his first two NFL seasons and was widely regarded as one of the best players at his position.
Indianapolis was acquiring more than just a starting cornerback. It was bringing in a potential defensive cornerstone who had already established himself among the NFL's elite.
That alone helps explain why Ballard was so willing to mortgage the franchise's future to get a deal done.
The Jets received Indianapolis' 2026 and 2027 first-round picks along with Mitchell, who had been selected in the second round of the 2024 NFL Draft. It was an enormous investment for a cornerback, even one with Gardner's pedigree.
Ballard was essentially betting that Indianapolis' championship window was open and that the draft selections would be late enough to justify sacrificing them for an established star.
Unfortunately, the remainder of the 2025 season did not go according to plan.
The Colts won their first game with Gardner, but lost the next seven straight, finishing 8-9. The team that once stood atop of the conference missed the playoffs entirely. Their 2026 first-round selection consequently became the No. 16 overall pick, which the Jets used to select Oregon tight end Kenyon Sadiq.
Had the Colts held onto their pick instead of trading for Gardner, some of the prospects still available at No. 16 for their selection included safety Dillon Thieneman, wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. (both Indianapolis natives) and a long list of talented edge rushers to improve what was and still remains a weak point for the Colts.
To make things worse for Indianapolis, their 2-7 record means their 2027 selection would be the No. 4 overall pick if the season were to end today. So there's a real possibility Indianapolis acquired an All-Pro cornerback in exchange for a top-20 draft pick, a top-five draft pick and a young wide receiver.
Purely on paper, the total trade package looks ugly for Indianapolis.
While the circumstances surrounding the trade have changed, Gardner remains the centerpiece of Indianapolis' return.
There is no questioning the talent that made him such an attractive acquisition. However, his time with the Colts has been interrupted by injuries and has yet to produce the consistent results expected from a player who commanded two first-round picks.
Gardner appeared in just three games following the trade during the 2025 season before suffering a calf injury that sidelined him for the rest of the year. He returned for the 2026 campaign but experienced another interruption to his availability, limiting the amount of time Indianapolis has had its prized acquisition on the field.
Through eight games this season, Gardner has recorded 26 tackles and seven passes defended without an interception. While those numbers don't tell the entire story of a cornerback's performance, they illustrate the relatively modest statistical production Indianapolis has received so far.
It would be unfair to place the Colts' defensive struggles entirely on Gardner. Indianapolis has dealt with injuries and personnel deficiencies throughout the front seven, and one cornerback cannot single-handedly transform an entire defense, regardless of the price Indianapolis paid to get him.
Nevertheless, the Colts acquired Gardner because they believed he could make a significant difference. His limited availability and inconsistent results have made it difficult to justify the enormous price.
That doesn't mean the investment cannot eventually pay off. Gardner is still young and remains under contract through 2030, giving the Colts plenty of time to see their investment pay off.
But evaluating the trade one year later requires acknowledging that Indianapolis has not yet received the impact it expected.
The other side of this transaction makes the evaluation even more complicated for Indianapolis.
While the Colts have been waiting for Gardner to establish himself as the centerpiece of their secondary, the Jets have begun turning their return package into meaningful pieces for their own roster.
New York used Indianapolis' 2026 first-round selection to draft Sadiq, who has shown flashes of significant potential during his rookie campaign. Through nine games, the Oregon product has recorded 21 receptions (second on team) for 235 yards and a touchdown.
Those numbers aren't necessarily eye-popping, but Sadiq has already demonstrated the receiving ability that made him such an intriguing prospect. His seven-catch, 105-yard performance against Detroit in Week 3 offered a particularly encouraging glimpse of what he could become.
Mitchell has also benefited from the change of scenery.
After struggling to establish himself in Indianapolis, the former second-round pick has received a larger opportunity in New York. He missed four games following a finger procedure but returned to record seven receptions for 142 yards and a touchdown against the Raiders in Week 8.
Through his first four appearances of 2026, Mitchell has logged 265 receiving yards while averaging 16.6 yards per reception, beginning to show the downfield ability that made him so intriguing to the Colts in 2024.
Neither player has established himself as a definitive building block just yet, but both have provided the Jets with meaningful contributions and enough optimism moving forward for New York to believe they won the trade by a landslide.
The most significant asset, however, is still waiting to be realized.
New York has yet to use Indianapolis' 2027 first-round selection, which is likely to wind up being another top-half selection, at worst. The Jets will have a chance to some more top-end talent to their roster.
That gives New York a considerable advantage when evaluating the early returns of the transaction. The organization has already acquired a promising rookie tight end, given a young receiver an opportunity to develop and retained another first-round pick for the upcoming draft.
Indianapolis, meanwhile, has one player to show for the entire package.
Jumping to conclusions on who the trade benefited more would be premature. There's still plenty of time for that equation to change. Gardner has the talent to reestablish his status as an elite cornerback, and his remaining contract gives him an opportunity to provide value well beyond the first year of the deal.
What was once viewed as an aggressive move to help Indianapolis compete for a championship has become a reminder of the risks…

title: Colts vs. Dolphins Preview: Can Indy Finally Stop the Slide?
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts are back home Sunday, and if you’re looking for a matchup between two teams fighting for their season, this probably isn’t it.
Indianapolis enters Week 10 at 2-7 on a five-game losing streak. Miami comes to Lucas Oil Stadium at 1-7.
We’ve got the Colts’ 28th-ranked defense in yards allowed against Miami’s 31st-ranked scoring offense. What a barn burner.
But forget the season outlook for a minute. The Colts should still win this football game, and there are a few things they absolutely have to do to make sure that happens.
The trade deadline has passed, the smoke has cleared, and Keenan Allen and Josh Downs are gone. Those two accounted for 70% of the Colts’ wide receiver receptions and 61% of their receiving yards before being traded Tuesday.
That leaves Daniel Jones throwing to a depleted receiver room, with Tyler Warren standing as the only proven option left.
Jonathan Taylor needs to look like Jonathan Taylor again. He has 656 rushing yards and eight touchdowns this season, but has totaled just 69 rushing yards over the last two games.
If Indianapolis is going to move the ball consistently, Taylor has to produce even when Miami knows the run is coming. I would expect the Dolphins to make Jones find someone other than Warren.
Defensively, this is where I want to see the young guys take another step.
Adetomiwa Adebawore had four pressures and three quarterback hits against Dallas, while Hunter Wohler finished with 16 tackles, Bryce Boettcher had 12 and CJ Allen added 10. Caden Curry and Jaylahn Tuimoloau each added a sack, as this defense is finally giving its young players opportunities to make an impact.
And there really isn’t a better chance to build on it.
Miami will start Kyle McCord after Malik Willis was placed on injured reserve with a groin injury. McCord has yet to throw a regular-season NFL pass, meaning the Colts will be facing a first-time starter at home.
That doesn’t guarantee anything with this defense, but the game plan should be pretty simple: stop the run, make McCord beat you, and don’t give away explosive plays.
This game screams low-scoring. Then again, both teams have shown enough offensive struggles and defensive breakdowns that a couple of mistakes could turn an ugly game into something much more chaotic.
This matchup should also serve as a reminder of the expectations surrounding this franchise. Eight or nine wins in Indianapolis usually has this fanbase calling for everyone's job, but even during a fire sale and a five-game losing streak, this is still a game Colts fans expect to win.
Losing at home to a 1-7 Dolphins team starting a quarterback making his first NFL start would be a new low.
Sunday should be about putting the trade deadline behind them, feeding Taylor, and seeing whether this young defense can finally start building something.
Michael Greene is a graduate of Indiana University and the Scouting Academy. He's in his first year covering the Indianapolis Colts and NFL, with a unique focus on fantasy football.

title: 3 Draft Receivers Who Fit the Bill for Colts After Josh Downs Trade
full_text:
It's fair to say the Indianapolis Colts' wide receiver position is incredibly underwhelming following the team trading away Josh Downs .
The Colts traded Keenan Allen too, but he wasn't expected to play beyond this season; Downs looked like a piece of Indy's future.
Add on that Alec Pierce is dealing with more injuries than expected, and suddenly the future at the position is in question.
With the team committing to rebuilding and losing Downs, a wide receiver is a must-draft in 2027.
It's never too early to talk about the draft, so with that in mind, here are three prospects to keep an eye on next April for the Colts to select as offensive weaponry for the future.
For quick reference, these wide receivers are projected Day 2 or 3 prospects since Indy has no first-round pick.
Why not start with a hometown hero like Indiana University's Nick Marsh?
Marsh and fellow dynamic pass-catcher, Charlie Becker, have formed one of the deadliest wide receiver duos in college football.
Marsh would factor in as an immediate starter for the Colts, and while he stands around 6'3" and weighs a robust 210 pounds, he is incredibly explosive and has grit as a blocker.
Through nine games this year, Marsh has put up 669 receiving yards on 38 catches and eight touchdowns. The most impressive stat for Marsh is his yards per reception, which stands at 17.6.
Indiana’s Nick Marsh is such a violent player. Violent blocker, violent after the catch, and violent with his route running. Marsh is top 20 nationally in yards per route run (3.23) pic.twitter.com/C0xYTMoo0X
Indianapolis needs another top wide receiver to pair with Pierce for the future, and Marsh not only embodies what you want at the position, but he's also a fantastic route-runner with blazing speed and the willingness to do the dirty work.
A versatile weapon as a slot operator is just what the doctor ordered for Indianapolis, and there may be no more explosive variation of that than Texas A&M's Mario Craver.
Craver can operate as both a quick-win receiver and a deep threat, and his career college numbers reflect that. Below are the catch totals by season.
Craver is lightning in a bottle; he can soak up catches inside while also being a danger to take it to the house anytime he touches the football.
Mario Craver had the entire defense in a BLENDER pic.twitter.com/ka0jZDpGiJ
Indianapolis can use a multi-role receiver like Craver, and while he'll factor more into the slot than anything else, he'll always keep a defense on its toes.
Cooper Barkate is a technician at the position, and he can serve as an ultra-reliable pass-catcher that Indy's next franchise QB can lean on.
Barkate started his college career at Harvard (2022-2024), but transferred to Duke in 2025 and immediately produced.
He played 14 games and hauled in 72 catches for 1,106 receiving yards and seven touchdowns.
Barkate would ultimately end up with the Miami Hurricanes for the 2026 campaign, operating in the offense with one of the most electrifying pass-catchers in Malachi Toney.
Barkate took on the role as the number two option in the passing game, but after Toney sustained a high ankle sprain in practice on November 4th, things changed.
Immediately, this thrust Barkate into the WR1 role against the Notre Dame Fighting Irish. Expectations were high, but not only did Barkate answer the call, he aced the test.
Barkate finished with nine catches for 75 receiving yards and a pair of critical touchdowns to keep the Hurricanes close. He'll likely be the top option in the Hurricanes' wide receiver room going forward.
Cooper Barkate refuses to let Miami go away. The Hurricanes WR scores his second TD of the night to make it 24-31 against Notre Dame. pic.twitter.com/Tz2yJMUhWk
Barkate is looking like a Day 3 pick, which Indianapolis has accumulated plenty of for the 2027 draft. That type of projection means the Colts shouldn't rely on Barkate to be a top pass-catcher, at least not right away.
Regardless, Barkate is a high-IQ and efficient receiver who can make plays when they matter most, secure catches consistently, and be a reliable weapon.

title: Every Pick Colts Added at Trade Deadline (and Who They Should Target in Draft)
full_text:
As 4 PM Eastern came and went Tuesday afternoon, the Indianapolis Colts' 2027 roster remained entirely intact. No player with a contract stretching beyond the maligned 2026 season was shipped off for draft capital of any kind.
Carlie Irsay-Gordon is seemingly wiping the slate entirely clean for whoever is chosen to shepherd in the next era of Colts football. The trade deadline was about ensuring that was the case while maximizing the value of players the next general manager would have no input on.
The remaining parts of the roster however, will be under the proverbial microscope.
Holding on to Jonathan Taylor guaranteed the Colts wouldn't be receiving a first-round pick (or, of course, an equivalent) to add to their armada of 2027 draft capital, but they are still well stocked with a projected 12 picks in the upcoming draft.
Where are these picks projected to land in April, and what players might a new regime look to target with them?
According to Tankathon , the Colts added the current 82nd pick in the third round, 123rd and 131st picks in the fourth round, the 162nd pick in the fifth round, and the 194th pick in the sixth round.  They also sent the 253rd pick to the Chiefs via Buffalo in the Josh Downs trade.
Despite not having a Round 1 Pick, the Colts are 8th in @tankathon ’s Draft Power Rankings for total pick value. Every team ahead of them has either a projected Top 10 pick &/or multiple Round 1 picks Next GM has a good war chest of picks & cap $ (5th most) to start the rebuild. https://t.co/GJov7a5cuD pic.twitter.com/rkFj6ovs6H
For the 2028 draft, they also added a fifth-round pick from the Seahawks in the Quenton Nelson trade.
Now, in all likelihood these picks will fall somewhere in the range of where they're currently listed; but the situation obviously remains fluid as the season progresses.
The Colts are in the unenviable position of already looking forward to the 2027 NFL Draft. Unfortunately, without a first-round pick, they won't be awarded the chance to take a blue-chip talent at the top of the draft. Still, with the influx of draft picks and projected compensatory picks , Indianapolis has given its future general manager plenty of ammo to maneuver around the draft board.
The wide receiver room is in quite a quandary following the trade of Josh Downs and Keenan Allen . Without a franchise quarterback on the roster or likely to come during the 2027 offseason, Indianapolis would be wise to begin looking to revamp the position group for a potential rookie entering the fold in 2028.
There’s a world where the Colts go sign a Yaya Diaby type and draft a fireballer or two off the edge with Day 2 picks. Then you’ve got a nice little stock of pass rushers that can win in a variety of ways. The defense could be pretty decent in ‘27 with new coaching/vision. https://t.co/oexHUDnrEU
Indianapolis will also enter the offseason with substantial cap space and a chance to give a facelift to a beleaguered defense. Coinciding with this movement, a new defensive play caller and identity on that side of the ball will need to be established.
The Colts have a relatively precocious linebacker room that could use a quality veteran to fortify and instill this new culture. For example, if the Colts were to hire Anthony Campanile, the current Jaguars defensive coordinator, as their next head coach, he could bring along breakout linebacker and upcoming free agent Ventrell Miller.
Whichever direction a new general manager takes, it'll be hard to criticize any approach with the litany of needs the Colts appear to have.
Frankly, it'd be an exercise in futility attempting to project who the Colts may take with any exact pick come April.
Luckily, I keep a cursory list of prospects I've enjoyed watching on tape for one reason or another. You won't see any Jeremiah Smith types, as I've attempted to be realistic given the current consensus on where these guys are expected to be drafted. Information can and will change drastically as the college season rolls on, eventually giving way to the NFL Scouting Combine and various All-Star games.
If you're like me, however, and enjoy the college scouting process, hopefully this list gives you a jumping-off point for your own research into potential future Colts.
The round range is my own projection of where the Colts could look to take that position. A star (*) indicates that the prospect is a personal favorite of mine.

title: Colts Trades Present Massive Opportunities at 3 Vital Positions
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is officially in the rearview mirror, and the Indianapolis Colts were very busy, given that the franchise is at the beginning of a full rebuild.
The Colts traded off defensive tackle DeForest Buckner (San Francisco 49ers), guard Quenton Nelson (Seattle Seahawks), and wide receivers Josh Downs (Kansas City Chiefs) and Keenan Allen (49ers).
With four key players traded away, it drastically shakes up the defensive tackle, guard, and wide receiver rooms for the Colts for the rest of the 2026 season.
With that in mind, let's look at the pecking order for those three positions for Indianapolis and which players will need to step into the fray as the Colts try to make something out of their 2026 season.
The Colts traded Buckner to the 49ers for a 2027 fourth-round pick. Immediately, this took away one of the best defensive players Indianapolis has had over the last seven years.
However, the Colts felt better about this decision after Adetomiwa Adebawore emerged as a candidate to keep for their rebuild.
This led the Colts to extend Adebawore on a two-year, $35 million deal.
The Colts and DT Adetomiwa Adebawore agreed to terms on a two-year, $35 million extension that includes a $13M signing bonus and $22.5M in new money through 2027. Still only 25, Adebawore has a chance to get back to the market again as he enters his prime. The deal was… pic.twitter.com/D4TVQLVbvO
Through nine games, Adebawore leads the Colts with 4.0 sacks and is second in QB pressures (20) to defensive end Laiatu Latu (23). Adebawore will get eight more games in 2026 as Indy's top man in the defensive trenches.
As for Grover Stewart, he'll resume his position as the Colts' premier run-stuffer. Stewart wasn't traded at the deadline, but there was an offer in place that the Colts didn't execute.
Stewart's contract expires after this year, and it's hard to imagine Indianapolis will re-sign him in 2027, especially after trading Buckner.
Jerry Tillery, Tim Smith, and Kevin Givens will round out the room behind Adebawore and Stewart.
In a lost season where the Colts are gearing up for a refresh next year, it's mostly about Adebawore getting more experience as the undisputed top defensive tackle in the Circle City.
After playing eight illustrious seasons for the Colts, Nelson was traded to the Seattle Seahawks for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick.
Trade! The Colts are sending eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports . pic.twitter.com/O1EN6vHWSF
Buckner was a big loss for the defense, but Nelson is a future Hall of Famer who was still playing at an elite level upon being traded. However, this gave Indy's 2026 fourth-rounder, Jalen Farmer, the green light to take over.
Offensive line coach Tony Sparano Jr. was one of Farmer's biggest fans during the draft process, and felt that the former Kentucky Wildcat enforcer was a special talent, and made that excitement well-known after he was selected.
It’s officially the Jalen Farmer era in Indianapolis. The #Colts have a new starting left guard for the first time in almost a decade. Lord knows OL Coach Tony Sparano Jr. is excited to get to work. https://t.co/3UctqjGZxD
Farmer hasn't played much this year as the starter, but as expected, he's struggled to fill Nelson's shoes.
Per Pro Football Focus, Farmer has grades of 39.4 overall, 45.7 run-blocking, and 26.8 pass-blocking. He's also allowed seven pressures and three quarterback hits through two games played.
Matt Goncalves remains the undisputed starter at right guard, while Dalton Tucker serves as the swing piece in the room.
The rest of the season is all about Farmer gaining valuable experience to become the left guard of Indy's future.
However, expect him to have big-time growing pains, as he's only 22 and is getting a crash course in what it's like to start in the NFL.
Indianapolis dealt away Downs and Allen, who were both the best wide receivers for the Colts after Alec Pierce was placed on Injured Reserve early in the year with a heel injury.
With Downs and Allen no longer on the roster, Indy's wide receiver corps is incredibly underwhelming, and just might be the worst in the NFL.
This isn't to pile on talents like Laquon Treadwell, Ashton Dulin, and Deion Burks, but when we consider Treadwell, Dulin, Burks, Nick Westbrook-Ikhine, and Anthony Gould have just 27 catches as a whole, it puts things into perspective.
However, this presents huge opportunities for the top three receivers.
Dulin has been mostly a special teams ace in Indianapolis, but now gets a shot to be possibly the top pass-catcher out of nowhere.
Treadwell can get more playing time as a starter than perhaps he's ever seen throughout his 11 years in the league.
Burks will immediately become the top deep threat for the Colts, and will also get work in the slot after the Downs trade.
This offense was already in deep trouble with Downs and Allen on the field, so things could get even more dicey for the passing game and quarterback Daniel Jones.
Regardless, while it gives Dulin and Treadwell the chance as starters, perhaps none of these players will benefit more from the thin wide receiver room than Burks.

title: Colts GM Vacancy Became More Attractive After Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts ' general manager vacancy looked like a difficult proposition when Chris Ballard was relieved of his duties in October . The team was struggling, the roster was headed for a significant overhaul, and Indianapolis doesn't own its 2027 first-round draft pick.
However, the Colts' activity at the NFL trade deadline has changed the outlook considerably . Indianapolis parted ways with four established starters, accumulated additional draft capital, and created an opportunity for its next general manager to reshape the roster.
There is still plenty of work to be done, but the resources and flexibility now available could make Indianapolis a more appealing destination for potential candidates than it was just a few weeks ago.
One of the biggest selling points of the Indianapolis job is the collection of resources the next general manager will have at his disposal. Between additional draft selections and projected salary-cap flexibility, the Colts have several avenues to begin rebuilding their roster.
Indianapolis currently owns 10 selections in the 2027 NFL Draft, before compensatory picks have been awarded. OverTheCap projects the Colts to receive two more picks , a fith-rounder and sixth-rounder, though that's yet to be confirmed. Still, the prospect of having a dozen selections should be attractive.
Additionally, Indianapolis holds eight more picks in 2028 following its trades. The Colts acquired six total picks in those four transactions while surrendering one seventh-round selection to Kansas City in the Josh Downs deal .
While Indianapolis does not own a first-round pick in 2027 after including its selection in the trade for Sauce Gardner at last year's deadline, the volume of additional selections gives its next general manager plenty of opportunities to fill the roster with players that fit his or her style.
The Colts also have the flexibility to package selections to move up the board or pursue established players through the trade market. No shortage of options with it comes to utilizing draft capital.
There is also the financial component to consider.
Indianapolis is currently projected to have approximately $48 million in salary-cap space for the 2027 season, according to OverTheCap . That figure could change as the offseason approaches, but it gives the next general manager considerable financial flexibility to pursue free agents, retain key contributors and address the roster's most glaring deficiencies.
The quarterback situation could provide another opportunity to create financial flexibility. Daniel Jones currently carries a projected $46.8 million cap hit for 2027, making his future one of the most consequential financial decisions facing the organization. Jones has played nowhere close to the level the Colts paid him to play at, making a parting of ways the most likely outcome in the offseason.
Releasing Jones with a post-June 1st designation would clear up to $38 million in cap space, leaving $86 million in total for the next regime to use at their discretion.
The combination of additional draft capital and significant projected cap space gives the next general manager multiple ways to approach a rebuild. Rather than being restricted to the draft or free agency, Indianapolis can use both avenues to accelerate its roster reconstruction.
Perhaps just as important as the resources available to Indianapolis' next general manager is the freedom to determine what the roster should look like moving forward.
The Colts have already begun their locker room overhaul, but several significant decisions remain. The most notable involves Jonathan Taylor, who surprisingly remained in Indianapolis despite considerable trade interest leading up to the deadline.
Multiple teams reportedly offered a second-round pick or better for the three-time Pro Bowl running back, but Indianapolis ultimately held onto its franchise player. That decision now leaves Taylor's future in the hands of the next general manager.
There is a legitimate argument for keeping Taylor and building around one of the league's most productive running backs. However, there is also a case for moving him while his trade value remains high, particularly with Indianapolis entering a rebuilding period that could extend beyond the remainder of his prime.
Either way, the next general manager will have the freedom to decide what to do with Taylor. He can evaluate his value to the organization, determine whether his timeline aligns with the team's plans and decide whether another trade attempt makes sense.
The same flexibility exists at quarterback.
Jones remains in Indianapolis after the trade deadline, but his long-term future is far from settled. The Colts can evaluate whether he is the right quarterback to lead the next iteration of the franchise or whether it makes more sense to pursue another option through the draft or free agency.
There is also the possibility of giving Anthony Richardson another opportunity, depending on how the new leadership evaluates his future with the organization.
Beyond those two positions, the next general manager will have considerable freedom to determine which remaining veterans fit the team's long-term plans and which young players deserve further opportunities to establish themselves.
That level of autonomy is an important selling point for any potential candidate.
All that said, Indianapolis is certainly not an easy job. The roster has significant deficiencies, the team is coming off a disappointing season and the next general manager will have their work cut out for them to turn the franchise around.
However, the Colts have positioned themselves to offer something that isn't always available to incoming front-office executives: the resources and freedom to build an organization in their own image.

title: Jaguars-Titans Week 10 National Predictions Roundup: Why Jacksonville Can't Overlook Tennessee
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars have an important AFC South battle in Week 10, with a chance to keep their momentum rolling as they battle for seeding in the AFC.
But the Jaguars can't afford to focus on anything about seeding, the AFC, or their new pieces when 1 p.m. comes along. The Jaguars are set to battle a Tennessee Titans team that has played its best football of the season over the last three weeks, losing two one-score games against teams with winning records and earning their first win of the season in Week 6 on the road against the Indianapolis Colts.
The Jaguars, sitting at 6-2 after back-to-back post-bye week wins, will need a road win in Nashville to keep their own momentum. That momentum got a jolt over the week with trade deadline additions of Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates III, and Davon Godchaux, but the Jaguars believe they have kept their eyes on the ball during their preparation for the week.
“I think sometimes when you maybe make a player acquisition like this, and you get some star power, you get some big names and things like that, I think maybe there's a – I've seen in the past some teams that, like almost kind of, ‘Oh, okay, we're good now. And those guys will make the play.’ And I don't think that's how our building operated at all when that news broke," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said this week.
"It was almost just like, ‘Alright, we know we're a good team. We know we're a good team and these players are only here to help us take it to the next level.’ But we're not going to sit back and say, ‘Okay, well, Jessie Bates will make the play or Jordan Davis and Davon, they'll make the play. We don't have to go and do it.’ I think our guys have a lot of pride in the way that they prepare, the way that they practice."
How do the national predictions see this one playing out, however? We take a look below.
Albert Breer: Jaguars Eva Geitheim: Jaguars Mitch Goldich: Jaguars Mike Kadlick: Jaguars Gilbert Manzano: Jaguars Conor Orr: Jaguars John Pluym: Jauars Matt Verderame: Jaguars
Matt Bowen: Jaguars                                                                                                                                                       Mike Clay: Jaguars                                                                                                                                                     Jeremy Fowler: Jaguars                                                                                                                                                  Dan Graziano: Jaguars                                                                                                                                                  Kalyn Kahler: Jaguars                                                                                                                                                   Pamela Maldonado: Jaguars Eric Moody: Jaguars                                                                                                                                                     Jason Reid: Jaguars                                                                                                                                                          Ben Solak: Jaguars                                                                                                                                                           Lindsey Thiry: Jaguars                                                                                                                                                   Seth Wickersham: Titans
Jeremy Bergman: Jaguars Brooke Cersosimo: Jaguars Gennaro Filice: Jaguars Bobby Kownack: Jaguars Dan Parr: Jaguars
Joe Buscaglia: Jaguars Jon Greenberg: Jaguars Larry Holder: Jaguars Nick Kosmider: Jaguars Josh Kendal: Jaguars Austin Mock: Jaguars
The Jaguars do not get the sweep here, earning 29 of 30 votes. Still, that is quite an easy summary of what people expect to happen in this one. The Jaguars are one of the AFC's best teams and have been the most-talked-about team of the trade deadline week after their all-in moves, though two of the three defenders they traded for will not appear against the Titans.
Even without Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III on hand , the Jaguars will have a high standard on defense. The Jaguars do not like how many rushing yards they allowed to the Baltimore Ravens last week, just like they didn't like the fact that they didn't complete the shutout against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8. With that in mind, they are facing a Titans team that has played much better offensively as of late.
The Titans offense has flirted with being ranked in the top-half of teams in terms of both offensive EPA/Play and Success Rate after their big scoring outputs against the Cleveland Browns and Cincinnati Bengals. Cam Ward is playing better after early-season struggles, and Tony Pollard has been amongst the NFL's most productive runners over the last few weeks. This isn't the hapless Titans offense from the start of the year, even without Carnell Tate.
But the Jaguars' defense simply feels like it has been hitting on all cylinders. The only quarterbacks to really have success against them this season in terms of moving the ball have been CJ Stroud and Joe Burrow, and Ward is not that. The Jaguars can't afford to treat the Titans like the Ravens a week ago, but this should still be a game that they control.
On the other side of the ball, the Titans have lost their two best defenders in Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker due to trades, and the numbers have reflected it. It does not feel like their secondary should be able to keep up with the Jaguars, and I am going Jacksonville 34, Titans 12 in this one.
John Shipley has been covering the Jacksonville Jaguars as a beat reporter and publisher of Jaguar Report since 2019. Previously, he covered UCF's undefeated season as a beat reporter for NSM.Today, covered high school prep sports in Central Florida, and covered local sports and news for the Palatka Daily News. title: Jaguars Week 10 Rooting Guide: How Jacksonville Can Propel Themselves in AFC
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars could take a serious step toward the No. 1 seed in the AFC with the right results in Week 10.
That, of course, starts and ends with the Jaguars getting the job done against the Tennessee Titans in Nashville on Sunday. But as long as the Jaguars do what they are supposed to do against the TItans, there is a real path toward their position in the AFC strengthening this week.
So, what else do the Jaguars need to happen this week, outside of a win against the Titans? We break it down below.
The Jaguars have several teams elsewhere in the AFC who they are set to be fighting for the top spot in the AFC. One of those teams is the Chiefs, who are sitting at 6-2 entering a game with the Atlanta Falcons. The Chiefs do not have that many wins over quality opponents this season, but the middling Falcons teams are also not really a quality opponent, are they? The Falcons will also be without Jessie Bates III after the blockbuster that sent him to the Jaguars, though the Chiefs will also be without Kenneth Walker.
A Chiefs loss and a Jaguars win would put the Jaguars firmly in front of the Chiefs in the AFC standings moving into Week 11. The Jaguars need any edge and momentum they can get, and this would certainly be a good way to start building some momentum during the start of the second-half push.
The Jaguars will obviously be rooting against the Houston Texans each and every single week until the scenario actually occurs where they are in the Indianapolis Colts/Tennessee Titans category of “oh, who cares.” It is far from a guarantee that happens since they have a relatively easy second-half schedule and still have a very talented quarterback, but they have lost several games already this year that they never should have let happen.
The Browns upsetting the Texans would be far from the most surprising result of the 2026 season. The Texans are set to be missing a lot of key players due to injuries. The Texans have the quarterback advantage by far with Stroud over Deshaun Watson, but the Jaguars would really be boosted by a Texans loss in any shape or form this week.
This one ... does not feel like it is going to happen! It is the NFL, and stranger things have happened I suppose. But the Jets have been one of the NFL's biggest losers over the last few seasons and I do not think Aaron Glenn's group is going to suddenly figure things out against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills, who have simply found ways to win this year.
There will still be chances for the Bills to tumble over the next few weeks and months ahead. With that said, they have several easy games against the AFC East, and this is one of them with some certainty. This should not be an issue.
Rooting Interest: Steelers
This one really could go either way since the Jaguars are in a race with both teams to the top of the AFC. The reason why I say the Steelers here instead of the Bengals is because I am of the belief that the Bengals are the greater threat to the Jaguars for the No. 1 seed, especially considering their schedule for the rest of the season. The Bengals losing feels like it would be good news for the Jaguars.
The Jaguars will get to face off against the Steelers in a few weeks, too. For right now, they are 3-0 against the AFC North. Getting the sweep against the four teams up north after a win against the Steelers would put the Jaguars in a good spot when it comes to tie breakers.
