title: Grading Every Jaguars Starter Halfway Through the Season: From Bhayshul Tuten to Ventrell Miller
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are at the halfway point, and the second-half of the season is set to be even more critical than the first stretch of the season was.
The Jaguars are sitting at 6-2 and as one of the top team's in the AFC entering their ninth game of the  season, a clash with the Tennessee Titans in Nashville on Sunday. So, how has each of the Jaguars' key pieces played a part in that climb to the top of the AFC South? We break it down below by grading each starter and key depth player who might as well be counted as a starter ... of which there are several.
So, which Jaguars have been at the top of their game this season as the Jaguars are set to go all-in? We break it down below.
We have said it once, we will say it again. Trevor Lawrence has played at an MVP-level during the 2026 season, and for our money he has been the best player on the Jaguars' roster this season. Lawrence is having the best season of his career and he could see his numbers go up even more in the weeks to come.
If Trevor Lawrence has been the best player for the Jaguars this season, than Bhayshul Tuten's name is not far behind. He has been one of the best and most productive running backs in football this season. Tuten is the entire spark behind the Jaguars' running game.
It has not been all bad for Brian Thomas Jr. He caught a touchdown in a close win over the Cincinnati Bengals, is one of six Jaguars with multiple receiving touchdowns, and has been on the winning side of some important blocks throughout the season. The drops and dip in production bring him down to this grade, though there is time to turn things around still.
Parker Washington's production has not completely exploded this season, but the first- and second-half splits make it clear that this is the result of the Jaguars getting in blowouts and just killing the clock during second halfs of most games. He has been the Jaguars' No. 1 receiver and best big-play threat when all things have been equal.
Jakobi Meyers has been terrific for the Jaguars as a middle of the field target, which is exactly where Liam Coen and Trevor Lawrence have been looking to attack defenses in the passing game. His numbers would be even better if he got a higher volume of passes. He is still playing really, really good football.
Brenton Strange looks like he is on the verge of another career season. He has been explosive in the passing game and has once again been a weapon for the Jaguars in the running game and as a blocker in space.
Walker Little has been one of the best pass-blockers in football since he stepped into the starting lineup for an injured Anton Harrison a few weeks ago. He will need to continue to give the Jaguars such a boost as they look to make their playoff run, but he has been rock-solid thus far.
Emmanuel Pregnon has made a strong impression for the Jaguars as a rookie, even if he is one of the lower-graded starters. He has done a good job to help improve the running game, especially in between the tackles. He has to clean up the penalties, but he has a bright future.
Robert Hainsey has once again been reliable for the Jaguars. He has not had many operational mistakes outside of the Eagles game, and he has done a good job spearheading some of the space blocking the line does in Coen's scheme.
Ezra Cleveland has once again been solid for the Jaguars, offering them efficient and quality play as both a run-blocker and pass-blocker. He has had a few reps where he has been beaten, just like any other offensive lineman, but he has been a key piece of the offense as a whole.
Cole Van Lanen had a bit of a slower start to this season, which was expected considering he was coming off of injury. But he has had some real quality performances as of late, and his best football should still be ahead of him.
Josh Hines-Allen has seen his numbers go down as a pure pass-rusher, but he has been the top play-maker of the defensive line considering the pressures that have led to turnovers that he has produced. He has also had a very, very strong year against the run once again.
Davon Hamilton looked like the MVP of the defense until his season-ending injury. Losing him as the anchor of the defense is the reason they went out and made the Jordan Davis move, after all. Hamilton was having the best season of his entire career.
Arik Armstead has made some big plays for the Jaguars this year as a pass-rusher, though there have also been the few games where his impact has been more hit and miss than it perhaps was last season.
Travon Walker has been the Jaguars' most productive pass-rusher and he has once again had a very strong season against the run. Finishing on a few more of his pressures would have him even higher on this list.
Foyesade Oluokun is playing some of the best football of his career lately. He has made big plays as a blitzer, against the run, and in coverage. He has also been on the right end of some of the biggest plays of the season, such as his red-zone interception of Joe Burrow in the Week 4 win over the Cincinnati Bengals.
Ventrell Miller has not just had the best season of his career, but he has been one of the top linebackers in football on a down-to-down basis. He simply does not make many mistakes, and his physical brand of football lets him fly around and get in on the action frequently. He is a plus-run defender and blitzer/
Dennis Gardeck has done some truly good things for the Jaguars as a rotational pass-rusher off the edge and he has been rock solid at the outside linebacker spot like he was a year ago as well. He is simply just a good football player.
Travis Hunter has been everything the Jaguars could have ever hoped for at cornerback. He has two interceptions, both of which came in clutch moments in the red-zone. He also had an interception negated against the Bengals and has been extremely close to interceptions in games against the Denver Broncos and Indianapolis Colts. He is a true shut down cornerback.
Jarrian Jones has seen a lot of passes go his way as teams have stayed away from Travis Hunter for long stretches, and he has played much better than anyone has really given him credit for. A few missed tackles are the only reason his grade is even just a B.
Montaric Brown's numbers have been better in recent weeks, though he certainly did not have a hot start to the season. An early-season hamstring injury also limited his impact, but he has had two terrific performances in back-to-back weeks since coming back from the bye week healthy.
Jourdan Lewis has once again been strong in the run game and as a blitzer, and he also has recorded three timely interceptions this season. He has once agaain been a reliable piece of the Jaguars' defense.
Eric Murray or Rayuan Lane was the option here, but Murray has started more games and played more snaps. I thought Murray was having a solid season before his season-ending elbow injury, playing at about the same level he played for the Jaguars last season. He is now set to be replaced by Jessie Bates next week.
The turnovers have perhaps not been there for Antonio Johnson so far the way they were a year ago, but he has been a key piece of what the Jaguars do. He can play in the box, cover tight ends, making an impact as a blitzer and in the running game. He has had his best year as a pro in terms of simple down-to-down consistency.
Cam Little has once again had a strong season for the Jaguars, and he is just a few missed kicks away from being perfect. He has missed one of his 26 extra point attempts and two of his 16 field goal attempts, though one of those would have been a record-breaking kick so let's not ding him too much for it.
The simple truth is that Logan Cook has not had to punt very much. Of all players with at least eight appearances at punter this seasom, Cook ranks No. 21 in punts but still ranks top-9 in yards per punt and net punting. 15 of his 28 punts have been touchbacks, and his 8.1 yards allowed per punt return is…

title: Jaguars Rookie Stock Report: Weighing the Draft Class's Impact at the Midseason Point
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are at the halfway point of the 2026 season, which makes it the perfect time to take a look at the Jaguars' rookie class.
As Jaguars general manager James Gladstone has pointed out, the Jaguars value draft picks and high-volume classes , even if they also value using picks at all different points of the NFL calendar as well. The Jaguars' 2026 class was one of those high-volume classes, with the Jaguars making 10 picks and also keeping one undrafted free agent on the 53-man roster.
So, where does each rookie stand at the midseason point? We take a look below with the latest rookie stock report.
We have not added these two rookies to most rookie power rankings, but it is still worth taking a look at their time with the Jaguars halfway through 2026. Linebacker Parker Hughes, the Jaguars' final pick in the seventh-round, was placed on injured reserve this offseason and thus can not play this year.
Zach Durfee, the Jaguars' other seventh-round selection, was placed on injured reserve with a designation to return at the end of training camp, and he has spent his rookie season on injured reserve thus far as a result. He has not yet had his practice window opened to begin his way back from the injured reserve list.
The Jaguars' fourth-round pick has not yet been active as a rookie, serving as a healthy scratch for the first eight games of the season after making the 53-man roster out of training camp. The Jaguars traded up in the fourth-round to select Williams and clearly have high hopes for him moving forward, but he would be one of several young defenders who will have had to bide their time to get on the field.
With that said, the eventual return of BJ Green from injured reserve makes it seem unlikely we see Williams this season unless the Jaguars get some injuries at the defensive end position. We will be able to get more of a look at him when next year's offseason program rolls around.
CJ Williams can basically copy-and-paste and everything we said above for Wesley Williams. He was at least active and got some playing time in Week 1, but otherwise the Jaguars have had CJ Williams inactive this season as they have rolled with just four full-time receivers on most game days. Part of this is because they also have been carrying four tight ends most games , while Travis Hunter can also act as a fifth receiver for depth purposes. It is unlikely we see Williams unless there is an injury at wide receiver.
Jalen Huskey spent the first month sidelined as a healthy scratch, but he has played in three of the last four games and played his first 37 defensive snaps of his career in the last two weeks against the Indianapolis Colts and Baltimore Ravens. Huskey recorded a sack and three combined tackles in the process, giving him some solid flashes in his first chance at playing time this season. With that said, the trade for Jessie Bates III makes it seem like Huskey is once again set to be a healthy scratch on game day more often than not.
The Jaguars' third-round pick did not play a ton of snaps over the last month, but he did play a career-high 20+ snaps against the Ravens on Thursday Night Football. He played well in his first extended run in the middle of the Jaguars' defense, though it could be tough for him to get much playing time moving forward. Regis is set to be one of the players most impacted by the Jaguars' trade deadline moves, which makes Week 9 likely the biggest stage he will get this season.
Perhaps Regis is active against the Tennessee Titans in Week 10, but the Jaguars are set to have Davon Godchaux still make his debut at defensive tackle. The Jaguars often have four defensive tackles active, and you can consider Arik Armstead, Ruke Orhorhoro, and Matt Dickerson already accounted for as well.
Tanner Koziol did not play much at the start of the season, but he is starting to see more and more snaps in recent weeks. Koziol could easily rise a few spots on these rankings depending on how the Jaguars deploy him down the stretch, but he went from a game day healthy scratch to a real part of their multiple-tight end sets. He has even had a few passes thrown his way in the last few weeks as a result, which indicates that the arrow could be pointing up on the Jaguars' athletic fifth-round tight end moving forward.
The lone undrafted free agent to make the roster this season, Bryan Thomas Jr. has played a real role as the No. 4 defensive end in the Jaguars' rotation behind Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker. He has had a very similar role as second-year defensive end Danny Striggow, serving as the top backups behind Hines-Allen and Walker, as well as linebacker Dennis Gardeck on passing downs. There does exist the possibility that he could be inactive moving forward, too, since BJ Green is returning eventually.
Josh Cameron has been a home run Day 3 pick for the Jaguars, catching nine passes for 123 yards and two touchdowns while also serving as a key special teamer and a key part of the Jaguars' running game in 12 and 13 personnel sets. Cameron has played a very real role in the Jaguars' offensive plans, even if the ball is not going his way all that often. It will be fascinating to see what he develops into, because he has already proven to be a versatile and high-ceiling option for the Jaguars, which is always a win on Day 3.
The Jaguars made a lot of waves when they selected Nate Boerkircher at No. 56 overall (for some reason). Yes, it was a "reach" by the consensus, but the Jaguars were clearly a team looking to shift toward more 12 and 13 personnel, and the No. 56 pick oddly got treated like the Jaguars just spent a top-10 pick on a blocking tight end. Boerkircher has caught nine passes for 144 yards and two touchdowns, making him an efficient and effective target despite being a low-volume one.
How about this from Next Gen Stats when it comes to the rookie tight end: "Boerkircher leads tight ends with 12.0 yards per target and is fourth among tight ends with 9.1 air yards per target (minimum 10 targets). Despite his deeper depth of target and league-high 33.3% tight window target rate (<1 yard of separation), he has caught 9 of his 12 targets (75.0%) for 144 yards and two touchdowns. His average route speed of 12.95 miles per hour is 9th among tight ends with at least 75 routes run."
Our pick for the Jaguars' rookie of the year to this point, Emmanuel Pregnon has spent each snap at left guard for the Jaguars this season. He has had some issues with penalties here and there, but the Jaguars have also seen him play some solid football in eight straight starts at the left guard position after winning the starting job coming out of training camp. Pregnon has been rock-solid for the Jaguars more often than not as a rookie, and he has a big future beyond 2026.
Pregnon and left tackle Walker Little have done some good things on the left side in recent weeks, and the Jaguars should feel good about the duo holding down the fort on that side of the line after the loss of Anton Harrison for the season.

title: What Does the Jaguars' War Chest of Draft Picks Look Like After Explosive Trade Deadline?
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars made the biggest splashes of the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline, and now it is time to reassess.
After three trades on Monday for Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates III, Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis, and New Orleans Saints defensive tackle Davon Godchaux, the Jaguars packaged quite the cache of picks to send away for some immediate impacts.
Over the deadline, the Jaguars dealt a 2027 first-round pick, 2027 second-round pick, 2028 fifth-round pick, a conditional 2028 sixth-round pick, and a second-round pick in 2029. It is important to note that some of the Jaguars' strategy is rooted in the compensatory draft pick game , which sometimes can not be fully accounted for until all picks are official.
"It's in the volume of picks that's important, and it ties back to how we operated in free agency this past spring. Not signing external free agents is an important piece when you have internal free agents signing elsewhere that can earn you a compensatory pick, thus supplementing the loss of any other draft selection that you may choose to use outside the three days that exist in April to make a selection," Jaguars general manager James Gladstone said this week.
"It's a very symbiotic process that encompasses a lot of layers to it, but it's certainly not ‘eff them picks.’ While that's been characterized as the approach, it's not necessarily—we actually value picks. We don't always use them on the three days that exist in April.”
So, what does the Jaguars' current accumulation of draft picks look like over the next three-year window after the latest days of wheeling and dealing from Gladstone and the Jaguars? We break it down below.
The Jaguars will have just one top-100 pick as things presently stand after trading their first- and second-round picks for Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates. The Jaguars are also projected to get a second sixth-round compensatory pick, though one of those would have to go to the New Orleans Saints as part of the trade for Davon Godchaux. If the Jaguars do not get awarded a single sixth-round compensatory pick, which seems highly unlikely, then they would have to send a 2028 sixth-round pick.
As things are right now under those conditions, the Jaguars would have six picks. That is a good bit lower of a number than the Jaguars have drafted with in the past two seasons, which could be recouped with trade downs or any potential offseason trades.
The Jaguars have all of their top-100 picks for the 2028 class (for now, at least!), but they do only have four picks overall. The fifth-round pick is going to Atlanta, their sixth-round pick went to Miami for Quinn Ewers in August, and the seventh-round pick given to Arizona as a part of the Hunter Long trade. As a result of having so few picks in this draft, it can be expected that the Jaguars will once again play the compensatory game and try not to sign too many free agents, if any at all.
The Jaguars have a number of experienced and productive players on expiring deals such as Arik Armstead, Davon Hamilton, Ezra Cleveland, Ventrell Miller, and Antonio Johnson, meaning there Jaguars could have several chances to add Day 3 picks via the compensatory pick system as long as they do not spend much in March. As things stand today, we can probably expect the Jaguars to sit out free agency once again.
The Jaguars are looking healthy in 2029, though they are missing their second-round pick due to the Jordan Davis deal. Otherwise, the Jaguars have six picks at their disposal to deal with in the 2029 NFL Draft, including their first-round pick as a potential trade piece like they used their 2027 and 2026 first-round picks as in the Davis and Travis Hunter trades over the years.
As things stand today, the Jaguars are projected to have 16 picks over the next three years. Here is how they get divided.
That means the Jaguars have six of their nine top-100 picks over the next three years, at least before any other moves are made. They have multiple picks in every round but the second-round, which is also a round the Jaguars have touched just once in the first two years of the Gladstone era. Ultimately, the Jaguars are missing a first, two seconds, a sixth, and a seventh.
If the Jaguars can get comp picks over the next free agency cycle or two, they could reasonably get back to nearly seven picks a draft, even without getting their top-100 picks back. The Jaguars have a clear direction they can take to get back to a high volume of picks, but they are in a good spot outside of Day 3 of 2028 right now. Those picks will likely be addressed in March and impact their free agency plans.

title: 4 Jaguars Facing Critical Opportunities Before Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates Make Their Debuts
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- It will be one more week until the Jacksonville Jaguars introduce two of their new faces on defense, which gives several players one more chance to make a big impression before the lineup and rotations change.
The Jaguars are set to sit defensive tackle Jordan Davis and safety Jessie Bates III against the Tennessee Titans in Week 10, with head coach Liam Coen opting to give the veteran pair the bye week they never got with the Philadelphia Eagles and Atlanta Falcons.
That means a few players will continue to play key roles for the Jaguars defensively when they face off with the Titans , players who Coen says have already ramped things up in practice following the additions of Bates, Davis, and defensive tackle Davon Godchaux.
“Yeah, I thought Wednesday was a really good practice. I thought yesterday started a little bit slow on offense, but it got a lot better. Defense, I thought, had a great practice. Offense threw it and caught it really well. It was competitive, I thought you could feel the competitive juice a little bit," Coen said.
"Albert Regis, Matt Dickerson, a lot of guys that obviously are going to be somehow impacted by these trades. It's just natural. I felt an uptick in competition and urgency, and I think these guys are going to go into this weekend understanding that the standard doesn't change. We have to continue to get better and it's about us and the way that we perform, the way we prepare and I'm excited about getting out there today to see what that looks like.”
So, which Jaguars have one more chance to make a big impression in Week 10 against the Titans? We break it down below.
One of the key cogs of the Jaguars' defensive tackle depth the last two easons has been veteran defensive tackle Matt Dickerson. He earned a spot on the active roster last year after starting out first on the practice squad before eventually elevating himself to the game day roster thanks to some performances in practice. This year, he has played 30% of the Jaguars' defensive snaps and he has appeared in all eight games with one start, which game last week against the Baltimore Ravens.
Dickerson got the nod to start at nose tackle in Week 9 due to the injury to Davon Hamilton, though that remains to be seen if it will be the case in Week 10 due to the debut of Godchaux. He will get snaps though since Davis will not be playing, a case that may not remain the same next week against the New York Giants. Dickerson making a big impact this week in his role could go a long way for him to still have a spot in the rotation once Davis makes his debut.
Jaguars third-round rookie defensive tackle Albert Regis has appeared in four of the Jaguars' eight games, but the injury to Davon Hamilton led to Regis playing nearly half of his rookie year snaps in one game against the Baltimore Ravens. Regis got a career-high 21 snaps against the Ravens on Thursday Night Football, rotating with Dickerson at nose tackle and making a few plays in the process.
It might not be a sure thing that Regis is active this week, though it would make sense to have him active with Godchaux still being such a new addition. If he does get on the field, it could be his last time being active this season unless the Jaguars end up getting hit with more injuries at defensive tackle. That is worth making an impression for.
Over a quarter of Rayuan Lane's career defensive snaps have come in the last two weeks after the Jaguars lost Eric Murray to a season-ending injury. He averaged fewer than seven defensive snaps a game as a rookie but has almost doubled his rookie year snap total in 2026, playing a career-high 60 snaps against the Colts in Week 9 and then making his second-career start against the Ravens last week.
Lane should still get snaps as the team's third safety once Bates is in the starting lineup next to Antonio Johnson from Weeks 11 onward. But unless the Jaguars see any injuries to Bates or Johnson, this could be the last start Lane makes in 2026. He has earned a real spot in the defense thanks to his recent performances, and this could be another chance for him to continue to impress.
Jaguars third-round rookie safety Jalen Huskey has appeared in three of the Jaguars' last four games after not getting a game day nod during the first month of the season. The last two weeks have been especially big for Huskey, with him recording three tackles and his first career sack in Week 8 against the Colts and then playing 10 defensive snaps against the Baltimore Ravens last week.
With Bates heading into the lineup next week, though, this could be the last time we see Huskey active for a bit. The Jaguars clearly have Lane and Merriweather ahead of him in the pecking order at safety, which means the Jaguars would have to take five safeties into a game to have Huskey active beyond this week.

title: Jaguars Midseason Awards: Trevor Lawrence, Travis Hunter Headline AFC South's Top Team
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are at their halfway point, and there has been a lot of good football in the first nine weeks.
The Jaguars are set to kick off the second-half of their season in Week 10 against the Tennessee Titans, which gives us some time to take a look at how the first-half of the season played out exactly. With the Jaguars sitting at 6-2, how did they get there exactly?
We take a look at our Jaguars superlatives for the first-half of their season, with a nod to the players who best helped the Jaguars get in position for a playoff run in the AFC. So, who wins MVP, Rookie of the Year, and more?
For my money, the Jaguars' best player so far this year has been quarterback Trevor Lawrence. He is making throws every single week that defy logic, and in all of the best ways. He has improved in really every possible metric this season, and he is arguably playing better football now than he did when he had hot runs in 2022, 2023, and 2025. Lawrence looks like an MVP, and it stands to reason that his elite-level play is the biggest reason the Jaguars have felt comfortable making so many big moves over the last two years.
There are a few different players who earned consideration here, such as Bhayshul Tuten. But at the end of the day. the second-most impactful Jaguars player week-to-week has been Travis Hunter in his role as a top cornerback for the franchise's top-ranked defense. We will talk more about Hunter later but, for now, it is only right to give Lawrence his flowers as the Jaguars' best and most impactful player in 2026 so far.
Runner Up: Parker Washington
Bhayshul Tuten has been one of the best running backs in football this season. He had big shoes to fill after the departure of Travis Etienne, but he has done a great job filling them. He has shown the full gauntlet this season, leading the Jaguars in touchdowns and scrimmage yards while showing off speed, toughness, and every trait needed out of a top back. He has been a true home run Day 3 pick for the Jaguars out of their 2025 draft class.
There is a real chance we see Travis Hunter get a Pro Bowl nod or All-Pro votes at the end of the year if he continues along his current trajectory. He has developed into a true shutdown cornerback, showing off play-making skills with two stellar red-zone interceptions. He has also played the run well and has simply taken off as he gets more and more reps at the cornerback spot. He has effectively taken away half of the field for the Jaguars' defense.
Part of the reason the Jaguars made such big moves along the defensive line has to do with the loss of Davon Hamilton for the season. Hamilton was having the best year of his career in 2026 and looked like the most important part of the defense as he set the tone against the run and freed up other play-makers throughout the front. Ventrell Miller would have been my third pick for this spot.
This is a close one, and really you can give it to any one of Emmanuel Pregnon, Nate Boerkircher, or Josh Cameron. I am going to give the nod to Pregnon because he has had solid tape, solid metrics, and has started every single game for the Jaguars' high-powered offense this season. He can still improve, of course, but so far he looks like a major hit in the third-round. This should be the start of a long and productive career for Pregnon at the left guard spot, and he should only be able to build off of this momentum moving forward.
Boerkircher and Cameron have each played big roles for the Jaguars in 12 and 13 personnel, with Boerkircher catching two touchdowns and a 50+ yard pass over the last three games. Cameron has been reliable as a blocker and as a pass-catcher, and all three of these young players look like they are going to play important roles for the Jaguars' offense for years to come. The best is not yet here for this group, but these three players have all been very productive draft picks to date for the franchise.
Linebackers coach Tem Lukabu has once again overseen a stellar pair of linebackers in Foyesade Oluokun and Ventrell Miller. A year after Devin Lloyd had his breakout season under Lukabu, Miller is now one of the league's most impressive and consistent linebackers, while Oluokun is having one of the best years of his entire career. Running backs coach Chad Morton deserves to be shouted out, too, but it is Lukabu who gets the nod here.
“I think Tem's done a phenomenal job. I've known Tem for a long time. I've always respected the job that he's done on the defensive side of the football. He's coordinated at Boston College and at a high level in college. And if you look at over the course of the last year, obviously Devin [Panthers LB Devin Lloyd] having the success he had last year, and then everybody is worried about that and what are we going to do there?" Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said on Friday.
"I think Branson's [LB Branson Combs] improved tremendously. Ventrell has helped us tremendously. I think that Tem does such a good job because the standard is so high. He holds those guys to the same standard of Foye every single day in the meeting room, the way they communicate, the way they practice. It's a high standard and Tem's done a phenomenal job.”

title: Jaguars-Titans Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Full-Go Status Puts Focus on Rushing Attack
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars have a clean injury report after their mini-bye week, giving them a healthy roster entering into Week 10.
The Jaguars are set to be without Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III against the Titans as the Jaguars give them their bye week, while defensive end BJ Green will also be out as he works his way back from the injured reserve list.
That leaves several Jaguars players who are dealing with injuries and missing some practice time as full-go for Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans, including starting running back Bhayshul Tuten. With Tuten set to play, the Jaguars can now put their focus on a running game rebounding from a down Week
Tuten played in last week's game against the Baltimore Ravens despite not practicing that week with a foot/ankle injury, and he also sat out the first two practice days this week. He ended up getting 12 carries for 29 yards and a touchdown a week ago and did participate in Friday's practice as a limited participant, giving him the green light for Sunday against the Titans.
"I think it's usually case by case in general. You want practice performance equals game reality every week, but it's also a fine line and every situation's different. I think with the running back position, it's one of those that ultimately, you can play and not practice a ton because the runs are the runs," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Friday before practice.
"I think it's very hard for quarterback or offensive line and things like that where there's a lot of adjustments, communication involved on the offensive side of the ball, specifically. So Tuten will run around today and buzz around. So, he'll be good to go on Sunday.”
With Tuten in the line up and set to go without any limitations, the Jaguars should look to him to spark a running game that has been strong throughout the year but slipped a bit last week against the Ravens. He clearly was not 100% against the Ravens, but it was tough sledding for every member of the backfield, not just him.
The Jaguars had their third-worst rushing performance in terms of EPA/Rush during the 25-game Coen era on Thursday Night Football. Part of this had to do with execution, while another part of it had to do with a run-heavy second-half script after the Jaguars got up on the Ravens at halftime. Add in some bad weather that took the ball out of the hands of the passing game, and the Jaguars' rushing attack had the perfect storm for a regression game.
"You're in a setting where you're kind of running it, they know you're running it, everybody thinks that's easy, it's not. When you're not throwing it, you're not as balanced in those settings, and the weather and all that kind of played a part," Coen said last week. "It's that fine line of alright, we're going to keep our foot on the gas and go score 50 while not putting your quarterback and guys in harm's way as well when you know you kind of have the game wrapped up. So frustrating for sure in the moment. In the grand scheme of things, not concerned with those things at all.”
As Coen said, there should be no long-term concerns. But in an AFC where the race for the No. 1 seed will be important week in and week out, and the Jaguars will need their running game to continue hitting its stride over the second-half of the season.
The Jaguars' offense is at its best when its running game is hitting all cylinders since it allows Coen and Trevor Lawrence to lean into the play-action game, and because it keeps defenses on their heels when the Jaguars have a balanced attack. The balance needs the running game to make it work, and that running game needs to have a better outting this week.

title: Jaguars Mailbag: How the Dust Has Settled in Duval After Wild Trade Deadline
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The dust has settled from the NFL Trade Deadline, and the Jacksonville Jaguars are set to be back on the field in just a few days.
The Jaguars are set to visit the Tennessee Titans in Week 10, and there is certainly a buzz around the game after the Jaguars' busy week of trades, even with Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis set to miss the game.
In this week's Jaguars mailbag, we take a look at the fallout from the trades, what is ahead for the team, and much more.
Re: Godchaux Trade Did the Jags give up a 2026 or 2027 6th round pick? pic.twitter.com/sejPorIAPR
A: It is honestly a really interesting trade because I am not sure I have ever seen this kind of condition in a trade? It is a 2028 6th-round pick if the Jaguars do not end up getting a 2027 6th-round pick ... but the Jaguars are expected to get a sixth-round pick in the compensatory draft pick formula before next April. So, it is bascially going to be a sixth-round pick.
Do you think without D-Ham going down for the season they still make as big a splash as they did with Davis for say an Edge or true 3T DT, or did they just happen to find their player due to the injury need and who was actually made available aligning?
A: This is my take, and it is just a gut take: I think we can now say that the Jaguars were never going to leave this year's deadline with their first-round pick. They crave the trades. They yearn for the trades. Their stance is that they value picks, because it can help them year-round. They have made 12 trades not counting draft-day trades since the start of 2025. I think they were going to make a blockbuster even before the Davon Hamilton deal, though I am sure that still played a factor.
Everyone says Jordan Davis is a big-time run stuffer. And while that was his primary job in Philly, doesn't he possess pass rush abilities that could be just as needed in the interior?
A: There are a few layers to this. The way the Eagles used Davis was certainly as an early-down player. He was asked to hold the line of scrimmage and two-gap and react to blocks than he was asked to simply get upfield. With that said, he also did have his fair share of snaps at three-technique with the Eagles. There were chances for him to cash-in on production as a pass-rusher, and he did take advantage of those chances during his breakout 2025 season. I do think Davis has plenty of physical traits to suggest he has not yet had his talent tapped into. I think the Jaguars will let him play on more third downs than the Eagles did, though, which could be what he really needs. The Jaguars need him and BJ Green to make an impact there.
Now is anything missing from the Jags roster?
I think every team still has weaknesses. There is no juggernaut with a flawless team this year, though the Jaguars are maybe the closest thing through nine weeks. The Jaguars' offensive line has played mostly-well as a unit, but it will be a group that continues to get tested. They play a few disruptive edge rushers over the next three weeks before Jeffery Simmons after that, which should give us a barometer of where they are really at.
how does the addition of Jessie Bates change the likelihood of keeping Parker? and which player is a better candidate for the franchise tag if it comes to that?
I don't think it changes it that much, honestly. The Jaguars have been in the business of keeping their core pieces since the start of the 2025 offseason, and I think Washington is one of those pieces like Travon Walker was last season, and others before him. There are a few other guys who I could see walking, but Washington is not one of them. It would be more expensive to do for Washington, which could give them even more motivation to get him signed in the event they have to tag Jessie Bates.
Who is the 3rd safety now when Bates and Johnson are active: Merriweather or Lane? Will Huskey return to being inactive each week?
I think Rayuan Lane, who I believe is going to start against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday now that we know Jessie Bates isn't going to play . Lane has done some good things for the Jaguars this season and they certainly view him as more than just a special teams player. I think once Bates is in the lineup, the safety depth chart will have Lane at the No. 3 spot, Kaevon Merriweather at the No. 4 spot, and Jalen Huskey likely inactive like he was earlier in the season. This room has played well since the injuries hit, and they deserve another week in the sun in Week 10.
What's the transition period for Bates to fully understand the playbook/make calls in the backend. He's known as one of the smartest players in the NFL, but when would he be comfortable enough to translate what he sees, with his years of experience, to the other, younger DBs?
I think we will see Bates step into that kind of role very quickly. It might not take much time for him to step up as the true leader and voice of the unit; Jakobi Meyers made an impression at wide receiver in that same fashion a year ago. I think we will see his impact made on the rest of the younger secondary as early as Week 11 against the New York Giants.
Can Godchaux and Davis play DT at the same time, sparing some Armstead early down reps with the hope that he’s more efficient as a pass rusher? If not, how do you see the DT rotation playing out? Maybe Godchaux gets some reps against the run to give Davis some on 3rd down?
I absolutely think so. I think both guys can play both three-technique and nose tackle in the Jaguars' defense on early downs, something the Jaguars have done with their defensive tackles even before the Davon Hamilton injury. I think you will see Davis and Godchaux lead the way at the nose tackle spot, but they can also use them interchangbly with Arik Armstead, Ruke Orhorhoro, and Matt Dickerson.
Aside from an injury, what could derail the team from a deep playoff run? I would say the play of the CBs not named Travis Hunter; what about you?
A: The offensive line against an elite front. Them against the Denver Broncos' front would be a ... matchup to watch.
Let’s say the Jags make the playoffs and get a high seed. Who’s the one wildcard team you don’t want to see and why is it the Texans?
I would take the Jaguars against any of the other teams in the AFC right now. I think my answer though is Buffalo, just because of Josh Allen and what he can do to a team when he gets on a roll like he did a year ago. Houston is close due to CJ Stroud and a defense that I believe is still talented. The Bengals and Broncos are on the same tier, but for opposite reasons. The Bengals have a great offense but I think the Jaguars can get after their defense. The Broncos have a great defense, but I think the Jaguars can get after their offense.
Who do you think the Jags will let walk in free agency to keep their compensatory strategy going this offseason?
A: I think Arik Armstead and Ezra Cleveland are the locks. Davon Hamilton is one to at least consider with the future of the nose tackle spot clearly being spearheaded by Jordan Davis moving forward. Antonio Johnson and Ventrell Miller are two I am torn on. I could see them coming back like Montaric Brown did, but it might depend on the price tag.
Is there any realistic scenario where Camp stays?
Realistic? Sure. I think Anthony Campanile has deserved a shot to be one of the league's top head coach candidates in 2027 no matter how the rest of this season plays out. I also think teams are so into the mindset of hiring offensive coaches that I am not sure if there will be the perfect fit for Campanile quite yet. I think there is a chance he stays because of this reason, while I think the odds are smaller for offensive coordinator Grant Udinski. For example, I do not agree with it but it feels like the New York Jets would be hard-pressed to hire another first-year head coach with a defensive background after the Saleh-Glenn back-to-back attempts.
What will it take for the media to realize that Gladstone isn’t going…

title: Why the Jaguars Are Making the Right Call Slow-Playing the Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates Debuts
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars will have to wait one more week for the debuts of Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III.
"Jesse Bates and Jordan Davis will not play on Sunday due to not having a bye," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said on Friday.
"With their workload and the way the season falls from a scheduling standpoint, we want to be able to make sure that we're in player safety, putting them in a position to succeed. Also, learn the system, and just give those guys a week to be able to do that. So neither one will be playing on Sunday."
Not having either of their new pieces in Week 10 against the Tennessee Titans means their debuts will come in Week 11 against the New York Giants, and there are plenty of reasons why the Jaguars look to be making the right moves.
With the way the Jaguars are set to deploy Davon Godchaux in Week 10 against the Titans, it is clear the Jaguars are making this move based simply on the bye weeks. Godchaux got his bye week with the New Orleans Saints in Week 8, while Davis and Bates have each already played nine games this season. This trend goes back to last year, too, when the Jaguars made in-season trades for cornerback Greg Newsome and for wide receiver Jakobi Meyers.
Newsome was traded to the Jaguars before Week 6, just five weeks into the season. He got his bye week when the Jaguars got theirs in Week 8 that season. Meanwhile, Meyers already had his bye week when his trade to the Jaguars was completed after Week 9, which meant he would not be playing an extra game despite the trade.
Davis and Bates have each had rest days during their first two practice days with the Jaguars, which was the first indication that neither might play in their first Jaguars game in Nashville. The Jaguars have thus slow-played their onboarding process compared to other players they have drafted in the past, but neither player is in the situations Newsome, Meyers, or Godchaux were in.
Asking two veteran players to play 18 games would have made little sense for the Jaguars. And if the Jaguars feel like they needed Davis and Bates to do so to beat the Titans in Week 10, that would have rung quite a few alarms. Jacksonville beat the Baltimore Ravens last week before making any of these trades, and they are 6-2 for a reason. They would have been one of the best teams in the AFC regardless of their trade deadline moves, so this doesn't change much for them considering it is likely to be just for a week.
The Jaguars are of course not taking the Titans lightly by not playing Bates and Davis, because they would almost positively be sitting them if they were playing the Buffalo Bills or Denver Broncos in Week 10. But the Jaguars are taking a big-picture view with their new pieces. They will need them more in January than they will need them to beat Cam Ward, Robert Saleh, and Tony Pollard on Sunday.
Teams do not often complete blockbusters without the expectation of immediate impact and production. The Jaguars are comfortable with that impact coming in Week 11 against the New York Giants instead of this Sunday, and it feels like the right and mature decision.

title: What Might Josh Downs’ Workload Look Like in His Chiefs Debut?
full_text:
After the Chiefs broke out of an offensive slump in last week's drubbing of the Jets, Kansas City made a splash before the trade deadline passed by adding Josh Downs . This move bolstered KC's questionable receiving corps and gave it an elite separator in the slot.
While the underwhelming production from Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy has left plenty to be desired this season, midseason receiver acquisitions historically take a while to become acclimated to the offense. Downs only has a few days of experience within Andy Reid's offensive scheme and likely doesn't know a good chunk of the playbook despite his efforts to get up to speed . As Kansas City's matchup against the Atlanta Falcons approaches, Downs is set to make his debut in a red and gold uniform tomorrow. His workload may not be as substantial as many people think.
The Chiefs may implement a more pass-heavy game plan than usual due to the absence of running back Kenneth Walker . Even so, that doesn't mean Downs will immediately be thrust into a high-volume role in the passing game.
Rice and Worthy will still account for a large portion of the snap count, and there may be certain packages where Reid isn't comfortable deploying him yet. At 5-foot-9, 171 pounds, Downs isn't exactly the type of receiver built to play every down. Across nine games in Indianapolis, Downs caught 33 passes for 354 yards and one touchdown . He was catching passes from Daniel Jones in the Colts' anemic passing attack, but he's never been much of a big-play threat. Downs is at his best when he's breaking down opposing defensive backs in man coverage.
The North Carolina product should be heavily featured on third downs and short-route concepts, which is where he excels most. Where he shouldn't be expected to produce much is on longer-developing plays and rushing formations.
Between the three receivers the Chiefs have traded for at the deadline (Kadarius Toney, Mecole Hardman, DeAndre Hopkins) in the past half-decade, none of them surpassed two receptions or 30 yards in their first Kansas City game — Hardman being an asterisk since it was his second stint with the franchise. Regardless, Downs could be in for a quiet afternoon if that trend continues.
Since Worthy is active while he battles back from a hamstring injury and Jalen Royals and Cyrus Allen remain in the mix, there's little reason for the Chiefs to keep Downs on the field every play.
After he spends a few weeks with the coaching staff and learns the ins and outs of the offense, Downs will be in line for a larger role. Until then, though, this transition period could take some time for the former Colts standout.

title: Without Kenneth Walker, Emmett Johnson is Key in Chiefs vs. Falcons
full_text:
The New York Jets were fully capable of being feisty last week, and the same can be said this week, perhaps even more so. The Chiefs passed Week 9’s test resoundingly, but this is also a road game for Kansas City, and Atlanta has a ton to play for.
The Falcons are 3-6, but the division is so weak this year that they're only half a game behind the 3-5 Carolina Panthers and the New Orleans Saints. Their wins include a 21-point victory over the 6-3 Green Bay Packers and a nine-point win over the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers.
They may have just signaled how good or bad they think they are by trading away safety Jessie Bates and starting center Ryan Neuzil, but they are still in the thick of the NFC South race, and they seem to be playing hard for first-year head coach Kevin Stefanski.
Plenty of weapons will be on the field Sunday at noon. Atlanta has wide receiver Drake London and tight end Kyle Pitts, while the Chiefs have Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice, and newcomer Josh Downs . But make no mistake: this game is all about the trenches and the run game on both sides. Let’s dig into those two matchups.
A wrinkle emerged in the Chiefs’ rushing-game plans late Friday afternoon when Kenneth Walker sat out of practice with groin tightness. Andy Reid said at the time that they would not put him at risk, and it appears Kansas City's brass is exercising caution.
Sources: #Chiefs star RB Kenneth Walker (groin) is OUT for Sunday’s game vs the #Falcons . I’m told the injury is not a long-term concern, but the team is playing it safe. pic.twitter.com/ODtxiueYp1
With Walker officially inactive for Week 10, rookie Emmett Johnson will draw the start. Walker is second only to Bijan Robinson in rushing this season, has already passed 1,000 yards from scrimmage, and has 11 total touchdowns, so his absence will hurt. Still, his long-term outlook matters more than a midseason game in Atlanta, and Johnson has proven to be a worthy backup.
Johnson does not get many opportunities, but when he does, he makes the most of them. The fifth-round pick out of Nebraska has only 26 carries, but is averaging 4.3 yards per carry and has one rushing touchdown.
He has been even more impressive through the air. Thanks to a big game against the Denver Broncos, Johnson has more receiving yards than Walker, on 19 fewer targets and 12 fewer receptions. He has three catches of more than 20 yards, is averaging 16.9 yards per reception, and has a receiving touchdown.
Perhaps the most impressive part of his game has been his forced-missed-tackle rate. According to PFF, he has amassed 22 missed tackles forced on his 42 touches. If the offensive line blocks for Johnson the way it did for Walker last week, it should be a big day for the ground game.
Atlanta is in the middle of the pack at 118 rushing yards allowed per game, but near the bottom of the league at 4.4 yards allowed per carry. Kansas City will need to establish the run because its starting tackles will be Kahlil Benson and Josh Ezeudu , who were third and fourth on the depth chart heading into the season. Establishing the run game will only help Patrick Mahomes and his tackles in the passing game.
The Chiefs’ defensive line and linebackers have the toughest matchup on the field, facing the NFL’s leading rusher, Bijan Robinson. He is a touchdown waiting to happen on any given play, on the ground or through the air.
He is averaging 5.2 yards per carry with 880 yards and five touchdowns through nine games. He also has 250 receiving yards and a touchdown this year, after posting over 800 yards and four touchdowns as a receiver last season. That means linebackers Nick Bolton and Drue Tranquill need to be at their best.
The Chiefs had a terrific run defense in 2024, weaponizing players like Leo Chenal, and that year, they held Robinson to a jaw-dropping 1.9 yards per carry, just 31 yards and a touchdown. This year, Kansas City ranks 10th in rush defense at just over 97 yards per game, and sixth in the NFL at 3.6 yards per carry.
While all of that is true, they have faced the 27th, 15th, 12th, 31st, 16th, 18th, and 20th-ranked rushing offenses. This is by far their biggest test of the season, and it is not easy to prepare for when you also have to worry about London on the outside.
Still, Kansas City is best off centering its game plan around stopping Robinson, given how poorly quarterback Michael Penix is playing. If the Chiefs force the Falcons into passing situations, the defense will have a much easier job.
According to PFF, Penix is the worst quarterback in the league under pressure, with a 28.8 completion percentage, one touchdown, three interceptions, and a 13.8 percent turnover-worthy play rate. For perspective, Trevor Lawrence has the next-highest rate at 9.2 percent. It may not be possible to do to Robinson what Kansas City did in 2024, but if the Chiefs can limit him to some degree, they should coast to victory.

title: Should the Chiefs Reunite with Hollywood Brown?
full_text:
Even though the Kansas City Chiefs acquired wide receiver Josh Downs just before the NFL trade deadline, the team's wide receiver depth chart still has room for more talent. Could a familiar face be the next addition? It's complicated.
On Thursday, the Philadelphia Eagles released wide receiver Marquise "Hollywood" Brown after a disappointing few months in Philly. He caught only five passes for 63 yards in four games with the Eagles. That pales in comparison to his 49-catch, 587-yard, five-touchdown season with the Chiefs in 2025. The Eagles have had an avalanche of issues this season, but Brown never found his role in Philadelphia.
Certainly, Brown isn't at the top of his game, but in his age-29 season, he also isn't beyond a potential resurgence in a reasonable role. So, should the Chiefs and Brown be viewing each other as solutions to the other's problem? Let's look at the pros and cons.
With Tyquan Thornton on injured reserve for the forseeable future , the Chiefs still lack a proven deep threat who can stretch opposing defenses and present a plausible target for a couple of deep shot attempts per game. Xavier Worthy has the requisite speed to stretch the field, but he's never seemed entirely comfortable or productive in that role.
Meanwhile, Brown wouldn't (and shouldn't) impact Downs' role in any way. Downs will step in as a short- and intermediate-level threat who can separate against man-to-man coverage; Brown would be doing an entirely different job if he were to return.
The biggest feather in Brown's cap is his familiarity with the Chiefs' offense. When Andy Reid discussed potential receiver additions before the deadline, he began by saying that he'd "hope they'd be familiar with the offense." Brown certainly is, after spending two years in Kansas City before his brief time in Philly. If the Chiefs have interest in adding another pass-catcher who should be comfortable in the system, Brown would check that box.
Andy Reid shares what he'd look for in a potential addition at WR: “You'd hope they'd be familiar with the offense. If they're not, they gotta be smart and be able to pick it up quickly — I've had players that have done that and done it well, but I would tell you there better be… pic.twitter.com/xvBMCkrwxo
While the Chiefs would certainly value Brown's familiarity with the offense, would Brown be excited to sign with the Chiefs for a third time after an up-and-down 2025 campaign? Teams like the Steelers and 49ers, also often rumored to be in the receiver market, may have a more direct role for Brown as opposed to a deep-threat-and-depth position with the Chiefs.
From Kansas City's perspective, signing Brown would likely add another layer of insulation in front of rookie Cyrus Allen, whose regular season production hasn't yet lived up to his training camp hype. (It could also lead to a demotion for Worthy, who has led the receivers in snaps taken this year by a wide margin.) Do the Chiefs see room for late-season growth from Allen, or have they retained their optimism for Worthy's role in his third year? If so, adding Brown as the team's fourth or fifth receiver might not make sense for either side.
Another hypothetical to monitor: Are the Chiefs still keeping a door open for Tyreek Hill's potential return? In a battle of veteran receivers who are familiar with the offense, I would guess that the Chiefs would have more interest in the 32-year-old Hill, though his health and potential league-discipline status are both publicly unknown as of mid-November. I don't think the team is likely to invite both Hill and Brown back to Kansas City, ultimately adding three receivers during the middle of the season.
The Chiefs could pass on both free agent vets, but if they sign one, I wouldn't expect to see the other back in red.
Given the number of snaps that have recently been allocated to receivers like Jalen Royals and Andrew Armstrong, and with the practice squad addition of Justin Watson , I couldn't be upset with a return to Kansas City for Brown. Even in the midst of an entirely disappointing year that began with the Eagles, capable NFL receivers are hard to come by, and players with comfort in Reid's offense are even more valued.
Still, if the Chiefs think that the new duo of Downs and Rashee Rice is enough to lead the way alongside Travis Kelce, with Worthy as the deep threat and Allen waiting in the wings as the next man up, I wouldn't begrudge them for passing up on this reunion.

title: Kenneth Walker’s Status for Chiefs-Falcons Clash in Jeopardy With Concerning Injury
full_text:
Two days before the Kansas City Chiefs kick off their road tilt with the Falcons , they received some extremely concerning news on the injury front this afternoon.
During Andy Reid's media availability, he revealed that star running back Kenneth Walker III is dealing with a groin injury. As a result, Walker did not participate in Friday's practice session and could be designated as questionable leading up to the matchup. "Kenneth Walker came in this morning and had a tight groin, so we just sat him out of practice," Reid told reporters today. "We'll see how he feels this afternoon with rehab and through tomorrow."
Kenneth Walker didn't practice Friday because of a tight groin.
Reid explained that Walker informed the coaching staff in the morning that he had tweaked something and needed to get checked out. He also noted that Walker isn't the kind of player to sit out unless something is really bothering him.
The former Seahawks tailback has been sensational in his first year in Kansas City , leading the NFL in rushing yards per game and amassing over 1,000 yards from scrimmage and 11 total touchdowns across eight appearances. However, there appears to be a chance he is absent from the lineup this Sunday. Walker was always considered an injury-prone player in Seattle, though his only scare with the Chiefs before this one was a minor ankle ailment that forced him to miss the preseason finale . The 2025 campaign marked the first time in his career that he was able to suit up for all 17 games.
If the highly anticipated ground game battle between Walker and Bijan Robinson doesn't take place, fifth-round rookie Emmett Johnson will make his first NFL start in the backfield. Reid said that he would be the next Chief in line for carries and expressed confidence in his ability.
The Nebraska product has been remarkably productive lately , as he's totaled 177 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns on just 12 touches over the past two weeks. He is a dynamic rusher who ranks among the NFL's best at forcing missed tackles, even with limited opportunities.
Aside from Johnson, Kansas City's running back depth is dangerously thin. Brashard Smith is currently on injured reserve, while third-string Jadyn Ott is questionable for Sunday's contest with a hamstring injury. Should he and Walker not be available this weekend, the Chiefs will only have one active ball carrier on the roster before making any corresponding moves.
Because of how late Walker popped up on the injury radar, it's difficult to say what his outlook is for KC's Week 10 matchup, but initial indications certainly aren't too promising. Reid did not disclose whether Walker's groin started tightening up recently or whether he had been battling through it for some time.
Fans should soon find out more about the severity of this injury and whether he can take the field at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.

title: ESPN Matchup Predictor Analyzes Chiefs vs. Falcons Showdown in Week 10
full_text:
After making a statement at Arrowhead Stadium, the Kansas City Chiefs will head back out on the road in Week 10 as the hosting Atlanta Falcons will attempt to play spoiler. KC is looking to build on its blowout win over the Jets in its previous outing.
The Falcons have lost four of their past five matchups but aren't technically out of it given the dire state of the NFC South. As a result, Kevin Stefanski's group is viewing this contest as a must-win if they want to stay in the playoff race. Despite Kansas City's impressive 6-2 record, Andy Reid and Co. have dealt with special teams struggles and offensive inconsistencies. Those issues have put a damper on what has otherwise been a successful start.
Most analysts view the Chiefs as heavy favorites, but what does the ESPN Matchup Predictor forecast? Here's what the computer model expects two days before kickoff.
ESPN Matchup Predictor Chances at Victory: Chiefs 78.1%, Falcons 21.6%.
With nearly a four-in-five chance of coming out victorious, the matchup predictor heavily favors Kansas City this weekend.
Chiefs fans can only take things one week at a time. Until the Broncos lose and give Kansas City an opening, all the Chiefs can do is beat the opponents in front of them.
The biggest storyline of this road clash is the arrival of Josh Downs , who landed with the Chiefs shortly before the trade deadline passed. The shifty slot receiver may not be featured too much out of the gate due to his unfamiliarity with the playbook, but there are bound to be some bright spots in his debut in the red and gold.
Kenneth Walker III is a dynamic weapon in the backfield , but Bijan Robinson is on another level. In spite of poor quarterback play, Robinson is virtually unstoppable in the open field and possesses elite vision as a runner. He has three games in which he surpassed 100 yards this season and is averaging 5.2 yards per carry. Atlanta is unsurprisingly a significant underdog coming into this one, though it really depends on which version of the Falcons show up on Sunday. They were blown out by the Bengals last time out and shut out by the Buccaneers a week prior, but they also hold upset victories over the 49ers and Packers.
The drastic shifts in Atlanta's play have fans scratching their heads, largely due to the play of quarterback Michael Penix Jr. A week after taking home NFC Offensive Player of the Week honors in Week 7, he tossed a career-high four interceptions and failed to get his team a point.
Heading into their final game before a bye, the Falcons are going to throw everything they can at the visiting squad to stay in contention. This is the type of matchup that could see the Chiefs fall into an early deficit if they aren't careful.

title: Chiefs Week 10 Injury Report: Two Key Trenches Players Remain Absent From Practice
full_text:
While the Kansas City Chiefs handily defeated the New York Jets last Sunday, several offensive starters came away with injuries. There seemed to be a good chance that KC would be without several contributors for this week's matchup against the Falcons.
Patrick Mahomes (elbow/knee) and Xavier Worthy (hamstring) have fully participated in practice the past two days, suggesting they are trending toward playing. However, a pair of key players in the trenches are currently in danger of missing the Week 10 contest. Two Chiefs were listed as nonparticipants on Thursday's injury report , those players being right tackle Jaylon Moore and defensive tackle Peter Woods. All signs indicate they won't be cleared to return by Sunday.
Amid the messy Josh Simmons fiasco , Moore has been thrust into a full-time role at right tackle while undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson mans the left side. The 28-year-old has started all but one game for the Chiefs this season, his only absence coming in Week 7 when he was in the NFL's concussion protocol .
Now, the veteran swing tackle is dealing with an ankle ailment that forced him to exit the Jets win in the second half. In his place, Joshua Ezeudu stepped in on the outside, and he could be in line for his second start as a Chief if Moore doesn't take part in Friday's practice session.
Meanwhile, rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods continues to work his way back from a neck stinger that has plagued him for nearly a month. It was not initially considered a long-term issue when he first sustained it , but he's now on track to miss his second consecutive week for KC.
Many Chiefs fans have eagerly awaited the return of Omarr Norman-Lott, the franchise's second-round draft pick last year. He tore his ACL in Week 7 of his rookie year and has been rehabbing back since. Kansas City designated him to return from the physically unable to perform (PUP) list on Oct. 28. The Chiefs have listed him as a limited participant on Wednesday and Thursday, signaling his long-awaited 2026 debut may be nearing. Regardless, time is running out for Norman-Lott to be activated before his 21-day practice window closes.
Although Norman-Lott does not technically need to return for the Chiefs' upcoming game, he only has until Nov. 18 to be added to the 53-man roster. Otherwise, he will revert to the reserve list permanently for the remainder of the year, closing any avenue for him to get back into game action.
Considering Woods is likely to be unavailable against Atlanta, Norman-Lott's presence would do a lot for the pass rush , which recently broke out with a five-sack outing versus New York.

title: Josh Downs’ Biggest Goal After Joining Chiefs Should Be Music to Fans’ Ears
full_text:
Whenever a team acquires a player at the NFL trade deadline , it always opens the door for exciting possibilities the rest of the way that season. It also presents an obstacle or two, however, and the Kansas City Chiefs have shown that as much as any club in recent years.
In reality, 2024 might be the most apt example of that. Wide receiver DeAndre Hopkins was heavily involved early on, only to see his production taper off over time, and defensive end Josh Uche never carved out a real role after coming over to his new organization. Kansas City-specific additions frequently encounter steep learning curves and adjustment periods.
The prized newcomer of 2026, wide receiver Josh Downs , is trying his best to ensure his transition is as seamless as possible.
As a short-area savant who operates primarily out of the slot, Downs figures to compete for some of the work tight end Travis Kelce and fellow wideout Rashee Rice are getting. That includes a variety of concepts and potential choice or option routes, giving the fourth-year man plenty to absorb as he enters a new system.
Heck, not quite having complete mastery of the offense is part of the reason why rookie Cyrus Allen's involvement has lagged behind the hype nine games into his Chiefs tenure. Can Downs catch on quicker and make a good impression with quarterback Patrick Mahomes?
Speaking to the media this week, he said that's what he's setting out to do.
"Build that relationship with him and then on the field, when he throws me the ball, just catch it," Downs said. "And keep making plays when he throws it to me. Just do anything I can to learn the offense as fast as possible. I don't want to be a guy that's asking everybody what the play is [or] what the formation is. I feel like that's when you kind of get left behind, so I want to do everything I can to learn as fast as possible."
Downs also opened up on going from the 2-7 Colts, who have already lost to Kansas City this season, to a 6-2 club that anticipates both qualifying for the postseason and making a run at the Super Bowl.
"It's great to join a team like this with so much history and so much winning in their past, and even now," Downs said. "So I'm excited to be able to be a part of a group like this and contribute where I can."
In three-and-a-half years as a Colt, Downs was targeted an even 350 times in the passing game and managed to log 231 receptions for 2,494 yards and 12 touchdowns. That came with a 66.0% catch rate and 50.6% success rate, although his sophomore effort may have been his best in totality. Downs was effective last year despite playing 6% fewer snaps than the campaign prior.
After requesting a trade and having that ask met by his old franchise, Downs has nothing but love for Indianapolis and is ready to hit the ground running for his new one.
"I know they made a decision based off the betterment of their organization," Downs said. "I respect them for sending me to an organization like this. Those are great people over there, and I feel like they did right by me. This is the choice they made."
If Downs can accomplish his goal and grasp the playbook with efficiency while also earning Mahomes' trust, both he and the Chiefs will be all the better for it.

title: What Does Chiefs’ Reported CB Trade Interest Before Deadline Say About the Secondary?
full_text:
The only trade the Kansas City Chiefs made at the deadline saw them acquire former Colts receiver Josh Downs to bolster the receiving corps. However, that wasn't the only position group Brett Veach hoped to improve on the open market.
According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , the Chiefs held substantial interest in adding a cornerback before Tuesday's deadline. While no deal came to fruition, it may have revealed how the front office views the defensive backfield and its confidence in the current personnel. In the last two games, KC has primarily operated with Nohl Williams and Kristian Fulton on the outside, mixing in Chris Roland-Wallace as the primary slot corner. That rotation would look significantly different if it weren't for the injuries to the secondary.
Although he has been a full participant in practice this week and is expected to return against the Falcons, Mansoor Delane's shoulder has has been a recurring problem all year long. He suffered a hairline fracture in his right shoulder blade during OTAs in the offseason, forcing him to wear a non-contact jersey throughout most of training camp. The LSU product reaggravated it in his NFL debut after coming down with an interception, and a setback in practice last month forced him to miss the past two contests .
The concern with Delane isn't how he's performed, as he's been quite effective during his rookie season. Despite having missed three games, he holds the highest Pro Football Focus defensive grade (79.7) among all NFL rookie cornerbacks, allowing just 14 receptions for 227 yards in coverage.
Still, it shouldn't come as a surprise that the Chiefs were exploring their options given the depleted state of their defensive backs. Since placing L'Jarius Sneed on injured reserve with a knee strain, Kansas City's pass defense has been compromised by a lack of continuity.
Fowler's report didn't provide much insight into the caliber of player the Chiefs were pursuing, but the lack of a move doesn't necessarily mean they are comfortable with their current group. It's possible the franchise views Delane's shoulder ailment as an ongoing question mark for the remainder of the season. Part of Kansas City's reluctance to overpay for a cornerback could be attributed to Fulton's unexpected resurgence. While he was an afterthought coming off a lackluster first season in the red and gold, Fulton has surprisingly looked like a lockdown corner since being thrust into a bigger role this season.
Kristian Fulton has allowed just 50 receiving yards over 8 catches (15 targets) this season Qbs are registering a 32.6 passer rating when targeting KC's veteran CB
Having Fulton as a dependable depth piece has benefited KC tremendously. Regardless, the Chiefs may not have complete confidence in him as the secondary boundary cornerback starting in a playoff game should Delane's injury worsen at some point.
Williams has served as a stabilizing presence all year and has emerged as a real star in his second NFL season . The good news is that his strong play has helped offset concerns about Delane's availability.
Steve Spagnuolo is confident in the cornerbacks on his roster, and the Chiefs' interest in making an addition was probably more a product of their injury concerns than dissatisfaction with the players' performances. Either way, this group is only a season-ending injury away from being dangerously thin, and Kansas City didn't do anything at the deadline to provide insurance.

title: Chiefs’ Kicker Decision for Week 10 Is Bordering on Blind Faith
full_text:
With nine weeks of play and the NFL trade deadline in the books, the Kansas City Chiefs are in good standing overall but have some potential red flags. One of them is in a lesser-appreciated realm, but it could continue to loom large if not resolved in time for the postseason.
Head coach Andy Reid's squad and Dave Toub's special teams unit still can't rely on the kicking game to produce quality results. Longtime starter Harrison Butker's nightmare season rolled on in last weekend's win over the New York Jets, presumably making his seat even hotter with another subpar performance.
Is that actually the case, though? Despite former Pro Bowler Justin Tucker being ready to go on a moment's notice, KC has yet to make a swap at the position. Those expecting a changing of the guard on Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons will have to wait at least one more week.
Speaking to the media on Wednesday, Reid announced that he's trotting Butker out again in Week 10.
"As far as the kicking part goes, I'm going to stick with Butker this week," Reid said. "We'll go from there."
Reid and Toub have remained consistent in their backing of Butker , routinely pointing to his past accomplishments as justification for the unwavering faith. Instead of a new norm, the coaching staff is echoing that this is merely a cold spell of sorts.
"Listen, Harrison's done such a great job for us over time here," Reid said. "Sometimes, you go through these little peak and valley things. You give him a chance to work through them; we'll see how things go."
Another week of Butker highlights a multitude of concerns with the club's current approach to rectifying the ongoing kicking woes.
First and foremost, believing Butker is going to return to prime form borders on blind faith. The 31-year-old is perfectly fine on kicks inside the 50-yard line, going 10-for-11 on the year, but it's his long-range ability that — at least statistically — seems unlikely to come back.
After going 2-for-5 on field goals of 50-plus yards in 2024, he "rebounded" to post a 5-for-8 mark last season and is a career-worst 2-for-8 this year. In a sport where more and more kickers seem to be gaining either distance or accuracy, Kansas City's go-to man is losing both. This doesn't pass the smell test of someone who, in Reid's words , is "off a bit."
There's also the Tucker aspect of it all. If the Chiefs were so confident in a Butker resurgence, why would they bring in competition on the practice squad and keep him around for this long? That's on top of the reality that Tucker is in as a 36-year-old player who hasn't kicked in a game since the 2024 season and made only 73.3% of his tries, including converting on six of 11 attempts from that all-important long distance.
Maybe there is a world where Butker levels out. He found his stride, to some degree, in 2025-26 after a slow start out of the gate. Perhaps even if he doesn't, there's a concession from the coaching staff and Tucker proves to be closer to his 2023 self than the version we last saw. It's improbable, albeit not impossible.
But this comes off as a team hoping to catch lightning in a bottle rather than one that's truly getting to the bottom of a pressing issue.
