title: Chiefs Winners and Losers After the Trade Deadline: Actually a New-Look WR Room?
full_text:
The unofficial second half of the 2026-27 NFL campaign is here, which coincides with the passing of the annual trade deadline . Several teams capitalized on opportunities to add to their respective rosters, with the Kansas City Chiefs being among the group of perceived winners.
By acquiring wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts, Kansas City improved the route-running quality of its skill players while also maintaining some flexibility for the future. Whether the move can raise the upside of the offense or is worth the cost is another argument, but there's no denying that at least trying to get better was a good call in a vacuum.
In this post-deadline world, where do the Chiefs stand on an individual front? Let's dive into who should benefit from the move, as well as whose roles might be changed in negative ways.
The following players should benefit from the Downs trade by way of either increased production, decreased pressure, or both.
What better way to start than with the man himself? It feels like forever ago that the Colts' offense was viewed as football's best, but the reality is that was only a calendar year ago. Through 10 weeks of play in the 2025 campaign, per RBSDM , Indianapolis led the sport in EPA per play on that end (0.183) and was second to only the Los Angeles Rams in success rate.
Everyone knows what a horrific collapse Indianapolis had down the stretch, partially due to getting exposed but also because quarterback Daniel Jones tore his Achilles tendon. Despite Jones' return for the 2026-27 season, things still haven't gone even close to smoothly for head coach Shane Steichen's crew.
It's safe to say that going from catching passes from Jones to Patrick Mahomes could have a positive effect on the fourth-year wideout's prospects.
Josh Downs went from Daniel Jones to Patrick Mahomes - here is how they stack up in catchable aimed pass attempts in 2026 🎯 Catchable pass rate (rank of 29 QBs): 0-9 yds: Jones 83% (24th) → Mahomes 91% (2nd) 10-19: 59% (26th) → 68% (12th) 20+: 21% (29th) → 45% (17th) pic.twitter.com/acJg1HA8ai
Speaking of which, having another reliable pass catcher figures to come to Mahomes' aid as well. It's a two-way street.
Coming into the season, Kansas City was banking on several things to happen at the receiver spot. Not only did Xavier Worthy need to look more like he did as a rookie — or perhaps even better — but Rashee Rice was supposed to return to his pre-injury form and Tyquan Thornton was expected to take a step forward. It's safe to say that plan, which was on thin ice to begin with, hasn't worked.
If anything, Worthy has regressed and now has a bum hamstring . Rice sustained a hamstring injury of his own in Week 4 and isn't remotely as productive on a volume basis as he was last year. Thornton, who was actually living up to the hype, is done for most or all of this season with a dislocated ankle . Enter Downs, who now might be the best separator and technician Mahomes has had in years at the receiver position.
WR percentile separation & YPRR vs man coverage pic.twitter.com/NWbBKMMNRi
No. 15 has still managed to turn in a good season, throwing for 14 touchdowns and four interceptions, but his life's been much more difficult than is needed. This move should assist him on all downs and make the offense hum more efficiently as a result.
On a per-target basis, tight end Travis Kelce's been more effective in 2026 than he has in several years. He's producing a career-high 14.6 yards per reception and 10.0 yards per target, paired with an average of 10.0 yards after catch per reception. Kansas City isn't force-feeding him volume, instead allowing him to pick his spots while playing 4% fewer snaps than he was last season.
Had Kelce been at or near his peak involvement, he'd be a bit more of a loser than a winner with Downs coming to the Chiefs. Because his catches cut deeper this campaign, though, it's hard to not see him either maintaining his current output or reaching new heights in what could be the final stretch of his first-ballot Hall of Fame career.
The jury is out in the "losers" category, as the welcoming of Downs to the lineup likely changes some things moving forward.
After a slow start while recovering from offseason knee surgery , Rice went off for seven receptions and 88 yards in Week 3. Since returning from injury in Week 8, he's averaged six receptions and 51 yards across two games while also scoring a touchdown. Whatever momentum he had from a stat-sheet-stuffing standpoint may be slowing down with another peer to compete with, however.
Josh Downs averages 0.23 EPA/target this season, per @SumerSports Rashee Rice entered today with the highest EPA/target among Chiefs WRs at 0.15
Adding to the SumerSports data , Rice is 29th out of 111 wideouts with at least 100 routes at a 2.0 yards per route run mark. Downs is way down at 76th at 1.14, but that number is pretty deceiving given the injuries to the Colts' receiver unit and how inept the offense has been. If Downs gets the looks from Mahomes many are expecting, it means Rice's ceiling is capped.
There's also the element of these two thriving in similar areas of the field. According to Pro Football Focus , 46.7% of Rice's targets are coming within 0-9 yards of the line of scrimmage. That threshold is 61.5% for Downs.
After combining for 19 offensive snaps in his first five games, rookie fifth-rounder Cyrus Allen's figures were 16, 31 and 19 over his next three outings. Week 9 marked a regression for the former Cincinnati standout, unfortunately, as he fumbled on a kickoff return and also went without a catch on offense. Worthy's injury didn't see him get unleashed, either, so his stock was already down .
It's virtually impossible for a true breakout to happen as long as the trio of Rice, Downs and Worthy is healthy and available. Allen can still perhaps make a couple plays a game as a supporting piece, although that isn't the rest-of-season path some wanted him to take. Chalk that up to a classic tug-of-war between expectations and reality.
This one is unfortunate, but it's sometimes simply a numbers game when it comes to roster math. The Chiefs needed to make room for a better player, which meant special teams ace Nikko Remigio got the boot by way of being waived on Wednesday morning.
Remigio has several years of teams experience, on top of a thorough understanding of the offensive system, but it became clear when Rice was out in both 2025 and 2026 that he was never going to find an expanded role. Downs having his name added to the depth chart essentially signaled the complete extinguishment of those hopes for the former undrafted free agent.
Side note: Downs was spotted warming up with the punt team in Wednesday's practice. I'm still hard-pressed to believe he'll take many of Remigio's old reps, especially with this being more of a standard procedure during the week than anything else.
I struggled with where to put Worthy. While it seems likely that his overall workload and involvement in the offense will decline with Downs in the fold, it could take some pressure off him and make him a more impactful player overall. We'll wait and see.

title: Why Did Chargers Leave Out 1 Critical Name When Talking Untradeable Players?
full_text:
While trying to control the messaging around a lost season and a botched NFL trade deadline, the Los Angeles Chargers made some pretty interesting comments that might shine a light on where things go from here.
Granted, comments from players and reporting suggests the Chargers have lost the locker room. Pounding the table for the core group of players, then trading one of them in a panic to a rival at a deadline, only to botch the trade and get that player back, tends to do that to a team.
But while addressing these happenings over the last week or so, Chargers general manager Joe Hortiz made a noteworthy comment, where what he didn’t say seemed to be pretty notable.
Endless reporting and common sense said the Chargers were never going to trade players like quarterback Justin Herbert and wide receiver Ladd McConkey.
But other recognizable names were quite a bit more debatable. This week,Hortiz made sure to address the “core” group of players who entered the trade deadline as untouchable.
An excerpt from The Athletic’s Noah Furtado hits on this point: “He offered his list of hard noes by name. Quarterback Justin Herbert. Wide receiver Ladd McConkey. Tackle Joe Alt. Safety Derwin James. Cornerback Tarheeb Still. He stopped there, but perhaps he could have continued.”
Really astute onlookers will notice a missing name: Tuli Tuipulotu.
We’re not going to outright claim this is a sign of things to come for the Chargers. But Hortiz rattling off core players and omitting a 24-year-old pass-rusher with 29 sacks in 58 games due a major contract extension feels like it could be a big deal.
And hey, maybe not. Lots of factors went into the list of names and not everyone was going to get included. But there’s a smudge of deja vu here. Hortiz, after all, traded for Odafe Oweh, watched him break out at the age of 26 and refused to pay him market rate last offseason and then compensated by using a first-round pick on an “older” prospect like Akheem Mesidor to attempt to immediately fill the production gap.
In other words, misguided bargain hunting that burned unnecessary draft capital. Who is to say the same doesn’t happen again? There have already been rumblings that the Chargers and Tuipulotu talked extension and it didn’t work out.
There are other future factors at play, like franchise tags. But scanning the Chargers’ roster, Tuipulotu is 100 percent a building block who should be a hard-no as a trade candidate, or at least mentioned as such.
Not this time with Hortiz though, it seems.

title: Former Raiders Executive Goes Scorched Earth on Mike McDaniel, Chargers
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are having a season to forget in 2026. They are currently 0-8 and after hiring the top offensive coordinator candidate on the market in the offseason, they are still searching for an indentity and for general answers on offense.
Los Angeles, through the first nine weeks of the season, currently rank at or near the bottom in every offensive category and analytical measurement. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel has been trying to get the offense going in the right direction and has resorted to changing up where he is calling plays from in hopes of finding the elusive answer.
The move to the booth did not help much as the Chargers continued to struggle to score points against the Houston Texans. The Chargers did face a sudden gameplan change against Houston as their top wide receiver, Ladd McConkey, was hurt during warmups and ruled out of the game before taking a snap. The gameplan curveball is not an excuse for the continued struggles, just a simple note of context for McDaniel's first game in the booth.
Injuries across the offense has been a consistent hindrance for the Chargers. Despite the consistent lineup changes, the bottom line, as many point out, is that quarterback Justin Herbert does not look comfortable is what he is being asked to do in the offense.
Justin Herbert has six seasons of consistency prior to 2026. Former Raiders CEO Amy Trask believes that the Chargers and Mike McDaniel are not putting Herbert in a position to be successful. She did not hold back on her opinion of how the situation is being handled.
“The best coaches don’t take great players and try to push them into a schemes. They build a scheme around the players.” Former Raiders CEO Amy Trask says the Chargers aren’t putting Justin Herbert in the best position succeed . #hqsocial pic.twitter.com/fJXYCjKc9f
Trask added in her observations and said "It strikes me that what they are asking Justin to do, is to fit into a scheme for which he's not best suited." The sentiment that McDaniel is asking Herbert to do things that aren't best suited to him seems to be the most common belief amongst experts, including former NFL executives and even quarterbacks.
Multiple former NFL quarterbacks have publicly stated that it appears that the motions, ball handling and excessive designer plays while lacking the proper personnel has created an environment where Herbert is struggling to see the field, even when it is clean. Brothers and former NFL quarterbacks Derek and David Carr have their own podcast and Herbert has been the subject of their conversations on multiple occasions throughout this season.
The Chargers are still searching for their first win this season. What do you think is holding them back? 🧐⚡️ pic.twitter.com/5cORWGMVr1
Derek Carr believes the issue plaguing the Chargers is a combination of the scheme and personnel not aligning. "It doesn't fit Herbert," Derek says.
Another common critcism hitting the Chargers and McDaniel is that it appears that everything is too complex. It appears they are trying to run before they learned to walk. Derek Carr also believes that may be an issue for the Chargers pointing to some of the advanced scheme options being asked of Herbert that are more inline with McDaniel's late time in Miami as opposed to the year one identity establishment and mastery of the basics.
Despite the 0-8 start, Derek and David still have kind words about Mike McDaniel 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/Yktj4zKLt4
It appears that former rivals from the Raiders in both Derek Carr and Amy Trask see that the Chargers have not been putting Herbert in the best place to succeed. Herbert's performance and stats bear out those results. The biggest question heading forward is has there been irreparable damage done to Justin Herbert? If the Chargers can't figure out how to protect him more effieciently, that question will grow louder.

title: Chargers Officially Lost Locker Room During NFL Trade Deadline Disaster
full_text:
Deep in the throes of a winless season and a winless NFL trade deadline, those running the Los Angeles Chargers have only managed to make things worse.
Headed up by general manager Joe Hortiz, a front office more concerned with PR messaging than anything else attempted to explain itself before Week 10 for the botched Daiyan Henley trade .
All it did was create more questions , instead.
Hortiz and the Chargers, after all, were reportedly confusing other teams with their reluctance to make trades at the deadline. Chargers coaches insisted they could still win games and didn’t want to lose guys, only for the front office to turn around and trade a young core piece like Henley to a division rival , before the agreement collapsed.
If the locker room wasn’t lost before, it is now.
Before the deadline, one could’ve made the argument that the Chargers were still playing hard and, if nothing else, the locker room was probably fineish.
Chargers players about to be confronted with the trade deadline debacle made their feelings known to reporters this week.
“Don’t ask hard questions to us; ask hard questions to them,” veteran edge rusher Bud Dupree said, according to The Athletic’s Noah Furtado , unprompted. “Ask the hard questions. Everybody pull they cameras out and go upstairs and ask questions to them. Everybody. Walk upstairs and ask them.”
Those who want to read that as joking or something else might want to look away for the next bit.
According to Furtado, the public disgruntlement from some players about the Henley trade online was very alive in the locker room, too: “But many teammates expressed disappointment, whether in the locker room or on their socials, that Henley had been dealt in the first place.”
The Chargers had been endlessly focused on messaging amid the chaos this season. And ( surprise!) the players in the locker room were just as confused by the team demanding continuity and no changes and this is the core group needed to win…before shipping away a young core piece to a rival at the last second.
The Chargers aren’t going to stop “trying” to win games. Tanking doesn’t really exist in the NFL, at least from the players’ end, because of contract factors, and losing would just make way for their replacements, etc. Things are so broken on the offense, the roster is so injured and the quality assembled so poor that the losses will keep flowing.
But the locker room? From afar, at least, it feels like the Chargers managed to finally lose it.

title: The 5 Most Disappointing Chargers Players So Far This Season
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers have had a rough season to say the least.
There are always certain expectations for every player going into any season. Some perform better than predicted, however, that is simply not the case for every single athlete that steps foot on the gridiron.
Here are five guys who have not moved the needle in a positive direction when it comes to overall execution.
Justin Herbert has arguably been the biggest disappointment of the 2026 season.
Entering the year, he was expected to be the centerpiece of an offense capable of competing with the best teams in the NFL. Instead, his performances have become a major part of the team’s struggles. Herbert has thrown for 1,591 yards, six touchdowns and 11 interceptions. His 70.4 passer rating is a troubling number for a quarterback with his experience and ability. Even more concerning, he has been sacked 31 times.
The turnovers have been particularly damaging. Herbert has struggled to consistently protect the football, putting additional pressure on an offense that already has difficulty sustaining drives. Herbert always seems to be on the short end of the stick, so that surely doesn't help. However the elite quarterback needs to put up better performances regardless.
Omarion Hampton entered the season with an opportunity to establish himself as one of the most important pieces of the offensive attack. Unfortunately, his production has been inconsistent and the running game has not developed into the reliable weapon the team desperately needs.
The lack of carries have definitely been a factor, but still you would like to see a little more outta him.
There is still plenty of potential, but his first eight games have not delivered the kind of impact expected from such an important young offensive player.
Cole Strange has become another concerning part of an offensive line that has struggled to provide consistent protection. His individual performance has been especially disappointing considering how important interior blocking is to the success of the entire offense.
The veteran guard has struggled to consistently win his assignments, creating problems for both the passing and running games. When interior protection breaks down, quarterbacks have less time to make decisions, while running backs have fewer opportunities to find open lanes.
He has not provided the level of stability expected from an experienced offensive lineman.
This might not shock some people, but Quentin Johnston has not shown enough this season. The whole offense is a disaster, and he unfortunately is a part of that.
The former TCU standout has had a rough couple years, to say the least. He has improved every year, but cannot put together an elite season.
A first-round pick should provide an exceptional amount of help when they need it the most. The reason they are drafted is to provide what the team has been missing for years. Yet Johnstoin just hasn’t been the player most thought he would be by now. He is a very talented player, but this year hasn't shown much of that.
Donte Jackson rounds out this list after struggling to provide the dependable coverage performances expected from an experienced NFL cornerback.
The secondary has had difficulty consistently limiting opposing passing attacks, and Jackson has experienced some particularly difficult moments during the season.
His performance against the Texans was especially concerning. In the 44-22 defeat, Jackson received a reported overall performance grade of 28.6, highlighting the problems he experienced during one of the team’s worst defensive outings.
Cornerbacks are regularly placed in difficult situations, but experienced players must find ways to limit mistakes and prevent opposing receivers from consistently winning their matchups. Jackson’s struggles have become another example of how problems across the roster have contributed to the team’s disappointing start. He still has the experience to improve, but the secondary needs much more consistency from him moving forward.

title: Chargers Seem More Worried About PR Than Trades, Wins Right Now
full_text:
While trying to send the proper messages to drive narratives, the Los Angeles Chargers are managing to send all the wrong messages.
The fact “messaging” was a theme at all coming from the team and reporters ahead of the NFL trade deadline was pretty telling. Word was, they wanted to hang onto players like Khalil Mack because they didn’t want to send the wrong “message” to the locker room or fans.
But the Chargers then turned around and sent a weird “message” anyway, trading a younger, popular player like Daiyan Henley…to the AFC West rival Denver Broncos.
Weird, and yet it got stranger: The trade fell apart and the latest “message” from the Chargers is just more odd PR work from an 0-8 club.
According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter , the Henley trade fell apart due to confidence the Broncos had with his knee after a physical. The two sides discussed different trade packages to make it work, it seems, then called the whole thing off.
Schefter’s colleague, Ian Rapoport , added this borderline ridiculousness: “Part of the reason was because the Chargers never really wanted to trade Daiyan Henley. They got an offer from the Broncos they couldn’t refuse, so they took it."
Hear that, folks? The Chargers didn’t actually want to trade the player they traded, but only after the trade fell through and the player came back.
By the way, the can’t-miss trade compensation was… a fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick.
Look, this little nugget from Rapoport was probably the Chargers trying to be nice about this, or even Henley’s agent trying to smooth things over as he goes from a 7-2 locker room back to an 0-8 one. The team that traded him away didn’t want him and it’s pretty clear contract negotiation talks hadn’t worked out, so he’ll be a free agent soon anyway.
But this is just one of those little things to throw on the Chargers pile, which happens to be on fire right now. The Chargers seem misguided, more laser-focused on PR and messaging than anything else.
Obviously, that’s not 100 percent the case. But it all adds up to a team that feels unfocused and doesn’t know what direction it wants to really go in, which is summed up pretty well by the winless record and move-less trade deadline.

title: The Chargers Have a Legit Chance of Landing Newly Released Wide Receiver
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers should take a serious look at Hollywood Brown. The Sooners alumni recently got released by the Philadelphia Eagles and now is l ooking for another team.
Brown has built his game around acceleration, movement and turning a small opening into a big play. Those qualities are valuable for a team looking to make its passing attack more dangerous.
For the Chargers, the appeal would be about more than adding another name to the receiver room. A player who threatens defenses vertically may create easier opportunities underneath for the rest of the offense. Also, looking towards the future is honestly the best thing now.
There would still be questions before making a move.
Brown’s role, health, contract expectations and the team’s cap space would matter. The Chargers would need to decide whether his skill set matches the coaching staff’s plans and whether the price makes sense. Speed is exciting, but a roster decision has to work beyond the highlight plays.
The connection between the franchise and Brown runs deeper than people think. Joe Hortiz was the director of college scouting for the Ravens for many years. He eventually became director of player personnel, which led him to having a big role in drafting Brown.
Having connections like this really makes a difference. Every year we see players head to organizations where they had previous relationships with either the staff or fellow athletes.
Brown is most dangerous when timing and trust are clear. The offense would need to get him involved early, rather than asking him to wait for a few deep chances each game. Screens, motion, crossing routes and vertical patterns could help make his presence felt. A varied role would make it harder for opponents to predict where the ball is going.
There is no guarantee the Chargers will pursue Brown, and a potential fit should not be confused with a completed deal. Still, the idea is easy to understand. The Bolts could consider a receiver whose speed might change the geometry of the field and give its offense another dimension. If the opportunity is realistic and the terms are right, Brown could be an intriguing addition. The Chargers would not need him to carry the passing game alone. They would need him to win matchups, create space and make defenses pay when they leave him room. In a league where one explosive play can swing a game, that kind of weapon is worth evaluating.
It was clear that the Eagles signing Hollywood Brown was never going to work from the start of the regular season when he was a healthy scratch. title: What Has Been Joe Hortiz's Biggest Mistake in 2026?
full_text:
Every general manager makes decisions that look better on paper than they do once the season gets underway.
Some make encouraging moves, important decisions, and reasons to believe the organization is heading in the right direction. For Joe Hortiz of the Los Angeles Chargers , those factors have not been met to the full extent.
When evaluating Hortiz’s work this year, one particular area stands out. It isn’t necessarily the flashiest position on the roster , nor is it a decision that will dominate every conversation among fans. But it could have a much bigger impact on the team’s ceiling than people realize.
The biggest mistake Hortiz made in 2026 was not doing enough to strengthen the offensive line around Justin Herbert.
This isn’t a new conversation. Protecting Herbert has been a recurring challenge, and the organization has spent considerable time trying to establish consistency up front. For a quarterback with his arm talent, mobility, and ability to make plays outside the structure of an offense, there is little reason to leave him constantly dealing with unnecessary pressure.
Hortiz had an opportunity to give the offense another layer of security. Adding an experienced offensive lineman could have provided valuable depth and prevented the team from having to rely so heavily on its existing options. Instead, the position remained an area that deserved more attention. And when you’re building around a quarterback like Herbert, this is not somewhere you want to take unnecessary chances. I could give you all the statistics in the world backing up these claims, but the majority of people have a good idea what those numbers would look like.
There is also a bigger picture worth considering . The offense has already experienced enough changes over the past several seasons. Different coordinators, different systems, and adjustments to personnel have all played a role in shaping the unit. Establishing stability up front should be one of the organization’s main priorities. Hortiz deserves credit for recognizing the importance of surrounding Herbert with talent, but that responsibility extends beyond adding weapons and making headline grabbing acquisitions. Sometimes the most important addition is the player who keeps a defensive lineman from getting anywhere near your quarterback.
That is particularly important when your franchise quarterback is the centerpiece of everything you’re trying to accomplish. Hortiz has shown that he understands what this organization needs to become a legitimate contender. But if there is one area where his approach deserved more attention this offseason, it’s protecting the player who gives this team its best chance to win.
A roster can have plenty of talent, but none of it matters if the quarterback doesn’t have enough time to use it.

title: Chargers' Updated Draft Picks After Failed Daiyan Henley Trade
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-8 and need to understand that their season is effectively over. Fans are encouraged to do the same, with the unfortunate truth being that this team is better off rebuilding. A big part of rebuilding and still having some excitement for a terrible team is the NFL Draft.
It is like an NFL holiday. All 32 teams come out with a new draft class and players for fans, coaches and media alike to all be excited about. For the Chargers, this is the only hope of turning around this franchise under Justin Herbert and Jim Harbaugh.
With that, it is important to take a good look at what the Bolts currently have as draft capital to help reload and restock this horrid roster.
Before the NFL trade deadline, the picture was pretty clear about what the Chargers should expect their NFL draft capital to be. However, in classic Chargers fashion, that was muddied due to a weird interdivision trade that was put through and then rescinded.
Simply put, the Los Angeles Chargers decided to trade their young LB, Daiyan Henley , to the Denver Broncos for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. This trade, a day later, did not go through after Henley failed his physical. This had the Broncos back out and made the Chargers and Jim Harbaugh very upset.
Now, with all of these changes, the Bolts' draft capital situation has been in flux. Below is the most up-to-date list of what the Chargers have for the 2027 NFL Draft and the 2028 NFL Draft.
2027: LAC 1st LAC 2nd LAC 3rd LAC 4th Comp 4th (Odafe Oweh) LAC 5th SEA 6th (Avery Smith Trade) LAR 7th (From BAL, Alohi Gilman Trade )
2028: LAC 1st LAC 2nd LAC 3rd LAC 4th LAC 5th LAC 6th CAR 6th (Te-Rah Edwards Trade) LAC 7th NYJ 7th (Ja'Sir Taylor Trade)
It should be noted that compensatory picks for the 2027 NFL Draft have yet to be finalized, as the season is still in flux. These are estimated picks according to OverTheCap . Former Chargers IDL Otito Ogbonnia, now on the Cowboys , has been playing well, possibly yielding the Chargers an extra selection if he were to continue his play and get into the range to allow for a compensatory pick.
As for 2028, compensatory picks have not yet been evaluated as free agency has not occurred. The Chargers overall seem to have a quite healthy draft capital situation, hopefully healthy enough to help turn this roster around.

title: Sean Payton’s History Makes Failed Chargers Trade Suspicious
full_text:
The world of NFL front offices is built on relationships, connections and ultimately trust. George Paton may be the general manager for the Denver Broncos but head coach Sean Payton has a less than stellar history when it comes to trust, trickery and gamesmanship in the NFL.
The Los Angeles Chargers had a trade agreement in place for their homegrown starting linebacker, Daiyan Henley, to send him to the Denver Broncos. The trade that was finalized at the 11th hour before the trade deadline came to pass was for a 2027 fourth-round pick and 2028 fifth-rounder pick.
Late Wednesday night, the Broncos decided to pull the plug on the trade after trying to renegotiate the trade compensation after getting Henley in the building in Colorado. The Broncos cited a failed physical designation for Henley and specifically cited arthritis in his knee which immediately raised eyebrows and suspicions. The Chargers are now left to deal with the fallout .
Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk raised concerns with the Broncos' evaluation and mentioned arthritis being a common issue for NFL linebackers.
"The Broncos discovered an issue with Henley’s knee. It has, we’re told, arthritis. (As one source with neither the Chargers nor the Broncos told PFT, most if not all starting linebackers in the NFL have some degree of arthritis in their knees.)" - Mike Florio
The entire situation smells fishy. Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh is asking the NFL to look into how the loophole, which allows trades to be adjusted by compensation past the deadline. Harbaugh pointed out the obvious issue with how this trade fell apart, the Broncos did not fail Daiyan Henley for his physical, they were only going to pass him if the trade compensation was reduced.
HC Jim Harbaugh says Denver failed Henley's physical to back out. "The Broncos based a pass/fail on a medical grade on whether we would take less compensation." Harbaugh says the Broncos would pass Henley's physical if the picks were downgraded from the agreed upon 4th + 5th. pic.twitter.com/xwoVCILJyl
The Chargers are 0-8 and had not made any other moves at the deadline. Henley was one of the few trade assets the Chargers had that could net any relatively significant draft capital. If this sounds shady and suspicious, there is good reason.
Sean Payton has a long history of holding grudges and operating on the margins of good and bad faith. Payton was famously suspended for a full season for his role in the New Orleans Saints Bountygate scandal.
Payton has a longstanding beef with the Minnesota Vikings going back to Bountygate and the 2009 NFC Championship and later to the Minnesota Miracle game in 2018 playoffs. He later took credit for and bragged to reporters about playing a game of smoke and mirrors to trick the Vikings in the 2024 NFL draft.
Sean Payton and Jim Harbaugh may not have a full-on beef with each other but they do have history. Back in 2011, there was a preseason controversy between Payton and Harbaugh over an unspoken gentleman's angreement , that Payton took as a slight, on how to handle their preseason matchup.
Payton took a year off from coaching and was working in media during the 2022 season. During the season, Payton was agressively pushing for the Chargers head coaching job, the job that went to Harbaugh the following year.
Did Sean Payton and the Broncos operate in bad faith in regards to Daiyan Henley and the trade? Did they try to use a loophole to leverage the Chargers and steal a player for less draft capital? The entire situation seems suspicious, and Sean Payton's track record does little to calm those suspicions.

title: Joshua Karty's 'Dirty Kickoff' Is Making a Big Difference for Rams Special Teams
full_text:
Special teams has been a consistent theme for the Los Angeles Rams this season. For much of the first eight weeks of the season, the Rams were by far the worst special teams unit in the NFL.
Through eight weeks, the Rams had a -12.9 special teams DVOA. While the Rams still have the worst special teams unit, they’ve improved to a -9.5 special teams DVOA over the last two weeks.
A big reason for that improvement has been the addition of Joshua Karty and the “dirty” kickoff. It’s certainly been unconventional for the Rams to roster two kickers, but it has worked out for their special teams. Karty had inconsistencies last year on the field goal unit, but he excelled on kickoffs. Instead of a high, soaring kick with hangtime, Karty’s dirty kickoff is a low, wobbling kickoff designed to mimic a ground ball in baseball, making it difficult for returners to handle.
As seen in Karty’s return against the Los Angeles Chargers, there is some risk with the dirty kickoff. Given the low trajectory, there is a possibility of it landing before the landing zone, resulting in a flag that puts the offense at the 40-yard line.
However, for the most part, the Rams have reaped the rewards and it’s helped the kickoff coverage unit. Through the first eight weeks of the season, the Rams were allowing an average of 28.7 yards per kickoff return and teams were starting at the 34.7-yard line on average.
With Karty’s dirty kickoff, that has improved dramatically. It’s still a small sample size and teams may adjust as they see it more. With that said, over the last two weeks, the Rams have allowed just 18.8 yards per return and teams have started at the 29-yard line on average. That’s almost a 10-yard improvement per return and a better field position of 5.7 yards.
What makes that even more impressive is that Karty has done that despite two kicks landing short of the landing zone. However, Karty helped offset those mistakes with two touchbacks last week. Given that the ball hits the ground before the end zone on the dirty kickoff, touchbacks go to the 20 rather than the 35.
Karty's two "dirty kickoffs" that resulted in touchbacks. Returners may get more comfortable as they see it more, but there's also a reason these guys are playing football and not shortstop. pic.twitter.com/7lbXx8zJoR
There is still a lot of room for improvement with the Rams’ special teams, but the in-season implementation of the dirty kickoff is evidence of the coaching staff doing what it can to improve the operation. With limited roster spots, it’s also worth considering how long the Rams can afford to roster two kickers.
Outside of kickoffs, the Rams have also improved on the punt team in recent weeks. Over the last two games, Ethan Evans’ 44.6 net yards per punt is ninth in the NFL and he is PFF’s second-highest graded punter. Brandon McManus has yet to be tested on the field goal unit, but is perfect on extra points and his three field goal attempts.
For much of the season, the Rams' special teams were actively hurting their chances of winning games. Signing Karty and implementing the dirty kickoff shows the coaching staff continuously working to improve that facet. With the dirty kickoff, the Rams have found something that works, but they still need to prove they can be consistent. Given how costly special teams mistakes have been this season, that's at least a step in the right direction.

title: Rams Desperately Need Wide Receiver Help, But Is Hollywood Brown the Answer?
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are in a desperate spot at wide receiver following the injury to Puka Nacua. With Davante Adams set to be out at least the next two games, the Rams will be relying on Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, and CJ Daniels at wide receiver .
After the Rams struck out at the trade deadline, they will likely wait for players to become available as free agents when veteran players begin asking for their release. The Rams benefitted from this in 2021 with Odell Beckham Jr. and in 2022 with Baker Mayfield.
That process has already started. Late this week, wide receiver Marquise “Hollywood” Brown requested his release from the Philadelphia Eagles. According to Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk , that request is set to be granted.
Following the trade deadline, the Rams restructured the contracts of Kyren Williams and Kam Curl to open up around $3 million in cap space for situations like this and to help get them through the season.
As a cheap option, Brown makes a lot of sense. Due to the release happening after the trade deadline, Brown will be subject to waivers. His minimum base salary makes him an intriguing option for teams in need of a wide receiver.
The waiver order is updated weekly and is based on a reverse standings order. Heading into Week 10, the Rams would be 18th in the waiver order. However, given that Brown is asking for his release from the Eagles, it’s likely that he wants to play for a competitive team and his agent will make that known. According to NFL Insider Jordan Schultz, Brown is expected to sign with a playoff contender.
He wants to be here, bring him in Les pic.twitter.com/DGAsNw04st
Brown had 49 receptions for 587 yards and five touchdowns last season with the Kansas City Chiefs. However, this season with the Eagles, Brown has just five catches for 63 yards and hasn’t been a fit in that offense.
There’s no doubt that Brown would give the Rams a more experienced third option at wide receiver, which is what they are lacking. At the same time, he is very similar to the types of players the Rams already have an abundance of at the position.
Heading into Week 10, the Rams’ depth chart at wide receiver will include Tutu Atwell, Xavier Smith, and Brennan Presley. All of those players are listed under 5’10”, and Smith is the heaviest at 180 pounds. Brown is 5’9, 170 pounds.
If a player like Stefon Diggs, Brandon Aiyuk, or someone similar became available , it wouldn’t be surprising to see the Rams explore those options. Given the Rams’ current wide receiver room, it’s hard to see them signing another undersized wide receiver unless they were to move on from someone like Atwell or Smith. However, that seems unlikely given how the Rams seem to prioritize players with familiarity in their system.
The Rams should absolutely explore every available option at wide receiver, especially with some of their injuries at the position. Brown may be one of the more recognizable names to become available, but that doesn't necessarily make him the right fit.

title: Without Puka Nacua, It's Time for the Rams to See What They Have in Rookie Wide Receiver CJ Daniels
full_text:
It’s been no secret that the Los Angeles Rams haven’t gotten a lot of production out of their rookie class. With their first pick, they took Ty Simpson, who has been the emergency third-string quarterback most weeks. With their next two picks, the Rams selected depth players in Max Klare and Keagen Trost. The most productive rookie for the Rams has been undrafted free agent edge rusher Wesley Bailey.
Through nine weeks, the Rams rank 31st in snap rate for their rookie class at 1.7 percent. The only team worse than them is the Denver Broncos at 1.3 percent. For the most part, unless the Rams have been forced to play their rookies, they haven’t seen the field.
Rookie snaps for every NFL team What do you notice? pic.twitter.com/VVzHr2LAgZ
With the Rams down to just three tight ends against the Los Angeles Chargers, they reverted to 11 personnel to start the game, a personnel grouping they weren’t built for. The Rams’ offense struggled, and they were forced to play Klare in the second half. That adjustment and going back to 13 personnel was a turning point in that game .
Despite Klare playing well against the Chargers, he was back to playing 0 snaps on offense last week against the Washington Commanders.
As the Rams head into Week 10 against the Arizona Cardinals, they are in a similar predicament at the wide receiver position. Without Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, the Rams will be relying on Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, Xavier Smith, and CJ Daniels at wide receiver.
The x-factor in all that is Daniels. Throughout training camp and the start of the season, head coach Sean McVay has consistently described Daniels as a mature rookie. All accounts are that Daniels impressed in training camp and, from a production standpoint, he performed well in the preseason.
“He’s just had a mature presence, kind of no nonsense but it's not too big for him. He's so secure to be able to handle coaching or corrections,” said McVay on Friday. “He plays big at the catch point. He has a physicality. A lot of the things that you're looking for from our receivers, he's checking those boxes and he's very curious. That's what you really want from these guys is the humility and the passion for the game.”
There’s certainly a difference in the level of play and complexion of the offense being run in the preseason compared to the regular season. Throughout the McVay era, the Rams have typically brought rookies along slowly, especially those at the skill positions outside of a few exceptions. The Rams have shown that when rookies demonstrate they are ready and can handle the intricacies of the offense, they will get an opportunity.
Still, given everything that Daniels showed in the offseason, it seems odd that he has yet to get that opportunity despite some of the injuries to the wide receiver position. Based on body type alone, it would seem that Daniels would be the most logical replacement for Adams. McVay hinted at a larger role for Daniels last week, but he played just one snap.
“He's had a lot of great moments behind the scenes,” said offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase this week. “We've been really encouraged about his development and his progression as the year has gone on. He's been as fun of a player to watch on our practice field for the last few weeks. I'm obviously excited for him to continue to get opportunities, but they're opportunities that he's earned through a lot of hard work, through a lot of consistency in how he's approached.”
The Rams are at a point in the season given their injury situation that they have nothing to lose by playing rookies. While the Rams needed the wide receiver depth, it was almost concerning when they brought Xavier Smith back this week after striking out at the trade deadline. The worst thing the Rams can do is give an ‘edge-of-the-roster’ type player snaps over someone with upside like Daniels.
That’s not even to say that Smith isn’t a good wide receiver. He showed some value last season when he ranked second in the NFL in EPA per target, was fourth in targeted success rate, and was top 20 in yards per route run. However, he should be getting snaps over a player like Tutu Atwell, not Daniels.
It’s time for the Rams to see what they have with some of their rookie class, and specifically Daniels. During the preseason, Daniels earned the most targets per route among wide receivers. His 1.91 yards per route run ranked sixth.
“C.J. has done a hell of a job,” said quarterback Matthew Stafford. “You look at the crossover tape when  Stetson and Ty are working against our defense, he's showing up in a big way a lot of different times. I'm excited to get some chances to throw with him, get it out there on Sunday, and just get his feet wet.”
Without Adams, Daniels is arguably the only wide receiver with the size to play outside the numbers. From a size standpoint, he’s a 99 percent match to Nacua via Mockdraftable. He’s 6’2, 202 pounds. Heading into Sunday, the average size of the Rams’ wide receiver depth chart is 5’9.8, 182.4 pounds.
With the Rams missing their top two options at wide receiver, it’s time to see what they have in Daniels. Given the depth of the roster early in the season, it made sense to be patient with the rookie. If Daniels is as ready as the coaching staff has suggested, it's time to put him on the field and let him prove it.

title: Rams Injury Report: Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie Questionable vs. Cardinals
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams will be managing several injuries on Sunday as they take on the Arizona Cardinals for the second time this season in Week 10. While wide receiver Puka Nacua went on injured reserve this week , left guard Steve Avila has been ruled out as well. Additionally, after making his return in Week 9 against the Washington Commanders, Myles Garrett has officially been listed as questionable but is expected to play, according to head coach Sean McVay.
“We're not 100,” said Garrett on Friday. “We're trying to make our way there and the bye week is coming at a perfect time for all of us. I think being able to get some extra practice myself, being on the field and being able to train and work on some things, getting in my rhythm, even without some games, I think will help us all in the long run.”
In addition to Garrett, tight end Davis Allen, long snapper Joe Cardona, cornerback Trent McDuffie, and safety Kam Curl were all listed as questionable. After being a non-participant in practice on Thursday, Allen was limited in Friday’s practice. With Colby Parkinson not having an injury designation, the Rams should be in a good spot at tight end if Allen is able to go.
More importantly, the Rams will be looking to get McDuffie back in action. He was a non-participant in practice on Thursday but was upgraded to limited on Friday. After returning against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 8, McDuffie missed last week’s game against the Commanders and has been nursing a back injury.
“A lot of it is going to be contingent upon how that limited work goes today. He was rolling, doing a lot of good stuff yesterday,” McVay said. “He's chomping at the bit to play, but a lot of that answer will be predicated on how he handles the physical workload today. I think if you asked him, he would say that he's hopeful to be able to play and so are we, but that could change based on how the workout goes.”
Without Nacua on Sunday, the Rams will be relying heavily on their wide receiver depth . The Rams signed Xavier Smith back to the roster this week and also added Brennan Presley to the active roster. With Avila out as well, Beaux Limmer will likely take his spot at left guard. While the Rams are hoping to get McDuffie back, if he is out, the Rams will rely on Emmanuel Forbes and Josh Wallace for a second straight week.
On the Cardinals’ side of things, defensive lineman Zach Carter, center Hjalte Froholdt, and interior offensive lineman Jon Gaines have all been ruled out. Additionally, tight end Hunter Long, cornerback Max Melton, offensive lineman Jayden Williams, safety Andrew Wingard, defensive lineman Roy Lopez, and defensive lineman Darius Robinson are all questionable.
Despite the injuries, the Rams have managed to win three consecutive games and put themselves back in the playoff hunt. Sunday's matchup against the Cardinals will be another opportunity to build on that momentum before heading into the bye week. With a difficult stretch of games coming up, the Rams can’t afford another division loss, especially against a Cardinals team that already beat them earlier this season.

title: Rams Officially Place Puka Nacua on Injured Reserve, Make Two Roster Moves
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams have officially placed wide receiver Puka Nacua on injured reserve . After Nacua got hurt late in the fourth quarter against the Washington Commanders on Sunday, it was determined that he suffered a sprained PCL and turf toe. While the Rams weren’t initially sure whether they would place Nacua on injured reserve, they made it official on Thursday.
In corresponding moves, the Rams signed wide receiver Brennan Presley to the active roster and added Tyler Scott to the practice squad.
With Nacua on injured reserve, he will miss at least the next four games. While the Rams have a bye next week, that does not count against the time missed. Nacua would have to miss games against the Arizona Cardinals, Green Bay Packers, Kansas City Chiefs, and San Francisco 49ers. That would put Nacua back for Week 15 against the Dallas Cowboys at the earliest.
Prior to Thursday, the Rams were unsure whether they would place Nacua on injured reserve . Teams are only allowed eight return designations during the season. The Rams had already used return designations on Keagen Trost, Myles Garrett, Ronnie Rivers, and Terrance Ferguson. They are also likely to use return designations on Kobie Turner and Davante Adams. If they plan on using one on Nacua as well, that would put them at seven of their eight available return designations.
While Nacua is out, the Rams will be relying on Konata Mumpfield , Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels, and Xavier Smith to fill in at wide receiver. Additionally, Adams should be back following the Packers game in Week 12.
Now that Nacua is on injured reserve, the Rams are very thin at the wide receiver position. It makes sense to bring up a player like Presley. Presley has spent time on the practice squad the last two years and could provide some special teams value. At Oklahoma State, Presley earned All-Big 12 honors as a kick returner.
The Rams also added Scott to the practice squad. Scott was on the practice squad last year with the Rams and spent all of training camp with the team before being let go as part of final roster cuts.
The additions of Presley and Scott give the Rams some flexibility at wide receiver, but it's difficult to see either player making a significant impact on offense. With the trade deadline already passed, the Rams don't have many options to improve the position. For now, they'll have to hope that their young receivers can provide enough production to keep the offense afloat until Adams and Nacua return.

title: Rams Midweek Report: Are the Playoffs Still Realistic? Puka Nacua to IR, and Trade Deadline Leftovers
full_text:
Just as things were starting to look better and the Los Angeles Rams could see the light at the end of the tunnel, they were hit with another barrage of injuries. Last week, it was expected that the Rams would get Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson back. With Davante Adams set to return in a few weeks, it was looking like as long as the Rams could stay afloat, the playoffs were still within reach.
As quickly as Ferguson returned, he was out again, this time with a hamstring injury that he suffered during his first practice back. During the game against the Washington Commanders, Steve Avila left the game with a hamstring injury and Puka Nacua injured his knee late in the fourth quarter. That doesn’t mention that Trent McDuffie had to miss Sunday’s game with a back injury. It marked the third game in four weeks that McDuffie missed.
At this point, do we need to add that the Rams are without Jaylen Watson for the rest of the season? All season it’s been one step forward and two steps back for the Rams on the injury front. The Rams have remained mostly healthy on the offensive line, but at skill positions, it certainly feels like 2022 all over again.
It’s not all bleak, though. For as injured as the Rams have been, they finally went on a run they needed. With their third straight win last week, the Rams improved to 5-4 and moved above .500 for the first time this season.
Now it becomes a matter of whether the Rams can survive this next wave of injuries to still be in contention for the playoffs come December. According to several metrics, the Rams have one of the more grueling schedules in the NFL over the second half of the season.
So the Rams future schedule... is... sheesh pic.twitter.com/XpSkHTWoHj
Following the Rams’ bye week, they will play the Green Bay Packers and Kansas City Chiefs. The Rams will be without Adams for at least the Packers game and likely Avila as well. With Puka Nacua set to go on injured reserve, they will be without Nacua for those games as well.
The Packers and Chiefs certainly have their flaws, but both have top-10 defenses. Through nine weeks, the Packers rank sixth in defensive EPA per play and the Chiefs rank tenth. The Rams were already inconsistent on offense. With Adams coming off of a hamstring injury and without Nacua and Avila, it could make things even more difficult.
If the Rams beat the Cardinals and then lose back-to-back games to the Packers and Chiefs, that puts them at 6-6. At that point, they’d have to rattle off five straight wins or hope that 10-7 is good enough to make the playoffs in a very difficult NFC.
While it certainly hurts their playoff chances, it doesn’t eliminate them. At that point, the Rams would be mostly healthy going into San Francisco and be in a position to make a run. It doesn’t seem crazy to think that the Rams could win five straight games to finish off the season.
Even if they were to lose to the 49ers, The Athletic’s projection gives them a 72 percent chance to make the postseason. An 11-6 finish puts them at 99 percent.
This isn’t to say the Rams’ season is over or that there’s reason to have a negative outlook. That is a realistic scenario. The Rams managed to show toughness and grit to survive the first half of the season. Now they’ll need to do the same in the second half.
There had been some thought that t he Rams may not place Nacua on injured reserve . The Rams only have eight return designations to use throughout the season. They’ve used one on Keagen Trost, Myles Garrett, Ronnie River, and Terrance Ferguson. The Rams will likely use one on Kobie Turner and Davante Adams. By putting Nacua on injured reserve with the expectation that he will come back, the Rams have one return designation remaining.
With Nacua set to go on injured reserve, he will be out at least four games. The bye week does not count. That means the earliest Nacua can return is Week 15 against the Dallas Cowboys on December 20. His absence against the Cardinals, Packers, Chiefs, and 49ers certainly makes things interesting. The Rams need to find a way to survive that stretch.
Following Tuesday’s trade deadline, the Rams came away empty-handed. Despite needing a wide receiver, the Rams opted to hold on to their draft assets. It’s certainly an odd decision considering that the WR1 right now is Konata Mumpfield.
With that said, that doesn’t mean the Rams didn’t try. According to ESPN’s Dan Graziano, the Rams were among the teams that called about Ladd McConkey. The Rams also called on Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Rashod Bateman , but wouldn’t give up what was being asked for him. Cleveland Browns beat reporter Mary Kay Cabot reported that the Rams also called on Jerry Jeudy. However, the Browns wanted premium draft picks.
While the Rams made trade calls, nothing ever got serious. The thinking in the building remains that they will get Davante Adams and Puka Nacua back this season and that making a trade and giving up assets wasn't necessary.
It was initially reported that the 49ers were going to release Brandon Aiyuk on Tuesday after he reported to the team. However, with Aiyuk on the Commissioner’s Exempt List, the 49ers are likely to hold on to him for the next two weeks. Once Aiyuk does become available, he’s a low-risk signing that the Rams should consider . He provides a solid WR3 option, and if he can return to his pre-injury form, the Rams would be getting a player who was once a borderline top-10 wide receiver.
Without Adams and Nacua, it will be interesting to see what Sean McVay does on offense. Back in 2018, defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz said,
“The hardest thing gap-control wise is 22 personnel (two backs, two tight ends),” Schwartz says. “Thirteen (one back, three tight ends), if you don’t know exactly what you’re doing on defense, 13 personnel can wear your ass out.”
A serious argument can be made that the best two players on offense for the Rams on Sunday will be Blake Corum and Kyren Williams. It could make sense to get both players on the field. Williams especially has proven to run good routes while Corum has been one of the more efficient running backs in the NFL.
Two weeks ago against the Los Angeles Chargers, it took an entire half before Sean McVay’s hand was forced and he had to play rookie tight end Max Klare. Playing Klare was the best decision McVay made in that game and left some wondering why he hadn’t been playing him previously.
The same can be said about CJ Daniels. By all accounts, Daniels impressed in training camp and the preseason. However, he has played just six snaps on offense. Given the Rams’ current wide receiver situation, that needs to change. It’s time to give Daniels an opportunity .
Not too much changed from Wednesday’s projection. However, tight end Davis Allen was downgraded from a limited participant to DNP with an oblique injury. Additionally, tight end Tyler Higbee was added as a non-participant due to an illness. The biggest thing for the Rams on Thursday was Nacua officially heading to injured reserve.

title: Rams Film Review: Myles Garrett Could Exploit Major Weakness Against Cardinals
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams finally got a glimpse of what a healthy Myles Garrett looks like on their defense against the Washington Commanders. After being out for almost two months with a knee injury, Garrett made his return last week and showed the Rams why they traded for him.
Despite playing only 60 percent of the defensive snaps, Garrett made his impact felt. He played 28 pass rush snaps and finished with three sacks, including one forced fumble. The explosiveness and bend that Garrett lacked in Week 1 were on display against the Commanders.
Just look at that bend around the edge from Myles Garrett. Can tell he was really starting starting to feel like himself and gain confidence as the game went on. pic.twitter.com/P3Xeo1cl5w
In his first game back, Garrett had a 21.4 percent pressure rate and generated six pressures. His 28.6 percent pass rush win rate led all edge rushers for the week as well.  The Rams traded for Garrett to be their closer on defense and two of his three sacks came in the fourth quarter. His third sack was on a 3rd-and-4 to set up a 4th-and-17 and helped stop a late surge by the Commanders offense.
One of the main reasons Aaron Donald came out of retirement was to play alongside Garrett. It took two months, but the wait was worth it. It’s no coincidence that Donald’s best game of the season came with Garrett on the field.
Blocking Myles Garrett: LG, LT, TE Blocking Aaron Donald: RG (kinda), RT, RB Even with Myles Garrett, Donald still managing to get triple teamed 😭😂 pic.twitter.com/QZXxWcdRj5
For much of his career, offenses had to focus all of their attention on Donald. That’s not something they could do with Garrett on the edge. Donald finished Sunday’s game with a season-high four pressures and a 12.9 percent pressure rate.
“Myles obviously did a great job, but I thought ‘AD’ had a couple awesome things that allowed him to be able to get some one-on-ones and get freed up and thought the plan that we had was really beneficial,” said head coach Sean McVay. “Yesterday was the first day that it was on tape of how you're deploying Myles. It may or may not be the same or different as you continue to increase his snap count as he's feeling better and getting back to being able to play that workload that he's been accustomed to throughout his whole career, but it was very impactful as was ‘AD’.”
Using Garrett solely in pass rush situations gave the Rams more flexibility in how they deployed him. Throughout the game, Chris Shula occasionally mugged Garrett over the center. This is something that the Rams did with Verse occasionally, but Garrett also had success doing it in Cleveland.
The Browns defense aligned Myles Garrett over the center on four plays against the Bengals. Here were the results: -Sack -Incompletion -Incompletion -Incompletion Jim Schwartz is weaponizing him by moving him around the front. The entire Steelers OL better come ready to rock. pic.twitter.com/OHqhY2kZWl
Garrett lined up over the center on four plays against the Commanders. On those plays, he had two pressures, created a pressure for Donald on a stunt, and had one sack. Garrett’s size and speed make it very difficult for the average center to block one-on-one.
This is likely something that the Rams will try to take advantage of this week against the Cardinals as well. Hjalte Froholdt and Jon Gaines have been out of practice for the Cardinals with injuries. That would leave Hayden Conner as the third-string center, who is also technically the fourth-string guard.
The Cardinals could be down to their 4th-string center on Sunday. That could be a problem. The Rams situationally put Garrett over the center and had success with it. pic.twitter.com/JFf2EFuYlf
With the Rams down their starting two wide receivers, they may have to rely on their defense more. While the defense had been good for much of the season, Garrett helped take it to the next level that many have been waiting to see . The presence of Garrett could be enough to help carry the Rams over the next month until they get healthy on offense again.

title: How the Rams Offense Can Survive Without Puka Nacua and Davante Adams
full_text:
Over the next few games, the Los Angeles Rams will need to figure out how to manage without their top two wide receivers. Davante Adams is likely out at least the next three weeks and Puka Nacua could be out four. With Adams and Nacua out, the Rams will need to get what they can out of Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell. It’s not necessarily a predicament that the Rams want to be in.
Heading into Week 10, the Rams are one of two teams  that will play without a wide receiver who has even 250 receiving yards in 2026. The other team is the Indianapolis Colts, who traded away their top two wide receivers at the trade deadline.
Throughout the season, the Rams have been inconsistent on offense to say the least. Against the Los Angeles Chargers, they went three-and-out on each of their first five possessions. That’s not something a Rams offense had done this century, and that includes offenses coached by Jeff Fisher. Nacua was in the lineup for those games.
This isn’t to say that the Rams’ offense can’t figure it out or nobody will step up. However, it also wouldn’t be incorrect to believe that being without Adams and Nacua will make things more difficult offensively. That also doesn’t mention the absence of Avila at left guard.
At the end of the day, the Rams will be relying on Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, and CJ Daniels at wide receiver. Mumpfield is a seventh-round pick, Atwell  likely would have been cut by the Miami Dolphins had the Rams not traded for him, and Daniels has played six snaps on offense. The Rams also re-signed Xavier Smith, who was previously cut back in Week 3.
The Rams’ current wide receiver situation would leave some wishing for the days of Austin Pettis, Chris Givens, and Brandon Gibson. Head coach Sean McVay joked on Wednesday about the possibility of Robert Woods coming out of retirement. It’s bleak to say the least, but that’s where the Rams are at.
For as much as the Rams may want to lean on the defense and run game, they will have to be able to prove they can still throw the ball. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers won a game this season in which Baker Mayfield didn’t complete a pass. However, it’s highly unlikely that the Rams get blessed with monsoon conditions at State Farm Stadium on Sunday or back at SoFi following the bye.
This season, the Rams’ entire offense has been Puka Nacua. Nacua has 715 yards receiving. All other Rams wide receivers that have recorded a catch this season have combined for 753. Mumpfield and Atwell have a combined 261 receiving yards this season. Nacua had 230 yards in the last two weeks alone.
Offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase talked last week about how much the team trusts the wide receiver group behind Nacua. “I think the encouragement that we have is we have guys that we feel we can put trust in to be able to supplement him in the right ways.”
On Wednesday, quarterback Matthew Stafford also mentioned how much trust he has in that group.
“I still throw those guys every single day in practice and have a ton of trust in what they can do,” Stafford said. “With those guys, trust the route running techniques that they have. Trust themselves to go out there and make plays because these guys are here for a reason. I'm excited for their opportunity.”
Despite what Scheelhaase and Stafford have said, it’s become abundantly clear that they don’t have trust in that group. Mumpfield leads the Rams’ wide receiver depth with a 6.8 percent target share on the season. Among players who have run at least 100 routes, that ranks 101st out of 111 wide receivers.
Just in the last three weeks without Adams, Nacua has a 43.2 percent target share. Only CeeDee Lamb’s is higher. Mumpfield’s target share of 6.3 percent ranks 72nd out of 75 qualifying players. Atwell’s 9.5 percent ranks 63rd.
While some will say that Stafford has simply locked onto Nacua, you only have to look at the receivers around him to understand why that might be the case. Mumpfield has a targeted success rate of 39.1 percent. Atwell remains limited as a route runner. Almost half of his routes are deep corner or go routes.
For as much as Xavier Smith struggles as the team’s punt returner, he did show some upside at receiver last season. There’s a reason he was getting snaps over Atwell. Smith led the Rams in EPA per target and was only behind Nacua in targeted success rate and yards per route run. There is at least some logic to why the Rams brought him back with him having some success and being familiar in the system.
Again, Daniels has six snaps on offense this season. While he was a training camp and preseason standout, he hasn’t been able to see the field. McVay has shown in the past that if a rookie wide receiver displays an understanding of the offense, they’ll play. That has not been the case up to this point with Daniels.
Last week, McVay hinted at a larger role for Daniels . He played one offensive snap. With three healthy wide receivers, now seems as good of a time as any for Daniels to get his chance. At this point, it’s hard to understand why Daniels hasn’t gotten more involved given that Adams has been out the last three weeks.
As the game progressed, you really saw Ty Simpson start to get comfortable. With be interested if Rams let him off the reigns a little bit next week. Tight coverage on CJ Daniels and Simpson throws an accurate ball. pic.twitter.com/ZPOUISGzac
“I don't know that I could really say any areas of improvement until he truly gets his opportunity,” McVay said on Monday. “He is a guy that, no question about it, will get an opportunity to play more snaps moving forward.”
“C.J. has done a hell of a job,” added Stafford. “I'm excited to get some chances to throw with him, get it out there on Sunday, and just get his feet wet. It's an opportunity, like I said, for a lot of guys in this situation that we're in. I'm just excited to go be a part of it.”
The Rams have done a lot of talking about how much they trust their wide receiver depth and how good of a job they’ve done, but it’s time for them to turn words into action.
Outside of the wide receivers, the Rams could look to use their tight ends as well. The Rams will likely operate heavily out of 13 personnel. However, that could limit the passing game with Terrance Ferguson out nursing a hamstring. Tyler Higbee has shown some of his limitations as he’s gotten older. Without Ferguson at tight end, the rest of the group lacks explosiveness.
Throughout his tenure, McVay has devised one-off gameplans in these exact types of situations. In 2021, when the Rams were hit by COVID, McVay used six offensive linemen. When the Rams were injured for the Jacksonville Jaguars game last season, he implemented 13 personnel that has since become the identity of the offense.
If there is any head coach that can figure out how to run an offense with limited options at wide receiver, it’s McVay. The two best offensive players on the field against the Cardinals will likely be Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. It may be unlikely, but operating out of 22 personnel with two tight ends and two running backs wouldn’t be a crazy idea.
Without Nacua and Adams, an argument can be made that Williams is the best receiving option on the team. Williams’ 1.34 yards per route run is higher than Mumpfield or Atwell’s. Corum isn’t perfect as a pass catcher, but still averages 1.74 yards per route run, which also ranks seventh among running backs. Both Williams and Corum also rank inside the top 15 among qualifying running backs in first downs per route run.
Even if the Rams don’t go to the extreme and use 22 personnel, both will likely be used often in the passing game to some capacity. Williams had 10 receptions in Week 4 against the Eagles. Without Nacua in Week 3 against the Denver Broncos, Williams had six receptions.
The Rams are going to have to get creative in the passing game until Nacua and Adams return. It’s also possible they look at wide receiver options as they become available as well. McVay will need to…

title: Rams vs. Cardinals Prediction: Preview, Key Matchups, and What to Watch
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams will be looking to get their first division win on Sunday in Week 10 as they take on the Arizona Cardinals for the second time this season. Both teams will enter Sunday dealing with their own set of injuries . The Rams will have to manage without Puka Nacua, among others, while the Cardinals will be without Gardner Minshew at quarterback.
Since losing to the Cardinals back in Week 6, the Rams have won three straight games. The loss to the Cardinals marked rock bottom, but they’ve managed to climb back to .500 for the first time in 2026. However, the Rams continue to get bombarded with injuries. Along with Nacua, the Rams could be without Steve Avila, Trent McDuffie, and others in addition to the players already on injured reserve.
Carson Beck will be making his first career start for the Cardinals on Sunday, and it won’t be easy for him. The Cardinals will be without Michael Wilson and could be down to their fourth-string center. Beck will also be facing a Rams defense that looked good with Myles Garrett back last week.
Back in Week 6, the Rams were without Alaric Jackson at left tackle, and the Cardinals took advantage, blitzing Stafford relentlessly.For the most part, McVay was outcoached by defensive coordinator Nick Rallis. With Avila out and the Rams not having Nacua , it wouldn’t be surprising to see a similar game plan from the Cardinals.
The Rams will be one of just two teams in Week 10 playing without a wide receiver who has recorded at least 250 receiving yards in 2026. Throughout the season, the Rams have been inconsistent on offense, and that was with Nacua. It’s going to be much more difficult when the top wide receiver options are Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell. At some point, the Rams are going to have to be able to beat teams in the passing game and will need to prove they can still do so.
In the first game against the Cardinals, the Rams didn’t allow a single touchdown. However, they did allow long drives that ended in field goals. They allowed the Cardinals to play keep away and control the game. It wouldn’t be surprising to see the Cardinals come out with a similar game plan as they look to keep things simple for Beck in his first start.
Jayden Williams has allowed an 8.3 percent pressure rate this season. Among qualifying offensive linemen, that’s the 10th-highest in the NFL. The Rams got Myles Garrett back last week, and he made his presence felt with three sacks and a forced fumble. Chris Shula will likely move Garrett around and line him up over the center occasionally, but he should be set up to have another strong performance.
Given the amount of injuries on both sides, this is looking like it could be an ugly game. Both teams will be rolling out preseason-caliber options at wide receiver. With that said, Beck is making his first start and the Cardinals haven’t won at home since early last year. The Rams need a win going into their bye week to set themselves up well for the second half of the season. Without Nacua, the Rams will need to lean on the defense and run game. Prediction: Rams 16, Cardinals 10

title: Rams Injury Report: Trent McDuffie Status Uncertain as Rams Face More Injury Troubles
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams could be significantly short-handed on Sunday as they get ready for their Week 6 rematch against the Arizona Cardinals. Steve Avila, Puka Nacua, Trent McDuffie, Kam Curl, and Terrance Ferguson were all projected as non-participants in Wednesday’s walkthrough, with most of them likely to miss the game.
One player that the Rams will hope to get back this week is cornerback Trent McDuffie. After McDuffie returned against the Los Angeles Chargers, he missed last week’s game with a back injury.
“I think we're optimistic that this week he will be able to go,” said head coach Sean McVay. “With the injury that he sustained, it's weird because you have these muscles around it in the back, which in some of the movement, especially at his position. He's so damn tough but you want to make sure that you're putting him in a position to have a successful outcome.”
The Rams are set to be without Puka Nacua, Steve Avila, and Terrance Ferguson against the Cardinals. McVay noted on Wednesday that the Rams won’t place Nacua on injured reserve due to the limited return designations they have available. With Avila and Ferguson, the Rams are expecting both to be out a few weeks.
Also showing up on Wednesday’s injury report were Joe Cardona, Davis Allen, Colby Parkinson, and Myles Garrett, who were all projected as limited participants. Cardona has missed the last two games with an ankle injury. Allen and Parkinson will be players to monitor throughout the week. While Garrett showed up on the injury report, that shouldn’t be surprising going forward. The Rams will likely manage him during the week to ensure that he’s ready for gameday.
Despite the Rams being as injured as they are, the Cardinals might be in a worse spot. The Cardinals are set to be without Gardner Minshew, meaning Carson Beck will get his first career start against the Rams. Additionally, Michael Wilson injured his neck and will be out.
Hjalte Froholdt (concussion), Jon Gaines (ankle), and Roy Lopez (toe/ankle) were all non-participants for the Cardinals on Wednesday as well.
The Rams have dealt with injuries throughout the season, but the situation has become especially challenging over the last few weeks. With several key starters expected to miss Sunday's game, the Rams will once again have to rely on their depth to avoid getting swept by the Cardinals. They’ve managed to win three straight games despite their injuries, but continuing that success without players like Nacua and Avila won’t be easy.
