title: Kirk Cousins Trade Doesn’t Change That Vikings Will Still Have QB Needs in 2027
full_text:
Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley and head coach Kevin O’Connell made the right decision earlier this week by trading a 2027 third-round pick to the Raiders for Kirk Cousins, who was officially named the Week 10 starter on Friday . With a championship-level defense and an offense barreling off a cliff, something needed to change.
Thanks to the trade, the team returns to a familiar, safe face, and it’s clear the locker room and fanbase are optimistic about the potential of an all-in run for the Lombardi this season. If it works, I’m not sure many Vikings fans will care much about what comes next.
The quest for a quarterback has been a decades-long process for the Vikings, and odds are, it is nowhere near finished.
It probably isn’t shocking to anyone to say that a 38-year-old Kirk Cousins is unlikely to be the Vikings starter three to four years down the line. While making roster moves in a vacuum is typically a bad idea, this one simply had to be done. The Vikings defense has made this team a contender, and while the offense may not suddenly turn into the 2007 Patriots upon Cousins’s arrival, any bit of added consistency will help immensely.
Does this mean Teasley is kicking the QB can down the road? Not exactly. The first-year GM was asked what this move may mean for the future during his media availability on Wednesday, and he made it clear that they are still exploring all options.
LIVE: GM Nolan Teasley https://t.co/dLFPTysolV
It’s clear that Teasley understands his burden, and while Cousins may elevate the Vikings right now, there are still plenty of questions to answer for the future. The simplest path is to bring Cousins back and draft a QB for him to mentor, something he once seemed hesitant to do as he sought out a long-term deal in 2024. His current contract includes a two-year, $80 million option after this season, but the Vikings would almost certainly void it before negotiating a new contract.
Other options include soon-to-be free agent Mac Jones, whose youth and schematic fit may be appealing. Then there’s the big fish. The Vikings reportedly checked in on Justin Herbert before the trade deadline, but the Chargers quickly ended the call. I wouldn't be shocked if they call once again this offseason.
The #Vikings also inquired about Justin Herbert, Daniel Jones and Geno Smith before striking a deal with the #Raiders for Kirk Cousins, per multiple league sources. The Colts listened but did not want to move Jones, while the Jets felt Smith was too important to the team and the… https://t.co/UwF8tzZDU7 pic.twitter.com/4ghV7bd7JV
Whatever the path may be, the team is in desperate need of their quarterback hero, especially after their latest attempts have failed disastrously.
O’Connell and former Vikings GM Kwesi Adofo-Mensah were tasked with finding and developing a long-term answer at the QB position when they were hired in 2022. Although the process took some time, they eventually took a swing at J.J. McCarthy with the tenth overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft just over a month after Cousins left in free agency.
With Adofo-Mensah fired, McCarthy on the Giants , and Cousins back in Minnesota after stops in Atlanta and Vegas, it’s safe to say the plan was unsuccessful after only two years.
The Vikings signed Kyler Murray to a one-year minimum deal this past offseason, hoping the 29-year-old could be their answer for years to come. After only five full games as the starter, that dream came to a harsh end. Now, the Vikings turn back to Cousins, hoping for a run to the Super Bowl while they prepare for whatever comes next.
Let’s hope that Teasley and O’Connell have a better plan this time around.

title: 3 Most Important Things Vikings Fans Must Watch for in Week 10 Road Clash vs. Packers
full_text:
There’s new hope in the Minnesota air after an embarrassing passing performance on Monday Night Football led to the reacquisition of former Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Raiders.
Now, the Vikings head into Week 10’s matchup against the Packers with a fighting chance to showcase a competent offense , something that seemed impossible just a few days ago. With playoff seeding slipping away and the back half of a brutal four-game stretch now upon them, the urgency has never been higher for Cousins and the 2026 Vikings.
Here’s what to watch for as the Vikings look to get back in the win column.
It was a late October Sunday in 2023. Cousins and the Vikings had overcome a 1-4 start and were looking to complete the climb back to .500 with a win in Green Bay. Everything was clicking, even without an injured Justin Jefferson. Then, in the third quarter, disaster struck as Cousins hobbled off the field with a torn Achilles, ending his time in purple.
Vikings @ Packers this Sunday… Scriptwriters couldn’t have planned it any better. pic.twitter.com/PxPF9pMg0a
Even if he faces a hiccup or two after being named the Week 10 starter on Friday, the alternatives seem far worse , even as Cousins reacclimates. Safe to assume, then, that he’ll be making his return to the Vikings on the exact field he last donned the horned helmet on.
It’s hard to project exactly what we’ll see after only a couple of practices, but it will likely be a massive improvement over what we’ve witnessed with Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz.
If Cousins and Co. can walk away with a win, his teammates may have to bust out the chains and Rolexes again on the short flight home.
Sunday will mark the 10th matchup between Kevin O’Connell and Matt LaFleur since O’Connell took over as head coach in 2022. Both have been touted as two of the best offensive minds in the NFL, even as their own fan bases often criticize their play-calling and decision-making. Ironically, most NFL teams would gladly drop their current coach for a shot at either of them.
O’Connell will look to add a seventh win to his 6-3 record against the Packers, while LaFleur will be looking to make his series record a tad more respectable. With divisional and conference seeding in the balance, Sunday’s battle of the offensive minds should provide plenty of fireworks. That is, if another elite coach doesn’t have his say …
Make no mistake: the Vikings do not defeat the Packers in Week 1 without a stellar day from Brian Flores’s defense. Their ability to create short fields and turnovers set Wentz and the Vikings' offense up for a 39-22 comeback victory. But the Green Bay offense they’ll face this Sunday won't be the same as it was two months ago.
JORDAN LOVE CHRISTIAN WATSON PACKERS ARE DOMINATING GBvsNE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hxEPzs2KdC
The Packers' offensive line is healthier and much improved after allowing four sacks in Week 1. Their 17 sacks allowed through nine games are the 12th-fewest in the NFL this season. Their passing game is also finding its stride, with wideouts Christian Watson and Matthew Golden posting massive performances in a 45-27 victory against the Patriots last week.
Needless to say, the Vikings defense will need to bring its A-game against Jordan Love and the Packers offense on the road. Hopefully, their offense will now be able to get them some rest by sustaining a drive or two.

title: Vikings' Grim Week 10 Injury Report Will Likely Force Trio Into Bigger Roles vs. Packers
full_text:
The Vikings are entering their matchup against the Packers with key injuries on both sides of the ball. While this new guy at quarterback may provide some juice , there's no question that Minnesota still has to overcome significant hurdles against its division rival as injuries plague the roster.
The #Vikings final Week 10 injury report OUT: LB Blake Cashman, TE T.J. Hockenson, DL Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins, WR Jauan Jennings and QB Kyler Murray QUESTIONABLE: WR Jordan Addison (thumb), S Joshua Metellus (shoulder) and OLB Kyle Van Noy pic.twitter.com/WU1CfJg9Hr
With an injury report longer than Kirk Cousins' Kohl's shopping list, the Vikings will need to rely on their reserves to step up in a big way after ruling out multiple key players on Friday.
With Blake Cashman unable to clear the concussion protocol, Eric Wilson will likely be joined by a committee of Pace and rookie Jake Golday. Pace has seen his role reduced in recent years after a strong rookie campaign, but he did play very well last week against Buffalo, notching a sack in just 22 snaps.
Ivan Pace Jr. brings the pressure 💥 📺 Watch live on @NFLonDAZN , @SkySports and @talkSPORT pic.twitter.com/O7XREgogYK
Defensive coordinator Brian Flores will probably get Golday some looks as well after the rookie saw a career-high in snaps last week, but in all likelihood it'll be the veteran Pace who the defensive coordinator leans on. Pace's run discipline and pass coverage leave much to be desired, but if the Vikings need a Tasmanian Devil to get after Jordan Love before he finds a receiver 50 yards down the field, Pace is the man for the job.
The Vikings could also use more dime looks with Cashman out, and with how well the Packers stretch the field, it wouldn't be surprising at all. Still, Pace will have a chance at some redemption on Sunday in a contract year after falling out of favor over the last few seasons.
T.J. Hockenson has served as a great security blanket for the revolving door of Vikings quarterbacks this season, and now Kirk Cousins will have to play his first game back without the friendly face. The Vikings' second leading receiver will miss this Sunday's Packers game, and Bartholomew looks to be the next man up, with Josh Oliver already out for the year.
Bartholomew already stepped up big in one game this season, reeling in five catches against New Orleans after Hockenson went down early, and he'll now get called on again.
With Jauan Jennings also out, and Jordan Addison now potentially following suit, the Vikings' pass catchers will be awfully thin . Is it weird to say that Bartholomew will probably have a bigger game than Myles Price, Tai Felton or Odell Beckham Jr.?
Unfortunately, it doesn't seem weird in the slightest.
Banks was a healthy scratch last week, and now could be playing 30 or 40 snaps just days later at Green Bay. Head coach Kevin O'Connell confirmed that his benching last week was simply what the game plan called for, and now this week's will require that Banks plays "a ton."
"He'll be up and he's going to play a ton this week." - Head Coach Kevin O'Connell on DL Caleb Banks pic.twitter.com/1Rx5kBzmyw
The first-round pick hasn't made much of an impact yet, but with Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins out, Banks will get called upon whether he's ready or not. Banks was always looked at as a long-term developmental project, but early returns may be emphasizing the "long" aspect more than Minnesota had hoped.
Banks has the lowest Pro Football Focus grade among all rookie defensive tackles , but he's also only played 107 snaps. This week at Green Bay might provide the first real litmus test as to how far along the Vikings rookie actually is—or isn't.

title: Is Kirk Cousins Starting vs. the Packers in Week 10? Latest on Vikings QB's Return
full_text:
As the Vikings prepare to face the Packers for the first time since the season opener, fans across Minnesota are wondering one thing: Will Kirk Cousins be ready to suit up for Sunday's NFC North collision?
Even though Cousins has been around the block, it doesn't change the fact that he'd likely need some time to adjust to his old team again. Although some familiar faces from his last stint remain, these aren't the same Vikings from three seasons ago, and no one would blame him for sitting out at least one game to reacclimate .
Fortunately, Cousins is seemingly build different.
On Friday afternoon, Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell revealed that Cousins will be starting against the Packers this weekend . It'll be his first time putting on the Purple and Gold since tearing his ACL, ironically, against Green Bay in Week 8 of the 2023 season.
Head Coach Kevin O'Connell has announced that QB Kirk Cousins will start Sunday at Green Bay. pic.twitter.com/zSMqWo0pHQ
As great as it's been to see Cousins around his teammates and coaches this week, the only thing that truly matters is what he'll do on the field this weekend.
After all, Minnesota might be 6-2, but little of that success stems from the passing game. Whether it was Kyler Murray or Carson Wentz under center, the Vikings' offensive performance hasn't looked like it belongs to a team that's four games above .500. They currently rank 27th in points per game, 31st in total yards per game and 30th in yards per play.
The Packers' defense isn't as elite as the Vikings', but they still rank 11th in points and yards allowed per game. In other words, the status quo likely wouldn't be good enough, and all eyes are on Cousins to see if he can bring the improvements Minnesota's attack desperately needs. In fact, here's how he ranks among other QBs this season when it comes to:
It'll be nice to see Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison with a quarterback who can take full advantage of their talents.
Vikings fans still remember the magic that the Cousins-Jefferson connection created during the 2022 season, which saw the star WR pace the NFL in catches (128), receiving yards (1,809) and first downs before being named the AP NFL Offensive Player of the Year. Meanwhile, Addison posted a 36-482-7 stat line in the eight games he played with Cousins in 2023, making it interesting to see if they can rekindle that flame.
With T.J. Hockenson officially ruled out for Sunday , Cousins will need to maximize the damage he can do with each of his healthy weapons to keep the Vikings afloat at the top of the NFC North. Doing so will not only stop Minnesota's skid but also give fans an idea of what to expect for the rest of the season.

title: 3 Missed Vikings Trade Opportunities Nolan Teasley Should've Made at the Deadline
full_text:
The Vikings made one of the splashier trades before Tuesday's deadline by bringing back quarterback Kirk Cousins, but they also could've been a bit more active , too.
Ahead of the deadline, the Vikings were reportedly sniffing around deals for running back, offensive line, defensive line and more, but ultimately general manager Nolan Teasley called it a day after acquiring Cousins.
And while the Cousins deal should do wonders for the anemic offense , there were also three other deals the Vikings should've made.
Let's discuss how the deadline should've gone down after the QB reunion.
After the stunning Jordan Davis deal and the attempted Arnold Ebiketie trade, the Eagles were clearly open for business at the deadline. Guard Landon Dickerson's name had been floated as a potential trade piece with the 2-7 Birds entering a retool at bare minimum, but the 28-year-old stayed put.
And despite being one of the interested teams in Quenton Nelson a few weeks ago, the Vikings opted not to add a guard at the deadline.
The trade compensation for Dickerson likely would've been similar to that of the Cousins deal, and so it's always possible the Vikings weren't comfortable parting with both of their third-round picks. Still, a deal for Dickerson would've solidified the 2026 interior in front of Cousins and helped them move on from the underwhelming Will Fries in 2027.
The Vikings were reportedly looking at adding along the defensive front at the deadline, and one name that stuck out as a logical add was Robinson. The 31-year-old generated some interest around the league, but ultimately the Buccaneers never moved him.
Robinson has one of the more bizarre statlines for a defensive tackle this season with 24 tackles, one sack, eight quarterback pressures, and two interceptions. But what really sets Robinson apart is his run defense. His 86.2 Pro Football Focus grade against the run ranks second to someone Vikings fans may recognize: Jalen Redmond. Getting the top two-rated run defenders in the NFL on one roster would've made the league's best defense even more unstoppable, but it seems that no one was able to entice Tampa Bay enough.
The Vikings actually attempted to trade away Jennings to San Francisco , but the wide receiver essentially vetoed the deal. Perhaps no other teams had interest, but the Vikings clearly thought it best to move on from the failed free-agent signing and recoup whatever draft compensation they could.
Jennings has just six catches for 54 yards on the season, and potentially the addition of Cousins might ignite his production, but the Vikings were probably better off just getting their late-round pick and moving on. Tai Felton, Myles Price and Odell Beckham Jr. haven't exactly been stuffing the stat sheet either, but it was clear that there were some wide receiver-needy teams across the NFL willing to pony up.
In all, three receivers were moved before the deadline, but the Vikings will now hope Cousins can unlock Jennings a bit more.

title: Forgotten Vikings WR Suddenly Looks More Important Amid Jauan Jennings Injury Concerns
full_text:
The Vikings will look to avoid a third straight loss when they visit the rival Packers in Week 10 , but a lengthy injury list could make that job easier said than done. After Thursday, six veteran players have missed back-to-back practices to start the week , increasing the likelihood that head coach Kevin O'Connell & Co. will be shorthanded Sunday afternoon.
One of this week's absentees is wide receiver Jauan Jennings, who's been hampered by a calf injury. On Tuesday, his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said he didn't expect Jennings's injury to be serious (h/t VikingzFanPage), but it's becoming concerning that the 29-year-old WR still hasn't seen the practice field this week.
#Vikings WR Jauan Jennings (calf) should be back next week, per his agent @DrewJRosenhaus . He is not expected to be traded before today’s deadline. pic.twitter.com/SCrlDgW2iI
Jennings hasn't done much this season (six catches for 54 touchdown-less receiving yards), but he was starting to step up recently. Assuming that trend would've continued against the Packers, who've allowed the T-14th-most receiving touchdowns (13) this season, it's safe to say that Jennings's absence might be felt.
When one door closes, another opens, though. A certain Minnesota WR has fallen off the radar recently, but a potential Jennings absence in Week 10 could put the forgotten playmaker back in a spot to make some noise this weekend.
When the 2026 NFL season began, Tai Felton was one of the bigger question marks in the Vikings' offense. The former 2025 third-round pick spent more snaps on special teams (293) than on offense (46) as a rookie, resulting in three catches for 25 receiving yards and a lot of questions about how Minnesota would use him behind top WRs Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison.
Year 2 started with nothing to write home about, as Felton failed to haul in two targets in the first three games and averaged 11.7 offensive snaps per appearance. Week 4 vs. the Dolphins seemed to be a turning point, as Felton recorded a then-season-high 14-yard reception before following that up with two catches for 27 yards against the Saints one week later.
It truly seemed like Felton was turning the page ahead of the bye week, but that's where his momentum stopped. Since Week 7, Felton has been targeted only once while playing 12 offensive snaps in the last three games, including when fellow depth WR Myles Price out-targeted him 4-to-0 against the Bills.
His present outlook isn't promising, but it's far too early to give up on Felton, who won't even turn 24 years old until March. His confidence might be shot at the moment, but that can quickly change with a solid effort in a must-win NFC North collision.
The Packers have done a commendable job defending the air this season, but that doesn't mean they're perfect.
After all, Green Bay has allowed an average of 255.0 passing yards in its last three games—not only noticeably above its season average (213.9), but also the eighth-most league-wide during that stretch. Sure, the Packers beat the Patriots last week despite those flaws, but it's worth noting that the Vikings' rival allowed 320 receiving yards and three TDs on just 22 catches in the win.
Hopefully, Felton and the rest of the Vikings' pass-catchers find a way to have a stronger performance against the Packers than they did in Week 1. Although Minnesota notched the season-opening win, Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz combined for only 15-of-24 passing for 151 passing yards, three touchdowns, and an interception.
It was good enough to get the job done that day, but now, with the NFC North's walls closing in, probably not?
A returning Kirk Cousins (assuming he plays) would be the first step toward having more aerial success against an arch-rival. Felton stepping up and proving why he was worthy of a Day 2 selection last year would be a solid second step.

title: Vikings Face Potential QB Conundrum If Kirk Cousins Doesn’t Play in Week 10
full_text:
Kirk Cousins should be expected to start at quarterback for the Minnesota Vikings against the Green Bay Packers on Sunday. However, there is a chance that the veteran passer won't be ready to suit up for the Week 10 contest.
Playing a game with a new team with less than a week to prepare is a huge challenge for any player, even someone with 15 seasons of experience. The problem is that if the recently acquired passer doesn't play, there aren't many good options. On Wednesday, Cousins even admitted that it was too "early" to say if he'd be ready to face the Packers (h/t Bring Me The Sports ).
"I don't think I can give you a fair answer only because of how early in the week it is." Kirk Cousins on if he's prepared to start for the Vikings on Sunday. pic.twitter.com/RMgcBDYNww
Any divisional game is a big game, but it feels even bigger when it is a border battle against the Packers. Deciding who should start at quarterback if it isn't Cousins is a tough choice, but head coach Kevin O'Connell would have to make it with confidence.
If Vikings fans hadn't just seen Carson Wentz have a historically bad game against the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football, he would have been the obvious choice. He finished with a Pro Football Focus grade of 22.3 and a QBR of 2.3, completing only 32% of his passes, fumbling, and throwing two interceptions without scoring a touchdown.
Minnesota can not feel comfortable starting him again any time soon. Considering he is 33 years old and in his 11th NFL season, that might have been his final start as a pro before his retirement. He is also limited in practice on the injury report with an ankle injury, which makes the odds of him playing even worse.
Kyler Murray missed the game against the Bills with a hamstring injury and is still not practicing for Minnesota on this week's injury report. If he is healthy enough to play, he becomes the best non-Cousins option on the Vikings' roster.
However, even when Murray is healthy, he hasn't been great for the Purple and Gold. Despite a 5-1 record as Minnesota's starter and a five-to-three touchdown-to-interception ratio, he has struggled to get the Vikings' offense going, averaging just 170.3 passing yards per game and an ESPN QBR of 45.7.
Before last week, Max Brosmer wouldn't have been an option. However, when he entered the game against the Bills after Wentz was benched, he looked solid. He completed six of seven passes against Buffalo for 58 yards. That's only 25 fewer yards than Wentz passes while he threw over three times as many passes.
Still, Brosmer is the QB4 in Minnesota for a reason, and it will take more than one solid showing in garbage time of a game to earn a start in Week 10. Cousins should be the man for the job, and if he can't play, Murray should be the next man up, if he is healthy.

title: 3 Bold Vikings Predictions Heading Into Week 10 Showdown Against Packers
full_text:
It seems like yesterday that the Vikings were hosting the Packers in Week 1 to kick off the 2026 season. Now, the two teams will conclude their regular-season series with a chilly match at Lambeau Field. Vikings fans are still riding the excitement from a major adrenaline injection early this week as the team reacquired quarterback Kirk Cousins via trade with the Las Vegas Raiders. What once looked like a potential beatdown in Green Bay now looks like a massive opportunity for the Vikings to end a two-game losing streak and sweep their biggest rival.
There’s still a lot up in the air, especially since head coach Kevin O’Connell hasn't technically named Cousins the starter yet. But let’s be real: Cousins is starting unless there's a major setback . So, let’s dive into some predictions for Sunday, assuming “Kirko Chainz” makes his triumphant return.
Frick it, Justin Jefferson is down there somewhere. There is perhaps no larger beneficiary of the Cousins’ reunion tour than Jefferson. The seventh-year wide receiver is on pace to have the worst year of his career after poor QB play wrecked his 2025 campaign. Needless to say, it’s time for Jefferson to reclaim his spot on the wide receiver throne.
Jefferson’s 98.9 receiving yards per game with Cousins far surpasses his 65 ypg average through six full games this season. Cousins’ mission on Sunday is simple: feed Jefferson. I’m predicting Jefferson will have a vintage performance with over 150 receiving yards and at least one touchdown.
#Vikings QB Kirk Cousins says he saw Justin Jefferson today, and is excited to play with him again: “You don’t go chasing things, but you understand the player he is, and you go where your reads take you. You know he tends to make it right when you throw in his direction.” pic.twitter.com/zOoSnvilDO
Green Bay’s 24 points per game ranks 12th-highest in the league through nine weeks, while Brian Flores and the Vikings defense are allowing a league-low 14.5 points per game to opposing offenses. Minnesota has held two of the league's best offenses, Detroit and Buffalo, to 19 and 23 points, respectively. This feat is even more impressive given the complete lack of help on the offensive side of the ball.
“This roster has earned the right to explore the potential to maximize where we can take this thing.” -Vikings GM Nolan Teasley on the decision to trade for Kirk Cousins pic.twitter.com/TkkJVs0fsp
This one is pretty straightforward: I have the Vikings righting the ship against a talented Packers team and ending their slide down the NFC North standings. While many had assumed star pass rusher Micah Parsons would be back by now, the Vikings have the distinct advantage of avoiding him in both regular-season matchups.
Two of these teams will miss the playoffs pic.twitter.com/7VewNM4oiT
With a reenergized offense, a motivated Cousins returning to the scene of a career-altering injury, and O’Connell in “prove it” mode, I think we finally see a well-rounded 2026 Vikings squad in action.

title: 3 Vikings Coaching Decisions I'd Make If I Were Kevin O'Connell Ahead of the Packers Game in Week 10
full_text:
Kirk Cousins is back in purple , and his first game with Minnesota will be where everything changed the last time he was a member of the Vikings. It was at Lambeau Field that Cousins tore his Achilles three years ago, and now he'll get his first action as the newest Viking this weekend.
Getting the offense rolling is clearly a top objective, but the defense will also need to stay on top of the Packers' high-flying offense. It's a tall task, but the Vikings already took down the Pack once this season and can certainly do it again.
Here's everything I would do if I were in Kevin O'Connell's shoes this week.
Cousins didn't come here to play school, and while he hasn't been formally announced as the starter for Sunday, it's all but guaranteed. And while the temptation may be to reel things in a bit and let Cousins try to get his feet wet, that thinking is what's done the Minnesota offense in so far this season.
Trying to dink and dunk down the field hasn't resulted in any success this year, and while it's kept turnovers and big mistakes to a minimum, it also hasn't moved the ball. The Vikings' defense was on the field for an average of 38 minutes over the past two games, and that's clearly unsustainable.
Cousins can work the middle of the field, and while his arm isn't what it was, the mid-level throws are still very much in his wheelhouse. His 91.6 Pro Football Focus grade on intermediate throws (10-19 yards) ranks fourth in the NFL compared to Kyler Murray's 59.9. An interception or two isn't the end-all be-all so long as the offense moves the chains . What will spell doom, however, is refusing to let Cousins play despite his hurried attempts to relearn the offense.
Blake Cashman popped up on the Vikings injury report with a concussion, and with a short week, it does seem to be a question of whether he can clear protocol in time to suit up for Sunday.
If Cashman can't go, the Vikings will turn to Pace and Golday to fill his mostly irreplaceable shoes. And while Golday saw his highest share of defensive snaps last week against Buffalo, Pace should really be doing the heavy lifting this week.
Pace notched a sack on just 22 snaps against the Bills and played arguably his best game all season. His role has shrunk year after year since his breakout rookie campaign, but Pace's pass-rushing abilities are still second-to-none at the linebacker position, with a 90.1 PFF grade. Pace's coverage abilities are another story, but Jordan Love and the Packers tend to do most of their damage on the outside, with Matthew Golden and Christian Watson accounting for nearly two-thirds of all receiving yards.
Golday will get his chance, but Pace seems like the logical option to handle the lion's share if Cashman is sidelined.
The dreaded Bills rushing attack can't hurt the Vikings anymore, and they'll now be treated to an offense averaging just 68 rushing yards per game. It's the perfect opportunity to work the first-round rookie back into the mix.
Banks was sat against Buffalo simply because his pad level has mostly been awful this year. He's been washed away and was frankly becoming a liability. The Packers may offer a friendlier matchup with their high-octane passing attack, allowing Banks to get after the quarterback--something he's at least done to moderate success with three pressures from the interior.
His development is certainly crawling along, but the Vikings knew it would take some time before Banks was ready to contribute in a major way. Last week's healthy scratch was just a matchup decision, and there shouldn't be any concerns about his long-term outlook at this point. Banks should see his typical dozen or so snaps again this Sunday.

title: Patriots Week 10 Inactives vs. Lions: How Will Rhamondre Stevenson Look Following Knee Injury?
full_text:
Happy spieltag, or game day! The 5-4 New England Patriots are just 90 minutes away from their second-ever game in Germany, and their first in Munich. On the other side are the 6-2 Detroit Lions, who have never played a game in the country.
Both teams are sitting in second place in their respective divisions heading into the game and are both gunning for spots in the playoffs. Something will have to give. It's a big week for the Patriots, coming off a big loss last week and needing a valuable win heading into their bye week. But injuries continue to malign them .
Here's a look at who was announced as both the Patriots and Lions inactives for Week 10:
QB Behren Morton (emergency third QB)
OG Walter Rouse (concussion protocol)
S Brenden Schooler (hamstring)
The biggest storyline is the Patriots getting both Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) and A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) back in the fold. They were questionable this week, and Brown will suit up for the first time since Week 7 in Chicago. It will be just the fourth game the wideout will play since coming over in June's trade with the Philadelphia Eagles.
Walter Rouse and Brenden Schooler were both questionable, but won't end up going. Behren Morton will only play if Drake Maye and Tommy DeVito both exit the game with injuries and offensive guard Andrew Rupcich — yesterday's practice squad elevation — will make his season debut.
Last week, Stevenson got banged up and was limited all week with a knee injury. National reports said that the running back was dealing with a knee tendon issue and might miss several weeks. Not so fast, he said!
Stevenson was listed as questionable on Friday, and after the Patriots placed TreVeyon Henderson (illness) on injured reserve and declined to elevate Terrell Jennings from the practice squad, the writing was on the wall for Stevenson's active status.
How much he'll play is up in the air right now , but seeing Stevenson out on the practice field this week was inspiring for his teammates.
"I think that just speaks to, first off, the media not really knowing 100% what they’re talking about a lot of the time,” Maye said this week. "And just a guy that wants to be out there, wants to be back for his team and we’re in the midst of trying to make a make a run here and win a big one before the bye. This is a time for players, a lot of the players on this team that are trying to get out there, play with their teammates and knowing that he’s a great player and can help us out."
Prior to the game, the Patriots made several roster moves. Two of those included officially activating fullback Reggie Gilliam and offensive guard Greg Van Roten off of injured reserve and onto the 53-man roster.
Getting Van Roten back in the fold is a big get for an offensive line that's continually been banged up with injuries beyond belief — especially at the interior spots. Since Van Roten got hurt in Week 3 in Jacksonville, the Patriots have had to start Matt Pryor, Ben Brown and Rouse at guard.
Brown injured his knee last game against the Green Bay Packers and Rouse was questionable all week as he worked his way through concussion protocol — which he didn't clear. Van Roten, with 106 career starts under his belt, should end up sliding in at left guard.
It was a rough showing for the Patriots defense a week ago, allowing 45 points and really letting the game get out of hand quick. They were without Charles Woods, who was downgraded pregame with a hamstring injury — something he'll play through today.
But they'll also be without Carlton Davis, who's been hit with a lot of injuries so far this season. That will elevate Woods into the CB2 role and potentially mean more playing time for rookie Karon Prunty. The Wake Forest draft pick didn't have the greatest of showings a week ago, allowing a touchdown on his first drive, but will have a chance to bounce back.
The Patriots will also need some players to step up to help defend Jahmyr Gibbs and the Lions rushing attack. If the defensive tackle trio of Milton Williams, Christian Barmore and Cory Durden can help plug up the gaps, that opens up the defense for New England to get after the quarterback.

title: 3 Key Storylines to Watch in Patriots' Week 10 Matchup vs Lions
full_text:
The New England Patriots are looking to put last week's disappointing loss to the Green Bay Packers behind them as they prepare for a difficult matchup against the Detroit Lions. At 6-2, Detroit presents one of New England's toughest challenges of the season, and the Patriots will need a strong all-around effort to come away with a win in Munich, Germany. Here are three key storylines to watch heading into Sunday's matchup:
After allowing 11 catches on 12 targets for 192 yards and a touchdown in their Week 9 loss to the Green Bay Packers, Gonzalez is looking to rebound against Detroit. "When your best players don't play good, you don't have much of a chance in this league," head coach Mike Vrabel said when asked about Gonzalez's performance. "So, we expect a lot more. He expects a lot more."
Gonzalez, who became the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history when he signed his historic 4-year, $135 million contract extension in September, understandably faces different expectations than others week in and week out. However, a bounceback is a tall order against a Lions team featuring wide receivers Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams, catalysts of a Detroit offense ranking eighth in passing yards per game (252 yards/game). And with veteran cornerback Carlton Davis ruled out with a knee injury, more responsibility lands on Gonzalez's plate. "As confident as I always am," Gonzalez said. "It's a week-to-week league, like I've told y'all all week, it's a new week. It's the same confidence that I always have, the same confidence I'll always go in with."
On Saturday, the Patriots activated both offensive guard Greg Van Roten and Fullback Reggie Gilliam from injured reserve to the 53-man roster. Van Roten (thigh) was placed on IR after their Week 3 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars, and Gilliam (knee, ankle) has been on IR since Week 4 after suffering an injury against his former team, the Buffalo Bills. Their returns should provide some much-needed depth and starting-level play to an offense that has struggled to stay healthy. Van Roten and Gilliam aren't the only Patriots who could be nearing a return, either. New England is also monitoring several other key players, including wide receiver A.J. Brown and running back Rhamondre Stevenson. Brown has missed the Patriots' back-to-back games and six of their first nine contests this season while dealing with ankle and knee injuries. After the Patriots sent 2028 first- and fifth-round picks to acquire him in June, Brown has recorded just nine catches for 101 yards since arriving in New England. He traveled with the team to Munich and is listed as questionable. His potential return and integration into the offense would be a shot in the arm for a receiving corps marred by injuries.
From Friday: WR A.J. Brown (1) warms up at practice. Seemed comfortable. Fellow WR Pop Douglas shared how nice it has been to have Brown back, saying he is their leader. Mike Vrabel said the plan was to talk with head athletic trainer Jim Whalen, and Brown, and then set a plan. pic.twitter.com/RIrem3QRKR
Stevenson, meanwhile, exited Sunday's loss to the Green Bay Packers with a knee injury. ESPN's Adam Schefter later reported that the running back was dealing with a knee tendon issue that could sideline him for a short period of time. Despite this, Stevenson missed Wednesday's practice, then returned as a limited participant Thursday and Friday. His status is also questionable. "The more that we can get everyone back, I think the more that it contributes to what we feel like we want to be as a team," Vrabel told the media. "One guy certainly doesn't make the difference, but it's certainly the more that we can get guys back, It's exciting that, you know, the pieces can start to build and come together."
One thing these two teams have in common is their lack of takeaways this season, with both recording just eight forced turnovers (tied for 25th in the NFL). However, New England gives the ball away at a much higher rate, as their 19 giveaways tie them for last in turnover differential (-11). "We got a tough challenge looking ahead of us, but certainly can't win playing that way, turning the ball over, not creating turnovers defensively, and giving up X plays," Vrabel said after their Week 9 loss. And while the Patriots certainly are hoping their fortunes change in Germany, forcing a turnover against the Lions is no easy feat. Quarterback Jared Goff has only thrown two interceptions through eight games, and as a unit, the Lions have only given up the ball five times. In a matchup between two teams that have struggled to create takeaways, New England will need to find a way to win the turnover battle. Against an offense as efficient as Detroit's, even one extra possession could prove to be the difference.

title: 5 Players to Watch in Patriots vs. Lions Matchup in Germany
full_text:
The New England Patriots' matchup against the Detroit Lions early on Sunday morning may turn out to be one of the most important of the season.
New England currently stands in the playoff picture, but a slurry of losses against its tough remaining schedule could complicate things.
But until then, here are five players to keep an eye on this Sunday when New England and Detroit take a trip to the game field in Munich.
Last week against the Green Bay Packers, Gonzalez had the worst performance of his career. The 24-year-old allowed 11 receptions for 192 yards to Green Bay receivers Matthew Golden and Christian Watson alone.
This week, the challenge does not get any easier. Lions pass catcher Amon-Ra St. Brown sits fifth in the league in receptions (61) and 11th in receiving yards (657).
"When your best players don't play good, you don't have much of a chance in this league," Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said last Sunday when asked about Gonzalez. "So, we expect a lot more. He expects a lot more. We need more from him and everybody else."
New England has a tall task ahead in trying to slow down Detroit running back Jahmyrr Gibbs. The 24-year-old sits top-3 in the NFL in rush yards (847) and rush touchdowns (nine). Who better to apply the brakes than Elliss?
The 27-year-old leads New England's defense with 65 tackles. Plus, he sits second on the team in tackles for a loss with 5.5. If Elliss plays at his best tomorrow, the Patriots could have a chance at victory.
As is the case with a substantial chunk of the Patriots' roster, their running back room has plenty of uncertainty around it due to injuries. Starter Rhamondre Stevenson is questionable for Sunday due to a knee injury which was reportedly expected to hold him out for multiple weeks. Plus, top backup TreVeyon Henderson was placed on injured reserve on Saturday.
With New England not opting to make a gameday practice squad elevation at the position, that could point toward Stevenson being good to go against Detroit. However, with the likelihood of him not being at full health, I still expect Kiner to have a substantial role against the Lions.
"I think Corey is working extremely hard,"  Vrabel said on Monday. "I think Corey has done a really nice job. But there are also some things that Corey has to be able to improve on, ust like a lot of guys, as far as recognition of the pressure and then the ability to block the pressure that we saw (last Sunday), for example."
Against a well-rounded Lions offense, the Patriots may need to rely on their well-rounded edge rusher. Ponder leads New England with 7.5 sacks and 9.5 tackles for a loss this season.
He's also been a turnover machine this season. The 24-year-old accounted for one of the Patriots' six forced fumbles this year, while also leading New England's defense in fumble recoveries with two.
Against a top-tier pass and rush attack on the other side, the Patriots may need Ponder to bump the Lions offense backwards a few times on Sunday.
The Patriots' left guard spot has been on a rollercoaster in recent weeks. Walter Rouse had taken over the gig until he was benched midway through New England's matchup against the Miami Dolphins. That's when Ben Brown took over, who then started against the Green Bay Packers.
However, he suffered an injury against Green Bay which will force him to miss this week's battle against Detroit. Fortunately for New England, Greg Van Roten was activated off injured reserve on Saturday and could step into the starting role over Rouse.
Regardless, whoever gets the starting nod will have a tough challenge ahead. The Lions have tallied the third-most sacks in the NFL with 27. Expect them to bring the heat against the Patriots' depleted offensive line.

title: What TreVeyon Henderson's Move to IR Actually Means for Patriots
full_text:
The New England Patriots announced a slew of roster moves ahead of their Week 10 game in Germany, one of which included placing running back TreVeyon Henderson on injured reserve.
The second-year player, who's officially listed on the injury report with an illness, has dealt with a neurological issue that's kept him off the field (and in the hospital).
"I talk to TreVeyon every day, and just like everybody else that’s not available, he’s working hard to get back," Mike Vrabel said this week when asked if there was a status update on Henderson's health. "And when that is, I don’t know. I don’t have a timetable. So, but I love my interactions with him. I love talking with him and seeing how it’s going."
Henderson opened the year as one of the team's most electric players on the offensive side of the ball. Now, he'll be forced to the sideline for a larger chunk of time as the Patriots look to right the ship heading into the stretch run.
Here's what placing Henderson on IR will mean for the Patriots, both in the immediate short term and moving forward in 2026 as a whole.
Henderson's speed and skills are some of the best on the Patriots. His ability to evade tacklers and outrun anyone was on display all last year as a rookie. But he hasn't looked the same this year. An ankle injury in a practice leading into Week 1 forced him to miss the opener, and he suffered another ankle injury later in the year as well .
The Patriots have Rhamondre Stevenson, who'll continue to carry the load out of the backfield. But his elusiveness and breakaway speed don't line up to Henderson's. The Ohio State alum also had the capabilities to catch passes out of the backfield, though that wasn't a major part of his game when healthy this year.
Overall, Henderson is one of New England's best young players. Without him for a playoff push, the offense will have to adapt when it comes to using their running backs in a variety of ways.
Henderson has missed the last two games with the illness and was already ruled out for this week's game against the Detroit Lions. He, along with Ben Brown and Carlton Davis, didn't take the trip to Munich for the game. Being placed on IR means he'll also have to miss more than just this week.
Considering the Patriots' bye week looms right on the horizon, Henderson will remain out of football activities for Week 10 vs. the Lions, the Week 11 bye, Week 12 vs. the Los Angeles Chargers, Week 13 vs. the Buffalo Bills and Week 14 vs. the Minnesota Vikings. The earliest he could return is for Week 15 against the Kansas City Chiefs.
The Patriots have used five of their eight IR return to play designations to this point in the year, and with Romeo Doubs, Alijah Vera-Tucker and Dell Pettus all working their way back, that could also mean that Henderson's sophomore year in the NFL may already be over. They'll get two additional designations if they make the postseason.
Stevenson, Corey Kiner and Lan Larison are the three running backs on the Patriots active roster heading into Week 10. Terrell Jennings remains on the practice squad as the top backup option.
With Henderson out of the picture for more than a month, it's going to put some stress on that trio — especially Stevenson, who's questionable for Sunday's game with a knee injury. Considering he returned to practice in a limited capacity and the Patriots didn't elevate Jennings for the game, that is a good sign for Stevenson's health moving forward.
But Kiner and Larison, two players who have added value on special teams, will have to be larger factors on the offensive side of the ball. Kiner scored his first-career NFL touchdown in Week 9 against the Packers (in garbage time, albeit), but has shown he can carry the ball consistently. Larison hasn't gotten a large role yet, but may be called upon more in the wake of Henderson's IR placement.

title: Patriots Roster Moves: TreVeyon Henderson Placed on IR, Veterans Officially Activated
full_text:
The New England Patriots are set to play their seventh international game in franchise history this weekend against the Detroit Lions. One day before kickoff, the team is making a few moves to help with their depth.
The team announced Saturday that they've officially activated fullback Reggie Gilliam and offensive guard Greg Van Roten to the 53-man roster off of injury reserve. To make room, they placed running back TreVeyon Henderson on injured reserve. They've also temporarily elevated offensive guard Andrew Rupcich off of the practice squad.
Here's what these moves mean for the Patriots for their Week 10 game:
The Patriots have been without Henderson for the last few weeks after he has been dealing with a neurological issue that landed him in the hospital . The second-year running back hadn't looked like the same player this season and has dealt with ankle injuries as well as he worked his way back into the lineup. He'll now miss at least the next five weeks (four games, plus the Week 11 bye).
"Recently, I experienced an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms that required hospitalization for several days," Henderson said in a statement posted to social media. "During that time, I underwent extensive medical testing and evaluation. While the results of my comprehensive medical testing have come back positive and reassuring, the cause of this remains unknown and unexplainable.
"I will continue working closely with specialists and physical therapists to focus on my recovery, as these symptoms have affected my strength, coordination, and some of my physical functions. I am committed to doing everything necessary to return to full health. My health and long-term well-being remain my foremost priorities."
With Henderson now being on IR for at least the next four games, it puts his immediate 2026 future into question. If he's able to return, t he Patriots would have to use one of three designations on him during the regular season. If they were to make the postseason, they'd get two more slots to elevate a player off of IR.
Henderson has ran the ball 52 times for 203 yards and one touchdown in six games this year, missing the season opener in Seattle and the last two games against Miami and Green Bay. The Patriots also have Rhamondre Stevenson, Corey Kiner and Lan Larison on the active roster at running back.
"I talk to TreVeyon every day, and just like everybody else that’s not available, he’s working hard to get back," head coach Mike Vrabel said Friday when asked about Henderson's status. "And when that is, I don’t know. I don’t have a timetable. So, but I love my interactions with him. I love talking with him and seeing how it’s going."
The Patriots have gotten banged up constantly up front, losing several offensive guards in the first nine weeks of the season. After Mike Onwenu went down in Week 2, Van Roten stepped up to replace him at right guard. One week later, he'd go down and be placed on IR.
Because Ben Brown (knee) didn't end up making the trip and Walter Rouse is questionable in concussion protocol, the Patriots decided to have Van Roten offcially return. He had until Nov. 24 to be elevated back onto the 53-man roster before his season ends.
Through nine games, the Patriots haven't had the greatest rushing attack, but getting another offensive lineman back into the fold should help open up some more running lanes. As it stands right now, Van Roten will likely slide into the starting spot at left guard — willing out the offensive line with Will Campbell, Jared Wilson, Matt Pryor and Morgan Moses.
The Patriots also added Gilliam to their 53-man roster after releasing undrafted tight end Tanner Arkin earlier this week. Arkin had gotten reps at fullback in the wake of Gilliam's injury. Gilliam, a free agent signing this year, played in the team's first four games of the season before going down with a knee injury. He should be able to help in pass protection as well.
Rupcich, who has experience across the offensive line at various spots, was called up from the practice squad for Sunday's game. With Van Roten returning to the lineup and Rouse being a question mark health-wise, it was good for the Patriots to add some more depth at guard.
The 27-year-old spent the summer with New England before an injury forced the team to release him from injured reserve with a settlement. He didn't sign elsewhere and was brought back a few weeks ago as a depth option as injuries continued to pile up.
Considering that the Patriots didn't elevate running back Terrell Jennings or cornerback Kindle Vildor, that should be a good sign for the game statues of both Stevenson and cornerback Charles Woods — who both didn't play/finish in last week's game against Green Bay.
The Patriots currently have nine players listed as questionable for their game against Detroit, including Stevenson, Van Roten, Gilliam, Rouse, Woods, wide receiver A.J. Brown, tight end Cameron Latu and safeties Kevin Byard and Brenden Schooler.

title: Patriots Running Out of IR Designations: Ranking Who Should Return ... And When
full_text:
Like Mike Vrabel said this week, the New England Patriots have been "wearing out the MRIs" this season. Every week (or nearly every week), a key member of the team seems to get banged up and miss significant time on the field.
The Patriots have had to place 13 players on injured reserve all ready this season, and that's not even counting some of the players who have dealt with lingering ailments off the IR list. Currently, the team has used five of their eight allotted return designations from IR and might have some tough decisions to make in the second half of the season.
They've already added wide receivers A.J. Brown and Mack Hollins, and offensive tackle Marcus Bryant to the 53-man roster after their IR stints.
"Let's get past the injuries here. Let's try to focus on the Lions and what we need to do to try to find a way to win the game," Vrabel said Wednesday. "But the injuries and the injured reserve, I mean, if you pay attention, we don't have too many spots left here to bring guys back on injured reserve."
With the Patriots set to play eight more games this year and depth becoming an issue, here's a ranking of how the team should prioritize their IR designations — while also considering more players might get hurt in upcoming weeks.
Note: This list is not counting offensive guard Greg Van Roten and fullback Reggie Gilliam, who have already been designated to return, but not yet added to the 53-man roster. Offensive guard Mike Onwenu, who is eligible to return, has suffered a broken ankle and is not expected to play again this season, hence his omission. Edge rusher Harold Landry is on the physically unable to perform list.
The Patriots' final draft pick of the year , Hutchins had a strong summer en route to a spot on the 53-man roster out of camp. The Boston College rookie played in the team's first two games, tallying three tackles and 12 snaps on special teams — part of the reason why he earned a roster spot.
In Week 2 vs. the Pittsburgh Steelers, he suffered a knee injury that landed him on IR. A few days later, he posted a photo to social media with a boot on, indicating that he might have received surgery. Despite some depth issues off the edge, the Patriots have gotten great play out of Dre'Mont Jones, Gabe Jacas and Elijah Ponder, so Hutchins returning isn't the biggest of concerns right now.
One of three undrafted rookies to make the initial roster, Jacobs was immediately placed on IR with an undisclosed injury. He's yet to make his practice debut in the regular season, but the Missouri linebacker has been a constant in the Patriots locker room since the beginning of the year.
Jacobs' hard-hitting mentality would go great alongside veterans Robert Spillane and Christian Elliss, but his placement on IR feels more like a redshirt-type season. He has the talent to compete at this level, but might benefit from a year on the sidelines.
A key part of New England's special teams units since signing in 2024 out of Troy, Pettus has come along as a core special teamer and a surprising player defensively. In 36 career games with the Patriots, Pettus has 56 tackles, two sacks and four pass breakups. He went down with an ankle injury in Week 2 vs. the Steelers, and was placed on IR on Sept. 23 .
In the wake of Pettus' injury, the Patriots have relied on a lot of depth defensive backs to help pick up the slack, including Kindle Vildor, Mike Brown and Elliott Davison. Pettus might end up returning later on in the year if the team has a few spots to spare, but his role on the team in totality isn't as urgent as some others on the list.
Doubs was a big part of New England's offseason this year, signing a massive four-year, $68 million contract in free agency. After a slow start to the year and drops that plagued him in the opener, the wideout started to come on as a big part of this offense.
Against the New York Jets in Week 6, he caught a 42-yard touchdown in the first quarter after getting wide open. He'd injury his shoulder on the play after falling to the ground and was placed on IR after the game. He's eligible to return after the Patriots' bye in Week 11 and should help complete the oft-injured wide receiver room for the stretch run.
No position has gotten injured more this year than offensive guard. Onwenu is likely done for the season, Van Roten remains banged up , Ben Brown has dealt with a myriad of knee injuries and Walter Rouse is in concussion protocol. Vera-Tucker, who has been injured quite a bit during his career, is also part of that group.
The Patriots' starting left tackle got hurt in the team's win over the Jets in Week 6 and was placed on IR ahead of their Week 7 game in Chicago. Like Doubs, he's eligible to return after the Week 11 bye and soley because of how depleted guard is right now, Vera-Tucker must be the first player brought back when he's healthy. He's also been seen in the locker room at times since being hurt.

title: Predicting How Patriots Fare vs. Lions: Will Christian Gonzalez, Defense Bounce Back?
full_text:
The New England Patriots , for the second time in four seasons, are set to play in Germany. This time, instead of the Indianapolis Colts in Frankfurt, they'll do battle against the 6-2 Detroit Lions in Munich — a far tougher test for a team that's teetering on the edge.
"I think they know how to win. They've built, I would say, a program that I know that they're proud of, and Dan's (Campbell) a good football coach," Mike Vrabel said. "So, certainly it'll be a huge challenge. They don't turn the ball over offensively at all."
Ahead of Week 10, Patriots On SI beat reporters Ethan Hurwitz and Zac Ventola break down how the game will unfold, which players will be x-factors and predict a final score. Who do you think is right?
Last week, the Patriots defense got historically gashed. The Green Bay Packers used an air raid-style of offense to run up the scoreboard. 45 points later and the Patriots defense was embarrassed. That can't happen again, especially against an offense in the Lions that has more weapons than Green Bay currently has.
Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Sam LaPorta, Jameson Williams and Jared Goff make up a five-headed monster that can spin the dial at you from any which way. It doesn't matter if the Patriots can score at ease offensively this week. They'll need to be able to stop the Lions from doing the same.
X-Factor: CB Christian Gonzalez
Maybe the headliner from last week's loss was Gonzalez , who was on the opposing end of Matthew Golden and Christian Watson nearly every play. In four seasons, it was easily the cornerback's worst game as a pro. If the Patriots want to win, they can't have their best players like Gonzalez (and quarterback Drake Maye, who threw a trio of picks), struggling. Gonzalez — and the Patriots — need a major bounce back.
Final Score Prediction: Patriots 29, Lions 27
Because A.J. Brown and potentially Rhamondre Stevenson are options to return into the starting lineup, this is not a New England team that was depleted like they were a week ago against the Packers. Sooner or later, Brown's first breakout with his new team will come and it will help elevate the Patriots offense. Is that this week? I'm betting it is (but I've been wrong before).
With its current 5-4 record, the Patriots are far from locked into a playoff spot. Assuming New England will need to finish 10-7 (at worst) to get a postseason spot, it needs near-perfection for the remainder of regular season play. With five of its eight remaining games coming against teams currently in the playoff picture, Sunday morning might be a must-win.
In addition to the Lions, the Patriots still have battles with the Buffalo Bills, Minnesota Vikings, Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos on the horizon. In all likelihood, New England will need to win a pair of those games, with Detroit potentially being among the easier of the group.
X-Factor: LB Christian Elliss
Against a well-rounded Lions squad, the Patriots will first need to slow down the ground game . Detroit running back Jahmyr Gibbs has become one of the most dynamic playmakers in the entire NFL. The 24-year-old currently sits third in the league in rush yards (847) and is tied for second in rush touchdowns (nine).
Although the run defense has been far from New England’s defensive gripe—it allows the ninth-fewest rush yards per game in the NFL — stopping Gibbs is an entirely different challenge. The Patriots will need a herculean performance from their leading tackler — Elliss — to have a chance on Sunday against the Lions and their ground attack.
Final Score Prediction: Lions 37, Patriots 30
While I do not expect the Patriots offense to falter, I find it hard to see a world where it can out-produce the Lions. Detroit has built the perfectly terrifying two-headed monster between wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown and Gibbs. Plus, it found an ideal game manager in quarterback Jared Goff.
By the end of the battle, Gibbs will have over 200 all-purpose yards and a pair of touchdowns, St. Brown will tally a score of his own and the Lions will be partying all the way back home from Munich.

title: Patriots' Playoff Hopes Could Hinge on Critical Lions Matchup
full_text:
The New England Patriots are preparing for an overseas battle against the Detroit Lions with significant implications for their playoff hopes. At 5-4, Sunday's contest isn't necessarily a must-win for New England, but it's about as close as it gets. With a difficult stretch of games looming after their upcoming bye week, the Patriots have little room for error as they look to remain in the AFC playoff picture. Here's why this matchup matters, along with what New England needs to do to come away with a win.
For the Patriots, 10 is the magic number. If they reach that win mark by season's end, they'll have a good chance of punching their ticket to the postseason. Five more wins, and you're (likely) in. But their remaining schedule is not forgiving; if anything, it got harder after the Nov. 10 trade deadline. After facing the Lions and having their Week 11 bye, New England will play the lowly Los Angeles Chargers before a rematch with the AFC-leading Buffalo Bills. From there, the Patriots will have a short week, hosting the Minnesota Vikings on Thursday Night Football. Minnesota boasts arguably the NFL's best defense, allowing the fewest points per game (14.5) and 280 yards per game, good for second-fewest in the league. Their Achilles ' heel was their offense, as the QB rotation of Kyler Murray, Carson Wentz, and Max Brosmer led to a passing game ranking 31st in yards per game (266.8). However, their deadline acquisition of Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins potentially makes this matchup far scarier for New England.
Trade: The Raiders are trading QB Kirk Cousins to the Vikings, per @rapsheet and me. pic.twitter.com/7Hxjt6TyR5
The Patriots will then face Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs, who traded for Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs, on Monday Night Football before closing out the season against the New York Jets, Denver Broncos and Miami Dolphins. Realistically, New England has just three remaining games in which they will likely enter as the favorite: the Chargers, Jets and Dolphins. Say the Patriots can take care of business in those three matchups, they'll still need two additional victories against the Lions, Vikings, Bills, Chiefs or Broncos to reach the 10-win mark. Detroit is arguably one of New England's better remaining opportunities to pick up a quality win. Coming out of Munich with a win would put the Patriots in a much better position heading into their bye week, while a loss would leave them needing multiple upsets down the stretch.
Injuries have consistently limited New England's offensive personnel this season, but the Patriots could be getting some important contributors back for their bout in Germany. Wide receiver A.J. Brown returned to practice for the first time in two weeks as he continues dealing with ankle and knee injuries, the latter of which may be connected to a reported degenerative knee condition. Brown has been limited throughout the season, missing six games through the first nine weeks while recording just nine catches for 101 yards. He was a limited participant Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday and is listed as questionable for Sunday's matchup. Despite ESPN's Adam Schefter reporting that running back Rhamondre Stevenson is dealing with a knee tendon issue that could sideline him for a short period, the veteran back has made encouraging progress. After missing Wednesday's practice, he returned as a limited participant Thursday and again on Friday.
RB Rhamondre Stevenson (No. 38, knee) is working off to the side at Patriots practice in Munich. Still a chance he could play Sunday. pic.twitter.com/9froK0PKFZ
We've seen similar situations play out in New England this season. Offensive tackle Will Campbell was initially expected to miss time after suffering a reported knee sprain in Week 5 against the Las Vegas Raiders, while running back TreVeyon Henderson was reportedly dealing with a high ankle sprain the same week.
Both ultimately played the following game. "I think that's just, speaks to, you know, first off, the media not really knowing 100 percent what they're talking about a lot of the time," Maye said when asked about Stevenson practicing. Getting Stevenson back would be a significant boost for the Patriots; he's their leading rusher, and his work as a pass protector for Maye is invaluable. Fullback Reggie Gilliam (knee) and guard Greg Van Roten (hamstring), after spending time on injured reserve, have had their 21-day practice windows opened. Gilliam returned to practice this week, and Van Roten's window opened last week. Neither has been activated yet, but both are questionable for Sunday.
With fellow guard Walter Rouse also questionable while working through concussion protocol, the Patriots could have some important decisions to make regarding their offensive line depth. Getting even one or two of these players back would be a welcome development for an offense that has struggled to stay healthy. It could also come at an ideal time, as Detroit has been vulnerable defensively throughout the season. The Lions are allowing an average of 355 yards per game, tied for 26th in the NFL, and have struggled to create turnovers. Detroit has forced just eight takeaways through its first nine games, the same number as New England. The Lions have also ruled out safety Kerby Joseph and cornerback D.J. Reed for Sunday, potentially giving Maye and the Patriots' offense an opportunity to exploit a depleted secondary.
New England will have its hands full on the other side of the ball. Detroit's offense is one of the most volatile in the league, headlined by wide receivers Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams, along with running back Jahmyr Gibbs. With playmakers galore, Detroit's high-flying offense ranks 5th in yards per game (379.8). The Patriots will need a much better defensive performance than what they delivered last week against the Green Bay Packers. New England surrendered 478 total yards of offense and allowed the most points scored in Gillette Stadium to date (45). That change starts with Christian Gonzalez. The Patriots' star cornerback, who recently became the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history, is coming off one of the worst performances of his career. According to Pro Football Focus, Gonzalez allowed 11 catches on 12 targets for 192 yards and a touchdown against Green Bay. "As confident as I always am," Gonzalez said when asked about his confidence in bouncing back. "It's a new week. It's the same confidence that I always have, the same confidence I'll always go in with." New England cannot afford another performance like that against a Detroit offense with this much firepower. Gonzalez and the rest of the secondary will need to bounce back if the Patriots hope to leave Germany with a win.

title: Patriots' Drake Maye Faces Long MVP Odds Heading into Week 10
full_text:
Nine weeks into the season and the odds are currently not in Drake Maye's favor to win this year's Most Valuable Player award. After finishing second in the running in 2025, the New England Patriots quarterback is a bit away from that top spot.
But he's surprisingly closer than some people might have expected. Despite being tied for the league lead with 11 interceptions , Maye has the 12th-best odds to take him the trophy ( according to FanDuel Sportsbook ). He's right next to Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott with +10000 odds, and is a step above last year's MVP winner in Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford (+25000).
It's a quarterback award and 12 of the top 13 players all play the postion. Only Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (who the Patriots are set to play in Munich, Germany, on Sunday) is the only non-quarterback with better odds than Maye (+8000).
Here's a look at where Maye currently sits when it comes to MVP odds heading into Week 10:
Players With Highest MVP Odds
Current FanDuel Odds (As of Nov. 13)
Cincinnati Bengals QB Joe Burrow
Buffalo Bills QB Josh Allen
San Francisco 49ers QB Brock Purdy
Jacksonville Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence
Green Bay Packers QB Jordan Love
Minnesota Vikings QB Kirk Cousins
Chicago Bears QB Caleb Williams
Kansas City Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes
Houston Texans QB C.J. Stroud
Detroit Lions QB Jared Goff
Detroit Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs
New England Patriots QB Drake Maye
Dallas Cowboys QB Dak Prescott
Based on how Burrow, Allen and Purdy are playing to this point in the year, you'll be hard pressed to find someone who'll vote for Maye over those three. When you consider how injured this Patriots offense is though, that might warrant more of a discussion for Maye's case.
So far, he's played significant snaps without his top three wide receivers (A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs, Mack Hollins), his top tight end (Hunter Henry), his second-best running back TreVeyon Henderson) and a myriad of offensive linemen (Mike Onwenu, Greg Van Roten, Alijah Vera-Tucker, Ben Brown).
Compared to last year, 2026 hasn't been as kind to Maye as last year was. Through nine games, the 24-year-old is 178-for-272 for 2,501 total yards and 21 total touchdowns. Through the first nine games of 2025, he was 189-for-255 for 2,555 total yards and 19 total touchdowns.
The records were also vastly different. Sitting at 5-4 now, the Patriots are clinging onto the final AFC playoff spot. They were sitting at 7-2 last year and atop the AFC East at this point a year ago today.
Some of that has fallen on Maye, who has two games this year with three interceptions. A rough September put the Patriots behind the 8-ball, but he'd rebound perfectly one month later. Maye was named the AFC Offensive Player of the Month for October and rounded into form as the Patriots started to win.
As it stands right now, Maye walking away with the MVP award is a little far-fetched. But if he's able to regain control of the train and start conducting it down the rails like he did a season ago, those odds could easily shoot up.

title: Patriots Attempting to Snap Nearly Year-Long NFC Streak — Plus Major Playoff Implications
full_text:
An unfortunate trend started for the New England Patriots after taking a humiliating loss to the Seattle Seahawks in Super Bowl LX. Since losing to the Seahawks last February, the Patriots have now gone on a four-game losing streak against NFC opponents.
Back-to-back losses against Seattle in the Super Bowl and Week 1 of the 2026 season make up the first two dropped games. Then, a Thursday night football loss to Chicago in Week 7 and last week's let-down game against the Packers put the Patriots at an astonishing 0-4 in their last four games against NFC opponents.
The last win the Patriots had against an NFC opponent, came on December 1, 2025, when the eventual AFC Champions rolled past the New York Giants on Monday Night Football.
Heading into another game against an NFC opponent, the Patriots will try to right the ship against the Detroit Lions in Germany, Sunday morning.
The way NFL scheduling works requires each division to play another division within their conference and in the opposite conference. These matchups rotate every four years and this season, the AFC East was tasked with facing all AFC West and NFC North teams.
The Patriots have already won their first AFC West game, beating the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 5, but their series against the NFC North isn't going so well.
After dropping games to the Bears and Packers, the Patriots are 0-2 so far against the NFC North. This week's match against Detroit will be New England's third game in the series.
Widely considered to be the best and most competitive division in all of football, the NFC North has a combined record of 25-9 on the year and total four losses against non-division opponents.
The four teams in the North also have the highest point differential of any four divisional teams in the NFL, totaling a +145 point margin against all their opponents.
After playing the Lions in Week 10, New England will host the Minnesota Vikings in Week 14 to finish their slate against NFC opponents.
Unfortunatelty for New England, the four games they're assigned to play against the NFC North are arguably the four most difficult games they'll play all season. But, there is an upside to that.
While losing never helps your team secure a playoff spot, taking a loss against an NFC opponent has less implications on playoff seeding than losses against an AFC opponent.
When the NFL seeds playoff teams they look at each team in the following order: overall record, head-to-head matchups, common opponents, and strength of schedule.
Here's how the NFL playoff picture looks entering Week 10 Which team is the biggest surprise? pic.twitter.com/Ibm9GKA22N
Despite sitting just over a .500 record, the Patriots have only lost one matchup against an AFC opponent, dropping a Week 3 game in Jacksonville. The Jaguars are heavily favorited to win the AFC South, so this wouldn't have much of an effect on Wild Card seeding anyway.
Common opponents are the next layer of seeding considerations, and the Patriots have faired really well against the AFC. They have a valuable win over the Buffalo Bills, who have beaten every other team they've faced. Depending on how the rest of the season plays out, New England has held their own against AFC opponents, which sets them up for success when striving for a five through seven seed.
Lastly, the Patriots have one of the most difficult strength of schedules in the league. Not only did they play the best division in the NFC (and arguably the best division in the AFC), but they played a first-place schedule after winning the AFC East last year, which requires the Patriots to face other first-place teams like the Seahawks, Jaguars, and Steelers.
The NFC North is a PROBLEM 🔥 pic.twitter.com/mkox9AGH18
If the New England ends up in a tie-breaker situation with another Wild Card team, their strength of schedule will likely give them the higher playoff seed. Six of the last eight games for the Patriots are against AFC teams, and will have very decisive outcomes.
Regardless of AFC playoff seeding, if the Patriots can reverse their NFC misfortune this Sunday and enter the bye week at 6-4, they'll show that they're ready to compete with the rest of the NFL for the remainder of the season.

title: Saints Activate Travis Etienne Jr. From Injured Reserve Ahead of Panthers Game
full_text:
Running back Travis Etienne Jr. will be activated from injured reserve for the New Orleans Saints ' Sunday game against the Carolina Panthers , according to Tom Pelissero of The Ringer.
The 3-5 teams face off for sole possession of first place in the NFC South. Etienne has not played since Week 3 against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sept. 27, when he suffered a hamstring injury.
Upon returning to practice this week, Etienne fully participated by Friday and was listed as questionable.
In New Orleans, Etienne is expected to share backfield responsibilities with Audric Estime and Alvin Kamara . Estime posted a team season-high 72 rushing yards last week against the Cleveland Browns , while Kamara has recorded 157 yards with a 3.3-yard average through seven games.
The Saints rank 26th in the NFL in rushing, averaging 95.3 yards per game and 3.8 yards per attempt under head coach Kellen Moore . They will test a Panthers run defense that ranks 28th, allowing 133.4 yards per game and 4.6 yards per rush. In his three games this season before the injury, Etienne rushed for 128 yards (4.3 per carry), including 57 yards against Las Vegas, and added 11 receptions for 51 yards.
The 27-year-old running back joined New Orleans during free agency on a three-year contract after four seasons with the Jacksonville Jaguars , who selected him in the first round of the 2021 NFL Draft. Etienne topped 1,000 rushing yards in three of his four years with Jacksonville. A Louisiana native out of Jennings High School, he played at Clemson, earning All-America honors three times and twice winning ACC Offensive Player of the Year.
In additional roster adjustments, New Orleans placed defensive lineman Christen Miller on Injured Reserve. The team also promoted tackle Easton Kilty from the practice squad to the active roster and elevated kicker Charlie Smyth for Sunday's matchup with the Carolina Panthers.
Smyth stepped into the starting role following the release of Daniel Carlson and capitalized on the opportunity. The Irish kicker provided all nine of the Saints' points through three quarters in a low-scoring battle against Cleveland, going 3-for-4 on field goals with conversions from 30, 27, and 48 yards.
