title: David Bailey vs. Arvell Reese Debate Takes Center Stage for Jets Again in Week 10
full_text:
Sometimes a draft can come away with multiple transcendent talents. That makes the team that chose one over the other smart regardless.
That's the situation the Jets find themselves in with second overall pick David Bailey .
Before selecting him, the team had to choose between the star edge rusher and off-ball linebacker Arvell Reese. The Jets opted for the pure pass rusher instead and have watched him blossom. Reese, meanwhile, ended up going to the Giants and has changed life for their defensive unit.
Two elite players, two highly impactful rookie seasons.
As the debate begins over which player is better, perhaps that key point is what Jets and Giants fans need to remember.
Every time Reese and Bailey are on the field, they will be compared to each other. It's the nature of having both players drafted to teams in the same city and mere picks apart.
In Week 9, Bailey stood out with a two-sack, two-forced-fumble performance. Reese, meanwhile, dominated as well with a three-sack effort. Bailey has 7.5 sacks and five forced fumbles, while Reese has been all over the field.
In Thursday's win for the Giants, Reese totaled 13 tackles and a season-high 84.2 tackling grade on Pro Football Focus . Another feather in his cap.
Arvell Reese plays so free. It all looks so natural to him. pic.twitter.com/iALiPjJ5tP
But that doesn't mean the Jets made the wrong pick with Bailey. If anything, his skill set and production are unlike anything the organization has seen in league history.
"We always knew he had a fastball off the edge, and he's done a good job of that," Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said. "But it's the other moves that he's starting to learn how to add into his repertoire to make him a more dangerous player. So, listen, there's still a number of games left for him to improve on that, and I look forward to seeing him do that. "
Bailey is on pace to upend Javon Kearse's rookie sack record at 14.5. He has gotten better against the run each week and remains a wrecking ball as a pass rusher. He is growing into the kind of star many edge rushers turn into.
But what sticks out most is the way the rookie carries himself.
New York was right to take Bailey over Reese. The Jets needed someone they could rely on to rush the passer, and Bailey has lived up to that. There's no guarantee their current scheme would have been a fit for the style of play and athleticism Reese brings.
That said, the Giants are thanking all four teams in front of them for passing on Reese. They would not be in first place in the NFC East without him.
It leaves a clear message: it's ok for both teams to come away with excellent players. They will both be the faces of their respective New York organizations for years to come.
And neither the Jets nor the Giants made a mistake in taking them.

title: How the Trade Deadline Changed the Jets' Game Plan vs. Bills in Week 10
full_text:
The 2-7 Jets host the 7-1 Bills, coming off the trade deadline , in Week 10. The teams were on different sides of the same coin on Tuesday afternoon. Both teams were a part of only one deal, but one bought and one sold. New York sent safety Andre Cisco to the Lions , and Buffalo acquired safety Amani Hooker from the Titans.
It wasn't an electric deadline for either team, but both moves raise questions. The rosters have changed, and with that, game plans will change.
So how will New York react to the respective safety deals come Sunday?
Gang Green sent away the sixth-year safety for a sixth-round 2029 draft pick. This wasn't a blockbuster by any means; New York is getting rid of a second-stringer. Cisco wasn't seeing much of the field this season. He played 191 snaps for New York this season but only 23 since Week 4. His departure won't affect much on the field, but it does leave New York with only three healthy players at safety.
Dane Belton and Minkah Fitzpatrick will have their hands full with the Bills' offense, with only Malachi Moore coming off the bench. Rookie safety VJ Payne also logged back-to-back practices to begin the week , but can he be trusted against the Bills?
However, Aaron Glenn doesn't seem worried about his team despite the quiet deadline.
"Listen, we're not going to hide from the fact that we're 2-7. We own that, but man, we're still working our asses off to make sure we fix that," Glenn said (h/t ESPN 's Rich Cimini). "We feel like we like the players that we have in the building to be able to help us do that."
The Jets' defensive game plan won't change much come Sunday as Glenn looks to show the Jets have what it takes to win. They will be thinner in the defensive backfield, but New York will roll into Week 10 with basically the same lineup they had in Week 9.
The Bills' trade was more of a blockbuster, as they acquired Hooker and a fifth-round pick for a second-round pick . The safety has been a ballhawk this season, leading the league with five interceptions. While the safety just arrived, the Jets need to prepare for Hooker being on the field Sunday.
" I'm going to play Sund ay," Hooker said to Buffalo media on Wednesday.
We're live with Amani Hooker as he meets with the media for the first time at OBD. https://t.co/OKxGbNKzow
New York will have to factor Hooker's presence into its game planning. Hooker immediately bolsters a Buffalo team that just released C.J. Gardner-Johnson. Instead of struggling at the position, the Bills now have one of the league's best at the position. It will be paramount for the Jets to take him into account.
The Jets have relied heavily on their tight ends and slot receivers this season . It now looks as if the middle of the field won't be as open against Buffalo. In Week 9, Geno Smith threw 14 of his 18 completions inside the numbers. Offensive coordinator Frank Reich's unit may have to take an approach more like Week 8, when Smith had nine completions outside the numbers .
Hooker's presence on the field may affect the middle of the field, but Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell should see plenty of opportunities because of that. Hooker no doubt improves the Buffalo secondary, but New York can still dissect a defense that has given up 15 passing touchdowns this year.

title: Aaron Glenn Must Put His Money Where His Mouth Is After His Will McDonald IV Comments
full_text:
Despite a 2-7 record and a four-game losing streak going into Sunday's divisional game against the Bills, it was a quiet trade deadline for the Jets as they decided to keep their roster together for the second half of the season and try to salvage something from a disastrous start.
Aside from trading safety Andre Cisco to the Lions , which was not all that surprising considering the diminished role and expiring contract he had anyway, the Jets stayed put while other teams like the Jaguars and Vikings went out and made some big moves.
One player who was among those expected to be traded was defensive end Will McDonald IV, who has expressed his frustration over his reduced snap count. That said, the fourth-year DE has the second-most sacks on the team this season (three) behind rookie David Bailey (7.5) and head coach Aaron Glenn believes he has earned a bigger role.
"His pass rush is second to none and he's been in a lot of those situations where he can rush the passer," Glenn said in his Wednesday press conference (h/t SNY Jets ). "And it's just my job to make sure I put him in position to play more because he is improving and I've always said this that you earn the right to play and he's doing that."
Aaron Glenn says Will McDonald has earned a bigger role: "His pass rush is second to none" pic.twitter.com/oWcbE0KqdU
While you could argue that Gang Green's inactive trade deadline was not necessarily a bad thing and said a lot about the Jets' future plans , the inability to get the most out of their best players and put them in a position to succeed has been a recurring issue for Glenn and this coaching staff.
They ultimately decided to keep McDonald around after the frustrated DE requested a trade , but if Glenn is so confident in his pass rush and giving him a bigger role, it is time to prove it on the field by putting McDonald in situations where he can go out there and back his coach's talk up.
While the doors opened after some missed opportunities at the trade headline, McDonald certainly emerged as a clear loser. Although he still has one year remaining on his rookie deal with a fully guaranteed fifth-year option for next season, he has been relegated to more of a situational role this season and has gone from a primary pass rusher to a third-down specialist who has played less than 50% of the team's defensive snaps in 2026.
Since the Jets have shifted to a 3-4 base front that has put more of the attention on Bailey and Kingsley Enagbare, McDonald has not exactly been put in the best positions to effectively rush the passer to be able to utilize his athleticism and make the most of the opportunities he has had through nine weeks.
As someone who can deploy a signature spin move and create a burst off the line of scrimmage, lining McDonald up wider could allow him to use his speed instead of taking on double-teams and being limited in his pass rush.
With the attention that Bailey is rightfully creating due to his elite play so far, pairing McDonald alongside him more frequently in nickel and dime fronts would take some of the focus away from him and free him up to create some pressure.
If Glenn can do that and move him around to make use of his agility against the slower linemen, in addition to keeping McDonald fresh for early downs and passing situations, he could maximize his pass rush skills instead of being put in a precarious position against power run schemes, an area he has struggled in.
Considering the Jets have three first-round draft picks and will most likely use a high-value pick on the edge, McDonald is still at the top of the list of current Jets who could be leaving in the offseason .
It simply would not make much sense for Gang Green to hold onto the former first-rounder if the snap count does not see much of an uptick, but Glenn's comments say otherwise, assuming he actually backs the talk up or is just using coach speak.
Despite playing on a defensive front that has battled its share of injuries this season, McDonald has been nowhere near the 66% of defensive snaps that he played across his last two seasons with the Jets. With an explosive Bills passing attack led by quarterback Josh Allen up next, it is paramount that McDonald resembles a similar snap count to the last two seasons—roughly 60-65%—while taking on a reduced role on special teams to preserve his stamina.
Glenn has doubled down on the process despite possessing a 5-21 record with the Jets. He and McDonald may both be on their way out of Gotham by season's end, but if he truly wants to back up his comments and put his money where his mouth is, he may be wise to let McDonald show what he can do over the final eight games as the season continues to get away from the Jets anyway.

title: Confidence Meter: How Close Are Jets to Firing Aaron Glenn After the Trade Deadline?
full_text:
Disappointing, frustrating, and embarrassing.
Those are just a few words to describe the Jets’ 2026 season. With New York on the verge of missing the playoffs for the 16th consecutive season, head coach Aaron Glenn’s job security has been the main topic of discussion.
While it’s unlikely Glenn remains with the team beyond its regular season finale on Jan. 10, would Gang Green be willing to pull the plug on him before then?
Even though there’s little belief that Glenn will be able to turn things around, there’s practically no chance he'll be fired mid-season
After an historically bad 2025 season, Glenn entered Year 2 with one goal: improving. However, the Jets haven’t made much progress, as many of last year's issues persist.
New York has the same record through nine games this year as it did last year. The team continues to struggle with poor execution, questionable coaching decisions, and an inability to make proper in-game adjustments.
One embarrassing stat line that keeps popping up is their performance in the final two minutes of the first half, where they’ve been outscored 107-9 in Glenn’s tenure.
While Geno Smith has been night-and-day better than Justin Fields, the offense hasn’t significantly improved, averaging 20.2 points per game compared to 17.6 last year. Additionally, they continue to struggle in the red zone, ranking 31st in red-zone scoring rate (40.7%). Whether it’s play-calling or poor execution, the offense has consistently found ways to hold itself back.
Defensively, the Jets haven’t been any better. Despite calling play-calling his “superpower”, the unit hasn’t improved under Glenn's watch. While New York ranks fourth in passing yards allowed per game (197.8), it’s surrendered 16 passing touchdowns this season and has only one interception during Glenn’s tenure.
However, their run defense has been the most glaring weakness. Despite overhauling the defensive line during the offseason, the Jets still struggle to stop opposing rushing attacks, ranking 26th in rushing yards allowed per game (128).
These are the type of growing pains you expect from a first-year head coach, not someone in their second season. Ultimately, Gang Green hasn’t done what Glenn set out to do.
Even though the team has shown minimal improvement under Glenn, we shouldn’t expect New York to fire him mid-season.
Since Woody Johnson took over as owner in 2000, he’s fired seven coaches. The only coach he fired during the season was Robert Saleh, who was hired by his brother, Christopher Johnson, while he served as the U.S. Ambassador to the United Kingdom.
With Glenn being Johnson’s pick for head coach, isn't likely to fire him before the season ends. This was evident during the trade deadline, as the Jets didn’t trade any key players despite Will McDonald IV requesting a trade and Breece Hall being involved in trade rumors.
By standing pat, it shows Glenn has the support and backing that he can turn things around in the final eight games.
Glenn may have backing from ownership to finish out the season, but there’s only one way he can convince them he deserves another year, and that’s by winning games.
Since Glenn took over in 2025, New York has posted a 5-21 record, including 0-8 against the AFC East, and is trending towards missing the playoffs for the 16th consecutive season.
You could make a strong argument that the Jets should be 4-5 or 5-4 this season, but they’ve been unable to win tight contests. According to Next Gen Stats , New York is 1-5 in close games.
Some of those games they should’ve won were against the Packers in Week 2, where they had a 10-point lead in the fourth quarter; Week 7 against the Dolphins, where they failed to execute in the red zone; and Week 8 against the Raiders, where they scored on their first six possessions only to surrender 24 second-half points.
New York doesn’t need to miraculously win its remaining games for Glenn to stay a third year. However, the Jets have to beat the bad teams and pick up some division wins to give him a realistic chance of keeping his job.
Looking at their remaining games, there’s no excuse not to beat the Chargers, Dolphins, and Cardinals. Add in a win against the Bills and Patriots, and it would go a long way toward persuading Johnson to give Glenn another season.
Otherwise, we should expect Johnson and company to begin another head coaching search in 2027.

title: 3 Eagles Who Should Barely See the Field After the Bye Week
full_text:
The Eagles have proven that things change on a dime in the NFL. Philadelphia entered the season with Super Bowl hopes, but enters its bye week with the worst record in the NFC (2-7). A team that has been focused on hoisting the Lombardi Trophy now needs to shift toward planning for the future .
There's been a lot of new faces wearing midnight green. That'll happen when the starting quarterback goes down, a Pro Bowl offensive lineman retires, and a star defensive tackle is traded . The Eagles have an opportunity to retool by focusing on youth and development over the final eight games.
That means decreasing their reliance on short-term veterans. Here's a look at three Eagles who stick out.
The Eagles had agreed to trade defensive end Arnold Ebiketie to the Bengals in exchange for a sixth-round pick. That was until Cincinnati backed out when they determined the deal would result in a lost compensatory pick. Ebiketie will remain in Philly before entering free agency at the end of the season.
The fact that the Eagles were ready to part ways with Ebiketie shows he doesn't fit into their 2027 plans. The 27-year-old has failed to make much of an impact, posting 25 tackles and two quarterback hits in nine games (48% of the defensive snaps and 37% of the special teams snaps).
Shrinking Ebiketie's role in the defensive end rotation would allow rookie Keyshawn James-Newby to play increased snaps . The seventh-round pick flashed with two pressures in 20 pass-rush snaps in Week 6. James-Newby's 9.0 sacks with New Mexico in 2025 led the Mountain West Conference.
Cornerback Kenny Moore II was not expected to take on a major role in Philly's secondary when he was signed in September. That was before Michael Carter II's abdominal injury. Moore has stepped in at safety as of late, playing at least 48% of the defensive snaps in four of the Eagles' past five games.
The increase in snaps was simply injury-fueled, though. Moore has struggled in pass coverage, allowing a 158.7 passer rating when targeted. The former Pro Bowler was picked on for an eight-yard touchdown, a 30-yard completion, and a 20-yard completion during a Week 8 loss to Washington.
Moore is 31 and playing on a one-year deal. He should stay on the sideline once Carter returns. The second half of the season is also a chance for the Eagles to see what rookie safety Cole Wisniewski can add to the mix. The sixth-round pick has been a hard-hitting tackler on special teams.
The Eagles didn't even wait until the bye week to bench quarterback Tanner McKee in favor of Joe Milton, who had been in Philly for less than a month. This comes after Andy Dalton beat McKee for the backup QB spot in training camp. The franchise clearly doesn't view McKee as a long-term option.
It's a harsh reality for someone who has been on the roster since 2023. McKee was inconsistent in his three starts this campaign, completing 72 of his 114 passes (63.2%) for 638 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions. The Eagles averaged a disappointing 15.0 points across those three contests.
"The Eagles benched Tanner McKee way too soon!" They went with Joe Milton for reasons like this. He's a dynamic athlete and behind this OL, this type of escapability is needed. This led to the Eagles third first quarter TD of the season. #Eagles pic.twitter.com/QV2BR5wiaw
The final eight games of the season should be treated as a tryout for Milton to earn a roster spot in 2027. If he plays well, he could be Jalen Hurts's backup. If he plays poorly, the Eagles could cut bait. It'll be up to Philly's coaching staff to make the most of Milton's strong arm and scrambling abilities.

title: 3 Sneaky QB Prospects the Eagles Should Already Be Eyeing in the 2027 NFL Draft
full_text:
The Eagles' ongoing losing streak will remain where it is for now as they take a breather during a much-needed bye in Week 10. Seven consecutive losses following a 2-0 start have sucked the oxygen right out of the room in Philadelphia, and a quiet trade deadline performance further hammered home that there won't be much to celebrate this season .
With the halfway point of the 2026 season here, it's time for Eagles fans to start thinking about the future—whether that's potential offseason departures or free agency signings . Some folks are even thinking about the 2027 NFL Draft, where the Eagles' selections will happen earlier than they're used to.
That said, drafting a potential quarterback could be on general manager Howie Roseman's radar in April. Questions surround Jalen Hurts's outlook after blood clots knocked him out of the current season , and it's safe to say that Joe Milton, Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton have a long way to go toward proving their long-term value.
Even if Hurts makes a full recovery, the Eagles would be wise to start thinking about the future. If Philadelphia wants to use its upcoming first-rounder on another position, there are still at least three sneaky QB prospects Roseman & Co. should consider on Day 2.
Hurts's mobility is one aspect that helps make him so great, so no one would be surprised if head coach Nick Sirianni wants his next franchise QB to have a similar trait. That's why UCLA's Nico Iamaleava could be on the Eagles' radar once the second round begins.
Standing 6'5" and weighing 215 lbs, Iamaleava boasts the size and athleticism that NFL coaches love. He's displayed a well-rounded game during his time at UCLA and Tennessee, completing 521-of-818 passes (63.7%) for 5,840 passing yards and 38 touchdowns to 16 interceptions while converting 283 carries into 1,078 rushing yards (3.8 per attempt) and 11 TDs.
Nico Iamaleava at his best is a top 3 qb in college football pic.twitter.com/S3pUYq4b01
Unfortunately, Iamaleava's 2026 campaign ended last month when he tore his ACL in a 17-15 win over Oregon, ending his final collegiate season. That said, medicine has come a long way, and there's no reason to believe that Iamaleava can't be a franchise QB in the NFL one day. If anything, his season-ending injury might help him fall to the Eagles on Day 2, depending on where they draft.
One season after leading the Big Ten in passing yards (3,711), yards per completion (14.0) and passing yards per game (285.5) en route to third-team honors, it's safe to say Jayden Maiava picked up from where he left off.
The USC product currently paces the conference with 198 completions, 2,524 passing yards and 20 TDs through nine starts. He's thrown for multiple touchdowns in six of his nine appearances, which includes a career-best five-TD game against Louisiana back on Sept. 12.
Jayden Maiava is quietly one of the most efficient QBs in the country 👀 ▫️ 86.5 PFF Short Passing Grade (#1 FBS) ▫️ 2,525 Pass Yards (#1 Big Ten, #10 FBS) ▫️ 20 Pass TDs (#1 Big Ten) ▫️ 1.0% Turnover-Worthy Play Rate vs No Blitz (#3 FBS) He’s no longer just the gunslinger,… pic.twitter.com/ZTeQRFhOtD
Maiava isn't without his flaws, which is why he's a projected second-round pick in most mock drafts. His play sometimes drifts into sloppy territory when he isn't completely focused, which can lead to turnovers (one interception in the first four games vs. four INTs in the last five). And, unlike Iamaleava, Maiava isn't a mobile threat, as proven by his averaging 2.4 yards on 173 carries (although he has scored 15 rushing TDs).
The offensive line has gone through injuries and departures this season, but Sirianni and his coaches know how to protect a quarterback when the pieces are there. If the Eagles can recreate that magic, Maiava is the perfect pocket passer to take advantage of that protection—especially with the weapons he'd have at his disposal (DeVonta Smith, Saquon Barkley, Eli Stowers, etc.).
Dante Moore is yet another collegiate QB whose season is lost, having sustained a season-ending concussion in September . That said, the Eagles shouldn't let any concerns keep them from drafting the Oregon product.
After all, Moore has the release and pocket presence that NFL coaches admire. His lack of mobility might be a red flag to some, but that's negligible when considering what he can accomplish without his legs being a factor. Moore racked up 39 TDs (to 10 INTs) and 4,491 passing yards in 19 games for the Ducks over the last two seasons, completing 71.4% of passes along the way. He even boasted a 9-0 TD-INT ratio before his current campaign ended, illustrating how efficient he can be.
Let's also not forget that there was a time when Moore was projected to be the No. 2 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft , only to return to Oregon for another season. That potential doesn't just fizzle away overnight, even if this season hasn't gone as planned. The Eagles could be big winners if they can grab Moore and tap into that potential, and other QB-needy teams passing on him might further motivate him to prove the doubters wrong.
Throw in the fact that Hurts could take him under his wing to get him to use his feet more often, and the Eagles have every reason to take a swing on Moore next spring.

title: Eagles Have Nothing to Lose by Giving One Rookie a Sink-or-Swim Test Moving Forward
full_text:
With a losing season almost a guarantee at this point , it's time to start thinking about the future in Philadelphia.
The Eagles used a second-round pick in the 2026 NFL trade to select tight end Eli Stowers from Vanderbilt. It was a relatively high pick for a tight end, but the Eagles clearly viewed Stowers as the potential future of the position in Philadelphia.
Unfortunately, Stowers experienced a slow start to his Eagles tenure. He struggled throughout training camp and was then sidelined for an extended period at the start of the season due to a combination of hamstring and quad injuries.
Stowers finally made his Eagles debut in Week 7 against the Cowboys on Monday Night Football. He didn't have any catches in the game, but at least he made it onto the field, which was a dream come true for the Texas native. “It’s a dream come true just to be out there, working, getting better," Stowers said after the game. "Just to be out on the field was a blessing.”
Stowers followed his debut with a three-reception, 53-yard performance against the Washington Commanders in Week 8, then went without a reception again in Week 9 against the Giants.
The Eagles now have eight games remaining in the current campaign, and with their playoff hopes already dashed, getting increased on-field opportunity for some unproven young players should be a top priority for Philly, and Stowers should be at the top of that list.
The Eagles simply need to see whether he is the future of the TE position, and the only way to do that is by throwing him into the deep end.
Despite speculation that they would, the Eagles didn't trade veteran tight end Dallas Goedert before Tuesday's trade deadline, and there's even a chance that he could be back in Philly next season . He's also 31 years old, so the organization needs to identify a succession plan at the position. The Eagles obviously know what they have in Goedert, and with little to play for in terms of a postseason perspective, the team should let Stowers eat into a large chunk of Goedert's playing time moving forward.
Second week in a row we are seeing Eli Stowers (No. 87) give this kind of effort blocking a CB Baby steps! pic.twitter.com/l5FhR3fGRI
The Eagles will have to make decisions regarding the TE position this offseason. Should they bring back Goedert? Should they look to add another TE in free agency? Should they draft a TE again? The front office won't be able to answer these questions properly unless they see a larger sample size from Sowers—both in the blocking and pass-catching departments.
Whenever Stowers does see the field for Philly, his aim is to be as impactful as possible.
“ Every single play there’s something that you can do to help the offense be successful ,” Stowers said earlier this month (h/t NBC Sports Philadelphia ). “Everybody’s got a job on every single play and so it’s every single rep. How can you be intentional about what your job is? Whether it’s getting open, catching the ball, blocking for somebody, running off for somebody. How can you do that to the best of your abilities? That’s what I try to do.”
Stowers seeing the field more over the final two months of the season will be beneficial for a couple of reasons. First, it will let him gain some much-needed experience in some relatively low-stakes games. It will also provide the organization with an excellent opportunity to evaluate him—and the tight end position as a whole—heading into the offseason.

title: What Fred Johnson & Hollywood Brown's Releases Say About the Eagles’ Plans Moving Forward
full_text:
There could be tumbleweeds blowing through the Eagles' locker room next week. That’s only a slight exaggeration, but there will be plenty of vacant lockers after some roster destruction during the bye week.
The latest move involved the release of veteran swing tackle and sometimes guard Fred Johnson on Friday. That came on the heels of the release of receiver Hollywood Brown , which came on the heels of the release of running back Jaydon Blue earlier in the week. Combine that with the trade of Jordan Davis, and the Eagles have four open roster spots.
The #Eagles are releasing veteran OT Fred Johnson, source says. He's been with the team since 2023. pic.twitter.com/y3Ln9Jm8kN
Cutting Blue signifies that Tank Bigsby and/or Will Shipley could be returning in time for their game against the Steelers on Nov. 22. Bigsby has been on injured reserve since Oct. 6, when a core muscle injury sidelined him. Shipley has been on IR since Oct. 16 with a partial tear of the plantar fascia in his foot. Both have missed the required four games.
As for the release of Brown, the Eagles are likely to get both DeVonta Smith and Tay Wicks back after the bye. Smith has played in just four games this season while battling a hamstring injury, and Wicks has missed three straight games with an ankle injury.
Neither player was placed on IR, so they can return at any time.
Brown wore the number 0, which has become a jinx of sorts since the NFL allowed that number to be worn. Nobody who has worn it since has lasted more than a year. Eagles who wore it previous to Brown are:
Johnson had been with the Eagles for nearly four seasons. He played in six games this year, but played in all 17 games in his previous three years with the team, making 14 starts.
His release signals the Eagles’ readiness to turn to younger players on the offensive line. There is an intriguing prospect on the practice squad who could be summoned. That is Yale’s Kiran Amegadjie, who is 6'5" and 326 lbs. John Ojukwu could also be a possibility.
The Eagles may not be done unloading veterans, either, as they transition to a team that wants to see the younger players play.
Safety Marcus Epps could be in jeopardy, with the possibility that seventh-round pick Cole Wisnieski could see time. Also, the Eagles could release Arnold Ebiketie and/or A.J. Epenesa and turn to seventh-round pick Keyshawn James-Newby. The Eagles thought they had a deal to trade Ebiketie to the Bengals at the trade deadline, but the Bengals backed out.
It might not even be a surprise if the Eagles give Uar Bernard and Josh Weru opportunities over the final eight games.

title: Failed Hollywood Brown Experiment Underscores Eagles' Costly Free-Agent Trade-Off
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — The Eagles are waiving veteran wide receiver Marquise “Hollywood” Brown , according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, who framed the roster move as a mutual decision both sides viewed as beneficial.⁠
Sources: The #Eagles are waiving WR Marquise “Hollywood” Brown, as both sides agreed it would be beneficial for all involved. Brown had 49 catches for 587 yards and 5 TDs with the #Chiefs last season and is expected to land with a playoff contender. pic.twitter.com/3MGeYJnqpS
Brown, signed in March to a one-year deal worth up to roughly $6.5 million with $5 million guaranteed after snaring 49 receptions for 587 yards and five touchdowns with the Kansas City Chiefs in 2025, managed just five receptions for 63 yards across limited appearances for the struggling Eagles offense.
The move comes as the Eagles sit at 2-7 amid a seven-game losing streak and broader roster reshaping under general manager Howie Roseman, including the recent trades of offensive lineman Cam Jurgens and defensive tackle Jordan Davis .
Brown was also widely thought to be a potential pre-deadline trade candidate, but no deal materialized. As a vested veteran released after the trade deadline, Brown must clear waivers and could draw interest from a playoff contender who needs help at receiver.
Brown’s short, unproductive stint in Philadelphia carried a longer-term cost that highlights one of the more painful free agency outcomes of the offseason.
Signing Brown canceled out a projected sixth-round compensatory pick the Eagles would have otherwise received in the 2027 NFL Draft for losing former starting safety Reed Blankenship to the Houston Texans.
Compensatory picks expert Nick Korte noted that the Eagles cannot recoup that selection by cutting Brown, as the relevant rule allowing teams to restore such picks through midseason releases was eliminated in the 2020 collective bargaining agreement. ⁠
Signing Marquise Brown caused the Eagles to cancel out a 6th round compensatory pick from Reed Blankenship going to Houston. The Eagles cannot recoup this comp pick by cutting him, as the rule to do so was done away with in the 2020 CBA. https://t.co/8CHFSdu40S
Earlier projections from PhillyVoice and OverTheCap showed Blankenship’s three-year, $24.75 million deal with Houston (averaging $8.25 million) would project to a sixth-round compensatory pick that Brown’s roughly $5 million deal would offset.⁠
In hindsight, Blankenship’s departure was about pinching pennies and hand-wringing over upside rather than his demonstrated performance and leadership capabilities.
Originally an undrafted free agent out of Middle Tennessee State in 2022, Blankenship rose to become a multi-year starter, team captain, and the secondary’s primary communicator—often described by coaches and teammates as quarterback of the back end.
Blankenship organized coverages, relayed adjustments, kept younger players aligned, and mentored emerging talents such as Cooper DeJean and Drew Mukuba in Philadelphia while contributing to the Super Bowl LIX championship defense.⁠
Defensive coordinator Vic Fangio and others have spoken of replacing his voice and leadership “by committee,” underscoring the void left in a young secondary.
That committee, which has featured Mukuba opposite Marcus Epps, Michael Carter, and Kenny Moore at times, has struggled. Blown coverages have become more plentiful without Blankenship directing traffic.
The failed Brown experiment illustrates the high stakes and moving parts of free agency with production that never materialized, a leadership piece forfeited, and a compensatory pick lost to the fog of misvaluation.

title: Kracz: Examining Eagles' Chances of Avoiding a 15-Game Losing Streak to End the Season
full_text:
It’s a question I’ve been asked a lot during the bye week: Will the Eagles win another game this year?
My guess is they will, but not many. Losing out wouldn’t be so terrible, though, because it would ensure a top-five draft pick this spring and heighten a soft rebuild that general manager Howie Roseman secure a top-five draft choice this spring and accelerate a soft rebuild that general manager Howie Roseman put in place with savvy moves to acquire plenty of draft capital over the next three drafts.
There’s time to debate the course of action the general manager and his staff will take in the 2027 draft, and there will be plenty of discussion. Right now, it’s about finding a way to stem what could be a soul-sucking 15-game losing streak to close out the season.
The losing streak wouldn’t break an NFL record because two teams—the Lions and Browns—had 0-16 seasons.
The eight teams remaining on Philly’s schedule are a combined 34-32-1. That’s not a murderer’s row, but the Eagles have been pushovers too many times during their seven-game losing streak. They've been outscored 179-100 since their last win on Sept. 20 in Tennessee against the Titans, and there doesn't seem to be much hope for success over the final two months.
Maybe they can find a way to defeat the Cardinals in Arizona on Dec. 6. Maybe they can beat the Colts at home on Dec. 13. Perhaps they can beat the 49ers on Jan. 3 and/or the Giants on Jan. 10, but maybe only if both teams have clinched their positioning in the playoffs.
Then there is this: head coach Nick Sirianni is undefeated coming out of a bye week at 5-0. The coach certainly knows the right buttons to push during a week off.
“This week gives us a great opportunity to spend extra time,” said Sirianni. “You're always working self-scout; you're always trying to figure out what you do well, what you don't do well. This week just gives you more opportunities for that.
“We'll use it very similarly to how we've used it in the past. Obviously, we have new pieces here that have not been here, so we'll take the good things that we've used in the past here and the good things that our other coaches have used in the past, and we'll come up with our best path.”
To move to 6-0 following the bye, the Eagles will need to beat the Pittsburgh Steelers on Nov. 22 at Lincoln Financial Field. The Week 11 showdown was supposed to be nationally televised at 4:25 but was flexed to a 1 p.m. ET start because of the Eagles’ poor play.
As the Eagles' struggles continue, their upcoming game on CBS against the Pittsburgh Steelers has been flexed from to 1 p.m. The game was originally scheduled for 4:25 p.m. At 2-7, the Eagles have fallen from must-see TV to a team mired in disappointment, plagued by an… pic.twitter.com/h5LtlqKjM7
The Steelers will come in after playing for first place in the AFC North against the Bengals on Sunday night in Cincinnati. Maybe they will be due for a letdown after such an emotional game and turning around to play a 2-7 team.
The Eagles beat Pittsburgh coming out of their 2022 bye, 35-13. Before that, in Sirianni’s first year, Philly beat the Commanders, 27-17. They beat the Chiefs on Monday Night Football, 21-17, in 2023, eased past the Browns, 20-16, in 2024, and knocked off the Packers last year, 10-7, at Lambeau Field.
So, there could yet be some winnable games this season, but to what end? The best path might just be to lose out and secure a top-five draft pick.

title: Eagles Week 10: 3 Most Important Games to Watch During Philadelphia's Bye This Weekend
full_text:
Philadelphia's bye week has arrived at an opportune moment . The Eagles will benefit from an extra week of rest and preparation in the midst of a dreadful seven-game losing streak . While the Birds may not be taking the field in Week 10, that doesn't mean they won't be impacted by the final scores.
This weekend's 14-game slate is highlighted by an overseas matchup of playoff contenders and an intense divisional showdown at Lambeau Field. For the Eagles, the contests involving losing squads have much more meaning, though. Here's a look at three Week 10 games to watch during Philly's bye.
Sunday's battle at Nissan Stadium will mark defensive tackle Jordan Davis' first game since he was dealt by the Eagles at the deadline . Philly sent him to Jacksonville in exchange for two high draft picks. The Jaguars are hoping the massive run-stopper can take their elite defense to the next level.
Playmaker incoming 😮‍💨 📺: NFL + | #DUUUVAL pic.twitter.com/pEiVyFUSCE
It'll be intriguing to see how well Davis gels with veteran pros like Arik Armstead and Josh Hines-Allen. Checking in on a former Eagle isn't the sole reason to watch this divisional duel. The Eagles' 2-7 record has them holding on to the No. 5 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft entering Week 10.
Tennessee (1-7) is one of three NFL teams to earn fewer than two victories through nine weeks. An upset win by the Titans would draw them equal with the Eagles in the standings, strengthening Philly's chance of landing a top-five pick. Take note that the Jaguars and Titans will face off again in Week 12.
The focus remains on the 2027 NFL Draft when highlighting a Week 10 clash between the Dolphins and Colts. Philly could rip off a few wins down the stretch, but its chances of making the playoffs are incredibly slim. Wins from teams below the Eagles in the standings suddenly carry notable weight.
Miami (1-7) and Indianapolis (2-7) are two of those four teams. A Colts' victory would catapult them ahead of the Eagles with a 3-7 record. A Dolphins' victory would place them above the Eagles for the moment, due to strength of schedule. Either way, Philly will hold a top-four pick going into Week 11.
Miami quarterback Kyle McCord will make his NFL debut on Sunday, following Malik Willis' groin injury. He grew up an Eagles fan and played high school football at St. Joseph's Prep. McCord was selected by Philly in the sixth round of the 2025 NFL Draft, before being waived after the ensuing preseason.
The Chargers join the Titans, Dolphins, and Colts (first-round pick owned by the Jets) as the four teams currently standing in the Eagles' way of the No. 1 overall pick. Los Angeles travels to Baltimore on Monday night as the only winless squad in the NFL. It is the franchise's first 0-8 start since 2000.
It's possible the Ravens could get caught off guard here. Baltimore acquired quarterback Jacoby Brissett to be their starter after both Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (turf toe) suffered injuries. Wednesday was Brissett's first practice with the team as he aims to get acclimated quickly .
There have been two winless NFL campaigns since the turn of the century. The 2008 Lions and 2017 Browns each struggled to a 0-16 record. No one wants to join that club, so the Chargers should have added motivation to compete. Any Los Angeles win moving forward benefits Philadelphia.

title: Eagles Can't Hide From Bleak Coaching Staff Reality for Much Longer
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA - Nick Sirianni says the Eagles won’t change coaches just to change them. Fair enough. But that feels like it's only delaying the inevitable with Sean Mannion, Chris Kuper, and Ryan Mahaffey.
After another flat loss that pushed the Eagles to 2-7 and a seven-game skid into the team’s bye week, Sirianni was asked about potential staff moves. The head coach repeated a version of the same line he’s used before: everything is on the table, but you don’t just change for the sake of changing because the record looks bad.
Sirianni’s premise is that you look at what’s real, you need conviction, and you don’t react to outside noise. He has publicly stuck with Mannion as the play-caller and has defended Kuper in strong terms, saying the new offensive line coach is coaching hard, teaching fundamentals, and giving players tools even if the results on game days haven't show nit.
Mahaffey, the run-game coordinator and tight ends coach Mannion brought over from Green Bay, has largely stayed out of the direct spotlight, but he is part of the same rebuilt offensive group that replaced Kevin Patullo and, more significantly, the long-tenured Jeff Stoutland.
The problem is that the “real” is hard to isolate right now. Attrition has muddied every evaluation. Jalen Hurts is out for the year with blood clots. Lane Johnson retired. The offensive line has dealt with injuries, scheme changes, and the sudden absence of the coach who had been its constant. Saquon Barkley has played through multiple ailments while DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks have missed time at receiver.
The quarterback situation behind Hurts has already flipped from Andy Dalton to Tanner McKee to the Joe Milton experience.
Through it all, the offense keeps failing to generate sustained drives, protect the quarterback, or establish the run. That makes it reasonable to question the scheme, the teaching, and the coordination between Mannion’s calls , Kuper’s line work, and Mahaffey’s run-game plan.
It is also fair to note that the sample is incomplete and chaotic. Injuries and personnel losses make it easier to argue that the coaches haven’t had a clean look—and harder to argue that the current setup is producing anything worth preserving.
Sirianni insists he is results-aware. The results, however, are that the offense has looked disconnected and underwhelming for most of the season under a first-year coordinator.
Claiming you care about results while continuing to operate as if this particular group is the right one creates an obvious tension.
Running it back with Mannion, Kuper, and Mahaffey next season feels increasingly untenable. The body of work, even with the caveats of attrition, has not justified another year of the same voices installing and calling the offense.
That does not mean midseason changes would fix anything. Firing or reassigning coaches now, with the season already lost and the roster battered, is unlikely to produce better football over the remaining schedule.
New voices would still be working with the same depleted personnel, limited practice time, and a quarterback situation that is not ideal.
The practical reality is that you play out the string. You gather whatever additional data you can, you keep the locker room from fracturing further if possible, and you accept that the meaningful decisions—on the offensive coordinator, the line coach, the run-game coordinator, and potentially the head coach himself—belong to the offseason, when there is time to search, hire, and install properly.
Sirianni’s reluctance to change for change’s sake is understandable on its face. But if the evaluation is truly results-driven, the current offensive staff is on thin ice.
While attrition makes the grade incomplete; it does not erase the results. The Eagles can finish the year with the group they have. The harder question is whether they should start the next one with it. The evidence so far suggests they should not.

title: 3 Pending Free Agents Eagles Could Re-Sign After Not Trading Them
full_text:
Jordan Davis was the only player the Philadelphia Eagles traded directly before the 2026 NFL trade deadline. That means the Eagles held onto a plethora of pending free agents, despite the risk of losing them for nothing over the offseason. However, some of the guys they held onto could remain in Philadelphia beyond the current campaign.
Here's a look at three pending free agents the Eagles could re-sign in the offseason after hanging onto them at the deadline.
People have predicted the end of Dallas Goedert's tenure with the Eagles for over a year now. Many didn't expect him to be back with the Eagles after the 2025 season, but he was re-signed over the offseason. And again, there were assumptions that he would be moved prior to the deadline this week.
But the deadline is now in the rearview mirror, and Goedert remains on the roster in Philadelphia, and it isn't impossible to imagine a world where the Eagles decide to bring him back again for the 2027 season.
It's not like the Eagles have another starting-caliber tight end waiting in the wings. Rookie Eli Stowers might be the future at the position, but he's barely touched the field during his first season, so he'll need more time to develop into a reliable starter.
Plus, with all their other needs this offseason, the Eagles won't want to spend big at tight end in free agency, and Goedert would likely be relatively affordable. Also, he's still a productive player. He led the team in touchdown receptions last season and has tallied 308 receiving yards and two TDs this season, despite dealing with injury issues and subpar quarterback play.
At the end of the day, the best option for both Goedert and the Eagles could be to run it back again in 2027.
There was a lot of speculation that the Eagles could trade defensive tackle Moro Ojomo before the deadline since he's playing on the final year of his current contract and is projected to become a whole lot more expensive heading into next season.
But the Eagles surprised everyone and went in a different direction , trading Davis to the Jaguars instead. This should be viewed as a vote of confidence in Ojomo on the part of Philadelphia's front office. Given this decision, it now seems exceedingly likely the Eagles will hold onto Ojomo and sign him to a new contract in the offseason.
The Eagles holding onto Woolen at the deadline, as opposed to trading him , will afford the team an extended opportunity to evaluate him for the future. The Eagles don't have a long-term answer at CB2 alongside Quinyon Mitchell, so all options should be on the table. Woolen has been somewhat underwhelming for the Eagles this season, but he hasn't been terrible, and the defense as a whole has struggled, so it's hard to single him out individually. He does need to be better about committing penalties, though.
It's far from a guarantee that the Eagles will bring back Woolen over the offseason, but if he plays well over the back half of the season, it's certainly not impossible.

title: 5 Necessary Changes the Eagles Must Make After Their Bye Week
full_text:
Eight games remain in an Eagles season that resembles a Talking Heads song: "We’re on the road to nowhere." It will be more than two months since they last won a game when they return from their bye week to play the Steelers on Nov. 22.
Their last win was Sept. 20, when Jalen Hurts led the Eagles on a magnificent game-winning drive against the Titans.
This won’t help turn things around, but here are five things I’d like to see happen over the Eagles' final eight games once they come out of their bye week.
Even when/if DeVonta Smith and Tay Wicks return from injury, the rookie should see a healthy number of targets. He has improved with each game played and is one of the bright spots on this horrid offense.
With Smith missing four of the team’s nine games, Lemon is now the Eagles’ leading receiver with 312 yards, two more than Smith has.
It’s a small sample size, but since Week 7, Lemons has had three straight games with at least six catches and 50-plus yards, joining Puka Nacua and Jaxon Smith-Njigba as the only three on that sort of streak.
That Dallas Goedert wasn’t traded for something—anything—is curious. Maybe nobody wanted to give up anything for the veteran tight end.
Even more curious is why Johnny Mundt and Grant Calcaterra are still on the roster. Maybe Zach Ertz doesn’t have anything left, but wouldn’t fans rather see him out there threatening to break a franchise record for most catches in a career that has stood since 1983, when Harold Carmichael had 589? Ertz has 582.
Second week in a row we are seeing Eli Stowers (No. 87) give this kind of effort blocking a CB Baby steps! pic.twitter.com/l5FhR3fGRI
Even with Goedert still on the roster, Stowers needs more of a role. That the second-round pick only played seven snaps against the Giants in Week 9 is ridiculous.
Goedert played 57 snaps (81 percent). Come on, the odds are he won’t be back on a third straight one-year deal, so why shouldn’t Stowers cut into that kind of workload?
The trade of Jordan Davis will likely make this happen. The defensive tackle has played just 61 defensive snaps in his second season, but has held up well in a rotational role. He needs to play more just to see what the Eagles have in him over the next two years of his rookie contract.
Zion Wilson spent the preseason with the Eagles but was waived on cutdown day despite recording nine tackles, two tackles for loss or no gain, and four QB pressures in three preseason games. He was signed to the practice squad on Oct. 13.
Wilson, who is 6'3" and 315 lbs, was denied another year of college when he tried to transfer from East Carolina to Virginia, so he entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent. In 2025, with East Carolina, he had seven sacks. It would make sense to either elevate him from the practice squad or just sign him to the roster to take Davis’s place.
Barring Joe Milton leading the Eagles to a win or two, play Cole Payton in the final two games. Heck, even if Milton wins a game or two, playing Payton should happen. It’s evaluation time, after all.
Same thing for outside linebacker Keyshawn James-Newby and safety Cole Wisniewski, who has one practice squad elevation remaining. Why play Marcus Epps? He’s not part of the future. James-Newby has done some decent things in limited opportunities.
Then there’s guard Micah Morris. Why not give him some reps, too? He’s a big guy at 6'5" and 335 lbs.
Let’s see what these players have.

title: Steelers vs. Bengals Bold Predictions: Alex Highsmith's Career Day
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers attempt to stake their claim in the AFC North and the conference playoff picture.
Taking on the Cincinnati Bengals, the Steelers can take the season series against their rival while earning their seventh victory of the season. After a bye week, the team is hoping to shake off the cobwebs before Week 10 action begins.
It’s the middle of the regular season schedule, but there is a playoff atmosphere to this matchup. The Steelers can get their seventh win of the year, and a few of these bold predictions might come true as well.
It’s been a little too quiet for veteran outside linebacker Alex Highsmith. He recorded 0.5 sacks in the team’s latest win, but he hasn’t recorded an individual sack since Week 2 against the New England Patriots.
His previous in-game highs are 11 tackles and 3.0 sacks. Against the Bengals this week, Highsmith breaks the tackles record and posts multiple sacks.
Jaylen Warren is the best piece of the Steelers’ offense, and It’s undeniable. He’s one of the best running backs in the NFL this season and he’s single-handedly carried this offense at times.
What he hasn’t done, however, is consistently find the endzone. He has just two rushing touchdowns and one receiving touchdown on the season, with two of his total scores coming in the same contest against the Indianapolis Colts.
That changes in Week 10. Against the Bengals, I predict Warren will dominate both out of the backfield and as a receiving threat. As a receiver is where I believe he will do his most damage, finding the end zone twice on passing plays.
The Bengals might have a plan to limit Warren on the ground, but that’s not enough to keep him from making an impact.
One area the Bengals have been so successful on offense is converting on third down. It doesn’t matter if they have significant yardage to gain, they tend to convert. Senior NFL researcher Tony Holzman-Escareno shared an interesting statistic recently that sheds light on this specifically.
The Bengals are the NFL leaders at converting on third down whenever they have at least seven yards to gain. When they are facing a third and long situation like that, the Bengals are picking up the first down 39.5% of the time. It leads the next-best team, the San Francisco 49ers, by nearly 5%.
Highest 3rd & long (7+ yards) conversion rate this season: 1. Bengals – 39.5% 2. 49ers – 34.6% 3. Raiders – 31.4% 4. Panthers – 30.0% 5. Jaguars – 29.2% 6. Bills - 28.9% 7. Seahawks – 28.8% 8. Bears – 28.6% 9. Chiefs – 28.2% 10. Lions – 27.9% Lowest: 28. Vikings – 18.5%…
The Steelers are likely to put the Bengals in third and long situations throughout Week 10. The only difference between Cincinnati’s previous success and this matchup, is Pittsburgh's pass rush. While the Bengals lead the league in pass touchdowns and third and long conversions, the Steelers are the best team when it comes to taking down the quarterback. It's a matchup of two unstoppable forces, and I'm betting on Pittsburgh's pass rush to limit Joey B and the Bengals to less than a 20% success rate on third down.

title: Steelers Legend Jack Ham Released From Hospital After Medical Emergency
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — Jack Ham is one of the best players in the history of the Pittsburgh Steelers and he recently suffered a medical scare that he is recovering from.
Penn State play-by-play broadcaster Steve Jones reported during the pre-game show for their Week 11 matchup vs. Minnesota at Beavers Stadium that Ham was released from the University of Washington Hospital and is back in home in Pittsburgh.
Ham, a color commentator for the Penn State Sports Network, suffered a medical emergency before Penn State's Week 10 road matchup vs. Washington at Husky Stadium in Seattle, Wash., on Nov. 7.
Penn State head coach Matt Campbell praised the University of Washington medical personnel for saving Ham's life after the 28-25 win.
Jones also said Ham would've been home yesterday, on Nov. 13, had the FAA not grounded all departing flights, but was able to get back home today, on Nov. 14.
Ham grew up in Johnstown, Pa,  and played for Bishop McCort High School before starring at Penn State from 1968 to 1970.
He was a two-time First-team All-East in 1969 and 1970 and was a consensus All-American in 1970, and led the Nittany Lions to back-to-back 11-0 seasons in 1968 and 1969, finishing with 251 tackles in his three seasons as a starting linebacker.
The Steelers selected Ham in the second round of the 1971 NFL Draft with the 34th overall pick and he soon became one of the best players in franchise and NFL history.
Ham became a starting outside linebacker for the Steelers as a rookie, and his pass defense and great tackling made him a dominant player in the "Steel Curtain ."
The Steelers won four Super Bowls with Ham, and he was an eight-time consecutive Pro Bowl honoree, 1973 to 1980, six-time consecutive First-team All-Pro honoree, 1974 to 1979, and a two-time Second-team All-Pro honoree, 1973 and 1980.
Ham finished with 160 starts in 162 games in 12 seasons from 1971 to 1982, with 32 interceptions and 21 fumble recoveries, leading all non-defensive backs with 53 takeaways and his 32 picks the third-most.
His play landed him on the NFL 1970s All-Decade Team, NFL 75th and 100th Anniversary Teams, plus the Steelers All-Time Team and Hall of Honor.
The 77-year-old is among a few remaining living Steel Curtain members, like fellow linebacker Jack Lambert, defensive tackle "Mean Joe" Greene, cornerback Mel Blount and safety Donnie Shell .

title: Steelers Get Promising DT Back From IR
full_text:
A key piece of the Pittsburgh Steelers ' defense has returned just in time to face the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football in Week 10.
Defensive tackle Derrick Harmon (foot) has been activated from the reserve/injured list according to an announcement from the team, putting an end to his absence that last nearly a month-and-a-half.
The 2025 first-rounder suffered his injury in the first half of the Steelers' Week 4 loss to the Cleveland Browns on Thursday Night Football and was placed on IR following the contest.
Harmon's 21-day practice window was opened on November 11, and after missing the minimum of four games while residing on IR, he might be back in action at Paycor Stadium vs. Cincinnati in a battle of two 6-2 AFC North squads that are both in the midst of four-game win streaks.
The 23-year-old was listed as questionable on Pittsburgh's final injury report of the week, though he was a full participant in practice on November 13 and would appear to be trending towards playing against the Bengals now that he's off IR.
As a rookie, Harmon flashed some serious potential both as a pass rusher and against the run despite missing a total of five games due to knee injuries.
Over 446 defensive snaps in 2025, Harmon finished with 3.0 sacks and a total of 27 tackles with 22 pressures (per Pro Football Focus ).
He started 2026 slow with a zero-pressure outing in Week 1 vs. the Atlanta Falcons (per PFF), though he more than bounced back with four pressures and 0.5 sacks.
Then, in Week 3 vs. Cincinnati , Harmon recorded a strip sack of Joe Burrow with under a minute to go in the fourth quarter of a 30-27 game that Sebastian Joseph-Day recovered, which clinched the win for Pittsburgh.
As long as Harmon continues to grow as a pass rusher and becomes more consistent across the board, there's no reason he can't become the next Pro Bowl-level talent on the interior of the defensive line for the Steelers.
While Harmon has been out for four games while Joseph-Day (triceps) has missed two contests up to this point and may remain out long-term , Pittsburgh's defensive line has remained one of the team's better position groups.
Both Cam Heyward and Keeanu Benton have continued to step up, as expected, and been somewhat of a dynamic duo for the Steelers while Yahya Black is growing into a difference-maker at nose tackle.
Sixth-round rookie Gabriel Rubio has had his moments too, even if he's been inconsistent, and even undrafted rookie Kevin Jobity Jr. made a splash with a sack in Week 8 against the Browns.
Now, with Harmon returning, Pittsburgh's interior defensive line receives a major boost heading into the second half of its schedule.

title: Steelers Add Pat Freiermuth to Injury Report Just Before Bengals Game
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — Pat Freiermuth has played a big role in the Pittsburgh Steelers' offense in 2026, but they may not have him for their upcoming contest.
The Steelers announced that they added Freiermuth to their injury report with an illness ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium.
He hasn't missed a game in the past two seasons, and the last time he didn't play was back in 2023, when he missed four games with a hamstring injury.
Freiermuth was questionable with a calf injury for the Week 6 matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on the road, but still played , with two catches for 11 yards.
Freiermuth has started all eight games for the Steelers this season and made 25 catches on 35 targets for 235 yards and four touchdowns.
He had his best game in the 34-22 win over the Indianapolis Colts at Acrisure Stadium in Week 5, with five catches on seven targets for 44 yards and two touchdowns, a one-yard score in the second quarter and then a 17-yard grab to put the Steelers up 31-22 in the fourth quarter.
Freiermuth had a season-high 46 yards on five catches and a touchdown in the 20-13 home win over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 1.
He has been a reliable target for quarterback Aaron Rodgers all season and helped improve the Steelers' offense throughout.
The Bengals have been a team that Freiermuth has been strong against, with 51 catches for 649 yards and 11 touchdowns in 11 career games vs. the Steelers' AFC North rival.
Freiermuth made five catches for 111 yards against Cincinnati in Week 7 in 2025, which included a 68-yard touchdown from quarterback Aaron Rodgers.
The Steelers took a 31-30 lead with 2:21 left, but the Bengals came out on top 33-31 on a field goal in the final minute.
Freiermuth set career highs in both receptions and receiving yards in the 16-10 win over the Bengals in Week 12 in 2023, making nine catches for 120 yards.
The Steelers will have to turn to Darnell Washington if Freiermuth is out against the Bengals, who himself has had a great season.
Washington has made 19 catches on 28 targets for 254 yards and three touchdowns, making for a great tight end duo with Freiermuth.
He is coming off a strong showing in the 27-6 blowout of the Cleveland Browns at home in Week 8, with three catches for a career-high 94 yards, including a 58-yard reception in the third quarter.
Robert Tonyan, who has played in seven games for the Steelers this season with one catch for two yards, is the backup tight end.

title: Steelers DBs Taking High Road Before Bengals Game
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers are entering a playoff mindset midway through the regular season schedule. Traveling to Ohio to take on the Cincinnati Bengals, the Steelers aim to take the season series and control of the AFC North division.
Leaving Cincinnati with a win will be quite the challenge for the Steelers. Despite defeating the Bengals 30-27 in Week 3, these are two very different teams meeting in Week 10. The Bengals enter with the best passing offense in the NFL, leading the league with an average of More than 285 passing yards per game and 23 passing touchdowns. Their goal is to feed their top duo of Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, and hope the Steelers cannot match up in the secondary.
The Steelers know and respect just how explosive the Bengals’ offense can be, and they aren’t shying away from it. Contrary to a bit of bulletin board material Chase offered the Steelers ahead of this matchup, Pittsburgh’s defenders continue to take the high road when it comes to pre-game smack talk.
"I want to do it again, but I don't want to get fined." Great question by @pauldehnerjr to Ja'Marr Chase. Has he ever signed a picture of him giving Minkah Fitzpatrick the double bird? He definitely has. Set off a chain of questions and laughter. #Bengals @FOX19 pic.twitter.com/5kZzgo2DcJ
Speaking to reporters ahead of the Week 10 contest, Steelers cornerback Asante Samuel Jr. shared how much of a challenge it will be to go against two “great” wide receivers.
“They’re just great receivers,” he said about Chase and Higgins. “They got great routes. Strong at the catch point, yards after catch.”
Samuel’s comments are just the latest from this defense, sharing the same message. They have gone in the complete opposite direction in the buildup to this battle. Instead of taking the bait and offering any bulletin board material to the Bengals, the Steelers are the picture of gamesmanship.
That’s important for two reasons. The first is that the Bengals deserve that respect. With such a dynamic and productive passing game, it’s impossible to ignore. And it’s not as if the Steelers contained Burrow, Chase and Higgins. It was quite the opposite for the Black and Gold, winning in Week 3 despite allowing so much offense to come from Cincinnati’s top three players.
The Steelers are well aware, specifically, of the big-play capability the Bengals' offense presents. They’ve been able to make splash plays and keep drives going by picking up big plays at timely moments.
“That’s how they thrive, off of explosives,” Samuel said. “That’s their M.O., you know? We just gotta control that and make our plays that come to us.
The second is that it continues an ongoing mentality the Steelers have embodied this season. Running back Jaylen Warren said it best after they defeated the Cleveland Browns. There was a ton of trash talk going into that game, but following the victory, Warren summed up the Steelers’ mentality as “some walk, some talk."
The Steelers get the chance to walk instead of talk once again in Week 10.
“As a DB, you’re a competitor,” Samuel said. “You want to go against the best, and this is the best. So, it don’t get no better than this.”

title: Joey Porter Jr. Trade Continues to Look Better for Steelers
full_text:
Joey Porter Jr.'s stint with the Dallas Cowboys hasn't gone swimmingly up to this point, making the Pittsburgh Steelers' decision to trade him earlier in the season look better by the day.
While speaking with reporters on November 12, Porter Jr. stated that "the whole foot is jacked up" and that he tweaked it against the Houston Texans in Week 4 (per ESPN/NFL Network's Jane Slater ), which was his first game for Dallas after being traded from the Steelers.
"The whole foot's jacked up," Porter said, per ESPN's Todd Archer . "I was playing on it for a while, and it just kept getting worse to where I had to shut it down. I feel like all the guys are wanting me to get back. They know what I could do when I'm out there on the field. I bring a presence out there that is a game-changing type presence. I'm just trying to get back out there as fast as possible."
Porter Jr. has missed two games for the Cowboys, first back in Week 5 due to an illness and then in Week 9 with his ankle/foot injury.
He's reiterated that his absence isn't due to his lack of a new contract, but it's hard not to feel like Pittsburgh made the correct decision to move him when they did, especially considering the odds of Porter Jr. signing long-term with Dallas seem like they're dropping.
After Porter Jr. and the Steelers failed to reach terms on an extension ahead of Week 1 after he missed all of training camp while on the PUP list with a back injury, it soon became clear that he wasn’t going to suit up for the team in 2026.
Because Pittsburgh doesn’t negotiate contracts in-season, Porter Jr. would’ve had to wait until the offseason to restart talks with the organization.
Instead of playing out his rookie deal, though, he essentially held out for the first few weeks of the year in hopes of sparking some sort of movement on the Steelers’ end.
That entire saga came to an end when they traded him to Dallas in Week 4 for a 2028 second-round pick and a conditional 2027 sixth-rounder.
While it stung to lose Porter Jr., who looked like a potential franchise cornerstone after a breakout 2025 campaign, Pittsburgh landed strong value for him from the Cowboys and cut ties at the right moment instead of playing out the string.
With it now feeling less likely that Porter Jr. is going to sign an extension with Dallas, as previously mentioned, that only makes the notion that the Steelers won the trade even stronger.
About a month before moving Porter Jr. to Dallas, Pittsburgh also sent Broderick Jones and a 2027 fourth-round pick its way in exchange for a 2027 third-rounder and a 2027 sixth-rounder ahead of the roster cutdown deadline in late August.
That felt like a good haul for the 2023 first-round pick, considering he was coming off a season-ending neck injury in 2025 and did not look like he was back up to speed throughout the summer.
Jones also didn't have a locked-in spot with the Steelers after the team selected Max Iheanachor in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft in addition to rostering Dylan Cook.
The 25-year-old has gone on to log just 67 total snaps for the Cowboys, and since he's on an expiring deal after his fifth-year option was turned down, it's hard not to feel like Pittsburgh won that trade.
The George Pickens deal from May 2025 is more of a toss-up, as he's also set to become an unrestricted free agent much like Porter Jr. and Jones in the offseason unless he's franchise tagged for a second-straight year.
Pickens was excellent last season, posting 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns, though he's taken a bit of a step back in 2026 with 533 yards and two scores over eight games for Dallas.
The Steelers also used the 2026 third-rounder they received as part of the package for Pickens on Drew Allar, who they hope can blossom into their next franchise quarterback.
There's a world where the Cowboys don't sign either Pickens or Porter Jr. to extensions. If that happens, Pittsburgh's status as overall winners in its slew of trades with Dallas will only grow even further.

title: Where Steelers Stand in AFC After Trade Deadline
full_text:
The trade deadline came and went without the Pittsburgh Steelers making a move .
While the Steelers could've used another wide receiver and/or a cornerback, they're still in good shape at 6-2 and are currently riding a four-game win streak into their Week 10 road matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football.
The gap between Pittsburgh and the cream of the crop in the AFC has grown, however, meaning the black and gold have some work to do if they want to embark on a deep playoff run.
With that, here is where the Steelers stand in the conference now that the trade deadline is in the rearview mirror.
The Buffalo Bills (7-1) and Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) had already been positioned as the top contenders in the AFC before the deadline, and their statuses in that regard were only boosted at the deadline.
Buffalo sent a 2027 second-rounder and 2027 fifth-rounder to the Tennessee Titans for safety Amani Hooker, who is tied for the league lead in interceptions with five and will help solidify a Bills secondary that's been a weak spot so far this season.
Jacksonville, meanwhile, parted ways with a 2027 second-rounder and 2028 fifth-rounder in order to acquire Jessie Bates, one of the top safeties in the NFL, from the Atlanta Falcons before trading a 2027 first-rounder and 2029 second-rounder to the Philadelphia Eagles for nose tackle Jordan Davis.
The Jaguars also acquired defensive tackle Davon Godchaux for a conditional 2028 sixth-round pick.
With Josh Allen leading the way, Buffalo's offense is pacing the league in both yards (386.4) and points (32.0) per game while being tied for the best record with the San Francisco 49ers. Now, its defense becomes more formidable with the addition of Hooker.
As for Jacksonville, it is arguably the most complete team in the NFL, considering it scores the fourth-most (28.6) and allows the second-fewest (15.1) points per game while now adding multiple legitimate difference-makers to its defense.
It's unfair to say that either the Bills or Jaguars are unbeatable, but accomplishing that task just got a whole lot tougher for Pittsburgh come playoff time.
The next tier under Buffalo and Jacksonville feels like it consists of four teams: the Steelers, Bengals (6-2), Denver Broncos (7-2) and Kansas City Chiefs (6-2).
While little separates that group of teams, an argument could be made that Pittsburgh is the best or second-best squad amongst that bunch, largely due to the strength of its defense.
The Steelers are currently allowing the seventh-fewest yards (305.6) and fourth-fewest points (18.0) per contest in addition to being tied for the fourth-most sacks (26).
Pittsburgh's offense is more of a question mark due to its inability to generate explosive plays through the air, but Aaron Rodgers is playing rather well and the team could get back two of its top wide receivers from the reserve/injured list in the not-too-distant future with Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger).
With Jaylen Warren emerging as one of the top running backs in the league, as evidenced by his 998 scrimmage yards (fifth-most in NFL), there is a formula there for the Steelers to rely heavily on their run game and put up points that way while imposing their will on opposing offenses.
Kansas City, Cincinnati and Denver are all dangerous in their own ways as well. Running back Kenneth Walker III has been stellar for the Chiefs since signing with them in free agency this past offseason, plus they still have Patrick Mahomes at quarterback to go alongside a defense that's playing at a very high level.
The Bengals' defense has also taken steps forward this year, though they're far from a perfect unit. Where they get dangerous as a team, though, is with their passing offense led by Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.
Tied atop the AFC North with Pittsburgh, Cincinnati is going to remain relevant to the Steelers in the race for the division crown for the remainder of the year.
The Broncos' defense isn't quite as good as it was in 2025, though it's still an incredibly formidable unit. Quarterback Bo Nix and their offense have really struggled, however, as they average the fourth-fewest yards per game (277.3), but they've won 16 straight one-score games and always find a way to get it done in the end under head coach Sean Payton.
Pittsburgh is neck-and-neck with all three of those teams, and if it were to match up with any of them in the playoffs, it'd essentially be a coin flip that might come down to luck and who has homefield advantage.
The next tier under the Steelers includes the likes of the New England Patriots, Houston Texans, Baltimore Ravens, Cleveland Browns and Las Vegas Raiders. Considering those teams are all essentially fighting for the final Wild Card spot at the moment, however, they shouldn't impact Pittsburgh too much moving forward, as long as it handles its business.

title: The Biggest Reason Steelers Could Lose to Bengals in Week 10
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers face a difficult challenge in their first game after the bye week. The team earned their week off after starting with a 6-2 record, but that's the end of the gifts this year's schedule has given them.
The back nine of the Steelers' season is filled with playoff hopefuls and spoilers, beginning with the Bengals. Pittsburgh holds the edge on their AFC North rival this year, defeating the Bengals during their first meeting of the year in Week 3. Adding on to that confidence is the fact that the Bengals just played overseas, and coming off of an international contest, there's no denying the Steelers are the fresher of the two squads.
Still, this is no gimme for the Steelers. The Bengals are trying to stake their claim at the top of the division and prove they are legitimate Super Bowl contenders. It will be an absolute battle between these foes, and there is one towering reason to believe that the Steelers could exit Paycor Stadium and Cincinnati with their third loss of the season.
The Bengals are one of the best passing teams in the NFL, and if they play their cards right, they can disrupt and agitate the Steelers' defense all game long.
The wide receiver position remains the focus of both criticism and optimism for the Steelers, but providing the secondary with no help at the NFL Trade Deadline was the more disappointing development.
And because of the Steelers' vulnerability in the secondary, the Bengals could take full advantage. Cincinnati already leads the NFL in passing touchdowns this season thanks to perennial MVP candidate Joe Burrow tossing 23 TD passes in the first 8 games. He's led the Bengals to an average of just over 285 passing yards per game (1st in the NFL) and 30.0 points per game (2nd in the NFL).
Ja'Marr Chase leads the way for the receivers, hauling in seven of those touchdown receptions. Once again, he's joined by a dynamic force opposite him, with Tee Higgins posting a team-leading 748 yards and six touchdown catches. Through the first eight games of the NFL season, they are one of the league's most productive pass-catching tandems. They trail only the Green Bay Packers' receivers, Matthew Golden and Christian Watson, for the honor of having the most combined receiving yards of any two teammates.
Containing both is going to be a big issue for the Steelers. In their previous matchup, they were unable to do so, surrendering at least 90 receiving yards to both. The worst part about it was that the connection was consistent all game long. Burrow was a combined 15-of-19 with 188 yards and two touchdowns when targeting his top duo.
In this meeting, the matchup is largely the same. The Steelers still have questions in their secondary, and the Bengals can exploit that repeatedly.
The challenge is on the Steelers to find an answer and respond to the Bengals' ferocious passing game. Otherwise, Pittsburgh's return from their bye week will be a very unsatisfying one.
